Reheating: 4 to 5 minutes in the microwave, then 2 to 3 minutes per side in the very hot titanium pan to recover the crispness. You can also use the air fryer for a few minutes for the same result.

title: Almond-peanut bars with chocolate-coconut glaze
intro: It all comes down to the packing: a well-compacted base cuts cleanly and does not crumble under the icing.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots: the chocolate melts over very low heat without sticking, the coconut milk is stirred in off the heat, and you pour directly from the pan. A single utensil to melt, blend, and glaze.
steps: Plan ahead: the glaze must set in the refrigerator for approximately 2 hours; allow for this time before serving.
In a rectangular dish, combine the almond flour, peanut butter and maple syrup. Mix with a spoon until you obtain a homogeneous, soft and slightly sticky paste.
Add the chocolate chips. Mix again, gently, to distribute them without crushing them.

Press the paste firmly to the bottom of the dish with the back of the spoon. Press firmly, working from the centre towards the edges, until the surface is flat and dense. This compression is what holds the bar together.
Melt the chocolate in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring. Allow 3 minutes. Remove from heat, pour in the coconut milk and mix off the heat until the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Pour the still-warm glaze over the pressed base. Tilt the dish to spread it to the corners.
Refrigerate until the glaze is firm to the touch and no longer leaves an impression, approximately 2 hours.
Turn out onto a board and cut into small bars, using a blade rinsed in hot water and wiped between each cut.
Serve with fleur de sel, added at the last moment so it still crunches between the teeth.

title: Sweet potato pizza with beef
intro: It all comes down to two distinct cooking methods: a sweet potato roasted long enough for its flesh to become dense and sweet, and beef seared hot enough to color without drying out.
titane: The pan never leaves the worktop: it roasts sweet potatoes in the oven, sears beef on the stovetop, holds the pizza base, and then returns to brown. Always preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the ghee: this preheating time prevents the meat from sticking and gives it a nice color.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Prick the whole sweet potato all over with a fork and place it in the titanium pan. Bake for 50 to 55 minutes, until a knife inserted into the flesh meets no resistance and the skin begins to caramelize.
Remove the pan from the heat and transfer the sweet potato to a plate. Place the pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until a light smoke begins to rise.
Add the ghee, then the minced beef in a single layer. Season with salt. Do not touch anything for 3 to 4 minutes: the meat will stick at first, then detach on its own once a crust has formed.
Crumble the beef with a spatula and continue cooking for 2 to 3 minutes, until browned. Stop cooking while it's still pink in the center; it will finish cooking in the oven. Remove from the pan.
Cut the sweet potato in half, scoop out the flesh with a spoon and spread it directly in the pan to a thickness of 1 cm, pressing down to form a regular disc.
Distribute the beef, the sliced red onion, then the hand-torn mozzarella.
Bake the pan as is for 10 to 12 minutes, until the cheese is melted and the edges of the disc are slightly crispy.
Drizzle with raw honey, sprinkle with chili flakes and serve in the pan.

title: Puffed quinoa bars
intro: It all comes down to the melting: chocolate that is melted too quickly loses its shine and turns grey when it cools.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a double boiler. The chocolate starts cold, heats up with the metal, and you keep a close eye on it from beginning to end. No water buffer, so no respite: very low heat, spatula in constant motion. The quinoa is mixed in the same pan, off the heat.
steps: Plan ahead: the bars need 2 hours in the refrigerator before being cut.
Break the chocolate into regular pieces. Place them in a cold pan with the peanut butter.
Place over very low heat. Stir from the first second without interruption, scraping the bottom. Allow 3 minutes: the chocolate should be melted, smooth and fluid, never smoking.
Remove from heat as soon as the mixture is homogeneous. Prolonged heat would cook the chocolate and make it grainy.
Pour the puffed quinoa into the pan. Mix for 2 minutes to coat each grain: the mixture should be shiny with no dry pockets.
Transfer to a rectangular mould. Press down with a spatula, evenly, to about 1.5 cm thick.
Chill for 2 hours. Unmould, then cut into squares with a smooth-bladed knife dipped in hot water and dried.

title: Crispy tofu in rice paper
intro: It all comes down to the coating: the rice paper, soaked in a spiced liquid and then pan-fried, dries into a thin and brittle shell.

ing.note: for basting and for the pan

titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat on contact. No oven is needed: direct contact is enough to crisp the rice paper. Place the sticks on top, then leave them alone. When the surface is set, it will peel off easily. If it resists, it's too soon.
steps: Drain the tofu and dry it with a cloth. Cut it into 8 even sticks.
In a shallow bowl, whisk together the water, soy sauce, curry powder, cornstarch, baking powder, and salt. The mixture should remain liquid, barely cloudy.
Dip a sheet of rice paper in this liquid, as you would for a spring roll. A few seconds is enough: it should become pliable again without becoming sticky.
Cut the sheet in half and wrap each half-sheet tightly around a tofu stick. Repeat for all 8 sticks.
Lightly brush or spray each stick with grapeseed oil on all sides.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in a drizzle of oil: it should simmer without smoking.
Place the sticks loosely in the pan. Leave them undisturbed for 4 minutes. They will release easily once one side is cooked. Cook in two batches rather than overcrowding the pan.
Flip them over with a flick of the wrist and continue on each side, about 8 minutes in total, until a regular golden color is achieved.
Reduce the heat to medium for the last 2 to 3 minutes, until the crispness is even and the rice paper doesn't burn. Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to prevent condensation.

title: Chicken tikka masala, smoothed cream cheese sauce
intro: It all comes down to the crust: marinated chicken that browns nicely before going into the sauce, and the sauce that then absorbs everything the pan has retained.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature, allowing you to sear meat coated in dairy without it sticking. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, grease it, place the pieces inside, and then leave them alone: they will release on their own once a crust has formed. Next, combine the onion, tomatoes, cream, and blend everything in the same pan, without transferring anything.
steps: Plan ahead: the marinated chicken rests for 30 minutes in the refrigerator, allow for this time before cooking.

Cut the breasts and thighs into 3 cm cubes. Mix them with the yogurt, salt and spices, then leave to rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. The dairy product tenderizes the fibres and retains the aromatics against the meat.
Place the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the fat: it must become fluid immediately without smoking.

Lay the pieces in a single layer, without crowding them. Let them take colour without intervening. Turn them only when they come away on their own and show a well-browned side. Remove from the pan (take out of the pan and set aside separately).

Peel and thinly slice the onion. Reduce to medium heat, add the onion to the pan, then moisten with a little stock to deglaze (dissolve the brown juices stuck to the bottom with a spoon). Stir until the bottom becomes clear again.

Peel the garlic and ginger. Add them grated along with the concentrated tomato puree, then the pulp. Leave to simmer for 10 minutes over low heat, uncovered, until the sauce loses its water and darkens slightly.
Pour in the cream, then blend using an immersion blender directly in the pan until you obtain a smooth, coating texture. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Return the chicken and its juices to the sauce. Leave to cook through for 10 minutes at a gentle simmer, the meat finishes cooking without drying out.
At the same time, cook the rice in salted water in a saucepan for about 15 minutes, and the courgette cut into half-rounds steamed or in the same water at the end of cooking.
Arrange the rice and courgette, place the chicken pieces on top, coat with sauce.

title: Quesadillas with seared ground beef and pickle sauce
intro: Everything hinges on the crust: a piece of meat spread out, motionless, which only comes off when it is ready.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold meat arrives. Spread the beef out, set a mental timer, and don't touch anything: a golden crust will form, and that's what releases the meat from the surface. The same logic applies to tortillas in the same wiped pan: don't move them, just wait for them to release.
steps: Peel and thinly slice the white onion.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Then add the grapeseed oil or clarified butter: these fats keep the temperature high without burning.
Sauté the sliced onions in the hot fat until golden at the edges, 6 to 8 minutes. Remove them (take them out of the pan and set aside separately).
Increase heat to medium-high. Place the ground beef and crush it into an even layer over the entire bottom. Do not stir. Wait for the meat to release on its own: the brown crust has formed.
Chop the meat directly in the pan, using the edge of a rigid spatula, into fine and irregular pieces.
Lower to low heat. Incorporate the reserved onions, garlic salt, pepper, smoked paprika, the 115 g cheddar, mayonnaise, ketchup and mustard. Mix until everything is bound and glossy, then remove.
In a bowl, mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, chopped pickles, pickle juice and pepper. Transfer to a squeeze bottle.
Fill each tortilla with filling and shredded cheddar, then fold. Count 10 quesadillas.

Wipe the pan with paper towels, return it to medium heat. Brown the quesadillas on both sides, without moving them before they release on their own. Remove them when the crust is crispy and the cheddar has melted. Serve with the sauce.

title: Goat's cheese cream, pan-roasted sweet potato and pistachios
intro: It all comes down to the first side: a sweet potato that colors before softening is nothing like a sweet potato that cooks in its own water.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in minutes and handles intense heat relentlessly. You get the caramelized crust of an oven roast, then cover to tenderize the center. One pan only, no oven to preheat.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2 cm cubes. Regularity matters more than exact size: uneven cubes won't end up together.

Pour the oil into the hot pan. Add the stock cubes, salt, and smoked paprika, then spread them out in a single layer. Don't overcrowd the pan: if the cubes overlap, they will release their water instead of browning. Do two batches if necessary.
Let it sear (brown over high heat, without stirring) until the cubes detach themselves from the bottom. As long as they stick, a crust has not formed.
Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. It's ready when a knife inserted into the center goes in easily. Transfer to a plate.
While cooking, finely chop the parsley and mint.
Blend the fresh goat cheese, yogurt, juice of half a lemon, half the herbs, salt and pepper, until smooth and homogeneous.

Spread the goat cheese cream on the back of a spoon in each plate. Place the still-warm sweet potato cubes on top, sprinkle with crushed pistachios and the remaining herbs. Season with pepper and salt, and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Chicken quesadillas with queso sauce
intro: It all comes down to two stages of cooking: a long, covered cooking that keeps the chicken moist, then a quick sear that gives the tortilla its crispy crust.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before oiling. Place the quesadilla in the pan and leave it untouched: no pressing with a spatula, no moving. The even heat of the titanium pan will do the work, and the quesadilla will release itself once the crust has formed. That's the signal, not a timer.
steps: In a mixing bowl, combine the raw chicken with taco seasoning, garlic salt, pepper, drained green chiles (reserve the juice) and lime juice. Massage to coat.

Place the chicken in a cold pan, pour the chile juice, cover and place over low heat. Cook for approximately 60 minutes, stirring no more than two or three times. The chicken should be opaque throughout and easily shred with a fork.
Meanwhile, blend the cottage cheese, enchilada sauce, milk, salsa and taco seasoning until you obtain a smooth sauce, without lumps.
Off the heat, shred the chicken directly in the pan (separate the meat into strands using two forks). Let cool slightly.
Fold in both mozzarellas, pepper jack, queso sauce, pico de gallo and cilantro. Mix until the filling is uniform and well combined.
Spread each tortilla with a generous spoonful on one half, fold over. You should have 10 pieces.
Clear the pan (empty and wipe it), return it to medium-high heat and preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Drizzle with oil and distribute it over the entire surface.

Place the quesadillas two by two. Let them sit for 3 minutes without touching: they will release on their own when the side is golden. Flip, cook for 3 minutes more until they are golden brown on both sides.
Let cool slightly on a rack, then wrap each quesadilla in aluminum foil.

title: Gluten-free walnut bread
intro: Gluten-free, it is the psyllium that holds the dough together: respect its gelling time, everything else depends on it.
titane: The titanium pan serves as the first cooking chamber. Covered and over moderate heat, it sears the base and forms a thick crust that the oven alone cannot produce. It then goes into the oven, uncovered, to cook the crumb thoroughly: you save on preheating time and get a crispier loaf.
steps: Pour the water over the psyllium in a mixing bowl. Whisk for a few seconds, then let it gel (the psyllium absorbs the water and forms a gel) for 5 minutes. The texture should become soft and elastic.
In a second container, combine the flour, yeast, bicarbonate soda and the roughly crushed walnuts. Mix dry.
Incorporate the psyllium gel into the powders. Work first with a dough scraper, then by hand.
Knead for 10 minutes, until you obtain a smooth, homogeneous ball that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Shape a round loaf, slightly flattened, to the diameter of your titanium pan. Lightly oil the pan with grapeseed oil.
Place the loaf in the cold pan. Cover and cook on low to medium heat for 20 minutes. Do not try to turn it over until it detaches itself from the bottom on its own.
Turn it with a quick flick of the wrist. Cover again and continue for 15 minutes on the same heat until the second side is golden.

Preheat the oven. Place the pan uncovered in the oven at 190°C for 20 minutes. The bread is cooked when the crust is amber-coloured and it sounds hollow when you tap (tap with your fingertips) on the bottom.
Remove from the pan onto a wire rack and let cool completely before slicing: the crumb continues to set as it cools.

title: Chocolate protein ice cream with peanut swirl
intro: It's all about the texture: a well-hydrated base, a fairly long chilling period, and a marbling of melted peanut poured into the center of the pot rather than on the surface.
titane: The titanium pan serves only one purpose here: to melt the peanut butter chips with the coconut oil over very low heat. You watch the mixture change state, and you remove it from the heat as soon as it coats the spatula. The microwave heats in patches and solidifies the peanut butter into lumps; the pan allows you to stop the melting process with precision.
steps: Plan ahead: the base rests in the freezer for 16 hours, start the day before.

Combine the protein drink, sweetener, cocoa, pinch of salt and xanthan gum in a tall container. Blend with an immersion blender until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture with no cocoa particles in suspension. The xanthan gum must be dispersed, not in clumps.
Pour the base into the ice cream machine bowl. Close, lay it flat in the freezer and leave to set for 16 hours. One night is not always enough: the base must be hard from edge to edge.
Run the outside of the bowl under hot water for one full minute. The block should detach from the sides when you tilt the bowl.
Install the bowl and start the light ice cream programme. After the first cycle, the surface is often grainy: this is normal.
If the texture remains powdery, run another cycle. You are looking for a homogeneous and glossy mass that holds on the spoon.

Meanwhile, put the peanut butter chips, coconut oil and pinch of salt in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir constantly and lift the pan from the heat in bursts: the mixture must melt, never simmer. Allow one minute. Remove from heat (transfer out of the pan) as soon as it is smooth.
With a butter knife, dig a well in the centre of the ice cream down to the bottom of the bowl. Pour the melted mixture still warm into it.
Start the swirl incorporation cycle. The swirl must appear throughout the height, not just on the surface.
Sprinkle with crushed chocolate-peanut bite and serve immediately.

title: Beef rolls with cheddar shell
intro: It all comes down to the shell: cheddar melted until it bubbles, which detaches itself from the pan and encloses the filling in a golden crust.
titane: One pan for two contrasting uses. First, quickly sear beef over medium heat in a preheated, empty pan. Then, with the pan wiped clean and the heat reduced, slowly melt cheddar cheese. The rapid temperature rise of the titanium creates a smooth, even surface that releases easily, without sticking or needing to change pans.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Pour the grape seed oil: it should ripple slightly without smoking.
Add the ground beef and let it brown without stirring. It will detach on its own once the crust forms; this takes approximately 10 minutes total as you gradually break it up.
Season with garlic salt, onion powder, and Italian seasoning. Mix well.
Off the heat, stir in the turkey pepperoni, minced garlic, tomato sauce, and parsley. Cook for 2 minutes more, until the sauce coats the meat.
Mix until the filling is homogeneous, then remove from the pan and let cool slightly.
Divide the filling into 10 portions. Fill each with mozzarella, seal, and roll into firm logs. Place them seam-side up.
Wipe the pan. Over low heat, spread the cheddar in an even layer and let it melt for 3 minutes, until it bubbles across the entire surface.
Place the rolls seam-side down on the melted cheddar. Do not move them: the crust will form and detach from the pan on its own.
Turn with a quick flick and cook the other side until the cheese is golden and crispy.
Let cool on a wire rack, crispy side facing up.
Wrap each roll in aluminium foil or a sealed freezer bag. Keep frozen for up to 3 months.
To reheat, remove a roll from the freezer and wrap it loosely in a damp paper towel. Microwave on a plate for 3 to 4 minutes.
If you prefer it crispy, return the roll to the pan or air fryer for a few minutes.

title: Pumpkin and carrot puree, soft-boiled egg and parmesan
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the puree: enough body to hold under the egg, enough flexibility to coat the spoon.
titane: One pan from start to finish. Preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes, it receives the vegetables and a little water, covered: the short steam softens them without drowning them. Rinsed, it then receives less than 300 ml of water for soft-boiled eggs. No steamer, no saucepan.
steps: Peel the squash, remove the seeds, and cut the flesh into 2 cm cubes. Peel the carrots and cut them into thin slices.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the clarified butter or grapeseed oil. The even heat distribution prevents the vegetables from sticking.

Add the squash and carrots, 2 to 3 tablespoons of water, and cover. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. The pieces should be very tender and easily mashed with a fork.
Remove the vegetables (transfer them from the pan) to the blender bowl. Rinse the pan.
Bring 250 ml of water to a boil in the pan, plunge in the eggs and cook for exactly 6 minutes 30 seconds.
Transfer them immediately to a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking, then peel them (remove the shell) once they are cold.
Roughly chop the walnuts, finely chop the chives, and set aside.
Blend the vegetables with the olive oil, half the milk, salt, pepper, and smoked paprika until smooth. Gradually add the remaining milk until you reach the desired consistency.
Make parmesan shavings using a vegetable peeler.
Divide the purée between two bowls, place the halved eggs on top, then the walnuts, shavings and chives. Adjust the seasoning.

title: Buffalo chicken orzo
intro: It all comes down to two things: a good crust on the chicken, and a sauce added off the heat so that it doesn't curdle.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly: preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The chicken will stick at first, then release easily once a crust has formed—this is the only reliable indicator for turning it. The juices (caramelized deposits left at the bottom of the pan) then remain in place and flavor the orzo, which is cooking in the same pan.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese, buffalo sauce, cream cheese, 14 g of ranch, and 4 g of pepper until smooth and lump-free. Reserve in the refrigerator.
Place the chicken breasts between two sheets of plastic wrap, flatten them with a rolling pin or the bottom of a saucepan to an even thickness. Consistent thickness ensures even cooking.
Mix garlic salt, ranch, smoked paprika, onion powder, and pepper. Coat the chicken on all sides with no bare patches.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the oil: it should ripple across the surface.
Place the chicken without pressing it down, in batches if necessary. Do not touch it. Turn it when it releases on its own, continue until the crust is well browned and the chicken is cooked through.
Remove from the pan and set aside. Let rest for 5 minutes, then slice or shred.
In the same pan, over the drippings, sauté the onions and garlic for 3 to 4 minutes over medium heat until translucent.
Pour in the dry orzo and broth. Cover, reduce to low heat, allow 15 minutes while stirring regularly to loosen the browned bits. The orzo should be tender and the liquid absorbed.
Stir in the mozzarella. Remove from heat and let cool for 5 minutes, then add the buffalo sauce and mix. If added too hot, it will become grainy.
Divide into 10 portions, place the chicken on top, sprinkle with chopped parsley. Cool quickly before sealing the containers and freezing.

title: Pan-fried sunflower seed bread
intro: Without flour or yeast, this bread owes its crumb to two things: a fairly fine seed powder and sufficient resting of the psyllium, which structures the dough in place of gluten.

ing.note: plus 1 heaping tablespoon for the topping

titane: A covered pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty, it sears the bottom of the galette and creates a crust in minutes; the lid then traps the steam and steams the dough (cooking in its own moisture, covered), causing it to puff up. A single, decisive flip halfway through cooking.
steps: Blend the 200 g of sunflower seeds for 30 seconds, until you obtain a fine powder comparable to flour. Stop as soon as the texture is homogeneous: beyond that, the seeds release their oil and the powder compacts.
Add the eggs and salt. Mix until the preparation is smooth.
Incorporate the psyllium. Work for about thirty seconds: the dough thickens and becomes elastic, it stretches without breaking. Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Dampen your hands, then shape into a ball. Flatten it into a pancake with a diameter matching the bottom of your pan, about 3 cm thick.
Sprinkle whole sunflower seeds on top and press them lightly with the palm of your hand so they adhere.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil. It should ripple without smoking.
Place the pancake, cover and reduce to low-medium heat. Cook for 15 minutes without touching it. The bread will release itself from the bottom when the underside is set: that is the signal.
Flip it with a flick of the wrist. Cover again and continue for 10 minutes, until it is puffed up, golden on both sides and sounds hollow when you tap it with your fingertip.
Transfer to a wire rack and let cool for 15 minutes before slicing. If cut while too hot, it will crumble.

title: Butternut squash pancakes with cheese and a fried egg
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the puree: well drained, it gives soft pancakes that hold their shape without collapsing.
ing: 400g of butternut squash, peeled and cut into

ing.note: plus a little bit for the service

ing: egg per person for the fried egg
titane: Preheat the pan empty, for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, before adding any oil. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly: the pancakes brown all over, and the egg cooked afterward gets crisp edges in the same pan, without anything sticking.
steps: Peel the butternut squash and cut it into cubes.
Steam the squash cubes for 20 minutes, until a knife tip passes through them without resistance.
Mash them with a fork, then let cool uncovered to release the moisture. Aim for approximately 360 g of puree.
Grate the cheese.
In a bowl, combine the warm puree, milk, eggs, flour, baking powder, cheese and chives. Season with salt and pepper.
Whisk until you obtain a smooth batter, without lumps. It should fall heavily from the spoon.
Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour a thin stream of grape seed oil or clarified butter.
Drop 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake, spacing them apart. Do not touch them further.

Wait until the bottom detaches on its own from the pan, approximately 2 minutes, flip and continue for 2 minutes on the other side while gradually lowering the heat. Transfer (set aside off the heat) onto a warm plate.
Repeat with the remaining batter, in the same pan, adding a little fat between each batch.
Turn up the heat, grease lightly, crack the eggs and let them set without moving them: the white must be set, the yolk still liquid.
Arrange the pancakes, place an egg on top, add chives and pepper.

title: Pan-fried cookie & cream waffles
intro: Without a waffle iron, everything depends on the heat of the pan: hot enough to crust the surface, stable enough for the center to finish setting.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the cold paste is applied. This thermal shock solidifies the underside into a golden crust: the disc then detaches easily, without the need for a spatula or any resistance. Preheat empty for 2 to 3 minutes, no less.
steps: Whisk the egg with the almond milk in a bowl. Add the flour, baking powder, stevia, and salt. Mix until the batter is smooth and lump-free.
Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly on the surface.

Spoon a ladleful of batter into the center and let it spread into a thick disc. Leave it undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes. When the edges start to lift and the disc slides easily, flip it over and cook for another 2 to 3 minutes, until golden brown. Repeat this process, disc by disc, to maintain control over the cooking time.
Meanwhile, smooth the cottage cheese with the whey using a whisk until you obtain a smooth cream with no traces of powder.
Coat (cover with an even layer) the still-warm discs with cream and serve immediately.

title: Crispy tofu glazed with gochujang
intro: It's all about patience: the tofu should only be turned over once the crust has formed, never before.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold pieces are added. The crust forms dry and even with very little fat. The same pan then reduces the glaze: the juices from the searing pass directly into the sauce, without transfer or the need for a second container.
steps: Press the tofu for 20 minutes between two cloths, under a weighted plate. Cut it into 2.5 cm cubes: the more sides, the more crust.
Mix the cornstarch and spices in a bowl.
Roll each cube in the mixture. Each side should be matte, without any wet areas.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, before adding any fat.

Pour the oil over the cubes, then arrange them in a single layer, leaving space between them. Let them sear without touching them. After 3 to 4 minutes, they will release easily: that's the signal. Turn them over and brown the other sides, for a total of 8 minutes.
Remove the tofu from the pan and place it in a bowl. Keep the pan on the heat, then reduce the heat to medium.
Pour in the soy sauce, gochujang, vinegar and agave syrup. Scrape the bottom to collect the juices.
Let it reduce for 2 minutes while stirring, until the sauce coats the spoon (leaves a clear trace when you run your finger along the back of the spoon).
Return the tofu to the pan, coat with a flick of the wrist, and cook for 1 minute. Serve immediately: the crust softens quickly.

title: Feta and pan-roasted figs
intro: Everything hinges on the first three minutes: a feta seared before the oven develops a golden crust that a simple dish-bake will never produce.
ing: dried thyme or 3 sprigs of fresh thyme
titane: The pan heats up empty for two to three minutes, allowing the titanium to reach a consistent temperature. This is what allows you to sear the block of feta and the figs over medium-high heat, then slide the pan directly into the middle of the oven. A single container goes from stovetop to oven, with no heat loss during the transfer.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F), conventional setting. Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Cut each fig into six wedges. Roughly chop the pistachios with a knife.
Pour the olive oil into the hot pan. Place the block of feta in the center, the figs around it, cut side down.

Sear (cook over high heat to brown the surface without cooking the center) for 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without stirring. The feta is ready when it pulls away from the bottom of the pan on its own and the base begins to brown.
Add salt, pour the honey over the feta, sprinkle with pistachios and thyme.
Place the pan in the middle of the oven for 15 minutes. The feta should be melted in the center and the figs softened, glistening with their juices.
Season with pepper when it comes out of the oven. Serve in the pan, with toasted country bread and a green salad with olive oil.

title: Chocolate-coconut cream with a hint of peanut
intro: Two ingredients, no real cooking: everything depends on the temperature of the milk, which must melt the chocolate without ever overheating it.
titane: The titanium pan heats the coconut milk quickly and evenly, without creating a hot spot at the bottom. This prevents the chocolate from grainy (separating into small, granular lumps) when you stir it in. Heating and mixing are done in the same container: you don't need to take anything else out.
steps: Plan ahead: the cream needs at least 4 hours in the refrigerator; overnight gives a better result.
Pour the coconut milk into a cold pan. Heat over low heat while stirring, approximately 3 minutes. Stop as soon as the surface quivers: the milk must not boil.
Remove the pan from heat. Break the chocolate into pieces and place them directly into the hot milk.
Wait one minute, then stir off the heat until you obtain a perfectly smooth cream, with no traces of unmelted chocolate.
Transfer into four ramekins.
Place a dollop of peanut butter on the surface of each and stretch it into a spiral with the tip of a knife or a stick.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours. An overnight stay gives a much firmer consistency.

title: Hazelnut-cocoa balls
intro: It all comes down to roasting: a raw hazelnut gives a flat paste, a golden hazelnut gives aroma.
titane: Heat the pan empty for two minutes over medium heat before adding the hazelnuts. The heat is then already distributed across the entire surface: the nuts brown evenly instead of burning in the center. No oil is needed; titanium dioxide is enough.
steps: Heat the empty pan for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Pour the hazelnuts into a single layer. Dry roast them for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring frequently. They should brown lightly and become fragrant. Stop as soon as the aroma intensifies.
Remove them immediately (transfer them from the pan) to a cold plate. Let them cool for 5 minutes; otherwise, the pan will continue to cook them.
Blend them into a fine powder using short pulses. If you continue, the powder will turn into a puree.
Add the maple syrup and cocoa. Mix until you get a sticky dough that holds its shape between your fingers.
Shape into 8 balls by hand, pressing firmly. Refrigerate for 20 minutes to firm up.

title: Oatmeal porridge with melted banana
intro: It all comes down to the cold start: the flakes swell in the water as the temperature rises, and the banana melts instead of browning.

ing.note: piece (half sliced into rounds for cooking)
cc, to be adjusted according to your taste

titane: The frying pan offers a much larger, flat surface than a saucepan: the porridge spreads in a thin layer, evaporation is even, and thickening occurs more quickly, without any sticking in the center. With just 200 ml of liquid, the process is straightforward—no adjustments needed. Cooking and plating are done in the same pan.
steps: Pan still cold, off the heat: add the oats, banana slices from half a banana, cinnamon, vanilla, sugar and salt. Pour in the water and stir so that no flakes remain dry.

Turn on medium heat. Count 7 minutes, stirring often with a silicone spatula: the titanium pan heats up quickly and the heat covers the entire surface, you need to keep an eye on it. The preparation is ready when it coats the spatula (leaves a layer that doesn't run) and pulls away clearly from the bottom.
Remove from heat. Stir in the milk then the fresh cheese, and work vigorously for 30 seconds. The fresh cheese must not cook: it is what gives the creamy texture.
Pour directly into a bowl. Distribute the second half of banana in slices, the blueberries, the crushed pistachios and a hint of spread.

title: Tomato sauce thickened with white beans
intro: A tomato sauce that gains body and structure without cream or flour thickening: everything depends on the fineness of the bean puree, which must disappear completely.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before pouring in the mixture. The heat rises quickly and spreads evenly from one side to the other: the sauce thickens without sticking, without needing an extra pan.
steps: Drain the white beans and rinse them in cold water. Blend them on their own until perfectly smooth. No lumps should remain: this is what makes the addition invisible in the mouth.
Place the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Test: a few drops of water should bead and roll on the surface.

Reduce heat to medium-low. Pour in the tomato sauce and bean purée. Stir with a spatula, bringing the mixture from the edge towards the center, for 3 to 4 minutes, until the sauce is smooth and simmering gently.
Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper. Remove from heat or use directly over pasta.

title: Peanut udon noodles, zucchini spaghetti, and crispy smoked tofu
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the sauce: thick enough to coat the udon, flexible enough not to stick to the courgette.
titane: One pan, two zones. Heated high and dry, it sears the garlic and ginger in seconds without sticking. The udon noodles then finish cooking over low heat on one side, while the tofu sticks brown on the other, placed there and left undisturbed: they release themselves once the crust is formed.
steps: Use a spiralizer to create long spaghetti-like strands. If you don't have a spiralizer, cut it into julienne strips (thin, even strips).
Mince the garlic and ginger.
If you are working with dried udon noodles, cook them in a pot of water according to the package instructions, then drain. Set aside.
Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in a drizzle of sesame oil, add the garlic and ginger, and stir until fragrant.
Reduce heat to medium-high. Add the soy sauce, peanut butter, and hot water. Stir until smooth.
Add the udon noodles and zucchini. Cook over medium-low heat for 6 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce should coat the noodles; add a little hot water if it becomes too thick.

Push everything to one side of the pan. Heat the remaining area over medium-high heat with a drizzle of sesame oil, place the tofu sticks in the pan, and leave them undisturbed. Cook for approximately 7 minutes, turning them only when they release easily.
Roughly chop the peanuts with a knife.
Divide the noodles and zucchini between two bowls. Place the sticks on top, sprinkle with peanuts and chopped parsley, and squeeze in half a lime just before serving.

title: Tahini yogurt, caramelized tomatoes and a soft-boiled egg
intro: It all comes down to the tomato juice: it must be reduced to a syrupy consistency, because it's what seasons the yogurt on the plate.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The even heat distribution of the titanium caramelizes the tomatoes directly on the stovetop, without going through the oven, and concentrates their juices in about ten minutes. Arrange them in a single layer: an overcrowded pan will steam, not caramelize.
steps: Heat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the olive oil. Add the cherry tomatoes cut in half, the brown sugar, and a pinch of salt. Spread them out in a layer, cut side down.
Let cook without stirring. The tomatoes will release themselves once caramelization is done. Then stir occasionally, for 10 minutes total, until you have a syrupy sauce.
Transfer the tomatoes out of the pan into a bowl with all the cooking juices.
Meanwhile, bring a pot of water to a simmer.
Plunge the eggs into simmering water. Cook for 6 minutes 30 seconds for a runny yolk.
Transfer them immediately into a bowl of ice water, then peel them (remove the shell).
Mix the yogurt with the tahini, a pinch of salt, a squeeze of lemon juice, and the zest of half a lemon.
Spread the tahini yogurt over the bottom of two bowls. Add the tomatoes, the egg halved, and drizzle with the cooking juices.
Season with pepper, sprinkle with sesame seeds and fresh mint. Serve immediately.

title: Pan-fried glazed tofu popcorn
intro: It all comes down to the crust: tofu torn by hand, seared without being touched, then glazed in the same pan.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two to three minutes when empty, which is enough to crisp the tofu without using an oven or air fryer. Once the pieces are set aside, the glaze reduces in the same pan, incorporating the juices from the searing. A single utensil, from start to finish.
steps: Drain the block of tofu and press it briefly between two sheets of paper towel. Tear it by hand into walnut-sized pieces. The irregular edges will hold the sauce much better than if cut with a knife.
In a bowl, combine the cornstarch, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper. Add the tofu and gently stir until each piece is coated with the powder.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should dance on it before evaporating.
Pour the oil over the tofu, then arrange the pieces in a single layer. Leave space between them; if they touch, they will steam. Cook in two batches if necessary.
Don't touch anything. Allow about ten minutes in total: the tofu will release itself once the crust is formed. Then turn the pieces over, one side at a time, to brown them on all sides.
Remove (transfer from the pan) the tofu to a plate.

Reduce the heat to medium. In the still-hot pan, pour in the water, soy sauce, maple syrup, ketchup, brown sugar, then add the margarine. Scrape the bottom of the pan with a spatula to dissolve any browned bits.
Let it reduce for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. The sauce is ready when it coats the back of a spoon and is glossy.
Return the tofu to the pan and stir for 1 minute, no more: just enough time for the coating to set, before the crust gets soggy.
Divide into two portions. For meal prep, let it cool uncovered before closing the containers, otherwise the steam will make everything soggy.

title: Potatoes with garlic cream, quick vegan bolognese
intro: Everything hinges on the first cooking: wedges placed in a single layer, covered, and left alone until they detach on their own.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat under the lid: it replaces the oven for crisping potatoes while keeping the center tender. It then sears textured protein and reduces the sauce. One pan, three cooking methods, no oven required.
steps: Cover the textured protein with boiling water, let it soak for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze between your hands to remove excess water.
Cut the potatoes into even wedges, without peeling them. Evenness ensures even cooking.
Coat them with smoked paprika, herbs, salt, pepper and oil.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in a fat with a high smoke point (grapeseed or clarified butter). It should simmer, never smoke.

Arrange the wedges in a single layer, cover, and reduce the heat to medium. Cook for about 20 minutes, turning only when they easily pull away from the bottom of the pan. The crust should be golden brown on the outside and tender inside.
Meanwhile, whisk the plant-based cream with the nutritional yeast, garlic, salt, pepper and plant-based cheese if you are using it.
Remove the potatoes from the pan, reduce the heat to low, and return them briefly with the garlic cream until coated. Set aside.
Wipe the pan with absorbent paper, preheat it empty, add a drizzle of oil. Sear the textured protein over high heat without stirring: it will brown and release from the pan on its own.
Deglaze (dissolve the juices from the bottom with a liquid) with soy sauce, pour in the tomato sauce, simmer for 10 minutes over medium heat until the sauce coats the spoon.
Divide the potatoes and Bolognese sauce between the containers, allowing them to cool uncovered before closing.

title: Turkey, courgette and mushroom risotto
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the turkey browns first, then the rice benefits from the juices left at the bottom.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat. This thorough preheating does two things: it allows the turkey to caramelize and then release itself from the pan, and it keeps the surface smooth enough so the rice doesn't stick during the 20 minutes of cooking. Never change pans.
steps: Mince the onion. Cut the courgette into small dice, the mushrooms into quarters. Keep the broth hot beside you.
Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil or clarified butter.

Place the turkey, salt it, and do not touch it anymore. It will release from the pan on its own once the crust is formed: this is the signal to turn it. Finish cooking over medium-high heat, then remove it (take it out of the pan and set it aside covered).
Lower the heat to medium. Sauté the onion, then the courgette and mushrooms, until they release their water and become tender. The turkey juices will deglaze in the process.

Pour in the rice and stir for 1 minute, while it toasts (the grains become translucent at the edges). Moisten with a ladle of hot broth and let it be absorbed before adding the next, then top up with hot water if needed. Allow about 18 minutes, stirring regularly, until the rice is creamy and still slightly firm to the bite.
Cut the turkey into pieces. Fold it into the rice with the parmesan, mustard and cream cheese. Mix well to bind. Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper.
Sprinkle the mozzarella, cover and let rest off the heat for 5 minutes, until the cheese melts. Serve in the pan.

title: Pan-fried buffalo chicken turnovers
intro: It all comes down to two cooking steps in the same pan: a chicken seared and then finished covered, and a yogurt pastry spread thin enough to brown before the filling gets too hot.
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes, then add a high-smoke-point fat. The rapid heat-up of the titanium pan eliminates the need for hours in a slow cooker: the chicken is seared and then cooked, covered, in 25 minutes. For the turnovers, don't move them for the first few minutes. The lack of a coating results in a crisp, dry crust, and the pastry will release easily when it's ready. That's the only indicator you need to follow.
steps: Season the chicken breasts with garlic salt, smoked paprika, ranch spices and pepper.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Add a drizzle of high smoke point oil and sear the chicken without touching it. Turn it over when it releases easily.
Add the onion and salsa, cover and cook over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes depending on the thickness, until fully cooked through.
Meanwhile, blend the cottage cheese, cream cheese, buffalo sauce, milk, garlic salt, pepper and onion powder until smooth.

Remove the pan from the heat and shred the chicken (separating the meat into strands using two forks) directly into the warm pan. Stir in the protein-enriched buffalo sauce, the remaining 120g of buffalo sauce, half the mozzarella cheese, and the chives. Transfer to a separate container and let cool slightly.
Mix the flour, yogurt, garlic salt and Italian herbs by hand until you get a crumbly mixture.
Knead for 5 minutes, until the dough becomes smooth and supple. Divide it into 10 equal portions and shape them into balls.
Roll out each ball very thinly into an oval. A thick dough would remain raw in the center.
Fill one half of each oval with shredded chicken and the remaining mozzarella, leaving a 2 cm border. Fold over and pinch firmly to seal.

Clean the pan, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then add a drizzle of oil or butter. Cook the turnovers over medium heat, seam-side up, without moving them. Turn them over when they release easily and brown the other side. Allow approximately 10 minutes total per batch.

title: Beetroot, date and almond balls
intro: The beetroot provides moisture and color, the date provides sugar: the key is to cook it covered, which dries the surface without drying out the center.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty and then lightly greased, it diffuses a gentle heat that the lid reflects back onto the tops of the balls: the surface develops a thin, praline-flavored crust while the inside remains soft. The indicator is simple: the balls release easily when they are ready to be turned over.
steps: Cover the dates with hot water and let them soak for 10 minutes. Drain them, then gently squeeze them between your fingers.
Cut the beetroot into large pieces and put it in the blender bowl. Add the dates.
Pulse until you obtain a coarse puree, with no residual liquid at the bottom of the bowl.
Add the almond flour and mix again until you have a smooth dough that holds its shape when pressed with your finger. If it's too sticky, let it rest in the refrigerator for 5 minutes.
Shape into balls the size of a walnut. Roll them in the flaked almonds or sprinkle them on top, pressing them in to make them stick.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush it with a film of clarified butter or grapeseed oil, then reduce the heat to low.
Place the balls well spaced apart, without overcrowding the pan. Cover and cook for 7 to 8 minutes.
Gently turn them over when they detach on their own, using a flexible spatula. Cover again and continue for 7 minutes.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack to cool slightly. The texture will set as it cools.

title: Polenta au gratin with beef Bolognese sauce
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the meat first browns without being touched, then the polenta takes its place on the same wiped-off juices, and the gratin is done under a lid.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter

ing.note: Dried oregano, smoked paprika, sweet chili

titane: Leave the beef still for the first few minutes on a preheated pan: it will release easily once a crust has formed, and it's this caramelization that gives the sauce its depth of flavor. Then, wipe the pan with paper towels before adding the polenta—the starch will stick to any remaining juices. Finally, use the same pan as a gratin dish, with the lid on and the heat on low.
steps: Dice the onion and carrot into small, even pieces. Mince the garlic. Pick the basil leaves.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the fat: it should simmer and remain clear, without smoking.

Place the beef in a single layer, then add the vegetables and garlic on top. Leave it undisturbed for 3 minutes. When the meat starts to pull away from the bottom of the pan, stir and cook for another 3 minutes.

Add the chopped tomatoes, 200ml of water and the stock. Season and add the spices. Reduce the heat to low and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon without releasing any liquid.
Add the chopped basil off the heat, then transfer the Bolognese sauce to a shallow dish.

Wipe the pan with paper towels. Gradually whisk in the polenta, 250 ml of water, a pinch of salt, and any leftover stock. Stir over low heat, then add the remaining water in two or three additions, waiting for it to be absorbed each time. Cook for 10 minutes: the polenta should be creamy and fall slowly from the spoon.
Smooth the polenta in the pan, top with Bolognese sauce, and sprinkle with mozzarella.
Cover and cook over very low heat for 5 minutes, until the cheese melts and stretches. Serve in the pan.

title: Raw brownie with chickpeas and dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to two things: a base that is blended long enough to lose all traces of grain, and chocolate that is melted off the heat, never heated directly.

ing.note: rehydrated for 10 minutes in hot water

titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan for ganache (chocolate melted in a hot liquid). Its rapid and even heat distribution allows you to bring the coconut milk to a simmer without any hot spots, then remove the pan from the heat: the residual heat in the metal is enough to melt the chocolate. No lumps, no burnt chocolate at the bottom.
steps: Plan ahead: the brownie sets in the refrigerator overnight, start the day before.
Drain the chickpeas and rinse them. Rehydrate the pitted dates for 10 minutes in hot water, then drain them.
Blend the dates with the chickpeas and cocoa for 5 minutes, scraping down the sides halfway through. The mixture should be dense, smooth, with no texture perceptible on the tongue.
Transfer the preparation to a rectangular dish. Spread to about 2 cm thickness, press down with a spatula, smooth the surface.
Pour the coconut milk into the titanium pan. Heat over low heat until the first sign of simmering, never letting it boil.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the dark chocolate pieces. Wait 1 minute, then stir from the center outward until you obtain a glossy and perfectly smooth mixture.
Pour the still-warm ganache over the chickpea base. Tilt the dish to spread it in an even layer.

Refrigerate overnight completely. The mixture has set properly when the ganache resists under slight pressure from your finger. Cut into squares with a blade rinsed in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: 'Three no-oven snacks: almond, peanut, chocolate'
intro: Three preparations that fit on a single tray and a little bit of cold: what matters here is the texture, therefore respecting the setting times.
titane: For almond cookies, a covered titanium pan can replace the oven for a small batch. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, add a drizzle of high-smoke oil, place the cookies in the pan, and cover. Don't touch them: they will release on their own when the bottom is set. That's the only sign you need to wait for.
steps: Work the almond flour with the maple syrup until you obtain a soft and homogeneous paste that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Take even portions, roll them into balls, then flatten them slightly with the back of a fork.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add a drizzle of high smoke point oil.

Place the biscuits in the pan, cover, and cook over low to medium heat for about ten minutes. When they release easily and the bottoms are golden brown, turn them over and cook the other side. Transfer them to a wire rack to cool.
For the bars, combine the rolled oats, peanut butter, maple syrup, and salt. Press this mixture into the bottom of a baking pan lined with parchment paper.
Melt the coconut oil, then stir it into the melted peanut butter and maple syrup. The caramel should remain runny.
Pour it onto the base, smooth it out, and place in the freezer for one hour, until it is firm to the touch.

Melt the dark chocolate, mix it with the peanut butter and salt. Spread over the cold surface, let it set for two minutes, then cut into bars with a blade that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry.
Keep the bars in the freezer: they will keep for several months and are best eaten when barely at room temperature.
For the cups, mix together the almond flour, peanut butter and maple syrup, then add the chocolate chips without crushing them.
Press the dough into molds or a small mold, packing the edges down well.
Melt the chocolate, loosen it with coconut milk until you get a smooth ganache, and cover.
Refrigerate for one hour, until the topping has set.

title: Oat and applesauce pie crust
intro: Two ingredients, no fat: everything hinges on the slow drying of the dough, which must lose its moisture without browning.
titane: The covered pan works like an oven: the heat circulates under the lid and envelops the dough, but you maintain control over the browning of the bottom at all times. The end signal isn't the timer, it's the edges pulling away from the sides on their own. As long as they're sticking, the dough still contains too much water.
steps: Combine the oats and applesauce in a bowl. Mix with a spatula until well combined, with no dry flakes remaining. Let it rest for 5 minutes: the oats will absorb the liquid and the dough will firm up.

Pour the mixture into the still-cold titanium pan. Press it down with the back of a spoon over the entire surface, then push it up a 2 cm border against the side. Even out the thickness of the base; the more even it is, the better the cooking will be.
Place over low heat and cover. Let it dry (evaporate the moisture over low heat) for 18 minutes. The surface will no longer be sticky and the edges will begin to shrink.
Remove the lid. Continue cooking for 4 minutes over low heat to firm up the base. Gently lift one edge with a spatula: it should come away easily.
Turn off the heat and let it cool completely in the pan before unmolding. It is during this time that the dough sets properly.

title: Chocolate and cashew fudge
intro: It all comes down to how the chocolate melts: if it's too hot, it cuts through the cashew cream, and if it's cold, the fudge releases oil.

ing.note: soaked for 30 minutes in hot water then rinsed

titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its conductivity distributes heat evenly without hot spots: the chocolate melts in three minutes over very low heat, with constant monitoring, and you can keep your hand on the whisk from start to finish. No need to preheat the pan; the chocolate goes into it cold or barely warm.
steps: Plan ahead: the fudge sets in the refrigerator overnight, start the day before.
Cover the cashews with hot water and let soak for 30 minutes. Drain, rinse with clear water, set aside.
Chop the chocolate with a knife into regular flakes. The finer they are, the faster and more even the melting will be.

Pour the chocolate into the titanium pan on very low heat. Stir continuously with a spatula or small whisk. Allow 3 minutes: the chocolate must be perfectly smooth and fluid, never smoking. Remove from heat at this stage.
Place the drained cashews, plant-based milk and agave syrup in the food processor bowl. Pour the melted chocolate over it.
Blend at full power until you obtain a perfectly smooth cream, with no graininess on the tongue. Scrape the sides once or twice along the way.
Transfer to a mold lined with baking paper, or into individual moulds. Smooth the surface.
Let set in the refrigerator for a full night. The fudge unmoulds cleanly and remains firm, almost crispy, when removed from the cold.

title: Tomato tarte tatin with sheep's milk cheese
intro: It all comes down to the balsamic caramel: cooked enough to coat, yet soft enough for the tomatoes to sit on without slipping.
titane: The caramel rises over medium heat in the pan, the tomatoes are arranged on top, the batter is poured over everything, and the pan goes straight into the oven without being moved. When unmolding, the caramelized base came away easily: a quarter turn of the wrist was all it took.
steps: Plan ahead: the dough rests in the refrigerator for at least 15 minutes, and can wait up to 24 hours, organize accordingly.
Combine flour, butter, egg, water and salt in a mixing bowl. Knead until you obtain a homogeneous ball, without overworking.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 15 minutes. The dough can wait 24 hours at this stage.
Slice the tomatoes into regular slices of half a centimetre. Place them for a few minutes on paper towel to remove excess water.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Set the oven to 190 °C, traditional heat.
Pour the olive oil into the hot pan, add the balsamic reduction, honey and salt. Mix for 2 minutes: the caramel must become fluid and homogeneous. Remove from heat.
Arrange the tomato slices on the caramel in a tight rosette pattern. Cut additional pieces to fill the gaps: the surface must be full.
Grate the sheep's milk cheese and distribute it over the tomatoes.
Roll out the dough (flatten it with a rolling pin) into a disc extending 4 to 5 cm beyond the pan's diameter.
Place the dough over the filling, fold the edges toward the inside of the pan to seal, then prick the surface with a fork.
Bake the pan as is, without a cover, at mid-height. Allow 37 minutes, until the dough is clearly golden.
Remove the pan, let cool for 3 minutes. Place a serving dish on the pan and flip with a quick motion: the tart releases on its own.
Sprinkle with fresh thyme leaves and serve warm.

title: Beetroot pancakes, savory or sweet version
intro: These gluten-free pancakes hold together solely through the strength of rice and chickpea flours: everything depends on the batter resting and a really hot pan.

ing.note: g, juice from the preserved sachet

titane: Titanium heats up faster than a conventional pan: the batter cooks instantly, a crust forms, and the pancake releases itself. As a result, very little oil is needed, there's no sticking, and the whole batch can be cooked in the same pan. The oven is only used to keep them warm.
steps: Combine both flours, yeast, baking soda and salt in a bowl. Mix with a whisk to distribute the powders.
Drain the beetroot over a bowl and keep the juice from the packet. Add the diced beetroot and this juice to the powders: the colour will come from both the liquid and the flesh.
Pour the plant-based drink, oil and egg. Blend with a blender or immersion blender until you obtain a smooth paste that is uniformly pink.
Place the bowl in the refrigerator for about ten minutes while you prepare the toppings. This resting time hydrates the flours and gives a less sandy pancake.
Peel the avocado and slice it. Squeeze the half lemon.
Heat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes on medium heat. It must be hot before the first drizzle of oil.
Pour the grape seed oil, wipe away the excess with paper towel, then place a small ladle of batter per pancake. Lower the heat to medium-low to medium.
Do not touch them. Wait until the bubbles on the surface have burst and the disc detaches by itself from the pan, then flip and cook for 1 to 2 minutes on the other side.
Preheat the oven to a low temperature. Transfer off the pan onto a baking sheet and keep in the warm oven while you cook the rest in the same pan.
For the savoury version, arrange the salmon, avocado, sheep's milk cheese with herbs and sprouted seeds on the pancakes, then drizzle with olive oil and lemon.
For the sweet version, top the pancakes with apple and raisin compote, coconut yogurt, almond butter and granola.

title: Poached eggs, roasted sweet potato and lemon-flavored fromage blanc
intro: It all comes down to two textures: cubes of sweet potato that are truly caramelized, and an egg white that has just been set on a still-liquid yolk.

ing.note: skyr or ricotta are also suitable)

titane: The empty pan replaces the oven. The sweet potato cubes touch a surface that's already scorching hot, the sugars concentrate in a few minutes, then the lid finishes cooking them through. Wipe the pan, pour in 400 ml of water: the same utensil becomes a poaching basin. One wash is all it takes for the whole dish.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then pour in the olive oil.
Meanwhile, peel the sweet potato and cut it into one-centimeter cubes, as regular as possible: this ensures simultaneous cooking.
In a bowl, roll the cubes in the spices and salt until they are evenly coated.

Pour them into the hot pan in a single layer. Let them brown without touching them: the cubes will release on their own when the top is golden. Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and continue cooking for 20 minutes, stirring every 4 or 5 minutes.
Remove the cubes from the pan and place them on a plate, then cover them to keep them warm.
Whisk the fromage blanc with the lemon zest and juice, chives, salt and pepper. Keep chilled while poaching.

Wipe the pan with paper towels. Pour in 400 ml of water and the vinegar, and heat over medium heat until simmering. Reduce the heat immediately: the titanium cast iron retains heat and the water would boil.
Crack each egg into an individual ramekin. Create a whirlpool in the water with a spoon, slide an egg into the center, and cook for 2 minutes. The white should be set, the yolk still soft.
Drain the egg on absorbent paper and repeat with the other three, one by one.

Spread the lemon-flavored fromage blanc on the bottom of the plates, add the sweet potato cubes, and place two eggs on each plate. Finish with fresh thyme, a drizzle of chili oil, and a grind of pepper.

title: Chocolate and banana fudge
intro: Just two ingredients: everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas and on melting the chocolate gently enough so that it remains smooth.

ing.note: approximately 200g of flesh, skin speckled with

titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, without a double boiler. The coating distributes the heat evenly, preventing hot spots: nothing sticks or sears. The banana puree is added to the same pan, and you only need to transfer the mixture to another container once, to pour it into the mold.
steps: Plan ahead: the fudge takes a full night in the refrigerator, start the day before.
Peel the bananas and blend them until you obtain a perfectly smooth purée, without fibers or lumps. Set aside.

Place the titanium pan on very low heat and pour the chocolate into it. Stir continuously with a spatula, bringing the edges toward the center. It should take a few minutes: the chocolate must be melted, glossy and fluid, never smoking.
Remove the pan from the heat. Pour the banana purée over the chocolate and mix thoroughly until the mixture is homogeneous and silky. It thickens immediately: this is normal.
Pour into a square mold of approximately 15 cm lined with parchment paper. Smooth the surface with a spatula and tap the mold once on the work surface to release air bubbles.
Place in the refrigerator for one full night, at least 8 hours. The cold setting is what gives the fudge texture: if shortened, it leaves the mixture soft.
Unmold by pulling on the paper, then cut into 2 cm cubes with a fine-bladed knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Coconut-chocolate ganache, peanut marbling
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the coconut milk: warm, never boiling, otherwise the emulsion separates and the ganache becomes grainy.
titane: The titanium pan heats coconut milk quickly and without hot spots, then becomes the working container: melt the chocolate off the heat, pipe the design, and let it set in the refrigerator. Its thinness dissipates heat rapidly, accelerating the setting process.
steps: Plan ahead: the ganache needs at least 4 hours in the refrigerator, preferably overnight.
Pour the coconut milk into the pan. Heat over low heat, stirring, for approximately 3 minutes. Stop as soon as small bubbles appear around the edge: the milk must not boil.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the chopped chocolate all at once and let it melt for 30 seconds without stirring.

Mix in the center with small circles, then gradually expand to the edge. The mixture should form a smooth and glossy ganache, about 3 minutes. If it seems grainy, add one tablespoon of hot coconut milk and stir again from the center.
Smooth the surface. Drizzle the peanut butter in fine lines on top, then draw crossed lines with the tip of a knife or a stick to marble (blend two substances together without fully mixing).
Place the pan in the refrigerator for 4 hours minimum, preferably overnight. The ganache is ready when it resists under your finger.

title: Three chocolate snacks in the blender, one pan
intro: Three oven-free recipes, the success of which depends on one single point: melting the chocolate gently in an empty, preheated pan, without ever rushing it.

ing.note: rehydrated for 10 minutes in hot water

titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan over low heat for two minutes, then turn off or reduce the heat to low before adding the chocolate. The metal mass distributes heat evenly, without any hot spots: the chocolate melts by thermal inertia, like in a double boiler, but without a saucepan or bowl. Wipe the pan with paper towels between each batch and prepare all three chocolates in the same pan.
steps: Plan ahead: the cumulative resting time exceeds 3 hours, including one full night for the porridge, organize accordingly
Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Rehydrate the pitted dates for 10 minutes in hot water, then drain them.
Blend the chickpeas, drained dates and cocoa until you obtain a homogeneous paste, without grains. Scrape the sides of the bowl once during blending.
Spread this base over 1.5 cm in a small dish or square mould lined with baking paper. Press down with a spatula, making the surface perfectly flat.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, on low heat, for 2 minutes: it should be hot without smoking.
Away from high heat, on minimum setting, melt the 150 g of dark chocolate with the coconut milk, stirring with a flexible spatula. Allow 3 minutes, until you obtain a smooth and shiny mixture.
Pour the warm ganache onto the base, tilt the mould to even it out. Chill until set, approximately 2 hours.
Wipe the pan, preheat it empty again for 2 minutes on low heat. Melt the 200 g of 70% chocolate in it for 2 minutes, stirring. Incorporate the peanut butter if you are using it.
Away from the heat, pour the puffed quinoa into the pan and mix until completely coated, without crushing the grains.
Transfer to a lined mould, press firmly with the back of a spoon. Leave to set in the cold for 1 hour, then cut into bars.
In a bowl or jar, mix the plant-based yoghurt, chia seeds and agave syrup. Leave to swell for 10 minutes.
Spread the peanut butter on top in a thin layer, then the crushed peanuts.
Wipe the pan, preheat it empty for 2 minutes on low heat, melt the 50 g of chocolate with the coconut oil in it until you obtain a fluid mixture.
Coat the top of the porridge with this chocolate. Chill overnight: the chocolate forms a shell that cracks with a spoon.

title: Beef quesadillas, chipotle sauce
intro: It all comes down to the beef crust: a single pan, nice and hot, and ten portions ready to spend the week in the freezer.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding oil: the steak will sear beautifully instead of releasing its juices. The same principle applies to tortillas, which brown without any added fat. A single pan for meat, vegetables, and assembly, with no intermediate washing required.
steps: Season the steak on both sides with garlic salt and black pepper. Let it come to room temperature while the pan heats up.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently and coat the bottom without smoking.
Place the steak on the grill and leave it untouched. Let it cook for approximately 10 minutes, turning it over only once. The steak will release easily from the grill once a crust has formed.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a board. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Cut the steak into small, even cubes, working against the grain.
Return the pan to medium-high heat. Sauté the onions and peppers for 5 minutes in the remaining juices, until softened and browned in places.
Mix together the mayonnaise, chipotle paste, lime juice, garlic salt and pepper until you have a smooth sauce.
Top each tortilla on one half: a drizzle of chipotle sauce, the diced beef, the sautéed vegetables, the mozzarella. Fold over.
Brown the quesadillas over medium heat, 2 to 3 minutes per side. They will release easily when the surface is crispy and the cheese is melted.
Allow to cool on a wire rack, then wrap individually in aluminum foil or in airtight freezer bags.

title: Mashed potatoes, beef and mushrooms au gratin
intro: It all comes down to the color of the beef: a clean sear, without stirring, then a short jus that binds everything together.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold meat is added: this is what creates the crust. It then proceeds to reduce the juices and then brown the meat, covered, without changing the pan or transferring it to the oven.
steps: Heat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and cut them into thick slices approximately 1 cm.
Pour the slices into the pan with a little water and a pinch of salt. Cover and cook for 15 minutes, adding a little water if the bottom dries out. A knife tip should pass through without resistance.
Drain, transfer to a bowl. Mash with a fork, incorporate the cream, adjust the seasoning. Cover to keep warm.
Wipe the pan, return it to medium-high heat with the fat. Peel and thinly slice the onion, cut the mushrooms into quarters.

Place the beef in a single layer, add the onion and mushrooms. Do not touch anything: the meat sticks first, then releases on its own when the crust is formed. Allow 5 to 6 minutes. Then stir, season with spices.
Deglaze with the stock and reduce for 4 minutes uncovered, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

Set aside the garnish. Spread the warm mashed potatoes on the bottom of the pan, distribute the beef and its sauce over the top, cover with mozzarella. Cover, low heat, 4 to 5 minutes: the cheese should melt and stretch.

title: Bao burger with minced chicken and cheddar
intro: It's all about the contrast: a very tender steamed crumb against a crisply seared chicken crust, so the bread and the steak should never cook at the same time.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: One pan, two separate steps. First, the cut sides of the bao are placed dry on the hot titanium griddle: the crumb browns and releases itself when it's ready. Then, the chicken steak is placed in a thin stream of oil at a high smoke point (the temperature at which fat begins to burn). It's left untouched. As long as it adheres, the crust forms; as soon as it's formed, it releases itself. That's the signal to flip.
steps: Combine flour, yeast, salt, water and oil. Knead until you obtain a supple, smooth dough that no longer sticks to your fingers.
Cover and let rise at room temperature, 1 hour 30 minutes maximum.
Degas (release the fermentation gas by pressing the dough), shape into a ball, then let it rise again until it reaches one and a half times its original volume.
Cook the bao for 18 minutes in a steamer, in a dedicated steamer. This step cannot be transposed to a pan: the crumb requires humid, enclosed heat.
Turn off the heat and wait 5 minutes with the lid closed. A bao exposed too early to cold air will collapse.
Finely mince the thigh and half fillet with a knife. Salt, pepper, spice, then press the meat into a compact steak the diameter of the bread.
Cut the cucumber into very thin slices. Toss with vinegar, salt and stevia. Let marinate while the meat cooks: your express pickles.
Heat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Split the bao in two. Place the cut faces on the dry pan, 2 minutes, until they are golden and release on their own. Set aside.
Pour the fat, turn up the heat. Place the steak and leave it alone for about 5 minutes, until it releases. Turn over, reduce to medium heat and finish cooking through, 3 minutes.
Place the cheddar on the meat, cover, turn off the heat. The residual heat will melt it in one minute.
Drain the cucumber pickles before using.
Spread the base of the bao with miso mayonnaise, arrange the drained pickles, the melting steak, a second touch of sauce, then close.

title: Beef and vegetable tacos with a spicy white sauce
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: the meat crust, the vegetables cooked in the juices, then the grilled folding.
titane: On titanium, the ground meat sticks at first. This is intentional. Don't touch it while it's sticking: as soon as it releases itself from the metal, a crust has formed and you can crumble it. The juices (caramelized deposits remaining at the bottom) will then serve as a base for the vegetables, and the folded taco will brown in the same spot, without needing to change utensils.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Lay the beef in a single layer. Leave it untouched for about 6 minutes, until it releases from the pan on its own. Crumble it, then transfer it to a plate.
Meanwhile, peel the white onion, then cut the zucchini, bell pepper and white onion into small regular cubes.
Add the vegetables to the still-hot pan, directly onto the meat juices. Sauté them for 5 minutes over medium heat, until they are tender and browned at the edges. Return the meat and stir.
Peel the red onion and cut it into small dice. Set aside half of it for plating.
In a bowl, combine the remaining red onion, Greek yogurt, ketchup, mustard and stevia. Whisk until you have a smooth, well-emulsified sauce.
Push the filling to one side of the pan. Lay the tortilla flat, place the meat and vegetable mixture in the center, cover with cheddar.
Fold the tortilla over on itself and grill it for 2 minutes per side over medium heat: the surface should be golden and the cheese should be melted.
Slightly open the taco. Slide in the shredded salad, the raw red onion cubes and the sauce. Serve immediately.

title: Zucchini pancakes with Gruyère cheese
intro: Success depends entirely on patience: a vegetable pancake flips when it decides to, not before.

ing.note: or 120g of cottage cheese or yogurt

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. As a result, the first side develops a golden crust before the zucchini releases its water. Preheat the pan empty, lightly grease it, and then let it cook. When the pancake easily releases from the spatula, it's ready to be flipped.
steps: Grate the courgette without peeling it, on the medium grid.
Combine the zucchini, flour, eggs, fromage frais, milk, and yeast in a bowl. Mix until you obtain a smooth, thick batter.
Add the Gruyère cheese and chives, season with salt and pepper. Mix briefly.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Add a thin layer of fat: it should coat the bottom without forming a puddle.

Reduce the heat to medium. Drop about 2 tablespoons of batter per pancake, spacing them apart. Leave them undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes: the pancake is ready to be flipped when it easily releases from the pan.
Turn over and continue cooking for 2 to 3 minutes, until the second side is golden brown. Transfer to a plate.
Repeat with the remaining batter, wiping the pan with absorbent paper between batches and lightly re-greasing.
Serve with a soft-boiled, poached or fried egg, or a herb salad.

title: Coconut-chocolate ganache with peanut butter
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the coconut milk: hot enough to melt the chocolate, never boiling, otherwise the ganache (emulsion of chocolate and liquid) will curdle.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan. Its large surface area heats the 320 ml of coconut milk evenly in two minutes, without it sticking to the bottom. Keep an eye on it: what would take five minutes in a saucepan takes two here.
steps: Plan ahead: the ganache requires at least 4 hours in the refrigerator, preferably overnight, so start in advance.
Chop the chocolate into regular pieces the size of a die. Transfer it to a mixing bowl.
Pour the coconut milk into the titanium pan. Heat over medium heat for approximately 2 minutes, until the first signs of simmering appear on the surface. Do not let it boil.
Pour the hot milk directly from the pan onto the chocolate, all at once. Wait one minute without stirring: the chocolate should soften.
Mix in the center with small circular motions, then expand towards the edges. Allow 2 minutes until you achieve a smooth, glossy texture.
Distribute the ganache into four bowls. Place the peanut butter in small touches on the surface, then stretch them into spirals with the tip of a knife or a stick.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, preferably overnight: the ganache will become firmer and the cocoa flavor will develop.

title: Textured soy köfte
intro: It all comes down to the hydration of the soy: if it's too wet, the dough crumbles when cooked; if it's cooked properly, it holds together and forms a good crust.
