titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil. The rapid heating of the titanium immediately sets the surface of the köfte: they brown with just a drizzle of oil. Once in the pan, leave them alone. They will release on their own when a crust has formed—this is the only reliable sign to turn them over.
steps: Combine the textured soy, water, salt and soy sauce in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then maintain a gentle simmer over medium heat for about fifteen minutes, until the liquid is completely absorbed. The bottom should be dry.
Peel and chop the onion.

Pour the soy into the food processor bowl. Add the cumin, paprika, coriander, cinnamon, tomato paste and chopped onion. Pulse three to four times only: the texture should remain coarse, we want grain, not a puree.

Transfer the preparation to a mixing bowl. Incorporate the flour and parsley by hand. Work until the dough holds together and no longer sticks to your fingers. Add the fifth spoonful of flour if it remains sticky.
Shape into oval patties of approximately 5 cm, slightly flattened. Plan for about a dozen pieces.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the fat: it should smoke slightly.

Place the köfte without crowding, in two batches if necessary. Leave them to brown without moving for 3 to 4 minutes, until they release on their own. Turn them over and brown the other sides, 4 minutes more. Serve immediately.

title: Seared sweet potato, soy bolognese and lime yogurt cream
intro: It all comes down to the first side of the sweet potato: a really hot pan, no moving, and the crust forms on its own.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and maintains the temperature. It caramelizes the sweet potato cubes like an oven would, with a more pronounced crust, then proceeds with the sauce without going down the drain: the juices left by the sweet potato give the Bolognese sauce a rich base.
steps: Cover the soy protein with hot water and let it swell for 10 minutes. Drain, then press between your hands to remove excess water.
Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2 cm cubes, keeping them regular. Mix them with the smoked paprika and salt.
Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the oil at a high smoke point, it should ripple without smoking.

Place the cubes in a single layer, without crowding them. Do not touch anything for 4 to 5 minutes: when the colored side detaches on its own from the pan, turn it over. Lower to medium heat, cover and continue for 8 to 10 minutes, until a knife tip passes through without resistance.
Remove the sweet potato (take it out of the pan and keep it covered).

Peel the white onion and slice it thinly. In the same pan, without washing it, sauté it for 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the spices and stir for 30 seconds, just long enough for them to release their aroma.

Pour in the tomato sauce and soy protein. Let simmer uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring from time to time: the sauce should coat the spoon (leave a film that does not run immediately). Adjust the salt.
Meanwhile, whisk the plant-based yogurt with the olive oil, the juice of the half lime and the herbed salt. Keep chilled.
Arrange the sweet potato at the bottom of two bowls, coat with sauce, add the lime cream in a drizzle and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Green shakshuka with leeks and fresh goat cheese
intro: It all comes down to the leeks: they must melt completely before the eggs arrive, otherwise the pan-fried mixture remains stringy under an already cooked top.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding any fat. The onion and garlic will then sear nicely and release their juices without sticking. When it's time to add the eggs, the lid does the rest: the heat envelops the whites and cooks them without drying out the yolks.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Finely chop the onion. Press the garlic.
Trim the green parts of the leeks, slice the white parts into rounds, then wash them in a salad spinner and spin them dry. The sand will settle to the bottom, and the rounds will come out dry.
Pour the olive oil into the hot pan and turn up the heat to medium-high.
Add the onion and garlic. Leave them undisturbed for about 3 minutes: they will detach from the bottom on their own when they are just the right color.
Add the leeks, salt, lemon juice and stock. Cook for 15 minutes over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally, until the slices are soft and the liquid is almost absorbed.
Throw the spinach shoots on top and mix for 2 minutes, until they wilt.
Stir in the cream and mix to coat the vegetables. Reduce heat to low.
Make six wells in the greenery with the back of a spoon. Crack an egg into each one, cover and cook for 6 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny.
Season with pepper, scatter the crumbled fresh goat cheese and chopped chives over the top. Serve in the pan with toasted bread.

title: Rustic tart with cherry tomatoes and Abondance cheese
intro: It all comes down to the water in the tomatoes: remove it before cooking, and the pastry stays crispy right to the edge.
ing: fleur de sel for the dough

ing.note: Comté, Gruyère de France, Tomme de Brebis)

titane: The dough is rolled out directly in the cold pan, without parchment paper. Direct contact with the metal caramelizes the base during the 35 minutes in the oven. When the tart is cooked, it will release easily from the pan: this is your indicator of when it's done.
steps: Plan ahead: the dough must rest for at least 30 minutes in the cold, allow for this time before moving on to the filling.
Mix the flour, egg, butter, water and pinch of fleur de sel. Work until you obtain a homogeneous ball, no more.
Wrap the ball and reserve it in the cold for at least 30 minutes.
Cut the tomatoes in half, in quarters if they are large.
Press the garlic. Mix the tomatoes with the olive oil, pressed garlic, thyme leaves and fleur de sel. Let stand for 15 minutes to drain (the salt draws out the vegetable water).
Grate the cheese.
Preheat the oven to 195 °C, traditional heat with bottom and top elements. No convection heat: it dries out the filling before the base browns.
Roll out the dough into a circle of approximately 30 cm in diameter and place it in the cold titanium pan, letting the edges overhang freely on the sides.
Spread the mustard on the base, keeping 3 to 4 cm of free edge.
Distribute the grated cheese over the mustard.
Drain the tomatoes carefully, keep their juice to the side, then arrange them on the cheese.
Fold the edges of dough over the filling, in irregular pleats.

Bake the pan as is, without a lid, in the lower part of the oven. Allow 35 minutes: the base must be well browned and come away cleanly from the metal. Let cool for 5 minutes before sliding the tart onto a board.

title: Crushed cucumber and pan-fried potatoes, gochujang sauce
intro: It all comes down to the potatoes: no boiling water, no oven, a quick searing followed by covered cooking which makes them melt under a golden crust.
ing: large tablespoon of vegan spreadable cheese
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding any oil or butter. The potatoes go in raw, stick, then release on their own once a crust has formed: this is the signal to stir them, never before. The same skillet, simply wiped clean, is then used to sear the vegetables—it retains the heat necessary for the deep browning you expect from a barbecue.
steps: Crush the cucumber with the flat of a large knife, then cut it into irregular pieces. The broken edges will better absorb the seasoning.
Mix it with the vinegar, soy sauce, agave, garlic powder and chili flakes. Keep chilled while proceeding with the rest.
Cook the whole potatoes in boiling water for 6 to 7 minutes, then drain them.
Cut the potatoes into small regular pieces, the size of a walnut. This cutting ensures even cooking in the pan.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil. It should shimmer slightly.
Spread the potatoes in a single layer. Leave them for 8 minutes over high heat without touching them: they will release from the bottom on their own once the crust forms.
Season with salt, add the paprika and mix to coat.
Cover, reduce to medium heat and continue for 15 minutes, stirring from time to time. A knife tip should go through without resistance.
Meanwhile, whisk together the cream cheese, yogurt, vinegar, agave, gochujang and salt. Stir in the green onions and kimchi.
Pour the warm potatoes directly from the pan into the sauce. Mix: the heat softens the sauce and helps it coat the potatoes.

Wipe the pan with paper towels, return it to high heat and sear the steaks and skewers on each side, about 3 minutes, until the marks are distinct and the piece releases on its own. Transfer to a plate and serve with both salads.

title: Chocolate, pistachio and coconut tablet
intro: It all comes down to the melting temperature: chocolate that is melted too quickly becomes grainy and will never regain its shine.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots, allowing you to melt white chocolate and then dark chocolate directly over very low heat, without sticking. Use the same pan for all three melts, without washing it: any residue will melt with the next layer.
steps: Place the pan over very low heat. Add the white chocolate and stir constantly. As soon as the first pieces begin to melt, remove from the heat and finish melting it off the flame, using the remaining heat.
Pour the white chocolate in irregular streams into the bottom of the mold and marble it (draw lines with the tip of a knife to create veins). Place in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.
In the same pan, still over very low heat, melt half of the dark chocolate. Turn off the heat as soon as it is shiny and smooth: that's the signal, one second longer and it will seize.
Coat the entire base and sides of the mold over the marbled mixture. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Mix together the pistachio cream, grated coconut, and sweetened condensed milk. The mixture should form a soft ball when lifted with a spoon.
Spread this topping over the set chocolate, pressing down with the back of a spoon to remove any air pockets. Leave a half-centimeter border.
Melt the remaining dark chocolate in the same way, then completely cover the filling, making sure to join the edges well.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until completely set. Unmold with a sharp tap: the shell should break cleanly under the tooth, the inside remaining soft.

title: Pan-fried oat and hemp porridge
intro: It all comes down to evaporation: a wide pan cooks porridge twice as fast as a saucepan, provided you stir constantly.
titane: The open surface of the pan allows the water to evaporate quickly, and the oat starch is released upon contact with the hot base. The result: a creamy texture in five minutes, with no pan to scrub. If the mixture sets too quickly, reduce the heat and add a spoonful of water.
steps: In a bowl, combine the oat flakes, hemp seeds and vanilla protein. Mix dry to distribute the powder: it will form lumps if you add it after the water.
Pour the mixture into a cold pan, then add the water. Heat over medium heat.
Stir continuously with a spoon, scraping the bottom and sides. Allow 5 minutes, until the mixture coats the spoon and leaves a clear trail when you draw the spoon across the pan.
Remove from heat and let rest for 30 seconds: the porridge will continue to thicken. Transfer immediately to a bowl away from the heat source.
Arrange the granola on one side, place the spread in the centre and finish with a drizzle of maple syrup.

title: Chicken and creamy rice, one utensil
intro: Everything hinges on the browning of the chicken before the rice arrives: it is this that gives the dish its base flavor, the simmering only diffuses it.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and handles the intense heat without flinching. Take advantage of this to sear the chicken thoroughly right from the start: a crust forms in minutes, the juices remain at the bottom, and the rice absorbs them. All in one pan, from the first piece seared to the final gratin, without any detours to the oven.
steps: Cut the chicken into even, bite-sized pieces. Coat them with oil, salt, pepper, sweet paprika, and garlic powder. Let them rest while you chop the vegetables.
Slice the pepper and red onion into thin strips of uniform thickness: under cover, they will all cook at the same speed.
Heat the pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Then add the fat, which should ripple without smoking.

Arrange the chicken pieces in a single layer, without crowding them. Leave them undisturbed for 5 minutes: they will release on their own once a crust has formed. Turn them over briefly, then remove them from the pan and set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Pour the rice into the pan with the sliced pepper and onion, stir for one minute to toast the grains (heat them until they become translucent on the surface) and loosen the juices.
Spread everything out flat. Moisten with the stock, replace the chicken pieces and their juices, then pour over the cream. Do not mix.
Cover, heat gently, 25 minutes. The rice should be tender and the liquid almost completely absorbed.
Remove the lid, return to medium-high heat and cook for another 8 minutes, until the surface is golden brown and the cream has thickened. Serve directly from the pan.

title: Crispy pan-fried rice
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the pan and the thickness of the layer of rice: if it's too thick, it steams instead of browning.

ing.note: half a piece, cut into small cubes
half a piece, cut into small cubes
chiseled stems, plus a little extra for the finishing touch

titane: Preheat the empty pan over high heat for two to three minutes, until the first wisps of smoke appear. The titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat when the cold rice is added: you get a wok effect, a golden crust on direct contact, without the grains sticking or becoming soggy.
steps: Peel and thinly slice the onion, cut the peppers into small dice. Heat the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It should smoke lightly.
Pour the oil, then add the onion and diced peppers. Sauté for 2 to 3 minutes: they should take on colour while remaining firm to the bite.
Add the peas, cold rice, garlic powder, paprika and pepper. Spread in a thin layer over the entire surface.
Do not touch anything for 5 minutes. The rice sticks, forms a crust, then releases on its own: this is the signal to loosen it with a flick of the wrist.
Drizzle soy sauce along the hot edges, then stir vigorously for 2 minutes. The grains should come out dry, shiny and golden.
Tip out of the pan (transfer out of the pan to stop cooking) onto plates, sprinkle with spring onion and add sriracha if you like heat.

title: Chocolate and hazelnut cream in verrines
intro: With only three elements, everything hinges on the texture: a smooth cream that coats the skin without ever becoming elastic.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan. Its large surface area heats the milk more quickly and evenly, reducing the risk of lumps and shortening the thickening phase. However, it also heats up quickly: whisk continuously and scrape the sides, where the cream thickens first.
steps: Plan ahead: the cream rests for a minimum of 3 hours chilled; factor in this time before serving.
Remove the equivalent of a small glass of milk and keep it cold. Whisk the cornstarch into it until you obtain a perfectly smooth liquid with no sediment at the bottom.
Pour the remaining milk into the titanium pan over medium heat. Add the hazelnut spread and whisk for approximately 3 minutes, until it is completely melted and the mixture is uniform in color.

Return to the cornstarch milk, give it one last whisk (the cornstarch settles quickly) and pour it into the pan. Whisk continuously for 2 minutes, regularly passing along the edges. The cream is ready when it coats the whisk (it adheres in a thin layer) and when a pass leaves a clear trace at the bottom.
Transfer immediately into four glasses. Let cool to room temperature, then place in the refrigerator for a minimum of 3 hours.

title: All-chocolate muffins with a molten center
intro: It all comes down to the heart: a spread that is chilled before assembly, which remains melting in the center instead of diluting in the dough.

ing.note: one and a half sachets, or 10 g

titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe. Place the individual rings or small molds directly inside, then put the whole thing in the oven: no transfer, and as the heat rises from the bottom as well as the sides, the crust forms evenly around the still-soft center.
steps: Plan ahead: the spreads cores must spend 30 minutes in the freezer before assembly, prepare them first.
Place twelve small dollops of spread on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Place in the freezer for 30 minutes: they must be firm and grasp between the fingers without running.
Preheat the oven to 180°C, static heat.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until the mixture turns pale. Pour in the oil in a thin stream, then the milk, then the jam. Whisk again to smooth.
Sift together flour, cocoa and baking powder above the bowl. Mix just enough so that no trace of dry powder remains: dough that is worked too much gives tight muffins.

Lightly butter the cold titanium pan and the rings. Arrange them in the pan. Fill each with a layer of batter halfway up, place a frozen core in the center, cover with batter without exceeding three-quarters of the mold.
Sprinkle with chips. Cover the pan and place in the oven as is for 18 minutes. The muffins are puffed, firm, and the top no longer sticks to the finger.
Let cool for 5 minutes before removing the rings: the core is still liquid and the crumb needs to set.

title: Round zucchini breaded with tomato and mozzarella
intro: It all comes down to the breadcrumbs: they must brown dry in a pan that is already hot, without ever being immersed in oil.
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, then cover and cook. The base heats up evenly and sears the breadcrumbs, which release easily when ready; the lid creates the enveloping heat of an oven, melting the mozzarella without drying out the zucchini. One pan, no oven required.
steps: Cut the courgettes into even 1 cm slices. The consistent thickness ensures even cooking.
Brush each side with grapeseed oil, season with salt and pepper.
Coat the slices on both sides with breadcrumbs, pressing lightly to ensure they adhere. Tap to remove any excess.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over high heat.
Place the slices loosely in the pan, cover, and cook for 10 minutes over medium-high heat. Do not move them: they will release on their own when the breading is golden brown and the flesh is tender.
Turn them over. On only half of each slice, place a spoonful of tomato sauce and then a slice of mozzarella.
Fold the disc in half and secure it with a toothpick.
Cover again and continue cooking for 7 minutes over low-medium heat, until the mozzarella is melted and stretchy. Remove from the pan immediately and remove the toothpicks before serving.

title: Pistachio cream with white chocolate
intro: Two products, no additives: everything depends on the fineness of the grinding and on melting carried out gently enough so that the white chocolate never seeds.
ing: A few whole pistachios for finishing
titane: No double boiler. The white chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan, heat on low, spatula in continuous motion: the heat arrives by direct contact, without water, without steam, and without thermal shock to the base. A single utensil, zero condensation within the chocolate.
steps: Set aside a few whole pistachios for garnish. Pour the remaining pistachios into the bowl of your food processor.
Process in 30-second pulses, scraping down the sides between each pulse. The pieces become powder, then the powder compacts and releases its oil: continue until you have a smooth, glossy paste.
Chop the white chocolate into regular pieces. Place them in the titanium pan while still cold, then turn on the lowest heat.

Stir continuously with a flexible spatula for approximately 3 minutes, always pushing the edges toward the center. The chocolate should flow smoothly, without graininess or residue stuck to the bottom. Turn off the heat as soon as it is fluid.
Off the heat, fold the pistachio paste into the melted chocolate and mix with a spatula until the color is uniform.
Process the whole mixture in the food processor for one minute until the cream becomes perfectly smooth. Transfer to a clean container.
Chop the reserved pistachios and sprinkle them over the cream for garnish.

title: Apple and cinnamon porridge
intro: It all comes down to the apple: lightly caramelized before the cereals arrive, it flavors the porridge from the inside instead of just sitting on top.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding the apple cubes. The bottom heats up quickly and intensely: the surfaces in contact with the apples brown in seconds, unlike a saucepan. However, this same rapid cooking time can cause the porridge to stick if you forget. Reduce the heat to low once the milk is added, and stir regularly with a spatula.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It is ready when a drop of water sizzles briskly in it.
Peel the apple then cut it into 1 centimeter cubes. Place them in the hot pan, let them brown for 2 minutes without stirring.
Add the cinnamon and a splash of water, cover and continue for 8 minutes over medium heat. The cubes should yield under the tip of the knife while keeping their shape.
Remove one third of the apples and set aside for plating.
Lower to low heat. Pour the oat flakes, almond powder, chia seeds and plant-based milk over the remaining apples. Stir.

Cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring every two minutes and scraping the bottom well. The porridge is ready when it coats the spatula (it covers it with a layer that does not slide off immediately).
Pour into a bowl. Arrange the reserved apples, the granola, the almond butter and the maple syrup.

title: Pumpkin and cinnamon pancakes
intro: A dough without egg or butter, which gets its lightness from one thing only: the acid that awakens the bicarbonate just before the pan.

ing.note: It acidifies the dough and makes it rise.

titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the first ladleful. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly from edge to edge: the pancake browns evenly, without a pale ring around the perimeter or an overcooked center. Never flip it until the edge lifts easily—this indicates the base is cooked.
steps: Whisk together the soy milk, pumpkin puree, and lemon juice in a bowl. The mixture should be smooth, with no unblended puree strings.
Pour the flour, baking soda, and cinnamon over the top. Mix briefly until no dry flour remains. A slightly uneven batter is better than a perfectly worked one: gluten would make the pancakes elastic.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the grapeseed oil and spread it with a wrist motion.

Pour one ladleful of batter per pancake, two or three at most so the pan doesn't lose its heat. Let it cook for 2 minutes without touching it: bubbles will break the surface and the edge will detach on its own.
Turn it over sharply and continue cooking for 2 minutes. The second side should be golden brown and firm to the touch.
Remove from the pan and place on a warm plate. Serve with maple syrup and coarsely chopped pecans.

title: Agar-agar balsamic pearls
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the oil: if it is not ice-cold, the drop spreads out instead of taking a round shape.
titane: The pan spreads the 150 ml of vinegar into a thin layer. As a result, it boils in seconds, and you can see precisely when the agar-agar activates, just before it begins to set. Stay close; the volume is too small to forgive a second of inattention. You will then use a pipette to measure the agar-agar directly from the pan, without transferring it.
steps: Pour the olive oil into a tall, narrow glass and place it in the refrigerator for 1 hour. It should be thoroughly cold, almost syrupy.
In the still-cold titanium pan, whisk the vinegar and agar-agar until the powder is completely dispersed. No lumps should remain.
Increase the heat to medium. Once it starts to boil, cook for 20 seconds, then remove from the heat. Do not cook longer; the mixture will gel in the pan.

Remove the glass from the refrigerator. Draw the warm liquid through the pipette and let the drops fall one by one onto the surface of the oil, from a height of 2 or 3 cm. Each drop will solidify as it falls.
Work in small batches. If the mixture thickens in the pan, return it to low heat for 10 seconds.
Pour the contents of the glass through a fine sieve to collect the pearls. Do not rinse them: the thin film of oil prevents them from sticking together and prolongs their shine.
Arrange on toasted bread at the last minute.

title: Clementine crumble cake
intro: It all comes down to the balance between a very supple dough, full of juice and yogurt, and a crumble that is buttery enough to remain crisp despite the moisture of the quarters.
titane: The pan doubles as a mold: it goes directly from the countertop to the oven without transferring. Butter the bottom and sides generously, but don't flour them. The smooth surface doesn't need it, and the even heat distribution of the titanium cooks the edges without hardening them, even with the juice released by the clementines. When unmolding, the cake will release easily.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C using the fan setting. Butter the pan, base and sides, without flouring.
Cream the softened butter and sugar (work them with a whisk until you obtain a pale and airy mixture).
Incorporate the eggs one by one, mixing well between each addition. Add the seeds from half a vanilla pod.
In a separate bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, and salt. Gradually add this dry mixture to the butter mixture in three additions, mixing just until absorbed.
Add the clementine juice and then the yogurt. Mix until you obtain a smooth and pliable dough.
Pour the batter into the buttered pan. Smooth the surface.
Peel the clementines, separate the segments and spread them out on the dough, laying them flat.

For the crumble, rub the brown sugar with the seeds from the second half of the vanilla bean. Add the flour, almond flour, and cold butter cut into cubes. Rub the mixture between your fingertips (crush the butter into the flour with quick, light strokes) until it resembles coarse sand, without forming a dough.
Spread the crumble over the quarters, without packing it down.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 45 minutes. The top should be golden brown and a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let it rest in the pan for 10 minutes. The cake will easily pull away from the sides. Turn it out onto a wire rack, then turn it right side up again to preserve the crumble topping.

title: Quesadillas with marinated chicken
intro: It all comes down to two heat settings: high to crust the chicken, low and covered to melt the cheese without burning the tortilla.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: The pan heats up quickly and maintains the temperature: the marinated chicken, though moist, forms a crust instead of boiling. Wiped clean, the same pan becomes a miniature oven. Covered and placed over low-medium heat, it melts the mozzarella while the tortilla crisps—no oven required.
steps: Plan ahead: the chicken marinates for one hour in the refrigerator, account for this time before cooking.
Combine the chicken, garlic, bell pepper, onion and chili in a bowl. Add the lemon juice, salt, Mexican spices and Cayenne. Mix by hand to coat each piece.
Cover and place in the refrigerator. Allow one hour: below that, the spices remain on the surface.
Preheat the pan empty, medium-high heat, 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle and skate across it.

Pour the grapeseed oil. Add the drained chicken in a single layer, without pressing it. Do not touch it: it will detach on its own when the crust forms. Turn it, continue until cooked through, approximately 10 minutes in total.
Transfer the chicken to a plate. Wipe the pan with paper towel: burnt spice residue would burn under the tortillas.
Lower to medium-low heat. Place a tortilla directly in the pan, salt it and sprinkle it with spices. Spread one third of the mozzarella, then one third of the chicken. Close with a second tortilla.

Slide a small knob of clarified butter around the edges, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Flip firmly with the help of a plate, then brown the second side covered. The tortilla should be flecked with brown, the cheese melting. Repeat for the other two quesadillas.

title: Cloud cake with Greek yogurt and mascarpone
intro: A cake with little or no flour, whose success depends entirely on the degree of cooking: it should come out of the oven still wobbly in the center.
ing: Finely grated zest of a clementine
titane: The titanium pan acts as a mold. You fill it on the countertop and then put it directly in the oven. Its metallic mass distributes heat through the base and sides, preventing the edges from overcooking and the center from becoming runny. Lightly butter it, but not excessively: a thin film is enough for easy unmolding.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170 °C with fan circulation.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until the mixture is smooth and grainy free. There is no need to make it pale: we are seeking consistency, not volume.
Zest the clementine directly above the mixing bowl so that the essential oils fall straight into the mixture. Add the Greek yogurt and mascarpone.
Whisk until you obtain a perfectly smooth cream. If the mascarpone is cold, it will leave lumps: let it rest for twenty minutes at room temperature before starting.
Fold in the sifted cornstarch in a rain-like motion, stirring with a spatula so as not to reincorporate air.
Butter the titanium pan, pour in the mixture, and smooth the surface.
Bake for 45 minutes. The cake is ready when the surface has set and lightly browned, and the center still trembles noticeably when you shake the pan. Do not open the oven before 35 minutes.
Let it cool in the pan: the texture firms up as it cools. Unmold once the cake is at room temperature, or serve it directly in the pan.

title: Puff pastry knot with chocolate spread
intro: Everything depends on the regularity of the fire: the puff pastry must rise before it browns, otherwise the crust forms on a still raw dough.
titane: The titanium pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty and then covered, it diffuses a gentle heat that makes the puff pastry rise and browns both sides without drying out the dough. The lid traps the steam, while the base provides the crispness.
steps: Unroll the puff pastry on the work surface. Spread the spread over one half, leaving a one-centimeter border.
Fold the dough in half to enclose the filling. Press the edges with your fingertips, then cut two triangles lengthwise.
Fold the central part over itself and cross the triangles by their points to form a knot. Weld the joints by pinching lightly.
Brush with egg yolk, then sprinkle with cane sugar.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the clarified butter and spread it by tilting the pan.
Place the knot on top, cover, and reduce the heat to low. Cook for 10 minutes: the bottom will be golden brown and will easily detach when ready.

Flip with a flick of the wrist, cover again, and continue cooking for 4 minutes. The pastry will be puffed up, golden brown on both sides, and crispy. If it's browning too quickly, lower the heat further: the pan heats up more than an oven.

title: Pan-fried cherry tomatoes
intro: What matters here is patience over low heat: the tomato must lose its water without ever frying.
ing: olive oil to cover the jar
titane: A preheated titanium pan, then covered, replaces a low-temperature oven. The direct, even heat confits the tomatoes in 40 minutes instead of two hours, with a more pronounced caramelization on the surface. Wait until the tomato halves easily detach from the bottom; forcing them before then will tear the skin.
steps: Cut the cherry tomatoes in half lengthwise. Place them on absorbent paper, cut side down, while the oven preheats.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in a drizzle of olive oil: it should ripple slightly, without smoking.
Arrange the halved tomatoes cut-side down in a single layer. Season with basil salt and oregano.

Cover and reduce the heat to low. Let it simmer (cook slowly over low heat in fat) for 40 minutes, stirring occasionally. The tomatoes are ready when they are shriveled, the skin is slightly caramelized, and they easily detach from the bottom of the pan.
Remove from heat. Let cool in the pan: they will finish absorbing the flavored oil.
Remove from the cooking utensil and place in a clean jar, then cover completely with olive oil. Store in the refrigerator.

title: Pan-fried crispy apple rings
intro: It all comes down to two things: a paste thick enough to stick to the fruit, and slices that are well dried before dipping.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface: the batter sets instantly on contact and forms a golden crust, similar to that of a waffle iron. Do not touch anything during cooking. The pancake will release itself when that side is cooked: this is the signal to flip it.
steps: Whisk the egg with the milk, melted butter, 10 g sugar, and vanilla until you obtain a smooth mixture.
Add the flour and baking powder all at once. Whisk briefly: the batter should remain thick and coat the back of a spoon without running.
Peel the apple, then cut it into slices 0.5 cm thick and core the centre of each one.
Dab the slices between two sheets of paper towel. A dry surface retains the batter better.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, before adding any fat.
Pour the oil or clarified butter and tilt the pan to cover the bottom with a thin layer.
Dip a slice in the batter, let the excess drain for a moment, then place it in the pan. Work slice by slice.
Do not overcrowd: leave space between each piece, even if it means cooking in two batches to keep the pan hot. Allow approximately 4 minutes per side. Turn only when the slice releases on its own.
Transfer onto a rack for a few seconds, then roll the slices while still hot in the coating sugar.

title: Dark chocolate and roasted dried fruit bar
intro: It all comes down to roasting: dried fruits ripened just before bitterness sets in, and chocolate that never cooks.
ing: 200g of unsalted dried fruit, of your choice
generous amount of fleur de sel
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and dry: it toasts almonds without a drop of fat, then, once the heat is off, its residual warmth is enough to melt the chocolate placed on top. No double boiler, no dish to fill—the pan becomes the mold and goes straight into the freezer.
steps: Heat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It should be thoroughly hot before adding the first ingredient.

Add the dried fruit all at once, without any oil or butter. Stir regularly for about 5 minutes. Trust the smell and color rather than the timer: titanium cookware heats up quickly, and the color develops rapidly. The fruit should be golden, crisp, and fragrant.
Reduce heat to low. Press the dried fruit down with a spatula in an even layer that covers the bottom.
Turn off the heat. Scatter the broken chocolate pieces over the dried fruit, cover, and let it melt for 3 minutes using the residual heat. The chocolate should be soft and glossy, never bubbling.
Spread the chocolate with a spatula to coat everything and smooth the surface.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel, in a light mist, from a slightly higher vantage point to distribute the crystals.
Place the pan in the refrigerator (or slide the baking sheet onto a sheet of parchment paper) until completely set. Break into irregular pieces when ready to serve.

title: Upside-down puff pastry with beetroot, feta and goat cheese
intro: Everything hinges on the bottom of the pan: the balsamic must caramelize on contact with the hot metal before the beetroot is placed on it, otherwise the filling will release its water and make the puff pastry soggy.
titane: The pan goes straight from the stovetop to the oven without transferring, handle and all. You caramelize first, then bake, and flip with a single, swift motion when the batter has released itself from the sides. No mold, no sticking, just a clean disc.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the base becomes evenly hot.
Pour in the olive oil, season with salt and pepper, then add the balsamic vinegar. It should hiss and thicken in a few seconds on the hot base.
Arrange the beetroot slices in a tightly packed rosette pattern directly in the caramel. Let them set for 2 minutes without moving them.
Distribute half the goat cheese and half the crumbled feta over the beets. Turn off the heat.
Place the puff pastry over the filling and tuck the edges inside the pan, between the filling and the side. Prick the pastry with a fork in five or six places to allow steam to escape.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 20 minutes, until the dough is golden brown, firm to the touch, and its edges have pulled back from the side.

Remove the pan using a thick glove — the handle will remain hot for several minutes. Let it rest for 1 minute, place the serving dish upside down on the pan and flip it over with a quick, firm motion.
Crumble the remaining feta and sprinkle the crushed hazelnuts over the still-warm puff pastry. Serve immediately.

title: Hot tuna and cheddar sandwich
intro: It's all about the contrast: a dry, golden crust, a still-fresh filling underneath, and just-melted cheddar.

ing.note: It can withstand higher temperatures without

titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. This allows the bread to brown before it absorbs the filling and becomes soggy. Preheat the pan empty, then leave the sandwich alone: it will release itself once the crust has formed. As long as it's sticking, it's not ready. Just flip it once, no pressure—pressing the sandwich forces the air out of the bread and makes it compact.
steps: Drain the tuna thoroughly, pressing it with a fork against the side of the can. Mix it with the mayonnaise and dill. Season to taste.
Spread the filling on two slices of bread, leaving a half-centimeter free around the edge.
Place two slices of cheddar cheese on each sandwich, flat.
Cover with the remaining slices. Press down once lightly with the palm of your hand.
Brush the outside of the sandwiches with clarified butter, top and bottom, in a thin and even layer.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It is ready when a drop of water sizzles in it and evaporates immediately.
Place the sandwiches on the grill. Let them cook for about 3 minutes without moving them. Lift a corner: the bread should be evenly golden brown and no longer sticking.
Turn over once. Continue for 2 to 3 minutes, until the second side is colored and the cheddar is melted.
Remove (transfer from the pan) to a board, wait a minute, then slice diagonally.

title: Mushroom and Camembert Tarte Tatin
intro: Everything hinges on the caramelization of the mushrooms upon contact with the bare metal: if they release their water without coloring, the tatin will be bland and the pastry soggy.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the first drop of oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat when the mushrooms are added: they sear instead of boiling. The same pan then goes in the oven and is used as a mold for unmolding. Just make sure the handle can withstand 180°C (350°F).
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil: it should ripple slightly without smoking.

Add the balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper to the hot pan. Immediately spread the mushrooms and parsley evenly over the bottom. Let it cook for 4 minutes without stirring too much: they will release their water and then take on color.
Reduce the heat to low. Place the Camembert slices on top of the mushrooms in an even layer. Do not stir. Cook for 2 minutes, until the cheese has softened.
Turn off the heat. Place the puff pastry disc on top and tuck the edges inside the pan with the back of a spoon. Prick the pastry with a fork and brush with egg yolk.
Place the pan in the oven as is, for 20 minutes at 180°C. The dough should be golden brown and firm to the touch, with the edges slightly drawn back.

Remove the pan using an oven mitt and let it cool for exactly 1 minute. Place the serving dish on top of the pan and invert it in one smooth motion: the tart will release easily. If left for more than 2 minutes, the cheese will solidify and stick.

title: Butternut squash, breaded twice, pan-fried
intro: It all comes down to the breading: coated twice with egg and panko, it forms a shell thick enough to crisp up in the pan while the squash flesh confits inside.
titane: The titanium pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty and then oiled, it sears the crust by direct contact: a few minutes are enough where a baking sheet would take twenty. Key point: don't touch the slices while they're still sticking. Breadcrumbs that easily detach from the bottom are set. If you force them too soon, the crust will stick and the work will be wasted.
steps: Cut the butternut squash into 1 cm thick slices. Peel them one by one and remove the seeds from the slices cut from the bulb. Pat them dry if the flesh releases water.

Line up three shallow bowls. In the first, the flour. In the second, the beaten eggs, seasoned with salt and pepper. In the third, the panko breadcrumbs mixed with paprika, garlic powder, and Parmesan cheese.

Dust a slice of bread with flour, tapping off the excess. Dip it in the egg, then in the seasoned breadcrumbs. Dip the same slice in the egg again, then coat it once more in the panko breadcrumbs: this second layer forms the shell. Press down with the palm of your hand to seal it in.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil, which can withstand high temperatures. It should ripple and simmer gently.
Place the slices in the pan without them touching. Work in small batches: an overcrowded pan loses heat and the breading absorbs the oil instead of crisping. Allow approximately 6 minutes.
Turn over when each slice releases easily under the spatula. Continue for 5 minutes on the other side: the crust should be amber, the flesh tender under the tip of a knife.

Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack rather than paper towels to allow steam to escape. Season lightly with salt. Continue cooking, adding a drizzle of oil if needed, until the next batch is cooked.

title: Light chocolate and clementine mousse
intro: Everything depends on the temperature of the ganache at the time of incorporation: if it's too hot, it will cause the whipped cream to deflate.
ing: Chilled heavy cream (minimum 30% fat) for the mousse
Cold, full-fat liquid cream (minimum 30% fat) for the
titane: The frying pan replaces the saucepan for the milk and melting the chocolate. It heats up quickly, nothing sticks to the bottom, and the ganache is made in one go: heat it, remove it from the heat, and pour in the chocolate. A single container is all you need for the hot part. However, cooling is done in a bowl: the frying pan retains heat for too long and would delay assembly.
steps: Pour this milk into the pan and bring it to a simmer over medium heat, approximately 2 minutes. As it is a liquid, there is no need to preheat the pan empty. Stop as soon as small bubbles appear around the edges.
Off the heat, add both chocolates to the hot milk. Wait thirty seconds, then stir vigorously until you obtain a ganache (emulsion of chocolate and liquid) that is smooth and glossy. Allow 2 minutes.
Transfer the ganache to a bowl. Let it cool to room temperature, approximately fifteen minutes: it should be warm to the touch, never hot.
Meanwhile, whip the 30 cl of heavy cream in a cold bowl until it forms stiff peaks on the whisk.
Fold the whipped cream into the warm ganache in three additions, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from the centre towards the edges. Stop as soon as the mixture is homogeneous.
Divide the mousse among four cups and place them in the refrigerator.
Whip the remaining 20 cl of heavy cream in a second cold bowl, incorporating the icing sugar towards the end of whisking. The cream should hold its shape firmly.
Split the vanilla pod, scrape out the seeds and fold them into the cream, then add the Greek yogurt using a spatula, without overworking the mixture.
Peel the clementines to the pith and remove the segments between the membranes. Crumble the langues de chat under the palm of your hand.
Remove the cups, place the segments and then the crumbled biscuit pieces on the mousse.
Top each cup with a quenelle of yogurt cream and serve immediately.

title: Greek yogurt cheesecake with strawberries and pistachios
intro: A cheesecake without crust or oven, whose success depends entirely on the gentleness of the fire and patience in front of the lid.
titane: The covered titanium pan works like a small oven: the heat rises slowly, spreads evenly across the entire surface, and cooks the food without ever forming a crust. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before greasing it, then leave it alone. The signal is visual: the edges will retract and detach themselves from the pan.
steps: Place the empty pan over low-medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the knob of clarified butter and spread it with a brush over the bottom and sides.
In a bowl, combine the yogurt, eggs, and honey. Whisk, then gradually whisk in the cornstarch. Mix until perfectly smooth and lump-free.
Hull the strawberries and cut them in half or into quarters depending on their size.
Pour the mixture into the hot pan. Place the strawberries on top, sprinkle with pistachios.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Cook for 18 to 20 minutes without stirring or lifting the lid unnecessarily. The center should be set and the edges should pull away from the sides.
Turn off the heat, uncover, and let it cool in the pan. The center will firm up as it cools. Unmold once it's barely warm.

title: Cinnamon and dried fruit cake
intro: A cake without eggs or butter, where everything hinges on the balance between the fat of the margarine and the hydration of the oat drink: if mixed too much, it becomes elastic.
ing: mixture of dried fruits and oilseeds
A little margarine or neutral oil for the pan
titane: The titanium pan acts as a mold. You mix, you pour, you bake: no transfer, therefore no loss of batter on the sides of an intermediate bowl. Its even heat conduction cooks the sides at the same rate as the bottom, which avoids the dry corners of traditional cake pans.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
In a large bowl, combine the oat milk, melted margarine, sugar, and cinnamon. Whisk until smooth, with no lumps of solidified margarine.
Incorporate the flour, almond flour, baking powder, and salt. Mix with a spatula, cutting the dough rather than beating it, until all traces of flour disappear. Some irregularities are normal.
Add the dried fruit and give it three or four turns with a spatula to distribute it. Stop there: overworking the mixture develops the gluten and makes the crumb rubbery.
Grease the titanium pan generously, including the sides, then pour in the mixture and smooth the surface.
Bake uncovered for 48 minutes. The cake is cooked when the surface is golden and domed and a knife inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let it cool for 5 minutes in the pan before turning it over: the unmolding will be cleaner, the crust will remain whole.

title: Mini leek and goat cheese tarte tatins
intro: Everything hinges on the initial cooking of the leeks: seared directly on the metal, they release their water and then concentrate their sugars, and it is this slightly caramelized base that will support the entire tart.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding oil. The leeks will then fall onto a surface that is already hot, stick for a second, then release on their own: that's the signal. The pan then goes directly into the oven as is, filled, without transferring or using an intermediate dish — a single, continuous cooking process, from the leeks to the puffed pastry.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes: the heat should be felt a few centimeters above the bottom.
Meanwhile, slice the white parts of the leeks into even half-centimeter rounds. Rinse them and dry them thoroughly.

Pour the olive oil into the hot pan, add the leeks in a single layer, season with salt and pepper, and drizzle with balsamic glaze. Let them sweat (cook gently so the vegetables release their water without browning too quickly) for 5 minutes without stirring: the slices will detach from the bottom of the pan on their own when they are ready.
Remove from heat and gather the leeks into 6 small piles distributed in the pan. Place a slice of goat cheese on each.
Cover each mound with a disc of puff pastry, tucking the edges slightly towards the bottom of the pan.
Brush the dough with egg yolk, then prick it three times with a fork to let the steam escape.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 20 minutes, until the discs are puffed up and thoroughly golden.
Remove from the oven, wait 2 minutes, then turn each tart out onto a plate using a thin spatula. The caramelized balsamic glaze will help loosen them.

title: Pan-roasted potatoes with pickle sauce
intro: It all comes down to the cut side: a very hot pan, no movement for six minutes, and the crust forms on its own.
ing: Juice from the jar of pickles
titane: The preheated titanium pan acts as an oven. It sears the bare flesh and builds a golden crust in minutes, where a stovetop would take half an hour. The lid then takes over: the trapped steam cooks the inside without drying it out. Place the potato halves cut-side down and leave them. They will release themselves once the crust has set.
steps: Wash the potatoes, dry them thoroughly, then split them in half lengthwise. A dry surface browns better.
Place the empty pan over high heat. Count 3 minutes, until a veil of smoke rises from the bottom.
Pour in the oil, then immediately arrange the potatoes cut-side down in a single layer. Season with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with garlic powder.
Let them cook for 6 minutes without stirring or lifting. The potato halves will detach themselves from the bottom when a crust has formed: that's the signal.
Reduce heat to medium, cover and continue cooking for 12 minutes. A knife tip should pierce the flesh without resistance.
Meanwhile, combine the yogurt, mayonnaise, pressed garlic, diced pickles, juice from the jar, and spring onion in a bowl. Mix until you have a smooth, well-combined sauce.
Remove the potatoes from the pan to stop the cooking process and let them cool for 5 minutes. Then coat them generously with the sauce and serve.

title: Creamy orzo with carrots, peas and poultry sausage
intro: It all comes down to two things: really coloring the carrots before adding water, and pouring the broth in several stages so that the orzo absorbs it instead of boiling in it.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly: take advantage of this to sear the carrots without moving them, without touching them, until they detach from the bottom of the pan on their own. This is where the flavor develops. Then, add the stock in two or three additions: you'll have less than 500 ml of liquid in the pan at a time, so it's still pan cooking, not a disguised casserole.
steps: Peel the carrots, then cut them into slices. Peel the shallot and slice it thinly.
Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the grapeseed oil or clarified butter: it should simmer slightly.
Pour the carrot slices in a single layer. Cover and cook for 10 minutes without stirring. They are ready to be stirred when they detach on their own from the bottom, browned on one side.
Add the shallot and garlic. Sauté for 3 minutes, until the shallot becomes translucent.

Pour the orzo and about one third of the broth. Cover. Continue cooking for 10 minutes, adding the remaining broth in two additions as soon as the liquid is nearly absorbed. The orzo should remain al dente.
Add the peas, sausage slices, cream cheese, Parmesan and pepper.
Stir and cook for 5 minutes covered, until the sauce coats the orzo without puddles at the bottom of the pan. Adjust the seasoning: the broth and Parmesan already add a lot of salt.

title: Sparkling water crepes
intro: Adding sparkling water at the last moment lightens the dough: what matters is pouring it just before baking and not working it afterwards.
ing: Melted butter, brought back to room temperature
titane: Preheat the pan empty. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly, so the very first crepe comes out golden brown, without the usual string of white crepes you throw away. Then, just let it cook: don't touch the crepe until the edges have loosened on their own.
steps: Combine the flour, both sugars and the salt in a bowl. Mix together dry.
Make a well in the flour. Crack the eggs into the well, pour in the milk, then the cooled melted butter. Whisk until you have a smooth, lump-free batter.
Add the sparkling water at the very last moment. Mix with a few short movements, just long enough to incorporate it: the more you stir, the more the bubbles will subside.
Heat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 3 minutes. It is ready when a few drops of water appear on the surface and evaporate within a second.
Pour a thin stream of grapeseed oil. Spread it in a very thin layer with absorbent paper. On titanium, this single application is sufficient for the entire set.

Pour a small ladleful of batter into the pan, tilt it to spread it evenly. Let it cook undisturbed for about 1 minute: the edges will lift and the surface will no longer stick. Flip it over with a flick of the wrist, cook for another 30 seconds, transfer it to a plate, and repeat.

title: Apple and pear crumble, cooked in a pan and oven
intro: The fruit is first cooked covered to melt without releasing water, then the crumble finishes in the oven in the same pan: the texture holds because nothing is transferred.

ing.note: or grapeseed oil for a seizure

titane: The titanium pan goes directly from stovetop to oven without needing to be transferred. Simply sear the diced fruit on the baking sheet, sprinkle the batter over it, and bake. The heat circulates quickly in the base, so it will take slightly less time than using a Dutch oven to achieve soft, melted fruit. Before you begin, check that the handle is oven-safe.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Cut the apples and pears into even cubes, without peeling them. The skin holds up during cooking and retains its bite.
Preheat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. The air above the bottom should be noticeably hot.
Add the margarine or oil. Let it melt, then add the brown sugar and the diced fruit. Mix to coat.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes over medium heat. The fruit should be soft but still retain its diced shape.
Meanwhile, work the soft margarine with the sugar and cinnamon using your fingertips.
Add the flour and rub the mixture between your palms until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Stop as soon as the dough no longer forms a ball.
Remove the lid, scatter the crumbs over the fruit in an even layer, without packing them down.
Bake the pan uncovered for 17 minutes, until the surface is golden brown and crispy. Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: French toast filled with chocolate spread
intro: It all comes down to the crust: the brown sugar must caramelize on direct contact with the pan, not melt in the batter.

ing.note: slightly dry or from the day before
(it withstands high temperatures), or oil of

titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat. Sprinkle brown sugar on the still-raw side while the other side cooks: when you flip it, it will fall onto the hot metal and caramelize in seconds. Never force the spatula. The bread will release itself once the crust has set; if you force it before then, you'll tear it off.
steps: Beat the eggs with sugar and milk in a shallow dish wide enough to lay a slice flat.
Spread two slices of bread with spread until the edges, covering completely.
Close each one with a second slice. Press lightly with your palm on top to seal.
Dip each sandwich in the mixture, 20 seconds per side. The bread should be soaked through without collapsing. Drain it briefly over the dish.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the clarified butter, it should shimmer (take on a bright, fluid appearance) without smoking.
Place the sandwiches. Sprinkle the visible side immediately with brown sugar. Leave for 4 minutes: the crust forms when the bread stops sticking.
Turn with a quick, decisive gesture, without hesitation. Continue for 4 minutes until the second side releases on its own and is golden.
Remove from the pan onto a rack, not onto a plate: the crust stays crispy. Wait 1 minute before cutting, the spread is scalding hot.

title: Iced grape and chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the mixture must be set before the chocolate is added, otherwise the shell will sink instead of cracking.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan, without a double boiler. Preheat it empty for one minute over very low heat, then turn off the heat and pour in the chocolate and coconut oil. The residual heat from the bottom is enough to melt everything while you stir. You save yourself the need for a saucepan, a mixing bowl, and the risk of overheating that comes with them.
steps: Rinse the grapes and dry them thoroughly. Any residual water will cause ice crystals to form in the freezer.
Mix the raisins with the Greek yogurt in a bowl, until each grape is coated.
Spread the mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, in a layer about 1.5 cm thick. Place in the freezer for 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, preheat the titanium pan empty, over very low heat, for 1 minute. Remove it from the heat, add the chocolate broken into pieces and the coconut oil. Stir continuously: the melting should occur off the flame. The chocolate is ready when it is fluid and glossy, without any graininess.
Take out the baking sheet. Coat (cover with an even layer) the frozen mixture by pouring the chocolate directly from the pan in a continuous motion.
Return to the freezer for 10 minutes, until the shell sets.
Let it rest for 2 minutes at room temperature, then break into irregular bars.

title: Crown of chocolate-hazelnut puff pastry men
intro: It all comes down to two things: a layer of spreadable paste thin enough not to leak during baking, and little men close enough together to hold each other once the dough has risen.
titane: The titanium pan goes directly from the countertop to the oven without any transfer. You assemble the pastry ring on its parchment paper, slide it into the pan, and bake. The rapid heat conduction from the base browns the underside of the puff pastry instead of leaving it white and soggy, as is often the case on a baking sheet. The downside: keep an eye on it after 15 minutes, as the base browns faster than on other baking sheets.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Unroll the first sheet of puff pastry on the work surface, including the baking paper.
Spread the spread in an even layer, leaving a 1 cm border all around. If it is too firm, soften it for a few seconds in a bain-marie.
Place the second roll on top, making sure it's properly aligned. Roll over it with the rolling pin without pressing down, just enough to seal the two layers together.
Cut out stick figures using a cookie cutter, as close together as possible to minimize waste.

Draw a circle in pencil on a sheet of parchment paper, turn it over, and arrange the gingerbread men along the line, shoulder to shoulder, hands touching. This contact is what seals the wreath together during baking.
Brush with egg yolk to obtain a shiny and colored surface, but not excessively: too much yolk in the folds blocks the development of the puff pastry.

Slide the parchment paper and its ring into the titanium pan. Cover and bake for 20 minutes at 180°C (350°F). The pastry should be puffed up and a deep golden brown. Check after 15 minutes by lifting an edge with a spatula.
Let it cool for 5 minutes, sprinkle with icing sugar through a sieve and serve directly from the pan.

title: Caramelized chocolate palmiers
intro: It all comes down to the caramelization of the sugar through direct contact with the metal: moderate heat, lid, patience.
titane: The preheated titanium pan, empty, replaces the oven. The sugar melts on contact with the metal and forms a caramel crust under the palmier, while the lid traps the heat and allows the puff pastry to rise. Two minutes of preheating is all it takes, whereas an oven requires fifteen.
steps: Preheat the oven.
Mix the caster sugar and vanilla sugar in a bowl.
Unroll the first sheet of pastry on its paper. Brush it with melted butter all over the surface, including the edges. Sprinkle generously with vanilla sugar.
Place the second sheet of pastry on top, well aligned. Press flat with the palm of your hand to expel air. Brush with butter, sprinkle with sugar again.
Fold both long sides towards the centre until they meet. Fold a second time, one over the other: you now have a log with four layers.
Place the log in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. The chilled pastry will cut more neatly.
Slice into regular segments of 1.5 cm. Gently pull apart the two spirals at the end with your fingertips to create the heart shape.
Preheat the titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes without any fat. The butter in the pastry is sufficient.
Place 4 to 5 palmiers, well spaced apart. Cover, reduce to medium-low heat and cook for 8 minutes. The palmier will puff up and the sugar will brown on the underside.
Turn over only when the palmier releases easily from the pan. If it resists, give it another minute. Cover and continue for 8 minutes.
Remove from the pan to stop cooking, place on a wire rack. Wipe the pan, let it return to temperature and proceed to the next batch.
Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie. Dip each cooled palmier halfway up, place on baking paper and leave to set.

title: Caramel flan, pan cooking
intro: Everything depends on the color of the caramel and the gentleness of the heat afterwards: caramel stopped too soon remains flat, too hot a cooking time makes the mixture grainy.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and evenly: the sugar melts without any hot spots, the color develops clearly, and you stop exactly when you decide. Once the caramel is poured, the same utensil takes on a different role. A little simmering water around the mold, the lid on, and you have a stable bain-marie without turning on the oven.
steps: Plan ahead: the flan must refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight; start the day before.
Place the empty pan over medium heat and let it warm for 2 minutes. This preheating prevents the sugar from colouring unevenly.
Add the caramel sugar and water to the pan. Let it cook without stirring: the mixture will liquefy, then turn amber in about 3 minutes. Once the colour suits you, remove from heat.
Pour the caramel immediately into the mould and tilt it to coat the bottom with an even layer. It sets quickly, so work fast.
In a separate bowl, whisk the milk with the sugar and flan preparation. Beat until no lumps remain in suspension.

Pour this mixture over the set caramel. Place the mould in the pan, add water around it to mid-height, cover and maintain a gentle simmer for 10 minutes. Halfway through, stir the mixture in the mould with a spoon: it should thicken and coat the back of the spoon.
Remove the mould, let it cool, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Overnight gives a much firmer set.
When turning out, do not run a blade around it: a properly set flan will release from the sides on its own when you invert the mould.

title: Pumpkin, spice and dark chocolate pan cookies
intro: Everything hinges on the gentleness of the fire: if it's too hot, the base burns before the heart catches.
titane: Covered pan, low heat. The lid traps the heat and reflects it back onto the tops of the cookies, like an oven dome, while direct contact with the titanium caramelizes the base. The result: a crispy edge and a soft center. Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before greasing, then leave the cookies untouched until they stick.
steps: In a bowl, work the softened vegan butter with the pumpkin puree, brown sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger and salt. Mix by hand until you obtain a smooth mass.
Pour in the flour, add the chocolate and pecans. Mix briefly: the dough should remain soft, without being overworked.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Brush it with a film of grapeseed oil, then wipe off the excess with absorbent paper.
Shape the mixture into patties of about 40g, flatten them slightly and place them spaced apart in the pan. Allow three to four pieces per batch, no more.
Cover and reduce the heat to low. Let it cook for 10 minutes without touching it. The cookies are ready to be turned over when they easily release from the bottom and the base is golden brown.
Gently turn them over with a flexible spatula and continue cooking uncovered for 4 minutes, until the second side is browned. Transfer them to a wire rack; they will firm up as they cool.

title: Caramelized apple spring rolls
intro: It all comes down to two separate cooking processes in the same pan: a compote that caramelizes without liquefying, then a quick sear that transforms the rice paper into a brittle shell.

ing.note: (It can withstand higher temperatures without blackening)

ing: c. a c. d neutral oil
titane: The titanium pan eliminates the need for an air fryer or oven. Preheated empty and then brought to a boil, it sears the oil-coated rice paper on both sides, dry, and produces a golden crispness in just a few minutes without deep-frying. One crucial condition: do not turn a spring roll until it detaches itself from the bottom.
steps: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. It must be thoroughly hot before adding any fat.

Add the clarified butter. Dice the apples into even pieces, add them to the pan along with the brown sugar, and cook for 8 minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally. The apples are ready when they are soft, amber-colored, and pull away from the bottom of the pan on their own. Remove from the pan and let cool slightly.
Beat the egg in a shallow dish. Quickly dip a rice paper sheet on both sides: it should be pliable and coated, not soggy. The egg replaces the water and makes rolling much easier.
Place a strip of compote in the center, fold in the sides, and roll tightly. A loose spring roll will open when gripped.

Brush each spring roll with a light coating of neutral oil. Return the pan to high heat. Sear the spring rolls on one side at a time, approximately 6 minutes in total, waiting until each side is golden brown and releases easily before turning.
Serve within minutes: the crispiness doesn't last long.

title: Crustless quiche with mushrooms and spinach
intro: Everything depends on the water content of the mushrooms: as long as it remains, the device will not work properly.
titane: The pan is used for searing vegetables, then goes straight into the oven. No transferring, no gratin dish to wash, and the browning on the metal stays under the pan throughout the cooking process. Heat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat: this preheating prevents sticking.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Finely chop the onion and garlic, and quarter the mushrooms.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil or clarified butter.
Add the onion and garlic to the hot pan. Don't stir for the first minute; the pieces will loosen from the metal on their own when they're ready. Cook for 4 minutes, until translucent.
Add the mushrooms and spinach. Let them sweat (release their water over moderate heat) for about 6 minutes, until all the liquid has evaporated and the bottom of the pan is dry again.
Meanwhile, crack the eggs into a bowl. Whisk them with the milk, then the Greek yogurt until smooth. Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the Gruyère cheese.
Spread the vegetables evenly in the pan, off the heat. Pour the mixture over them and shake lightly to coat them completely.
Bake for 30 minutes. The surface should be set and golden brown, the center just firm to the touch. Wait 5 minutes before cutting.

title: Pan-fried chicken patties
intro: It all comes down to cutting the chicken with a knife, which retains some texture where a meat grinder would produce a mushy stuffing.

ing.note: half a piece, in very small dice

titane: The titanium cookware heats up quickly and withstands the cold weight of the pancakes without losing temperature: the crust forms in four minutes. Then, place the lid on; the trapped steam finishes cooking the cakes throughout, keeping the inside moist, whereas the oven would have dried out the surface.
steps: Cut the chicken breasts into 5mm cubes with a knife. The more uniform the pieces, the better the patties will hold together.
Combine the chicken, onion, bell pepper, and corn in a bowl. Season with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika. Mix to distribute the spices before adding the binders.
Incorporate the egg, cheese, mayonnaise, mustard, cornflour and basil. Work by hand until the mixture is homogeneous and holds its shape between your fingers.
Shape into eight patties about 2 cm thick. Press them firmly together by rolling them between your palms, then flatten them. Allow 5 minutes.
Preheat the pan empty for 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the oil. It should ripple without smoking.

Place the patties on a baking sheet, leaving two fingers' width of space between them, in two batches if necessary. Sear them for 4 minutes (start cooking on a very hot surface to form a crust) without moving them. They will release easily when the crust is set: that's the signal to turn them over.
Turn over, reduce heat to medium, cover and cook for 8 minutes. The patties should be firm to the touch and golden brown on both sides.
Remove (transfer from the pan to stop cooking) to a wire rack rather than paper towels, to keep the crust clean.

title: Potato and white asparagus gratin with parmesan béchamel sauce
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: vegetables cooked covered, béchamel sauce made on the same sides, gratin in the oven, without ever transferring.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before the first cooking stage: a few drops of water should bead and slide off. This gradual increase in temperature allows you to complete the three cooking stages consecutively without the béchamel sauce sticking, provided you wipe the pan clean between each stage.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Check with a water drop.
Slice the potatoes into thin rounds. Pour them into the pan with a little salted water, cover and cook for 15 minutes over medium heat. The tip of the knife should pass through without resistance.
Transfer the potatoes out of the pan into a dish.
Peel the asparagus (scrape them from the tip towards the base, in a thin but complete layer) and cut off the fibrous bases.
Wipe the pan, pour in the broth, lay the asparagus and cover. Poach for 15 minutes over medium heat: the blade should sink in smoothly.
Drain the asparagus and set them aside with the potatoes. Wipe the pan again.

Melt the butter over low heat, add the flour all at once and stir for 1 minute to cook the roux without browning. Pour in the cold milk in three additions, stirring smoothly with each addition. Allow approximately 8 minutes until the sauce is nappant (it coats the back of the spoon).
Off the heat, stir in two-thirds of the Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper, grate nutmeg over it.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Butter the pan, arrange the potatoes and asparagus, coat with béchamel, sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan.
Place in the oven for 20 minutes, until the surface is golden and bubbling. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

title: Pan-fried tarte tatin
intro: It all comes down to the color of the caramel: a true amber, never blond, otherwise the sugar disappears under the apples.

ing.note: or clarified butter (melted butter with the drained skins removed)

titane: One pan is all you need for all three stages of the recipe: caramelizing, cooking the apples, and baking. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding anything. The rapid heat conduction of titanium ensures a smooth caramel, without any burning spots, and the lack of a non-stick coating allows the tart to release cleanly from the pan.
steps: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Pour the water and sugar into the hot pan. Let it cook without stirring until amber in color. Remove from heat, add the 65 g of butter in pieces and stir until you have a smooth caramel.
Spread the caramel over the entire bottom of the pan. Set aside off the heat.
Peel the apples, cut them into quarters, and remove the cores.

Wipe out the pan. Melt the 55 g of butter in it over medium heat with the split and scraped vanilla pod and cinnamon. Place the apple quarters and leave them for 8 minutes without touching them: they will release on their own when ready. They should be coated and just barely tender.
Arrange the quarters in the caramel, tightly packed, rounded side down.
Unroll the puff pastry, cut out a circle slightly larger than the pan, place it over the apples and tuck the edges inside, against the sides.
Prick the pastry with a fork and brush it with beaten egg.
Preheat the oven.
Place the pan in the oven as is at 180 °C with fan circulation, for 42 minutes, until the pastry is golden brown.
Let rest for 7 minutes, no longer, then turn out onto a plate while hot. Cooled caramel sticks to the bottom.
Warm the apricot jam and brush it over the apples to glaze with a thin, shiny layer.

title: Vegan cinnamon pancakes
intro: A dough without resting, which stands up thanks to the reaction between the bicarbonate and the acidity of the lemon: it is the heat of the pan, well established before the first ladleful, that does the rest.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. As a result, a crust forms within the first minute, and the pancake releases easily. As long as it resists, it's not ready. Never force it with the spatula.
steps: Combine the flour, baking soda and cinnamon in a bowl. Mix with a whisk to distribute the leavening powder.
Pour in the protein drink and lemon juice. Whisk for just a few seconds until you reach a smooth batter. Over-mixing the batter will give you dense pancakes.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Add the grapeseed oil and spread it with a wrist motion.
Pour tablespoons of batter for each pancake, leaving space between them. Count about 1 minute: bubbles will appear on the surface.
Do not touch anything while the pancake is still sticking. Once it detaches on its own, flip it and continue for 1 minute on the other side. Transfer to a warm plate.
Wipe the pan between batches if residue sticks, keep the heat constant, and start again.
Peel the apple then cut it into thin slices. Plate the pancakes, drizzle with almond butter and maple syrup, dust with a veil of cinnamon.

title: Mini chocolate brioche logs
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the chocolate: too hot, it slips and doesn't hold; lukewarm, it coats the brioche with an even layer that sets in a few minutes.
ing: 2 tablespoons of decoration of your choice

ing.note: chocolate shavings, icing sugar, unsweetened cocoa

titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan and microwave. Preheated empty for one minute over very low heat and then removed from the heat, it retains a gentle and even warmth, without any hot spots: the chocolate melts without sticking or clumping (becoming grainy and dull). It then serves as a dipping bath, and its residual heat keeps the coating fluid while all the yule logs are coated.
steps: Remove the crust from the brioche slices on all four sides. Flatten each slice with a rolling pin, without crushing it: it should remain soft.
Spread a thin layer of spread over the entire surface, leaving one centimeter free on the edge opposite you.
Roll tightly, from the nearest edge to the free edge. Press the seam to seal it. Refrigerate while preparing the chocolate.

Preheat the empty titanium pan over very low heat for 1 minute. Remove it from the heat, add the chocolate broken into pieces, and stir with a spatula. Allow approximately 3 minutes: the chocolate should be smooth and glossy, never smoking. If the melting slows down, return the pan to very low heat for 20 seconds.
Place a log in the chocolate and roll it around to coat it. Lift it with a fork, let the excess drip off, and place it on a wire rack or a sheet of baking paper.
As soon as the coating begins to set, draw lengthwise grooves with the tines of a fork, to imitate bark.
Sprinkle with the chosen decoration before it sets completely, then let it firm up for 10 minutes at room temperature.

title: Roasted tomato and feta soup, cooked in a pan
intro: It all comes down to the roasting: the vegetables must brown in the pan before receiving the broth, otherwise the soup remains watery.
titane: Roasting and blending in the same utensil, on the stovetop, without going through the oven. Direct contact with titanium pushes the Maillard reaction (browning of sugars and proteins) faster and further than fan-assisted heat: the flavor concentrates, the soup gains depth.
steps: Cut the tomatoes, carrots and onions into pieces of similar size so they cook at the same rate. Peel the carrots and onions before cutting. Crush the garlic cloves with the flat of the blade.
Heat the titanium pan empty on medium-high heat for 3 minutes. Check the temperature: a drop of water should bead on the surface, not evaporate with a crackling sound.
Pour the oil, then spread the vegetables in a single layer. Let them brown without stirring for the first two minutes.
Place the block of feta whole in the center. Distribute salt, pepper, paprika and oregano over the vegetables only.

Cover. Lower to medium heat and let roast for 30 minutes, stirring the vegetables around the cheese from time to time. They are ready when they come away easily from the bottom and yield under the fork.
