Pour the broth into the pan. Blend with an immersion blender until smooth, then return to low heat for 2 minutes: the soup should coat the spoon.
Serve hot, with a toasted bread slice.

title: Lemon chicken and pan-fried potatoes
intro: Everything hinges on the first side: a skin seared without moving it, then a finish under lid which tenderizes the potatoes in the juices.
titane: Preheating the pan empty gives the chicken a crispier skin than the oven, because the contact is direct and dry. The lid then takes over from the oven: the trapped steam cooks the potatoes thoroughly without drying out the meat.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should bead on it without sizzling violently.
Meanwhile, combine the lemon juice, crushed garlic, oregano, paprika, salt and pepper in a bowl. Stir.
Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan. Place the thighs skin-side down and leave them untouched for 5 minutes.
Check: the meat will release easily when a crust has formed. Turn it over, cook for 2 minutes, then arrange the thighs on one side of the pan.
Arrange the potato wedges in the remaining space. Reduce the heat to medium and drizzle the lemon marinade over everything.
Brush the chicken with the spoon, then stir the potatoes to coat them.
Add the water. It will loosen the juices and create steam.
Cover, reduce heat to medium-low and cook for 30 minutes. Stir the potatoes every ten minutes. It's ready when a knife inserted into a wedge goes in easily and the chicken juices run clear.

title: Breaded Caprice des Dieux cheese, paprika-seasoned baby potatoes
intro: It all comes down to the double coating: it must form a shell strong enough to contain the cheese once it becomes liquid.

ing.note: which can withstand high temperatures) or oil

titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the fat. The panko will immediately sear on contact, forming a crust and sealing the breading before the cheese melts. The same pan, with the lid on, is then used to confit the new potatoes (gentle, prolonged cooking in fat): a single pan from start to finish.
steps: Beat the eggs in a shallow dish.
Pour the flour into a plate and whisk it for a few seconds: it should be perfectly loose, without clumps.
In a third bowl, mix together the breadcrumbs, panko, pepper, garlic powder and thyme.
Roll the cheese in flour, covering all sides and edges. Tap to remove excess.
Dip it in the beaten egg, then drain it for a few seconds over the dish.
Press it into the breadcrumb-panko mixture, pressing lightly to make the breadcrumbs adhere.
Dip the bun a second time in the egg, then in the breadcrumbs. This double layer is what will hold the melted cheese in. Refrigerate while you heat the pan.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then pour in the fat. It should ripple slightly on the surface.

Place the breaded cheese in the pan and leave it alone. It will release from the pan on its own once a crust has formed: that's the signal to flip it. Cook for approximately 8 minutes in total, browning each side and the slice.
Remove from the pan onto a warm plate and let rest while the potatoes cook.
Mix the baby potatoes with the butter, olive oil, paprika, garlic, salt and pepper.
Pour them into the still-hot pan, cover, and cook for 20 minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally. They are ready when a knife inserted into them goes in easily and the skin is golden brown.
Serve the cheese, cut in a cross shape, at the last moment, with the new potatoes around it.

title: Pretzel and chocolate fondant sandwich
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: it must become malleable, never liquid.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty and then reduced to the lowest setting, it provides immediate, low-temperature heat that you can turn off with a simple movement by removing it from the heat. You control the texture of the chocolate second by second, something a 100°C oven simply cannot do.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty, over low heat, for 2 minutes.
Lower the heat to the minimum. Arrange 12 mini pretzels flat in the warm pan, without overlapping them. Place a square of chocolate on each one.
Let the chocolate soften for 3 minutes. As soon as it's shiny, remove the pan from the heat: the residual heat is enough. The square should hold its shape and yield slightly to the touch.
Remove from heat and top each square with a second pretzel. Gently press to bring the chocolate up into the cavities.
Remove from the pan and place on a cold plate. Refrigerate for 1 hour to allow the chocolate to set.

title: Chocolate-apple skillet cake
intro: Three ingredients, no added sugar: everything relies on the apple, which provides the binding and sweetness in place of flour and butter.

ing.note: g, peeled and cut into pieces

titane: With the lid on, the titanium pan acts like a small oven: the heat circulates through the bottom and the trapped steam, allowing the batter to cook in the center without the edges drying out. Preheat it empty before greasing; the clarified butter film will then remain on the surface and the cake will release easily.
steps: Peel the apples and cut them into pieces.
Combine the apple pieces, eggs and cocoa in the blender bowl. Blend until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture, with no cocoa lumps or fruit fragments.
Heat the pan over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes without any fat. Then brush it with a thin layer of clarified butter, including the bottom and sides.
Pour the batter all at once into the center. Tilt the pan to spread it evenly to a regular thickness.
Cover, reduce to low heat and let cook for 18 minutes. The top should lose its glossy appearance and no longer stick to the finger, while the center should remain soft.

Turn off the heat while the center still trembles slightly: the residual heat finishes the cooking. Let cool for 5 minutes, the cake will detach from the sides on its own. Portion in the pan or turn out onto a board.

title: Clementine and chocolate shortbread cookies
intro: Shortbread cooked in a covered pan: the heat remains gentle, the butter doesn't burn, and the clementine zest retains its aroma.
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat, then lightly grease it. Cover during cooking: the hot air trapped under the lid works like an oven, while the surface in contact with the pan creates a golden base. Bake in small batches, six to eight cookies at most, to prevent the temperature from dropping with each batch.
steps: Plan ahead: the dough rests for 1 hour in the cold, allow time for this before baking.
Work the butter with both sugars and the tangerine zests until you obtain a homogeneous cream without grains.
Incorporate the egg then the tangerine juice. Mix briefly: the mixture may appear separated, it will come together in the next step.
Add the flour, cornstarch and salt. Mix just enough to bring the dough together, without overworking it (without developing the gluten, which would harden the shortbread).
Flatten the dough into a disk, cover with film and let rest for 1 hour in the cold.
Roll out to 5 mm between two sheets of parchment paper. Cut out with a cookie cutter and put the pieces back in the cold for 10 minutes while the pan heats.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat, then brush it very lightly with clarified butter.

Place the shortbreads without crowding them, cover and cook for 10 minutes over low heat at 170°C. The edges turn golden and the cookie releases on its own: that is the signal. Do not try to remove it before.
Transfer out of the pan onto a rack and let cool completely.
Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie, dip half of each shortbread into it, then let set on parchment paper.

title: Peach puff pastries with vanilla mascarpone cream
intro: It's all about moisture: well-drained peaches and puff pastry that stays dry underneath.
titane: Shape the dough directly in the cold pan, then bake it as is. The bare metal base absorbs heat more effectively than a baking sheet lined with parchment paper: the underside of the pastry dries quickly and develops its crispness. There's no transfer, so no risk of the braids losing their shape.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Drain the peach halves on absorbent paper, rounded side up, and let them dry while preparing the rest.
Work the mascarpone with the icing sugar and vanilla until you obtain a smooth, grain-free cream. Do not over-whip: the mascarpone will curdle (separate into grains and whey).
Cut out four discs from the dough, each about four centimeters larger in diameter than the peaches. Set aside the scraps and cut them into strips one centimeter wide.
Place the discs in the cold pan. In the center of each, place a heaped spoonful of cream, then a half peach, hollow side down.
Cross the strips of dough over the filling, two by two, and seal them around the edge of the disc by pinching lightly.
Brush the braids with egg yolk using a brush, scatter the flaked almonds, then the granulated sugar.

Cover, place the pan in the oven at 180°C (350°F) and bake for 20 minutes. The pastries are ready when the pastry is golden brown, firm to the touch, and easily pulls away from the bottom of the pan. Let them cool for five minutes before removing them from the pan.

title: Thin tarts with leeks and melted cheese
intro: It all comes down to searing the cut side of the leeks: that's what gives them their flavor, the puff pastry only covers them.

ing.note: cut into squares the diameter of the pan

titane: The preheated titanium pan, empty, handles a clean sear and allows the leeks to detach on their own once browned. It then proceeds to covered cooking, followed by a transfer under the grill, without any element changing containers.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes. It should be hot to the touch when held at a distance, without smoking.
Split the leeks lengthwise, rinse them between the leaves, then cut each half into two pieces. Pat them dry.
Cut the cheese into thick slices, rind included.
Pour the oil into the hot pan, add the vinegar, salt and pepper, and spread everything in a thin layer with a flick of the wrist.
Place the leeks cut-side down. Do not touch them for 3 minutes: they will detach on their own when they are colored and the juices (the golden deposits left by cooking) stick to the bottom.
Cover the leeks with the cheese slices, then place the square of puff pastry on top, making it fit snugly around the edge of the pan.
Brush the dough with egg yolk, then prick it with a fork in about ten places to let the steam escape.

Cover and reduce the heat to medium-low. Cook for 15 minutes: the leeks should be tender when pierced with a knife and the cheese should be melting around the edges. If the batter remains pale, place the pan (oven-safe handle) under the broiler for 3 minutes.
Remove from the pan by turning the tart upside down onto a board, leeks facing up. Slice in half and serve immediately.

title: Vegetarian shakshuka with scrambled tofu
intro: Everything happens in a single pan: a base of stewed vegetables on one side, seared tofu on the other, each cooked at its own temperature.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat it empty, then let the vegetables and tofu stick for a few seconds before moving them: this slight sticking is what gives them their charred notes. Use the same pan from the first onion to the plate.
steps: Place the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the oil: it should ripple on the surface without smoking.

Add the onion and bell pepper, tomato paste, smoked paprika, thyme, and salt. Reduce the heat to medium. Let it cook for 8 minutes, stirring only once the vegetables have loosened up from the bottom of the pan.
Add the tomatoes. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 12 minutes (until they reach a thick, jam-like consistency). The sauce is ready when it coats the back of a spoon.
Meanwhile, crumble the tofu by hand into irregular pieces. Mix it with the soy sauce, soy cream, turmeric, the second paprika, and pepper.
Push the sauce back onto one half of the pan. Add a drizzle of oil to the exposed surface, then spread the seasoned tofu on top.

Return to medium heat. Allow the tofu to absorb the heat for about 30 seconds before each stirring (stirring it immediately would prevent it from browning). Cook for 7 minutes: it should be golden brown and easily release from the pan.
Form four tofu nests on top of the sauce, directly in the pan. Serve without transferring.

title: Pan-fried golden hot dog
intro: It all comes down to the direct contact of the bread with the hot metal: a crispy base, while the lid melts the cheese.
titane: Preheat the pan empty, then cover it while cooking. The heat circulates under the lid and melts the cheese like in a convection oven, while the bottom of the bread toasts on contact with the titanium. Do not move the bread while it is still sticking; it will release on its own once golden brown.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush with a thin layer of grapeseed oil: it should barely smoke.

Open the bread without separating the two halves. Spread a layer of cheddar cheese on the bottom, place the sausage on top, and cover with the remaining cheese. The cheese will surround the sausage and melt on both sides.
Place the filled hot dog in the pan and cover. Cook for 5 minutes over medium-high heat. The bun is ready when it easily releases from the metal and the cheese has melted down the sides.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a cutting board. Add the pickle slices, ketchup, and mayonnaise, then the fried onions last so they remain crispy.

title: Crepe folded into quarters, chocolate, banana and kiwi
intro: It all comes down to a crepe that is thin enough and flexible enough to accommodate four different fillings without tearing when folded.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil or butter. This ensures the heat is evenly distributed across the entire surface, and the first crepe will turn out just as perfectly even as the fifth: no pale areas in the center, no burnt edges, and no sticking points. This evenness is what allows for a clean fold.
steps: Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the clarified butter and spread it by tilting the pan. The layer should be barely visible.
Pour the ladleful of batter into the center and twist your wrist to spread it. Let it cook for 2 minutes without touching it, until the edges pull away from the sides.
Turn over sharply and cook the second side for 1 minute 30 seconds, until lightly browned.
Remove (transfer from the pan) onto a flat plate.
Make a cut in the crepe from the center to the edge, in a single straight cut. This will divide it into four quarters.
Spread the spread on the first quarter.
Arrange the banana slices on the second layer, overlapping them.
Place the whipped cream on the third layer, without packing it down.
Arrange the kiwi slices on top.
Fold the pastry over, starting from the cut, until you have a closed triangle. Serve immediately, before the whipped cream falls out.

title: Homemade bread in a titanium pan
intro: No robot, no long kneading: everything depends on the cold rise and the heat accumulated by the pan, which replaces the cast iron casserole dish.
ing: Extra flour for the work surface and dusting
titane: Preheat the empty pan in the oven to 240°C (475°F), covered with its dome. The metal dome absorbs the heat and releases it suddenly under the dough: this thermal shock makes the bread rise and the crust develop. The dome traps the steam released by the dough for the first thirty minutes, just like a Dutch oven lid. Without it, the crust sets too quickly and the bread remains flat.
steps: Plan ahead: the dough rises for 3 hours at room temperature and then overnight in the refrigerator, start the day before.

Pour the water into a large bowl, add the yeast, then the flour and salt. Mix by hand, bringing the edges of the dough towards the centre, until no dry flour remains. The dough should be sticky and uniform: this is intentional, do not add more flour.
Cover the bowl with cling film or a tea towel. Leave to rise for 3 hours at room temperature.
Place the bowl in the refrigerator and allow the slow rise to proceed overnight, that is 12 hours.

Flour the work surface generously. Turn out the dough (deflate it by turning it out of the bowl to release the gas). Stretch one edge, fold it towards the centre, and repeat all the way around until a tight ball forms.
Place the ball, seam side down, on a sheet of baking paper. Cover with a tea towel and leave to relax for 45 minutes at room temperature.
Meanwhile, place the empty titanium pan in the oven, covered with a metal cloche or an oven-safe stainless steel mixing bowl. Preheat the whole to 240 °C.
Dust the ball with flour. Score it (make incisions on the surface with a very sharp blade, angled at 45°) according to your choice of pattern, 1 cm deep.
Remove the hot pan. Place the dough on it with its baking paper, cover with the cloche and bake for 15 minutes at 240 °C.
Lower to 230 °C and continue for 15 minutes, still covered.
Remove the cloche and continue for 15 minutes at 230 °C, until the crust takes on a mahogany colour and sounds hollow when the bottom is tapped.
Turn out (transfer from the cooking vessel) onto a board or a rack. Wait until the bread is lukewarm before slicing: the crumb continues to set as it cools.

title: Vegetable blinis, lemon-dill cashew cream cheese
intro: It all comes down to two things: cashews soaked long enough for the cream cheese to be perfectly smooth, and a hot pan before the first ladleful of batter.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
plant-based salmon with lemon zest and dill
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding any oil. A drop of water sprinkled onto the pan should sizzle and roll off. At this temperature, the blini will form a crust in seconds and release easily; only flip it when it's ready. Wipe the surface with paper towels between batches to ensure even cooking.
steps: Plan ahead: cashews soak for at least 1 hour; allow this time before starting.
Cover the cashews with hot water and let soak for at least 1 hour. They should crush easily between two fingers.
Drain and rinse them. Blend them with the soy yogurt, lemon juice and salt until you obtain a smooth cream without grittiness. Scrape the sides of the bowl once or twice as you go.
Finely chop the dill and fold it in with a spatula. Keep chilled while you cook the blinis: the cream will firm up slightly.
Mix the flour, salt and bicarbonate of soda in a bowl.
Pour the soy yogurt and plant-based milk onto the dry ingredients. Mix just enough so no dry flour remains. The batter should be thick and fall heavily from the spoon.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.
Pour a thin stream of grapeseed oil, spread it over the entire surface, then drop small spoonfuls of batter, spacing them apart. Increase to high heat.
Let sit for 1 minute without touching. Bubbles break through the surface, the edges lose shine, the blini releases on its own: flip it and cook for another minute.
Transfer onto a rack rather than a plate, so that steam does not soften the crust. Wipe the pan and repeat.
Lightly toast the bagels, open them, spread the cashew cream cheese on both sides and top with the plant-based salmon with lemon zest and dill.
Serve the warm blinis with the remaining cashew cream cheese and plant-based salmon with pink peppercorns.

title: Vanilla chestnut cream
intro: Everything depends on the temperature of the syrup: 103°C, not one degree more, otherwise the cream will solidify into a paste when it cools.

ing.note: plus a little hot water to adjust

titane: The pan comes into play when it's time to make the syrup. Preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes, it heats up quickly, and its uncoated surface absorbs the hot sugar without flinching. Stay close: the final degrees arrive in just a few seconds. Use a metal spatula, no special precautions needed.
steps: Make a slit in each chestnut with a knife on the rounded side, going through the shell without cutting into the flesh.
Place them in a large pot of boiling water and cook for 15 minutes. The large volume of water will be held in place by the pot.
Drain. Peel while the chestnuts are still warm: the shell and inner skin will come off together. Once cooled, they will stick.
Return the peeled fruit to the saucepan, cover with water and simmer for 30 minutes. They should be very soft and easily mashed with a finger.
Drain and blend into a smooth puree. Set aside.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the sugar, water, and the split and scraped vanilla pod (seeds and pod). Bring to a boil and cook until it reaches 103°C on a thermometer: the syrup should be smooth and runny between the fingers of a spoon.
Remove the pod. Add the chestnut puree to the boiling syrup and cook for 10 minutes over medium heat, stirring often with a metal spatula to prevent the bottom from sticking.
Blend the mixture until it reaches a perfectly smooth texture.
If the cream seems too thick, loosen it (soften it with a liquid) with a little warm water, spoonful by spoonful.
Fill the jars while still hot, close them and turn them upside down until completely cool.

title: Hazelnut and crunchy praline spread
intro: It all comes down to the blender: the hazelnut puree must become perfectly fluid before meeting the chocolate, otherwise the dough will remain sandy.
titane: The pan, filled with 2 cm of water, acts as a bain-marie (gentle cooking with steam and hot water, without direct contact with the flame). Its rapid and even heat conduction warms the water without creating hot spots: the chocolate melts slowly, without graining or sticking to the bottom of the pan.
steps: Blend the hazelnuts in pulses, then continuously. The powder compacts, forms a ball, then loosens into a puree. Scrape the sides regularly and continue until you reach a perfectly smooth texture. This takes several minutes: the first grainy phase is normal.
Pour 2 cm of water into the pan. Place a heat-resistant container with the chocolate broken into pieces on top. Heat over low heat for approximately 5 minutes, stirring, until completely melted.
Pour the melted chocolate over the hazelnut puree. Blend again until you obtain a shiny and homogeneous mass.
Fold in the praline with a spatula (flexible scraper), without blending, to preserve the crunch.
Transfer to a clean and dry jar. Let cool to room temperature before closing.

title: Ricotta, peach and apricot cake
intro: A cake with little or no flour, whose consistency depends entirely on the right amount of starch: too little, the mixture weeps; too much, it becomes elastic.
ing: Finely grated zest of a lime
titane: The frying pan acts as a mold. Coat it with clarified butter after gently heating it, pour in the mixture, and bake without transferring anything. The metal conducts heat better than a thin-walled mold: the edges brown more, while the center remains creamy.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170 °C.
In a bowl, work the drained ricotta with the caster sugar until the mixture becomes smooth and creamy.
Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well between each addition. Do not incorporate unnecessary air: this batter should not rise.
Flavour with the lime zest and vanilla, then sift the potato starch over and mix until all lumps disappear.

Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 minutes over a low to medium heat. Remove from the heat and brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter (melted butter freed from its whey, which withstands heat better).
Pour the batter into the still-warm pan and smooth the surface.
Arrange the peach and apricot slices flat, slightly pressed into the cream.
Sprinkle with cane sugar, then scatter flaked almonds over.
Bake for approximately 52 minutes. The surface should be golden and the centre firm to the touch, with no liquid wobble.
Leave to cool completely in the pan before turning out: the texture tightens as it cools and the cake then holds together as one block.

title: Potato pancakes with a vegan mozzarella center
intro: It's all about the contrast: a dry, golden crust, a still creamy interior, and mozzarella that melts without escaping.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, before adding any oil or butter. The heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without creating a cold spot: the surface of the pancake seals upon contact, and this is what holds the cheese inside. Don't touch it after that. The pancake will release on its own once the crust has formed—if you force it with a spatula, you'll tear the pancake open.
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut them into even cubes. Cook them in a saucepan of boiling salted water for about 15 minutes: a knife tip should slide in without resistance.
Drain thoroughly, then transfer to a bowl. Let the steam escape for a minute: overly wet purée will not hold its shape.
Mash with a fork or potato masher. Stir in the cornstarch, salt, and pepper. Work until you obtain a smooth, pliable dough that no longer sticks to your fingers.

Cut the vegan mozzarella into 8 slices. Divide the dough into 8 portions. Flatten each portion in the palm of your hand, place a slice in the center, fold the dough around it, then flatten again into a 2 cm disc. Check that no cracks appear on the edges.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. A drop of water should sizzle and form a bead on the surface. Then pour in the grapeseed oil.

Place the pancakes loosely on the griddle. Cook for 4 minutes without moving them. When they release easily from the pan, flip them over and cook for another 4 minutes. Serve immediately; the center will set as it cools.

title: Seared potatoes, smoked salmon and herb cream
intro: It's all about the skin: a good sear before the oven, and it stays crispy until serving.
titane: The titanium pan withstands preheating empty and then goes straight into the oven without a problem. The potatoes brown over the flame, finish cooking in the same spot, and you don't dirty anything else.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Wash the potatoes, dry them thoroughly, and pierce them all over with a fork: without these vents, they will burst in the heat.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently, without smoking.

Sear the whole potatoes (sear: brown quickly over high heat to form a crust) for about 8 minutes, rolling them on all sides. Don't force them: when a side is ready, it will easily detach from the bottom.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 40 minutes. It's cooked through when a knife blade pierces it without resistance.
Meanwhile, slice half of the salmon into thin strips. Mix them with the heavy cream and Greek yogurt, add the chopped dill and chives, season lightly with salt and pepper.
Split the potatoes in half lengthwise. Lightly mash the flesh with a fork to make room for the filling, then fill generously.
Arrange the remaining salmon in soft folds on top, and finish with chives. Serve immediately, while the skin is still crispy.

title: Pumpkin, oat and chocolate cookies
intro: Raw grated pumpkin provides moisture: it's what keeps the center tender when the pan browns the bottom.

ing.note: g, plus a handle for finishing

titane: The covered pan acts as an oven. The heat rises evenly, the lid directs the steam back onto the tops of the cookies, keeping the centers soft while the bases caramelize. There's only one way to turn them: the cookie should release easily. As long as it sticks, it's not ready. As soon as it slides, a flick of the wrist is all it takes.
steps: Cream the softened butter with both sugars using a whisk (work until the mixture becomes pale and smooth).
Add the egg and vanilla. Whisk briefly until the batter becomes homogeneous again.
Pour in the flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon. Mix without overworking, then add the oat flakes.
Add the finely grated butternut squash and chocolate chips. Mix with a spatula until evenly distributed.
Shape medium-sized balls and flatten them slightly so they cook flat. Place a few chocolate chips on top.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the fat, wait until it steams, then wipe off the excess with paper towels.
Arrange the cookies in a single layer, well spaced apart: the dough will spread. Work in several batches rather than overloading the pan.
Cover. Lower to medium-low heat and let cook for 10 minutes. The base should be golden and the edges beginning to set.
Check that a cookie releases on its own, flip it with a flick of the wrist. Cover and continue for 5 minutes.
Transfer off the pan onto a wire rack. While hot they are very fragile; they firm up as they cool.

title: Pan-fried tuna cakes
intro: It all comes down to the crust: a really hot pan, a pancake that isn't touched, and the breadcrumbs become a golden shell instead of a stuck-on deposit.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat even when the cold patties are added. This allows you to do everything in one pan: first, you sweat the onion (cook it without browning), then you sear the patties. Wipe the pan clean between the two, otherwise the onion bits will burn and leave marks on the crust.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should sizzle clearly on contact.
Pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil, add the onion and garlic. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally: the onion should become translucent, without taking on any color.
Remove the onion and garlic from the pan and place them in a bowl. Wipe the pan clean with paper towels; it can be reused as is.
In a bowl, crack the eggs, add the lemon juice, breadcrumbs, Parmesan cheese and chives. Mix until well combined.
Incorporate the flaked tuna. Season with salt and pepper, and work with a fork without mashing: the mixture should hold together but remain supple.
Form eight patties about 2 cm thick by pressing them between your palms. If they are uniform, they will all cook at the same rate.

Return the pan to medium-high heat with a drizzle of oil. Place the patties in the pan, leaving space between them. Do not move them: after 4 to 5 minutes, they will release on their own. Flip them over and cook for another 4 to 5 minutes, until both sides are golden brown.

title: Golden tofu, tomato sauce and coconut
intro: It all comes down to the tofu crust: a really hot pan, cubes that aren't touched, and the sauce that comes afterwards in the same pan.
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains heat when the cold cubes arrive: a crust forms on its own and the tofu releases easily. The sauce then remains below 500 ml of total liquid, allowing you to simmer directly in the covered pan, without transferring it to a saucepan.
steps: Drain the tofu, then cut it into 2 cm cubes. Place them in a bowl and dust with cornstarch, turmeric and half a teaspoon of salt. Mix by hand to coat each side.
Preheat the titanium pan empty over high heat for 3 minutes. It is ready when it is smoking lightly.
Pour the grapeseed oil, then place the cubes in a single layer. Do not move them for 5 minutes: they will detach on their own once the crust has formed. Turn them over to brown a second side.

Add the tomato pulp, coconut cream, curry paste, the remaining salt and the margarine. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes over medium heat. The sauce is ready when it coats the back of a spoon (it leaves a thin layer that is clearly separated by a finger stroke).
Meanwhile, cook the rice and green beans separately. Serve the tofu coated with sauce, rice and beans on the side.

title: Tube of chocolate chips
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: too hot it burns, too thick it never reaches the bottom of the tube.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Preheated empty for two minutes over very low heat, it distributes heat evenly across its entire surface: the chocolate melts without hot spots, therefore without graining (separating into dry lumps). Only one container is needed, no pot of water, no microwave.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty, over very low heat, for 2 minutes. The surface should be lukewarm, never smoking.

Turn off the heat or keep it on low. Pour the chocolate and sunflower oil into the pan. Stir continuously with a spatula for about 3 minutes, until you obtain a perfectly smooth and fluid mixture that flows in a ribbon from the spatula.
Place the tube of chips upright, still full, on a stable surface. Pour the melted chocolate over the top in several stages, allowing it to settle between each addition.
Close the lid. Shake the tube, turn it upside down, lay it on its side, roll it: the chocolate should coat each chip completely. Allow about a minute for this process.
Place the tube upright in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours. The chocolate should be firm and dry to the touch, without leaving any residue on your finger.
Cut the cardboard tube lengthwise with a utility knife and remove the block. Transfer it to your work surface and slice it into 1-centimeter rounds with a serrated knife to reveal the layers.

title: Crispy feta bites
intro: It's all about the contrast: a tight and crispy filo pastry around a feta that remains melting, so you sear it first, then finish it in the oven.
titane: The preheated titanium pan browns the bottoms of the bites before they go in the oven. A single piece of equipment, no muffin tin required: the crust forms on direct contact, then browns in the convection oven. Wait until the bite releases easily before turning it over; this is the sign that the crust is set.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the empty titanium pan over medium heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Lay a sheet of filo pastry on your work surface and brush it with melted butter. Cover with a second sheet, brush again with butter, and continue until all the sheets are stacked.
Cut the feta into even sticks, the same length as the rectangle of dough.
Arrange the sticks along the long edge closest to you, leaving a two-centimeter margin. Sprinkle with oregano and chili pepper.
Roll the dough over the filling, tightening with each turn, so that the roll is dense and the feta doesn't move.
Cut the roll into 11 equal-thickness sections.
Pour the oil into the hot pan. Place the pastries flat, cut-side down, spaced apart: a crowded pan creates steam, not a crust.
Sear (brown quickly in the hot pan) for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without touching it. Meanwhile, brush the visible sides with melted butter and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Flip each bite as soon as it releases itself. Bake the pan as is for 15 minutes, until the pastry is golden brown and crispy all around.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a wire rack. Drizzle with honey before serving.

title: Mushroom and spinach lasagna, assembled in a pan
intro: It all depends on the water content of the mushrooms: if you let it evaporate before assembling, the layers hold together and the béchamel sauce remains creamy.
ing: Button mushrooms or mixed forest mushrooms, sliced
Grated cheese, such as Comté or Emmental
titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding the fat. The surface heats up evenly, the mushrooms sear instead of boiling, and their juices concentrate. Use the same pan for the béchamel sauce, assembly, and gratin: go straight from the stovetop to the oven, without transferring.
steps: Heat the titanium pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. It should be thoroughly hot throughout.
Pour in the clarified butter. Sweat (cook without browning to release the water) the sliced onion and chopped garlic for 5 minutes, until they become translucent.

Add the mushrooms and parsley, season with salt and pepper. Let it cook for 10 minutes without stirring: only stir once the slices have started to pull away from the bottom of the pan on their own. The liquid should have evaporated.
Throw the spinach shoots on top and mix for 2 minutes, until they wilt.
Remove the filling from the pan and place it on a plate. Wipe the pan with paper towels; any residue will burn in the béchamel sauce.

Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). In a pan, melt 80g of butter, then sprinkle in the flour and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to make a roux. Gradually whisk in the milk. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Let it thicken for about 8 minutes; the sauce should coat the back of a spoon.

Pour two-thirds of the béchamel sauce into a bowl. Keep a thin layer of it at the bottom of the buttered pan, place lasagna sheets on top, spread with the filling, cover with béchamel sauce, and sprinkle with grated cheese and Parmesan. Repeat until all the ingredients are used, packing the layers tightly.

Finish with béchamel sauce, grated cheese, and Parmesan. Bake the pan as is for 40 minutes at 180°C (350°F), until golden brown and bubbly on top. Let it rest for 10 minutes before cutting: the layers will hold together.

title: Tahini banana bread
intro: Everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas: heavily speckled, almost black, they provide the sugar and softness that neither egg nor butter can compensate for here.
ing: neutral oil or vegetable margarine for the pan
titane: The frying pan replaces the cake tin and goes straight into the oven. Its thin walls conduct the batter quickly and evenly: the crumb rises without delay, and the edges develop a crisper crust than in a traditional pan. Grease the pan generously before pouring, making sure to cover the corners between the base and sides.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C with fan setting.
Lightly oil a 24 cm titanium pan, or line it (cover it with parchment paper) leaving two tabs overhanging for unmolding.
Peel the bananas, then blend them with the soy yogurt, tahini and brown sugar until you obtain a mixture (basic mix) that is perfectly smooth, without any banana strands.
Pour in the flour, yeast and salt. Mix with a spatula, lifting the batter, just enough so no dry flour remains. Overmixed batter gives a dense crumb.
Transfer to the pan, smooth the surface, then place in the oven for 50 minutes.
Check for doneness: the surface should be golden and cracked along the length, and a knife blade inserted in the center should come out dry. Extend for 5 minutes if it still sticks.
Let cool for 10 minutes in the pan before unmolding onto a cooling rack. The banana bread slices better once completely cooled.

title: Breaded chicken with pesto, arugula and mozzarella
intro: It all comes down to the double breading and the dry searing which sets it before baking: the crust remains dry and crisp instead of softening under the filling.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil or butter. The breading sets immediately, detaches easily once a crust has formed, and the same pan goes straight from the oven to the table. All in one piece, from countertop to serving.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Pat the chicken fillets dry. Season them on both sides with paprika, garlic powder, salt and pepper.
Beat the eggs with the pesto in a shallow bowl. Mix the breadcrumbs and panko in a second bowl.
Coat each fillet in egg and then breadcrumbs: first with pesto egg, then with a breadcrumb-panko mixture. Repeat this process a second time; the double layer creates a thicker, firmer crust.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil; it should simmer gently.
Place the fillets in the pan and sear for 3 minutes without touching them. They will release easily from the pan once a crust has formed.
Turn them over and grab the second side, 3 minutes, same marker.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 14 minutes. The juices should run clear when pierced with a knife.

Remove the pan from the refrigerator. Let it rest for 2 minutes, then top directly with arugula, halved cherry tomatoes, mini mozzarella balls, and Parmesan shavings. Drizzle with olive oil and a touch of balsamic glaze. Serve in the pan.

title: Chocolate and peach mousse
intro: Only two ingredients, so it all comes down to the blending time of the peaches: it's the air incorporated there that makes the foam, not the eggs.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the pan, without a double boiler. Use very low heat; do not preheat the pan: the fat content of the chocolate is sufficient. The even distribution of titanium eliminates hot spots that cause graininess (separation into dry lumps). Stir continuously and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth.
steps: Blend the drained peaches alone for at least 3 minutes. The purée should become paler and puff up: that is the air entering.
Add the syrup, then blend again for 30 seconds. The texture becomes lighter and takes on more body.
Place the chocolate in a cold pan. Heat over very low heat, stirring constantly, for about 3 minutes, until you obtain a smooth, glossy mass with no lumps. Remove from heat immediately.

Pour the melted chocolate over the peach purée and blend for 10 seconds, no longer, just long enough to emulsify (bind the fat and water into a homogeneous mass). The mousse thickens before your eyes.
Divide among four ramekins and refrigerate for 2 hours.

title: Chocolate reindeer
intro: It all comes down to the water temperature: if it's too hot, the chocolate will seize (absorb moisture and become grainy) and will no longer shine.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a bain-marie. Its flat and wide base heats the water evenly over low heat, without a hot spot under the bowl: the chocolate melts regularly, from the edge to the center, and remains smooth.
steps: Plan ahead: the chocolate needs 3 hours in the refrigerator, plan this time before serving.
Pour a shallow amount of water into the titanium pan, about 1 cm deep. Heat over low heat for 2 minutes: the water should barely simmer, never boil.
Chop the chocolate into regular pieces. Place it with the coconut oil in a heat-resistant bowl, set over the pan. The bottom of the bowl does not touch the water.
Stir with a spoon until the mixture is smooth and fluid, about 5 minutes. Remove the bowl as soon as the last pieces disappear: residual heat finishes the work.
Form discs of 5 to 6 cm on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, one spoonful per disc. A piping bag gives cleaner edges.
Decorate immediately, while the chocolate is still pliable: two mini pretzels inserted at the top for antlers, two sugar eyes, one red pearl for the nose.
Refrigerate for 3 hours, until the chocolate is firm and releases easily from the paper. Store in a cool place in an airtight container.

title: Breaded burrata, black tomatoes and olives
intro: It's all about the contrast: a dry, golden crust around a still-runny center, therefore a very short cooking time on a really hot pan.
titane: The preheated titanium pan, used empty, replaces the deep fryer. A drizzle of oil is all it takes for the panko to brown in a few dozen seconds per side. The heat remains on the surface, preventing the center of the burrata from liquefying.
steps: Dice the tomatoes into small cubes, kept at room temperature (cold mutes their flavor). Lightly salt, add the olives whole or roughly crushed. Set aside.
Check that the burrata is properly sealed. Dry it with paper towels.
Roll the burrata in flour, tap to remove excess, dip it in beaten egg, then in panko. Press the breadcrumbs with your fingertips to coat each side, without crushing the ball.
Preheat the titanium pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place the breaded burrata. Do not touch it again. After about 1 minute, the coating browns and releases from the bottom on its own: that is the signal.

Turn it over with a thin spatula, reduce to moderate heat and continue face by face, about 1 minute each time, until uniformly golden brown. Remove from the pan (take it out of the pan to stop cooking) immediately.
Spread the tomatoes and olives in a shallow bowl, place the burrata on top. Add hand-torn basil, a drizzle of olive oil, and a turn of the pepper mill.

title: Soft cake with nectarines, raspberries and lemon
intro: Everything happens at the moment the powders meet the appliance: mix as little as possible, otherwise the crumb will tighten and lose its softness.
titane: The pan acts as a mold. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat, butter it, pour in the batter, and bake: no need to transfer the cake, and the thin rim will release it in one easy motion once cooled. Before proceeding, make sure the handle is oven-safe.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Combine the flour, almond flour and baking powder in a bowl. Mix together dry ingredients.
In a second bowl, whisk the eggs and sugar vigorously until the mixture turns pale. Add the lemon zest, melted butter, and then the yogurt. Mix until smooth.
Incorporate the powders all at once. Mix just until the lumps disappear, no more.
Cut the nectarines into thick wedges, then cut each wedge in half. Add them to the batter along with the raspberries. Gently fold in with a spatula.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat. Grease it with clarified butter, bottom and sides.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and smooth the surface.
Bake for 45 minutes at 180°C. The center should be set and a knife inserted into the center should come out dry.
Let it cool in the pan, then transfer (out of the cooking container) to a wire rack before serving.

title: Pan-fried salmon, green beans and mushrooms
intro: Everything hinges on the first side of the salmon: a really hot pan, and you don't touch anything else.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven. It can withstand preheating empty, gives the salmon a golden crust in four minutes, then transforms into a casserole dish as soon as the lid is put on: fish and vegetables end up together, simmered, without drying out.
steps: Bring a small saucepan of salted water to a boil. Plunge the green beans into the boiling water for 3 to 4 minutes: they should be tender but still firm. Drain and set aside.
In a bowl, combine the garlic powder, mustard, honey, and olive oil. Season with salt and pepper, and whisk until smooth.
Coat the salmon fillets on all sides with this preparation.
Place the empty titanium pan over high heat. Let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour the grapeseed oil over the fish, then place the fillets flesh-side down. Let them sear for 3 to 4 minutes without moving them: when a crust has formed, the fish will detach itself.
Turn the steaks over. Distribute the sliced mushrooms and green beans all around, then reduce the heat to medium.
Cover and cook for about 6 minutes. The salmon is ready when its flesh flakes easily under the tip of a knife and the mushrooms have released and reduced their water.

title: Pan-fried pizza burger
intro: It all comes down to the base: a pastry that is seared in the first minute remains crispy despite a heavy and moist filling.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and powerfully. It sets the bottom of the dough before the juices from the steaks and sauce make it soggy. Then, the lid is placed on to steam the dough through, and finally, the same pan is placed under the broiler to brown the top. All in one pan, from countertop to plate.
steps: Generously flour your work surface, pizza dough sticks easily. Spread it out into a regular disc.

In the center, stack the following in order: a slice of cheddar cheese, a steak, caramelized onions, pickles, sauce, tomato slices, the second steak, and the second slice of cheddar cheese. Leave a wide margin all around.
Fold the dough over the filling, pinch the edges at the top, and fold the whole thing over, seam side down. You now have a large, well-sealed bun.
Brush the top with egg yolk, sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the fat: it should simmer gently, without smoking.
Gently place the dough ball, seam side down. Cook for 3 minutes over medium-high heat, without touching it. The dough is cooked when it pulls away from the bottom of the pan on its own.
Cover, reduce heat to low-medium and let it cook for 12 minutes. The steam cooks the pastry through and melts the cheddar cheese.
Remove the lid, place the pan under the grill at 200°C for 4 minutes, until the surface and sesame are golden brown.
Let it rest for 5 minutes before cutting, otherwise the filling will escape. Slice in half or into quarters.

title: Grilled tofu, butternut squash and mushroom terrine sandwich
intro: It all comes down to the regularity of the slices and patience: butternut, tofu and bread go into the same pan, one after the other, without ever being turned over before the time.
titane: The pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes, it sears the butternut squash slices, covered: the surface caramelizes while the trapped steam keeps the center moist. Then it's used for the tofu, followed by the grilled sandwich. Between each batch, wipe it with paper towels: any sugars from the syrup left at the bottom would burn on the next batch.
steps: Cut the butternut squash into very thin slices, 3 to 4 mm, as regular as possible. Coat them with a tablespoon of oil, salt, pepper, add smoked paprika and a tablespoon of syrup.
Heat the pan empty, high heat, 2 to 3 minutes: it is ready when a very slight wisp of smoke rises.

Lay the butternut squash slices flat, without overlapping them. Cover and lower to medium-high heat. Leave for about 15 minutes, turning only once, when the slices detach by themselves from the bottom. They should be tender and golden.
Transfer the butternut squash to a plate and wipe the pan.
Pat the tofu dry with paper towels, then cut it into thin slices. Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then pour the remaining oil: it ripples when it reaches temperature.

Place the tofu in a single layer. Do not touch anything for 4 to 5 minutes, until the slices detach by themselves. Turn, pour the soy sauce and a tablespoon of syrup, continue until the liquid coats and the tofu is caramelized. Allow 10 minutes in total. Set aside and wipe the pan again.
Spread two slices of bread with mushroom terrine. Distribute the tofu, then the butternut squash, the spinach shoots and a drizzle of syrup. Close.
Toast the sandwiches in the hot pan, medium heat, 1 minute per side, pressing lightly with a spatula. Cut in half and serve immediately.

title: Water crepes
intro: Without milk, the dough becomes finer and cleaner in the mouth: it all depends on the fluidity of the mixture and the heat of the pan.

ing.note: a drip for preheating, then between

titane: Titanium heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. Preheat the pan empty, then oil it: the first pancake is already ready. Don't touch it while it's cooking. It will detach itself from the edges, then from the center. That's the signal to flip it with a quick flick of the wrist.
steps: In a bowl, combine the lukewarm water, eggs and vanilla sugar. Whisk until you obtain a smooth liquid.
Gradually add the flour, a little at a time, whisking between each addition. The batter should remain smooth, without lumps.
Finish by gently whisking in the sparkling water. It lightens the batter: don't add it earlier, or the bubbles will be lost.
Heat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add a drizzle of grapeseed oil and spread it by tilting the pan.
Pour a ladleful of batter, twist your wrist to spread it into a thin layer. Let it cook for about 1 minute without touching it, until the pancake releases itself from the bottom.

Flip the pancake over with a decisive movement and cook for a few seconds on the other side. Remove it (transfer it to a plate) and repeat, wiping the pan between pancakes with a paper towel soaked in oil.

title: Basil salt
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the basil must dry out, never cook, otherwise the green turns khaki and the aroma disappears with the steam.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the two hours of sun-drying. Its heat is distributed quickly and without hot spots: over very low heat, the basil's moisture evaporates in ten minutes while the color retains its vibrancy. No oil is needed; the pan remains bare.
steps: Strip the leaves from the basil bunch.
Blend the basil leaves with salt until you obtain a homogeneous mixture that is green and slightly damp. The salt acts as an abrasive: it tears the leaves and releases their oils.
Spread the mixture in a thin layer in the cold titanium pan, without any fat. A thick layer would dry on the surface and remain damp underneath.
Place on very low heat. Stir with a spatula every twenty seconds, bringing the salt from the edges to the center. Allow 10 minutes.

Stop when the mixture is crumbly and the basil crumbles between your fingers. At the end of the drying process, do not leave the pan unattended: the salt heats up quickly and the basil can burn in a few seconds.
Transfer to a cold plate and let cool completely before putting in an airtight jar.

intro:
# Smoked Salmon Puff Pastry Crown

---
title: "Smoked Salmon Puff Pastry Crown"
servings: 6
prep_time_min: 5
cook_time_min: 20
theme_candidates:

- quotidien-des-chefs

- art-de-la-saisie
needs_review: true
---

It all comes down to the sealing of the two layers of pastry: a well-sealed crown rises straight and cuts without collapsing.
ing: Fresh cheese with garlic and herbs
The zest of half an untreated yellow lemon
titane: Assemble the pastry directly in the cold pan, then place the pan in the oven as is. No need to transfer it to a baking sheet or use parchment paper: the base remains sealed and the puff pastry won't tear when you put it in the oven. The pan can withstand 180°C without any special precautions.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Unroll the first roll of puff pastry and place it in the cold titanium pan, letting it adhere to the bottom.
Spread the cream cheese in an even layer, leaving a two-centimeter border. Leave this margin bare: it will be used to seal.
Arrange the smoked salmon slices in a single layer. Grate lemon zest over the top.
Place the second roll of dough. Press all around the edge with your fingertips to seal the two layers of dough, then lightly roll over with a rolling pin to remove air and even out the surface.
Using a star-shaped cutter, cut shapes from the top layer without cutting through the disc underneath. Work from the center outwards, keeping the cuts tight.
Remove the scraps around the stars. Replace the stars on the base disc, offset from each other, so as to draw a regular ring.
Beat the egg yolk with a teaspoon of water and brush the stars with the mixture. Sprinkle with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake the pan uncovered for 20 minutes. The wreath is ready when the dough has risen, browned evenly, and the tips of the stars crackle under your finger.
Let it cool for 5 minutes in the pan before serving: the puff pastry will firm up and detach cleanly.

title: Chocolate bars with roasted nuts
intro: It all comes down to roasting: dry-heated nuts develop a roasted bitterness that stands up to chocolate.

ing.note: almonds, pistachios, hazelnuts or cashews, depending

titane: The pan serves two purposes. First, dry, to toast the nuts, monitoring the color by eye, second by second. Then, off the heat, the residual heat in the metal melts the chocolate gently. No double boiler, no additional container.
steps: Plan ahead: the bar sets in the refrigerator for 45 minutes before it can be broken.
Place the empty titanium pan on medium-high heat. Let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes: a drop of water should dance across it before evaporating.
Pour the nuts in a single layer. Toss them for 4 minutes, stirring often. They should brown lightly and become fragrant. As soon as the aroma turns toasted, you are there.

Remove the pan from the heat. Break the chocolate into pieces and scatter them over the hot nuts. Wait one minute, then mix with a spatula for 2 minutes: the residual heat from the metal is enough to smooth everything.
Pour onto a sheet of baking paper. Spread in a layer approximately 1 cm thick and even. Sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Refrigerate for 45 minutes, until the mixture is firm and matte. Then break into irregular shards by hand.

title: Burrata, roasted asparagus and lemon
intro: It all comes down to the colouring of the asparagus: a really hot pan, and then you don't touch it anymore.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty over high heat, it gives the asparagus a crisp sear on the surface while keeping the center firm. Once the vegetables are pushed to the side, the same still-hot pan is all you need to toast the pine nuts (dry-roast them without oil). Just one pan, no other utensils required.
steps: Remove the burratas from the refrigerator and let them come to room temperature while you cook them. Snap off the fibrous ends of the asparagus, rinse them, and dry them thoroughly.
Zest the lemon directly over the asparagus. Add the olive oil, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Mix by hand to coat each stalk.
Heat the titanium pan empty, over high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. It is ready when a wisp of smoke escapes from it.

Arrange the asparagus in a single layer. Don't move them: they will stick at first, then detach on their own when browned. Turn them over and continue cooking over medium heat, turning them occasionally, for a total of 10 minutes. They should be golden brown on all sides and tender when pierced with a knife.

Push the asparagus to one side of the pan. Pour the pine nuts into the open space and toast them for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, stirring, until golden. Watch them carefully: they can go from golden to burnt in seconds. Remove them from the pan as soon as they are ready.

Place a burrata on each plate and slice it open with a knife. Arrange the asparagus around it, sprinkle with pine nuts, and drizzle with the cooking oil remaining in the pan, infused with the aroma of garlic and lemon. Add a final twist of zest and a grind of pepper, then serve immediately.

title: Nougat with pistachios and roasted dried fruit
intro: It all comes down to the thermometer: two degrees too high and the nougat becomes brittle, two degrees too low and it remains sticky.
titane: One pan for everything: it dry-roasts the nuts, then cooks the honey, and finally the sugar syrup after a quick wipe with a paper towel. The heat rises faster than in a saucepan, so the thermometer stays in place from start to finish.
steps: Preheat a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the dried fruit and pistachios, and toast them for 8 minutes, stirring regularly. Stop as soon as they smell toasty and turn golden. Transfer to a bowl and keep warm.
Wipe the pan clean. Pour in the 200g of honey and heat over medium heat until it reaches 130°C (266°F) on a thermometer. Transfer to a bowl and set aside.
Wipe the pan again. Mix in the sugar, water and the remaining 20g of honey, and bring to 150°C without stirring once it reaches a boil.
Meanwhile, whisk the egg whites with the icing sugar using an electric whisk until stiff and glossy peaks form.
Pour the honey at 130°C in a thin stream over the egg whites, whisking continuously. The mixture will thicken and become firmer.
Add the sugar syrup at 150°C, always in a slow stream, along the side of the bowl. Whisk until the mixture is smooth, glossy and significantly denser.
Incorporate the warm dried fruit with a spatula. Work quickly: the mixture will stiffen as it cools.
Line a mold with a sheet of rice paper. Pour in the nougat and smooth it with a spatula.
Place the second sheet on top, press down flat with a board to even out the thickness.
Allow to harden for 10 hours in a cool, dry place, never in the refrigerator.
Cut into bars or cubes with a smooth-bladed knife that has been rinsed under hot water and dried.

title: Cannelloni with green asparagus and ricotta
intro: The asparagus slides raw into the dry tubes: they cook in the steam of the flan that surrounds them, which concentrates their taste instead of diluting it in cooking water.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a gratin dish. Preheated empty for two to three minutes, it absorbs heat and radiates it through the bottom: the cannelloni brown underneath while the oven cooks the top. No transferring, therefore no filling to separate. Choose a model with a removable handle or one that is oven-safe.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Break or cut off the asparagus ends, then run the peeler over the bottom of the stems, without paying attention to the tips.
Thread the raw asparagus into the cannelloni, tip facing forward. If a stalk protrudes, trim it flush with the tube.

In a bowl, whisk the egg with the cream and milk. Stir in the ricotta, mashing it with a fork, then the roughly chopped spinach. You should obtain a smooth and pliable mixture (the liquid that binds and cooks the filling).
Season with salt, pepper, and grated nutmeg. Taste: the mixture should be slightly more seasoned than expected, as the dry pasta will absorb some of the seasoning.
Heat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Arrange the filled cannelloni in a single, tight layer, all in the same direction.
Pour the mixture over the tubes until they are covered. Sprinkle with grated cheese.
Cover and bake for 45 minutes at 170°C. Uncover for the last ten minutes: the surface should be browned and golden in places, and the tip of a knife should pierce an asparagus without resistance.
Let it rest for 5 minutes outside the oven before bringing the pan to the table. The mixture will finish setting.

title: Crustless quiche with mushrooms and spinach
intro: Without dough, everything depends on the moisture: really dry vegetables in a pan, and the mixture sets cleanly, without water at the bottom.
titane: The titanium pan goes directly from the stovetop to the oven without any transfer. You sear the vegetables in it, pour the mixture over them, and bake. No pie pan, no interruption in cooking, just a single, continuous heating.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (390°F). Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil. It can withstand high temperatures without smoking. Wait until it is barely simmering.
Add the onion and garlic to the hot pan. Stir for 3 minutes, until the onion becomes translucent.

Add the mushrooms, then the spinach. Let them release their juices (the water released by the heat) for about 6 minutes over medium heat. Don't overcrowd the pan: the vegetables should brown, not boil. They're ready when they pull away from the bottom of the pan on their own and there's no liquid left.
Meanwhile, whisk the eggs in a bowl with the Greek yogurt and milk. Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the grated Gruyère cheese.
Turn off the heat. Spread the vegetables in an even layer at the bottom of the pan, then pour the mixture over them. Shake lightly to ensure it settles evenly.

Place the pan in the oven as is, for 30 minutes at 200°C (390°F). The surface should be golden brown and the center just set, still slightly soft to the touch. Let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

title: Filo rolls with green asparagus and feta cheese, honey
intro: It all comes down to how tightly you roll the roller: if it's too loose, the dough unrolls and the feta escapes into the pan.
titane: A hot titanium pan, then covered, replaces the oven. Direct contact with the metal crisps the filo pastry while the steam trapped under the lid keeps the feta melted. When a roll easily detaches from the bottom, it's ready to be flipped: don't go looking for it before then.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees.
Break off the woody base of the asparagus, rinse them, and pat them dry carefully. Damp asparagus will make the phyllo soggy.
Cut the feta into batons the length of the asparagus, approximately the thickness of a finger.
Lay a sheet of phyllo on the work surface, brush it with grapeseed oil using a pastry brush, then fold it in half lengthwise.
Place an asparagus spear and a feta baton at one end, then roll tightly to the other end. Repeat with the remaining ingredients.
Brush each roll with egg yolk and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then drizzle in a thin stream of grapeseed oil.

Place the rolls without crowding them together. Cover and cook for 10 minutes over medium heat, turning once halfway through when they release on their own. Cook in two batches if the pan is full: each roll must touch the metal.
Transfer to a board to stop the cooking, drizzle with a thin stream of honey. Serve warm.

title: Thin zucchini and smoked salmon tart, without a crust
intro: Everything hinges on the first layer of courgettes: it's this layer that browns in the pan and serves as the base of the pie.
ing: Fresh cheese with garlic and herbs
titane: Titanium pan on low heat, lid on: the heat circulates and envelops the entire surface like in an oven, while the bottom continues to sear (cook quickly on contact to brown). You get a crispy bottom and a meltingly soft center without ever turning on the oven.
steps: Place an empty pan over medium heat and let it warm up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Cut the courgettes into regular slices, approximately 3 mm thick. In a bowl, mix them with a drizzle of grape seed oil, the breadcrumbs, half of the Parmesan and the pepper.
Pour a drizzle of oil into the hot pan. Arrange a first layer of slices, overlapping them slightly, over the entire surface.
Spread the fresh cheese on top, distribute the smoked salmon slices, then close with the remaining courgettes.
Drizzle with a final splash of oil and sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan.
Cover, reduce heat to low and let cook for 20 minutes. The tart is ready when the edges are crispy, the centre is creamy and the whole thing comes away from the bottom on its own.
Slide the tart from the pan onto a cutting board, without turning it over. Let it rest for two minutes before cutting it.

title: Clementine cloud cake
intro: A cake with little or no flour, whose entire structure relies on a gentle temperature and a center that is intentionally left wobbly when it comes out of the oven.
ing: The finely grated zest of a clementine
titane: The titanium pan goes in the oven: it becomes the mold. No batter transfers, so no air bubbles get trapped. The metal conducts quickly, the edges set at the same time as the center instead of drying out, and the unmolding is effortless once the pan has cooled slightly. Butter it generously, bottom and sides, before pouring.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Butter the titanium pan, including the sides.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until the mixture is perfectly smooth and slightly pale. There's no need to whisk it for a long time; we're not looking for volume here.
Add the clementine zest, then the mascarpone and yogurt. Whisk until smooth, but don't overmix once the mixture is uniform.
Incorporate the sifted cornflour (passed through a sieve to avoid lumps) by gently mixing until you obtain a smooth and fluid mixture.
Pour into the buttered pan. Bake the pan uncovered for 45 minutes at 170°C. The surface should be set and barely browned, the center still slightly wobbly when you move the pan.
Let it cool slightly in the pan before unmolding. When hot, the texture cannot withstand handling.

title: Cherry tomato and mozzarella tart
intro: It all comes down to the glaze (reduced cooking syrup that coats the bottom of the pan before adding the tomatoes: it is this that gives the tart its texture once it is turned over.
titane: The titanium pan withstands high heat and then the oven without needing to be transferred. The honey and balsamic vinegar caramelize directly on the bottom, the tomatoes are placed on top, and the pastry is poured over everything. When unmolding, the tatin releases itself: a single, clean movement, and the glaze stays on the tomatoes instead of sticking to the metal.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Pour the honey, olive oil, balsamic vinegar and oregano into the hot pan. Let it simmer gently until the mixture is homogenized, without letting it darken.
Remove from heat. Arrange the halved tomatoes cut-side up, tightly packed in a rosette pattern from the center. Season with salt and pepper.
Place the puff pastry over the tomatoes and tuck the edges inside the pan, against the side. Brush with beaten egg.
Place the pan in the oven as is, for 18 minutes, until the dough has risen and is evenly golden brown.

Remove the pan using an oven mitt. Place a serving dish on top and flip it over with a swift motion: the tatin will release easily. Tear the mozzarella by hand and place it on top of the still-hot tomatoes until it softens.

title: Udon noodles, caramelized soy protein, and silken tofu cream
intro: It's all about contrast: lacquered, almost sticky soy proteins placed against a cold, smooth tofu cream.
titane: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. The soy protein should sizzle on contact and remain still: it will release on its own when the surface is golden brown. Stirring too soon will result in a gray mush instead of a crust.
steps: Cover the textured vegetable protein (TVP) with very hot water and let it soak for 10 minutes. Drain, then squeeze it between your hands to remove the water: moist TVP doesn't sear, it steams.
Blend the silken tofu with 2 tablespoons of sesame oil, salt and pepper until smooth and glossy. Refrigerate.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Bring your hand a few centimeters away: you should feel a distinct heat.

Pour 2 tablespoons of sesame oil, spread it evenly, then arrange the textured vegetable protein (TVP) in a single layer. Don't touch anything. Wait until they release from the bottom on their own, a sign that the top is golden brown.
Add the soy sauce, chili sauce, and maple syrup. Reduce heat to medium.

Reduce the heat for about 10 minutes, stirring regularly. The mixture should become glossy, lacquered, and stick slightly to the bottom of the pan: this is caramelization. Remove from the pan as soon as this texture is achieved.
Meanwhile, plunge the udon noodles into a large pot of boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain without rinsing.
Arrange the noodles in the center of each plate. Place the caramelized TVP on one side, and a large spoonful of tofu cream on the other, without mixing.
Sprinkle with green onion and sesame seeds. Finish with a drizzle of the remaining sesame oil mixed with a touch of chili sauce.

title: Prawns in puff pastry with three seeds
intro: It's all about the contrast: a golden-brown crust underneath and on top, a shrimp that's still firm inside.
titane: The titanium pan serves as both an assembly surface and a baking tray. You assemble the pastry in it, brush it with the glaze, and bake it in it. The direct contact of the hot metal sears the underside of the puff pastry while the dome browns the top: no soft bottom, no transfer, no tray to wash.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
In a bowl, mix the shrimp with the lime juice, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Let them marinate while you prepare the batter.
Unroll the puff pastry on the work surface. Distribute the three seeds evenly over the entire surface.
Roll the rolling pin over the whole thing, pressing firmly: the seeds should become embedded in the dough and not remain on top.
Cut (into regular pieces) strips approximately 1.5 cm wide.
Drain the shrimp on absorbent paper, then wrap each one in a strip of dough, seeds outwards, ending under the shrimp.
Lightly oil the titanium pan. Arrange the puff pastry shrimp in it, seam underneath, without them touching.
Brush them with olive oil.
Bake the pan as is for 20 minutes, until the pastry is golden brown and crispy. With the leftover pastry, form twists and tuck them into the gaps: they will cook at the same time.
Serve hot, directly from the pan, with the tzatziki on the side.

title: Fudgy pan brownie with banana and Greek yogurt
intro: It all comes down to undercooking: the center must remain runny when the edges are already set.
ing: Dark chocolate with no added sugar
Milk, or plant-based drink of your choice
titane: Preheat the empty pan over low heat before greasing it. Once the lid is on, the heat circulates from the top like in an oven: the surface develops a thin, shiny crust while the crumb remains moist. As it cools, the cake shrinks and releases itself from the sides without sticking.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a bowl until it is a smooth puree.
Pour the still-warm melted chocolate over it. Mix immediately.
Stir in the Greek yogurt and vanilla. The mixture should be smooth and glossy.
Add the sifted flour, cocoa, and baking soda. Mix with a spatula, without overmixing once the dough is smooth.
Loosen (soften a preparation with a liquid) with the milk poured in a thin stream, until you obtain a soft dough that falls slowly from the whisk.
Add the chocolate chips or roughly chopped nuts. Give it three turns with a spatula, no more.
Heat the empty pan over low heat for 3 minutes. A drop of water placed on the surface should simmer without jumping. Then brush with a thin layer of fat.
Pour the batter into the pan, smooth the surface, and cover. Cook over low heat for 25 minutes without lifting the lid. The edges will firm up, while the center will remain soft to the touch.
Remove from heat and wait 5 minutes. The cake will release easily. Turn the pan upside down onto a wire rack or plate, then let it cool slightly before cutting into nine squares.

title: Salmon and feta spring rolls, panko breadcrumbs
intro: It's all about the contrast: a panko shell that's bright golden from dry searing, and underneath, a barely cooked salmon that the feta keeps moist.
titane: The empty titanium pan replaces the air fryer. The panko breadcrumbs adhere directly to the smooth surface and brown in minutes with just a drizzle of oil. The lid then comes into play, cooking over low heat to cook the fish through without softening the already formed crust.
steps: Beat the egg in a shallow dish. Dip each rice paper wrapper in the egg for a few seconds, until it becomes pliable and translucent. It should remain pliable, not sticky.
Place the steak in the center of the first galette. Season with salt and pepper, and sprinkle with dill.
Distribute the feta cubes over the fish, fold in the sides and roll tightly, like a spring roll. Double with the second galette, in the other direction, to close the ends.
Roll the roll in the panko, pressing lightly, several times, until the entire surface is covered.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 3 minutes. It must be hot before adding the fat.
Pour the oil, place the roller. Cook for a total of 6 minutes, rotating it a quarter turn each time it detaches on its own (this is the signal: as long as it sticks, the crust is not set).
Reduce heat to low, cover and cook for 6 minutes, turning once halfway through. The salmon should be just translucent (translucent in the center, more opaque at the edges) and the feta melted.
Remove from the pan onto a rack rather than a plate, while you slice diagonally.

title: Grilled spinach and vegan cheddar sandwich
intro: It all comes down to the crust: a nice hot pan, little fat, and above all the patience to not move the sandwich before it comes away from itself.
ing: can of plant-based tuna-style preparation with mayonnaise

ing.note: It can withstand higher temperatures without

titane: Titanium heats up faster than cast iron and releases food as soon as a crust forms. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the oil or butter, place the sandwich in the pan, and leave it alone. If it resists when you slide the spatula in, it's not ready. When it releases easily, it's golden brown.
steps: Pat the tomato slices dry with paper towels. Excess water will make the bread soggy during baking.

On a slice of bread, arrange half of the vegan cheddar slices. Spread the vegan mixture over them, then the tomatoes, spinach, and finish with the remaining cheddar slices. The cheese on each side binds the bread together and protects it from moisture. Close the sandwich.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A hand held ten centimeters above the pan should feel a distinct heat.
Add the clarified butter, let it spread, then place the sandwich on top. Don't touch it again.
After about 4 minutes, slide the spatula in: if the sandwich comes away easily, turn it over. Press it lightly to tighten the filling.
Continue cooking for 4 minutes on the second side. To finish melting the cheese without over-browning, cover for 20 to 30 seconds off the heat.
Remove from the pan onto a board, wait a minute, then slice diagonally.

title: Pan-fried golden banana fritters
intro: Very ripe bananas, three ingredients and a covered pan: the cooking is done without deep frying, and it is the direct contact with the metal that gives the crust.
titane: A titanium pan, preheated empty and then covered, replaces an air fryer. The heat circulates under the lid, cooking the doughnuts thoroughly, while the base, in direct contact with the doughnuts, develops a crisp crust. Preheat for three minutes empty before greasing: this prevents the dough from sticking.
steps: Mash the bananas with a fork in a bowl, without aiming for a smooth puree: a few pieces give it a soft texture.
Add the flour and baking powder. Mix until you obtain a smooth, thick dough that holds its shape on a spoon.
Preheat the titanium pan empty over medium heat for 3 minutes. It should be consistently hot, not smoking.
Drizzle with clarified butter or grapeseed oil. Scoop out small balls of dough, spacing them well apart. You should hear a light sizzle as you drop them onto the surface.
Cover and let brown for 4 minutes without touching. Turn over with a flick of the wrist as soon as the doughnuts detach themselves from the bottom, then cover again for 4 minutes.
Keep the heat at a constant medium temperature from start to finish: too high, and the outside will burn before the center is cooked. Don't overcrowd the pan; cook in two batches if necessary.
Remove from heat, roll the still-warm doughnuts in a little melted butter, then in sugar. Serve immediately.

title: Grilled corn salad and crispy tortellini
intro: It's all about the contrast: a corn-tortellini mixture seared dry until the crust forms, poured piping hot onto a cold salad at the last moment.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, until the water droplet test is successful (a drop of water will form a bead without immediately evaporating). The heat stored by the titanium replaces the oven: a crust will form in minutes, without any preheating time. Do not load the pan with more than a single layer—do this in two batches if necessary, ensuring each grain is in contact with the metal.
