steps: Place the empty titanium pan over high heat. Let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until the water droplet breaks apart.

Pour in the grapeseed oil. Add the drained corn, tortellini, paprika, garlic powder, Parmesan, salt and pepper. Spread in a single layer and sear for 8 minutes without touching. The mixture releases from the metal on its own when the crust is formed.
Turn with a flick of the wrist. Lower to medium-high heat and continue for 4 minutes, until golden brown on all sides. Transfer out of the pan to a wide dish to stop the cooking.
Meanwhile, peel the shallot, then slice it thinly. Cut the lettuce, halve the cherry tomatoes, dice the mozzarella, and slice the cucumber into half-moons. Combine everything in a salad bowl.
Whisk the fromage blanc with the mayonnaise, mustard, lemon juice and garlic powder. Season with salt and pepper. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon.
Coat the salad with sauce, toss, then pour the hot corn and tortellini mixture over the top. Serve immediately: beyond two minutes, the crispness will soften.

title: Chilled strawberry mousse
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the milk: if it's too hot, the gelatin loses its gelling power and the foam remains liquid.
titane: The titanium pan serves only one purpose here: to dissolve the gelatin in a small amount of milk without ever letting it boil. Its immediate conductivity makes the gentle heat easy to monitor—you see the liquid become clear before it simmers, and you remove it from the heat at just the right moment.
steps: Plan ahead: the mousse sets in the cold for 4 hours, allow this time before serving.
Plunge the gelatin sheets into a bowl of very cold water. Let them soften for 10 minutes.
Pour the milk into the titanium pan and place it over very low heat, without preheating empty. This is a delicate melting, not a searing.

Wring out the gelatin between your fingers, firmly: residual water dilutes the preparation. Add it to the milk and stir without interruption for 2 minutes. The liquid must become perfectly clear, without a single speck in suspension. No simmering should appear. Transfer out of the cooking vessel immediately.

Hull the strawberries and put them in the blender bowl with the fromage blanc and maple syrup. Pour in the milk with gelatin while still lukewarm. Blend until the mixture becomes fluffy and slightly pales.
Divide among four ramekins. Smooth the surface with a small spoon.
Refrigerate for 4 hours minimum. Below that, the centre remains runny.

title: Savory clafoutis with summer vegetables and mozzarella
intro: Everything happens before the appliance: the vegetables must be really seared, therefore coloured and free of their water, otherwise the clafoutis will release juice and remain pale.
titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding any oil. The heat will distribute evenly, allowing the vegetables to sear instead of boiling. Then, the same skillet goes straight into the oven, handle and all: no need to grease a baking pan, no need to transfer the vegetables, and the golden crust on the bottom will remain intact when unmolding.
steps: Place an empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Meanwhile, cut the vegetables into 1 cm dice. Peel the spring onion, then slice it thinly, keeping the white and green parts separate.

Pour the oil into the hot pan, add the vegetables and the white of the onion. Cook for 5 minutes over high heat, stirring occasionally: wait until the pieces release from the bottom on their own before moving them. They should brown on the edges.
In a mixing bowl, whisk the eggs with the cream, then sprinkle in the flour (incorporate it gradually while whisking to avoid lumps). Work until you obtain a smooth batter.
Add the mozzarella, Grana Padano, chopped basil, chives and the green of the onion. Season with salt and pepper.
Lower the heat to minimum, pour the batter over the vegetables and spread it with a spatula so that the dice are covered.

Place the pan in the oven at 180 °C for 22 minutes. The centre should be set, without any wobble, and the surface golden. Let cool for 5 minutes before cutting: the portions will hold together better.

title: Pan-fried vegetable arancini
intro: It all comes down to the rice: it must be cold and sticky, otherwise the balls will open up in the oil.
ing: block of vegan cheese for melting
titane: Grape seed oil withstands high temperatures without smoking, and titanium dioxide heats up quickly in it. A one-centimeter film is therefore sufficient to obtain a thinner crust than with deep frying, using significantly less oil. Once the arancini is in place, don't move it: it will detach on its own once the coating has set. Forcing it beforehand will tear it off.
steps: Add the rice, water, and crumbled stock cube to the pan. Cook over medium heat for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until all the liquid is absorbed. The rice should remain slightly mushy; this is what will help it hold together.
Remove the rice from the pan and place it on a large plate, spread it out in a thin layer, and let it cool to room temperature. It must be completely cold.
Rinse the pan, dry it, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the olive oil, add the soy protein and smoked paprika, stir for 1 minute.

Moisten with 100 ml of water and the tomato sauce. Let it reduce for 10 minutes over medium heat, until you obtain a thick filling that no longer releases any liquid. Season with salt and pepper, and let it cool slightly.
Cut the vegan cheese into about ten even cubes.

Take a large spoonful of rice in your moistened palm, make a well in the center, add a spoonful of filling and a cube of cheese. Fold the rice over the filling and firmly press it into a ball. Repeat for all ten pieces.
Whisk the plant-based milk with the flour until you have a smooth batter. Dip each arancini in this mixture, then roll it in the breadcrumbs, pressing to make them adhere.

Preheat a clean, empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes, then pour in about 1 cm of grapeseed oil. Sear the arancini in batches of three or four over medium-high heat. Don't touch them until they release easily, then turn them over to brown all sides. Cook for a total of 12 minutes.
Drain on absorbent paper as soon as it comes out of the pan and serve hot.

title: Leek and Parmesan Pancakes
intro: It all comes down to the whipped egg whites: they give the pancakes an airy crumb that stands up to the melted leek.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil or butter: the leeks will release their juices without sticking, and each pancake will develop a beautiful golden crust. When flipping, don't force it. The pancake will release easily when it's ready.
steps: Set the empty pan over medium heat. Let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until a drop of water sizzles briskly on it.

Peel the white parts of the leeks, then slice them thinly. Pour a drizzle of grapeseed oil into the pan, add the leeks and sweat them (cook gently without browning) for 8 minutes, stirring from time to time. They should be tender, never golden. Remove them from the pan and let cool.
Separate the egg whites from the yolks. In a bowl, whisk the yolks with the flour, baking powder, milk, salt and pepper. Work until you obtain a smooth batter, without lumps.
Fold in the Parmesan and the warm leeks. Mix.
Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks: the whisk should leave a clear trail and the tips should stand upright.
Add one third of the egg whites to the batter and mix firmly to loosen it. Fold in the rest with a spatula, lifting the mixture from bottom to top, without stirring. The batter should remain airy.

Wipe the pan with a paper towel, put it back empty for 1 minute over medium heat, then add a little fat. Drop small spoonfuls of batter, spacing them apart. Do not touch anything for about 2 minutes: when the pancake releases on its own and the edges are golden, flip it and cook for 2 minutes more. Wipe the pan between each batch.

title: Chicken and stir-fried vegetable tortillas
intro: It's all about the color of the chicken: a nice hot pan, spaced-out pieces, and don't touch anything for five minutes.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty, for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat, before adding any oil or butter. The surface should smoke slightly. This initial heat is what replaces the oven: the chicken browns in just a few minutes, the vegetables remain crisp, and you get a crisp stir-fry rather than a braised dish. Think of the pan as a work surface: push the cooked food to the side to free up the center, the hottest spot.
steps: Mix the diced chicken with the spices, lemon juice and a pinch of salt. Set aside while you cut the vegetables.
Peel the red onion, then cut it into strips along with the peppers.
Place the empty titanium pan over high heat. Wait 2 to 3 minutes, until a thin wisp of smoke rises.

Pour the grapeseed oil, then place the chicken in a single layer, pieces spaced apart. Do not stir for 5 minutes: the meat will release from the pan on its own once the crust has formed. Turn the pieces over.

Push the chicken to the edges of the pan. In the center, add the peppers and onion. Sauté for 8 minutes over high then medium heat, stirring regularly. The vegetables should be caramelized on the edges and still firm to the bite.
Drain the corn.
Mix the chicken and vegetables, distribute the corn then the grated cheese. Lower to low heat, cover for 2 minutes, until the cheese has melted.
Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds on each side in a dry pan. Fill them with the hot mixture and a spoonful of guacamole. Serve immediately.

title: Creamy noodles with butternut squash and teriyaki tofu
intro: It all comes down to the caramelization of the butternut squash: part of it goes into the sauce, the rest keeps its crispness.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat before adding the first drop of oil. This replaces the oven and air fryer: the butternut squash browns on the surface instead of steaming, and the teriyaki tofu develops a glossy crust in minutes. Work in small batches; an overcrowded pan will steam.
steps: Cut the butternut squash into approximately 1.5 cm cubes. Mix them with a drizzle of grapeseed oil, salt and pepper.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil: it should simmer gently.

Arrange the butternut cubes in a single layer, without packing them down. Turn them regularly, reduce the heat to medium after 5 minutes, and continue cooking for a total of 15 minutes. They will easily separate from the skin when one side is roasted.
Remove the butternut squash from the pan and set it aside on a plate. Quickly wipe the pan with a paper towel.
Sauté the broccoli for 5 minutes over high heat with a drizzle of oil and a tablespoon of soy sauce. It should brown in places but remain crisp. Set aside.

Sear the tofu in the same pan with a drizzle of oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes. Don't move it while it's sticking; it will release on its own once a caramelized crust has formed. Turn it over, brown the other side, and set aside.
Meanwhile, cook the noodles in a large pot of boiling water according to the package instructions, until al dente. Drain.
Blend the vegetable stock with the miso, the remaining soy sauce and about 250g of the roasted butternut squash. You will obtain a smooth, coating sauce.
Pour the sauce into the pan over low heat and deglaze (scrape the browned bits stuck to the bottom to dissolve them in the liquid). Add the noodles, broccoli, tofu, and remaining butternut squash.
Heat for 3 minutes, stirring constantly. Remove from heat and finish with the raw sesame oil. Adjust the seasoning.

title: Fig and brie puff pastries
intro: It all comes down to the pastry base: it must be heated before the filling, otherwise the juice from the fig will make it soggy.
titane: The pan becomes the mold. Preheat it empty for two to three minutes over medium heat, then press the squares of dough into it: the hot contact immediately sets the base. It then goes directly into the oven as is, without transferring, and arrives at the table with the pastries inside.
steps: Preheat the oven to 190°C. Trim the cheese (remove the rind if you find it too thick) and cut it into twelve pieces. Cut each fig into four wedges.
Cut the puff pastry into squares of approximately 7 cm. You will need twelve.

Heat the pan empty, over medium heat, for two to three minutes. Arrange the squares in a single layer, without overlapping them, and gently press them with your fingertips to form indentations. The edges will set in about twenty seconds.
Fill directly in the pan: a piece of cheese per square, a quarter of fig on top.
Cover and bake the pan for 15 minutes at 190°C. The pastry should be golden and puffed up, with the cheese melted.
Take out the pan, sprinkle with crushed pistachios and serve immediately, the pastry loses its crispness as it cools.

title: Chocolate hazelnut muesli bars
intro: It all comes down to compaction: a well-compressed mixture produces bars that hold together, a loose mixture produces loose granola.
titane: The covered titanium pan works like a small oven. The base transmits direct heat that seals and browns the muesli, while the lid traps steam and prevents the surface from drying out. Use low to medium heat, never higher: beyond that, the maple syrup caramelizes too quickly and the bottom burns before the muesli has set.
steps: Combine the muesli, hazelnut butter and maple syrup in a large bowl. Mix with a spatula until each flake is coated. The paste should be homogeneous and distinctly sticky.
Preheat the oven to 180°.
Line the pan with parchment paper, bringing it up over the edges. Pour the mixture and spread it over the entire surface.
Press down firmly with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass, paying special attention to the edges. Aim for a smooth, compact surface with even thickness.

Cover and cook for 10 to 12 minutes over low to medium heat. Lift the lid two or three times to check: the surface should be golden and dry to the touch, the underside coloured without any bitterness.
Meanwhile, melt the chocolate in a bain-marie or in short bursts in the microwave, stirring between each burst.
Off the heat, pour the melted chocolate over the still-warm biscuit and smooth with a spatula. The residual heat is enough to spread it thinly.

Let cool completely in the pan until it reaches room temperature. Unmould by pulling the paper, then cut into eight bars with a smooth-bladed knife. Complete cooling is essential: this is the condition for clean edges.

title: Feta and olive checkerboard
intro: Everything depends on the regularity of the cut: clean dice give a clean checkerboard.
ing: The zest of half an untreated lemon
titane: The pan doesn't heat up. It becomes the dish. Arrange the food in it, place it in the center of the table, as is: the raw metal serves as decoration and you avoid a transfer that would ruin the alignment.
steps: Drain the feta and dry it quickly with a cloth. Cut it into 2 cm cubes, as even as possible: lay the block flat, cut into strips, then cut into cubes.
Choose olives of a size close to that of the dice. If they are too large, cut them in half lengthwise.
Fill the cold titanium pan by alternating a cube of feta cheese and an olive, row after row. Offset each row by one notch so that the checkerboard pattern can be seen from a distance.
Drizzle with a little olive oil, leaving the bottom of the pan almost dry so that the design remains visible.
Sprinkle with dried oregano by rubbing it between your fingers (the warmth of the hand awakens the essential oils), then grate the lemon zest over it at the last moment.

title: Balsamic pearls
intro: It all comes down to the temperature difference: boiling vinegar syrup falling into ice-cold oil, and the pearl sets in a second.
titane: The titanium pan heats up much faster than a saucepan, and 15 cl of liquid covers a large surface area. The vinegar and agar-agar reach a boil in a few moments, leaving the mixture piping hot when pipetted—a necessary condition for the drops to remain round.
steps: Plan ahead: the oil must cool in the refrigerator for 1 hour before forming the pearls.
Fill a tall, narrow glass with olive oil to a height of at least 10 cm. Place it in the refrigerator for 1 hour. The oil must be thoroughly cold, almost syrupy.

Pour the vinegar into the titanium pan, disperse the agar-agar with a whisk and place over medium heat. Allow approximately 5 minutes until the first strong boils, then maintain them for 30 seconds: agar-agar only activates its gelling power from boiling onward.

Remove the glass from the refrigerator. Draw up the hot mixture with a pipette and let it fall drop by drop onto the surface of the oil, without haste. Each drop sets as it descends and deposits at the bottom as a small shiny bead.
Work in short batches. If the preparation thickens in the pan, place it back on the heat for a few seconds to make it fluid again.
Gently empty the glass into a fine strainer to drain the pearls of their oil. Do not rinse them: water would carry away the vinegar on the surface and the pearl would lose its flavor.
Keep refrigerated in a small closed container. They keep for three days.

title: Cheese-stuffed mushrooms wrapped in smoked turkey
intro: It all comes down to the order of operations: the meat crisps up first over high heat, then the cheese melts under the lid, without ever turning on the oven.
ing: portions of pressed cheese in balls
thin slices of smoked turkey breast
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its temperature. Preheat it empty, place the mushrooms on the seam of the slices, and leave them untouched: the meat will fuse together, brown, and then release on its own. You'll get a golden crust before you even have to think about the cheese melting.
steps: Brush the mushrooms dry. Unscrew the stem a quarter turn to remove it without tearing the cap.
Remove the wax from the cheese portions.
On the work surface, cross two slices of smoked turkey in an X shape.
Place a mushroom in the center of the cross, cavity facing upwards, and place a portion of cheese inside. It should be level with the surface, not protruding.
Fold the four meat tips over, one after the other, and press down. The seam is now at the top: turn the whole thing over so that it goes underneath.
Season each piece with pepper.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.
Pour in the oil; it should ripple without smoking. Place the mushrooms seam-side down. Do not move them for 3 minutes: they will detach on their own when the meat is browned.
Gently turn them over with tweezers and grasp the other sides, about 2 minutes, until evenly colored.
Cover, reduce heat to low-medium and let it cook for 10 minutes. The cheese should be melted in the center and the mushroom tender when pierced with the tip of a knife.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a warm plate. Serve immediately.

title: Moist fig and almond cake
intro: A muffin batter spread into a single cake, figs placed on top: it all comes down to a batter that is not too worked and a baking process carried out in two stages.

ing.note: /2 scraped cloves, or 1 tsp of extract

titane: The pan becomes the mold. You pour in the cold batter, start over low heat on the stovetop to cook the bottom, then slide the entire pan onto the oven rack. Uncoated, it can withstand the direct transfer to 180°C: a single, continuous bake, a golden crust, a moist center, and nothing to transfer.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Whisk the eggs with both sugars, honey and vanilla until ribbon stage (the mixture falls from the whisk forming a fold that remains visible for a second).
Pour the warm melted butter in a thin stream, whisk, then loosen with the milk.

Mix together separately the flour, almond flour, baking powder and sea salt. Incorporate them in two additions, using a spatula. Stop as soon as the flour has disappeared: overworked batter will give an elastic cake.
Pour the batter into the cold titanium pan. Even out the surface, right to the edges.
Cut the figs in half. Place them cut side up and press them down one-third of the way into the batter.
Sprinkle with sliced almonds and brown sugar if you want a crispy top.

Cover and let it set over low heat on the stovetop until the surface is no longer liquid. Uncover, place the pan in the oven on the rack at 180 °C and continue until a skewer inserted in the centre comes out dry and the top is golden. Allow about twenty minutes in total.
Let cool for a few minutes in the pan, then loosen the edges and turn out onto a spatula.

title: Grilled tofu sandwich with pickled carrot and avocado
intro: It's all about the contrast: a golden crust on the tofu, a carrot still crunchy under the marinade, and bread that remains dry.
ing: A few drops of sesame oil
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding the oil. The titanium dioxide heats up quickly, forming a crust in just a few minutes. Do not touch the tofu: it will stick at first, then release on its own once the crust has set. This is the signal to flip it.
steps: Cut the carrot into julienne strips (thin, even strips). Place it in a jar with the sugar, rice vinegar, and water. Shake well and let it marinate for 10 minutes.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. It is ready when a drop of water dances in it before evaporating.
Slice the tofu into thin, even strips, about 5 mm thick. The consistent thickness ensures even cooking.

Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan. Place the tofu slices in the pan without overlapping them. Leave them undisturbed for 3 minutes, until they begin to separate. Flip them over and cook for another 3 minutes. Transfer them to a plate.
Slice the cucumber and avocado. Finely chop the green onion.
Split the baguette in half, spread generously with sriracha mayonnaise on both sides. Drain the carrot well, squeezing it between your hands to remove excess marinade.
Fill with: tofu, cucumber, carrot, avocado. A few drops of sesame oil if you have some. Sprinkle with green onion, close, and cut in half.

title: Pineapple, ginger and turmeric ice pops
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the pineapple: if it is pale and fibrous, no amount of spice will compensate for the lack of sugar.
titane: Before blending, dry-roast the turmeric (heated without oil) in a titanium pan for 30 seconds over medium heat, stirring constantly. The powder loses its earthy bitterness and releases its citrus notes. Immediately transfer it from the pan to a cold bowl; after a minute, it will burn and become acrid.
steps: Roast the turmeric as described above. Set aside.
Peel the pineapples, remove the fibrous core and cut the flesh into 2 cm cubes.
Peel the ginger with a spoon and cut it into thin slices, across the fibers.
Blend the pineapple, ginger, cooled turmeric, and coconut milk until smooth and grain-free. This should take two minutes in a blender, scraping down the sides halfway through.
Taste it. The ginger should sting at the end of the mouth without overpowering the fruit; adjust with a few extra pineapple cubes if the burning sensation is dominant.
Fill the bags or stick molds three-quarters full: the mixture will expand as it sets.
Freeze for at least 1 hour, ideally 3. Take the sticks out 2 minutes before serving, to allow the aromas to develop.

title: Skyr bagels
intro: A dough without leavening or resting, which stands upright thanks to the skyr: everything depends on the tightness of the ring and on a glaze applied in two stages.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the worktop
(dried poppy seeds, onion and garlic, fleur de sel)

titane: When shaping, roll each piece of dough into a smooth log, then overlap the two ends by about two centimeters and roll the seam (the junction of the two ends) under your palm against the work surface. A simple pinch will reopen with heat; a rolled seam will hold up during baking and keep the hole neat.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C, fan setting. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, mix the flour, baking powder and salt. Add the skyr in three instalments, working by hand between each addition.

Flour the work surface. Knead for 3 minutes, until you have a smooth dough that no longer sticks to your fingers. Add flour by small handfuls if it remains moist, without overdoing it: a dough that is too dry will give a tight crumb.
Divide into 25 dough pieces of equal size, approximately 170 g each. Cover with a cloth while you work.

Roll each piece of dough into a log about twenty centimetres long, close it into a ring and seal as indicated above. Enlarge the central hole with your finger to 4 cm: it will close halfway during baking.
Arrange the bagels on the baking sheets, leaving 4 cm between each piece.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Brush on a first coat, wait 2 minutes, apply a second coat: this is what gives the shiny crust.
Sprinkle immediately with everything bagel seasoning while the egg wash is still wet.
Bake for 22 minutes, until the top is golden brown and the bottom sounds hollow when tapped with your fingernail. Transfer to a wire rack and let cool for 15 minutes before slicing.

title: Oat, peanut and dark chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the dough: firm enough to hold its shape, yet supple enough to remain melt-in-your-mouth after refrigeration.
titane: Melt the chocolate directly in the titanium pan over low heat, with the pan barely warm before adding the chocolate chips. Stir continuously with a spatula. The gentle heat retention of the titanium prevents the risk of burning that can occur with a poorly monitored double boiler. Turn off the heat when three or four whole chips remain: the residual heat will finish them off, and the chocolate will retain its shine.
steps: Combine the rolled oats, peanut butter, skyr and honey in a large bowl. Mix with a spatula until you obtain a homogeneous paste, with no visible streaks of skyr.
Let rest for ten minutes: the oats will absorb the moisture and the paste will firm up.
Divide the paste and shape into bars approximately 8 cm long by 2 cm wide. Work with lightly dampened hands to prevent the paste from sticking.
Arrange the bars on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, without letting them touch. Refrigerate for 45 minutes until they harden.
Meanwhile, melt the dark chocolate chips in a pan over very low heat, stirring constantly. Stop as soon as the mass is smooth and glossy.
Remove the bars. Dip them one by one into the still-fluid chocolate, or coat them with a spoon, then drain for a few seconds on the edge of the pan.
Return them to the parchment paper and refrigerate for 20 minutes, until the coating is brittle to the touch.
To store the bars, place them in bags and freeze: they will keep for up to 3 months.

title: Oat, peanut and date balls
intro: It's all about the texture: a dough that's firm enough to hold in your hand, yet supple enough not to crumble.
titane: Dry-roast the oats (heat them without oil to develop their aroma) in a titanium pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes. Stir constantly. As soon as they smell nutty and turn golden, transfer them from the hot pan to a cold plate. Let them cool to room temperature before mixing, otherwise the peanut butter will melt and the dough will become sticky.
steps: Open the dates, remove the pits, then dice the flesh. Set aside.
Toast the oat flakes as described above, then let them cool completely.
In a large bowl, combine the cooled oats and protein powder. Mix thoroughly to distribute the powder.
Pour in the honey and peanut butter. Work with a spatula, then by hand, until the mixture is uniform and there are no dry areas.
Incorporate the diced dates. Mix without crushing them, so they remain visible.
Add the chocolate chips last and give it just a few turns with a spatula.
Take about 40g of dough, roll it between your palms to form a smooth ball. Press firmly: a poorly compacted ball will crack.

Arrange the balls on a baking sheet, making sure they don't touch, and place them in the freezer for 1 hour. Then transfer them to an airtight container. They will keep for 3 months. Take them out 10 minutes before eating.

title: Courgette, dark chocolate and hazelnut muffins
intro: It all comes down to how well the courgettes are squeezed: if they're not pressed properly, they make the batter soggy and the muffins collapse.
titane: Melt the chocolate directly in the titanium pan, off the heat, immediately after heating it for thirty seconds over low heat and then removing it from the heat. The residual heat from the bottom is sufficient: the chocolate will cool down without ever exceeding 50°C, thus preventing it from becoming grainy. Stir with a spatula until you obtain a glossy ribbon.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Grate the raw courgettes, without peeling them, on the medium grater.
Gather them in a clean kitchen towel and press firmly over the sink. Repeat until no more liquid comes out. You should lose about a third of the weight.
In a bowl, mix the drained courgettes, flour, baking powder and eggs. Work just enough to combine: overmixed batter becomes elastic.
Divide the mixture into two bowls, in equal parts.
Melt the chocolate (see The titanium technique), let it cool for one minute, then fold it into the first bowl.
Fold the hazelnut spread into the second bowl, without trying to smooth it completely: some marbling holds better during baking.

Fill the muffin cups: a spoonful of chocolate batter at the bottom, a spoonful of hazelnut batter on top. Stop three-quarters up the height. You can, if you wish, add a little hazelnut spread on top before baking.
Bake for 20 minutes at 180 °C. A knife tip comes out clean in the centre, the top remains soft under your finger.
Turn out after five minutes of resting, then let cool on a wire rack.

title: Dark chocolate protein banana bread
intro: Ten portions at once, baked in the oven because the volume requires it: what matters here is the ripeness of the bananas, they alone give the sugar and the softness.
titane: The pastry itself goes in the oven. But the warmed slice is best enjoyed in a dry titanium pan over medium heat: two minutes per side, without any oil. The banana sugar caramelizes on contact, while the crumb remains soft underneath. It's the best way to revive a portion straight from the freezer.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl until you obtain a smooth puree, without any fibrous pieces.
Crack the eggs on top and whisk vigorously: the mixture (the basic blend) should become homogeneous and slightly frothy.
Add the oat flour and whey isolate. Mix just enough so that no dry powder remains.
Incorporate the skyr, yeast, vanilla extract and agave syrup. Work the dough until it is smooth, without overworking it.
Pour in the dark chocolate chips and give a few turns with a spatula to distribute them.
Fill individual molds three-quarters full. The dough will rise.
Bake for 20 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean: it's cooked through. Add 5 minutes if your molds are deep.
Remove from the pan and let cool completely on a wire rack before covering. A warm, covered cake will release moisture and become soggy.
Transfer to a storage container in an airtight box: 3 days at room temperature, 3 months in the freezer.
For a frozen portion, let it thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then reheat it in a pan, oven or air fryer.

title: Speculoos protein cheesecake
intro: A large, dense, and not very sweet cheesecake that can be cut cleanly and frozen in slices.
titane: Before binding them with butter, dry-roast the speculoos crumbs in a titanium pan over medium heat for two minutes, stirring constantly. The crumbs will lose their moisture, the cinnamon aroma will be released, and the base will remain crisp beneath the creamy mixture, which will be just as moist.
steps: Crush the speculoos cookies into fine crumbs. Dry-roast them, let them cool slightly, then mix with the melted butter, cinnamon, unflavored protein powder, and milk. The mixture should hold its shape when you squeeze it in your hand, without being sticky.

Press this mixture firmly into the bottom of a springform pan lined with parchment paper. Use the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass to press it down slightly up the sides. Refrigerate while you prepare the filling.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.

Work the cream cheese on its own until smooth. Add the Greek yogurt, then the eggs one at a time, the vanilla, the vanilla protein powder, and the agave syrup. Mix at low speed, being careful not to incorporate air: bubbles would cause the surface to swell and then crack.
Pour the mixture onto the cold base. Tap the mold two or three times on the work surface to remove any air bubbles.
Bake for 40 minutes. The cheesecake is ready when the edges are set and the center still jiggles when you move the pan.
Allow to cool to room temperature, with the oven off and the door ajar if possible: the slow descent prevents the central crevice.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. Unmold when cold and cut with a knife that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry between each slice.

title: Curried chicken wraps with rice and zucchini
intro: It all comes down to searing the courgettes and chicken: a really hot pan, few movements, and the cream will only bind juices that have already formed.
ing: salt for the rice cooking water
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes, before adding any oil or butter. The zucchini and then the chicken will brown without sticking, provided you don't stir them: they will release easily once a crust has formed. This browned base will give the sauce its flavor.
steps: Cook the rice in a saucepan of salted water over medium heat for about 15 minutes, until all the water is absorbed. This volume will remain outside the pan. Cover and set aside.
Cut the courgettes into 1 cm cubes or thin half-slices. Dry them in a cloth: surface moisture slows down the coloring.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour the grapeseed oil over the zucchini, then arrange them in a single layer. Leave for 5 minutes without touching them. They are ready when they easily release from the pan and are golden brown on one side.

Add the chicken and curry. Stir once, then let it sear for 8 minutes. Work in two batches if the pan is too full: an overcrowded pan will steam the chicken. The chicken should be very tender and opaque throughout.
Pour in the cream, reduce to low-medium heat and let it simmer for 4 minutes, scraping the bottom to loosen the juices.

Remove from high heat and, over low heat, stir in the rice and Parmesan cheese. Mix until the mixture is smooth and coats the back of a spoon. Adjust the seasoning with salt. Transfer to a bowl and let cool slightly before assembling.
Fill each galette with approximately 180g of the mixture, fold in the sides, and roll up tightly. Wrap individually in baking paper.
Store in the refrigerator for 3 days or freeze. Reheat in the oven at 180°C for 12 minutes, in an air fryer for 8 minutes, or in the microwave for 2 minutes.

title: Sugar-coated doughnuts
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the dough: slightly sticky at the end of kneading, it will give a stringy crumb and doughnuts that remain soft when cooling.
titane: No deep frying. Pour 2 cm of oil into the titanium pan and maintain it between 160 and 165°C: the doughnuts will float halfway down; turn them over only once when the base is golden. The light ring that appears around the edge tells you that the doughnuts have risen properly. Oil that is too hot will brown the crust before the center is cooked.
steps: Crumble the fresh yeast into the bowl of a stand mixer with half of the lukewarm milk. Let it rest for 10 minutes, until the mixture foams on the surface.
Add the egg, sunflower oil and the remaining milk. Mix with a dough hook until smooth.
Add the flour, salt, sugar, vanilla sugar and baking powder. Knead for 5 minutes at medium speed.
Incorporate the butter and knead for another 5 minutes. The dough should pull away from the sides of the bowl while still retaining a slight tackiness when touched. Do not add flour to correct this.

Oil your hands, transfer the dough from the bowl to a mixing bowl, cover with cling film, and then cover with a tea towel. Let it rise for 1 hour 30 minutes at room temperature, until doubled in size.
Deflate the dough (press down the fermentation gases with the palm of your hand), then roll it out on a floured surface to a thickness of 1.5 cm. Cut out 7 cm discs.
Place the discs on a floured baking sheet, cover with a cloth and let rise for 30 minutes. They should puff up without collapsing to the touch.

Heat the oil in the titanium pan to 160°C. Place three or four doughnuts in the pan, without crowding them. Cook for 2 minutes on the first side, turn over, and cook for another 2 minutes on the second side.
Drain on absorbent paper for 30 seconds, then roll them in granulated sugar while they are still warm: the sugar only sticks at this point.
Check the oil temperature between each batch before putting the next one in the oven.

title: Almond milk extracted
intro: It all comes down to soaking: a well-rehydrated almond yields its milk effortlessly, a dry almond clogs the screw and produces a thin juice.
titane: Feed the juicer in small handfuls, alternating almonds and water. The auger should always work in a soft mixture, never in a dry mass. If the motor struggles, stop, add a little water, and restart.
steps: Plan ahead: soak the almonds for a minimum of 6 hours, preferably overnight; start the day before.
Cover the almonds generously with cold water. Let soak for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight. The skin will wrinkle, the almond will swell and become tender to the bite.
Drain and rinse with clear water. Discard the soaking water, it is bitter.
Assemble the extractor: extraction chamber locked onto the motor unit, outlet cap closed. Place a container under each opening, one for the juice, one for the pulp.
Turn on. Introduce a few almonds, then a thin stream of water. Continue alternating until the 600 ml is exhausted.
Let run until the okara (residual pulp) comes out dry and crumbly, without a single drop. This is the sign that extraction is complete.
Open the cap, collect the milk. Stir before each serving: it separates naturally at rest. Three days in the refrigerator, in a closed bottle.

title: Raw couscous tabbouleh with chopped vegetables
intro: Here, the semolina does not go through boiling water: it rehydrates with only the juice from the chopped vegetables, which requires sufficient rest and well-ripened vegetables.
titane: Before assembling, toast the dry semolina in the titanium pan, without oil, over medium heat. Stir continuously for two to three minutes, until the grains become matte and release a nutty aroma. The stable heat of the coating prevents burning and evaporates residual moisture: the grains will then absorb the tomato juices more quickly and hold together without sticking. Remove from heat and transfer to a cold container immediately to stop the toasting process.
steps: Plan ahead: the tabbouleh should rest in the refrigerator for one hour before serving.
Toast the semolina using the titanium pan method, then let it cool completely.
Pour it into the food processor bowl. Add salt and olive oil, mix by hand to coat each grain.
Wash the vegetables. Deseed the tomatoes, peel the onions, remove the seeds and white parts of the bell pepper. Cut everything into regular pieces of two centimetres.

Add the vegetables to the bowl, on top of the semolina. Pulse the food processor five to six times, until you obtain a coarse chop mixed with the grains. Do not add water: the released juice is sufficient.
Chiffonade the mint at the last moment, incorporate it with the raisins. Mix with a fork to aerate.
Cover and keep in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour. Taste before serving: adjust the seasoning with salt and oil, the semolina will always absorb some.

title: Chocolate-hazelnut filled cookies
intro: It all comes down to how they come out of the oven: the cookies should look undercooked in the center, that's what keeps the spreadable center gooey.
titane: Melt the butter over low heat in the titanium pan and let it brown until it smells nutty, then remove it from the heat and transfer it to a cold bowl. This warm, not hot, brown butter flavors the batter without cooking the egg during mixing.
steps: Beat the softened butter with the brown sugar and sugar until smooth and glossy.
Add the egg and vanilla. Mix again, gently: the dough should only become homogeneous.
Fold in together the flour, salt, baking soda and baking powder. Finish with the chocolate chips, using a spatula.
Cover the bowl with cling film and let rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator. The firmed dough shapes neatly and spreads less during baking.
Preheat the oven to 170 °C, fan-assisted heat. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.

Scoop portions of dough the size of a large walnut. Make a well in your palm, place a teaspoon of chocolate spread, close the dough around it and roll into a well-sealed ball. Space them 5 cm apart on the baking sheet.
Bake for 10 minutes. The edges are set, the center remains pale and soft. Let cool for 10 minutes on the baking sheet before removing: the cookies finish setting as they cool.

title: Homemade yogurts at 40°C
intro: Everything hinges on the temperature: 40°C maintained for seven hours, no more and no less, that is the only requirement of this recipe.

ing.note: or a few drops of vanilla flavoring instead

titane: The pan is used here for warming, not cooking. Pour in the milk, place over very low heat, and remove from the heat as soon as the bottom of the pan is no longer cool to the touch. The titanium then slowly releases its heat: let the milk rest in it for two minutes; it will stabilize at around 40°C without ever coming close to simmering. Milk that is too hot kills the cultures, while cold milk slows down the setting process.
steps: Warm the milk in the pan using the method described above. Check: a drop on the inside of your wrist should be barely noticeable.
Add the sugar and whisk until completely dissolved. If you're using vanilla, add it now.
Dissolve the starter (or yogurt) in a ladle of lukewarm milk, then pour it back into the pan. Mix without creating foam: bubbles will give an uneven surface.
Divide into eight small jars. Close the lids.

Place the jars in a device capable of maintaining a stable 40°C – oven on the proofing setting, air fryer on yogurt mode, or yogurt maker. Leave for 7 hours. Do not shake anything during the setting process.
Check: the yogurt should hold its shape when tilted in the pot, slightly domed. Let it cool to room temperature, then refrigerate overnight before serving.

title: Mango milkshake, mascarpone whipped cream
intro: It all comes down to temperature: mango, milk, cream and the mixer bowl must be taken from the cold, otherwise the whipped cream will deflate and the milkshake will be lukewarm in the glass.
titane: No cooking involved here, but the pan still plays a role. For a more intense version, dry-fry a few cubes of mango in a very hot titanium pan for one minute per side, without any oil. The juices will caramelize, and the flesh will remain firm. Transfer (remove from the pan and set aside) to a cold plate, then let it cool completely before blending with the rest of the ingredients. A warm pan would cause the mango to sweat instead of sear.
steps: Place the robot bowl and whisk in the freezer 10 minutes before starting.

Pour the mascarpone and heavy cream into the bowl. Whip (to incorporate air and stiffen) at medium speed, then increase the speed for the last 30 seconds. Stop as soon as the whisk leaves a clean trail; beyond that point, the mixture will curdle.
Fill a piping bag with this whipped cream and refrigerate.
Blend the mango flesh with the milk in a blender, starting at the lowest speed to avoid heating the mixture. Gradually increase the speed until you obtain a smooth texture with no visible fibers.
Divide the milkshake into four glasses, leaving two good centimeters free at the top.
Pipe the whipped cream in a spiral, sprinkle with diced mango and serve immediately.

title: Carrot, turmeric and strawberry juice
intro: A raw juice whose entire balance lies in the relationship between the carrot, earthy and sweet, and the strawberry which rounds out the bitterness of the turmeric.

ing.note: to be adjusted according to the extractor

titane: Alternate the textures in the juicer's chute: a firm carrot, then two strawberries, then another carrot. The hard pieces push the soft pulp against the auger, resulting in a denser juice without the mush that sticks to the filter when you put in soft fruit all at once.
steps: Wash the carrots, peel them, and cut them into sticks that fit the juicer's feed chute. Hull the strawberries and rinse them quickly without letting them soak.
Pass the carrots and strawberries through the juicer alternately. If using fresh turmeric, insert it between two carrot sticks; if using powder, reserve it for later.
Pour the cold water into the chimney last: it carries away the pulp remaining in the screw and gives you 2 to 3 extra spoonfuls of juice.
Stir the turmeric powder into the juice and whisk for a few seconds. The powder doesn't completely dissolve; it remains suspended. Stir again just before drinking.
Transfer to a bottle, fill it to the brim to minimize contact with air, and refrigerate. Consume within 24 hours, one glass in the morning.

title: Chicken with potatoes, pan-fried then oven-baked
intro: The chicken is cut into pieces before cooking: this is the only way to get a really crispy skin in the pan and meat cooked through at the same time.
titane: Place the pieces skin-side down in a hot, dry pan with no added fat. The poultry fat will render and is sufficient. Leave them undisturbed for six to seven minutes: the skin will peel away on its own when it's ready. If it resists, it's not done yet.
steps: Blend the softened butter with the onion, garlic, tomato concentrate, parsley, salt, pepper, paprika and turmeric. You will obtain a smooth, homogeneous paste of a dark red colour.
Divide it into two equal parts. Coat the chicken pieces with the first part, slipping a little paste under the skin of the thighs. Leave to rest for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Mix the diced potatoes with the second part by hand until they are all coated.

Preheat the oven to 200°C. Heat the titanium pan over medium-high heat, dry. Place the chicken pieces skin-side down, without crowding. Sear for 6 to 7 minutes without moving them until the skin is brown and firm. Turn over and cook for 3 minutes. Remove from the pan and reserve on a plate.
In the remaining fat, brown the potatoes for 5 minutes over high heat, stirring occasionally. Pour in the water and scrape the bottom with a spatula to deglaze and release the cooking juices.
Place the chicken pieces back on the potatoes, skin-side up. Bake for 35 minutes. Halfway through cooking, baste the pieces with the red juice from the bottom of the pan.
Check that the chicken is cooked: the juices that run from a pricked thigh should be clear. Remove from the oven, leave to rest for 8 minutes in the pan before serving.

title: All-chocolate muffins
intro: What makes the difference here is not the quantity of chocolate but the dry roasted cocoa and the cold setting before baking, which gives the hump and the soft texture.
titane: Roast the cocoa (heat it dry to release its aromas) in a cold titanium pan over low heat. Stir constantly with a spatula for 2 minutes: the powder will become fragrant and slightly darker. Immediately transfer it to a cold bowl, otherwise the residual heat from the pan will make it bitter.
steps: Roast the cocoa as described above, then let it cool completely.
Whisk together the flour, sugar, cooled cocoa, baking powder and salt. Break up any cocoa lumps against the side of the bowl.
In a second bowl, whisk the eggs with the cream, oil or melted butter and vanilla.

Pour the liquids over the dry ingredients. Mix with a spatula, in fifteen to twenty movements, until all traces of flour have disappeared. The batter should remain slightly uneven: overmixing will result in dense muffins.
Incorporate the chocolate chips with three turns of a spatula.
Divide the mixture among 8 paper baking cups, filling them two-thirds full. Refrigerate for 30 minutes: the dough will thicken and rise more evenly during baking.
Bake at 160°C for 15 minutes in a fan oven, without overloading the basket. A knife inserted into the center should come out with a few moist crumbs, not dry.
Allow to cool for 10 minutes before removing the cupcakes from the molds.

title: Pineapple coconut frappé
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the pineapple: if it can be pierced without resistance with a knife, there's no need to add more sweetener.
titane: Before blending, set aside two 1 cm slices of pineapple. Heat a dry titanium pan over high heat, without any oil or butter: the flesh is moist enough to prevent sticking. Place the slices in the pan and let them sear for 2 minutes per side, without touching them, until they develop brown streaks and a caramel aroma. Transfer them to a cold plate. Add one slice to the blender, and place the other on top of the glass. This caramelization provides the subtle bitterness that stabilizes the drink, whereas a raw pineapple on its own would be flat.
steps: Cut off both ends of the pineapple, stand it upright, and remove the skin by following the curve of the fruit. Remove the remaining eyes with the tip of a knife. Remove the fibrous core, as it clogs the blender.
Set aside two slices for the titanium pan presentation, then cut the rest into 2 cm cubes. You should have approximately 600 g of flesh.
Blend the cubes with the coconut milk until you reach a smooth texture, 45 seconds at full speed. Scrape down the sides once during the process.
Taste. Add the sweetener in small amounts, blending for a few seconds between each addition: a very ripe pineapple may not need any.
Add the ice cubes and the caramelized slice cut into pieces. Blend for 30 seconds more, until the sound of the blender becomes regular, a sign that no ice shards remain.
Pour into two tall glasses that have been chilled beforehand. Place the second caramelized slice on the rim. Serve immediately, as the foam settles in three minutes.

title: Sushi cake with mango, salmon, and avocado
intro: It all comes down to the rice: rinsed until the water runs clear, cooked covered without ever lifting the lid, then seasoned while still hot so that it absorbs the vinegar.

ing.note: rinsed until the water ran clear

titane: This is done in a saucepan, not a frying pan: you need a thick base and a tight-fitting lid to trap the steam. The key is patience—ten minutes off the heat, with the lid on. This is when the grains finish swelling and become sticky. Lift the lid too soon, and the rice won't hold its shape.
steps: Pour the rinsed rice, water, and salt into a heavy-bottomed saucepan. Cover, bring to a simmer, then reduce to a simmer. Cook for 12 minutes, until all the liquid is absorbed.
Remove from heat. Let stand for 10 minutes without opening the lid.
Dissolve the sugar in the rice vinegar. Pour over the still-warm rice and mix with a spatula, using a cutting motion rather than stirring, so as not to crush the grains. Let it cool slightly.
Slice the mango and avocados into thin strips. Cut the salmon into even strips the width of the mold.

Line a loaf tin with cling film, allowing it to overhang the edges. Press down a first layer of rice to a depth of two centimeters with the back of a damp spoon. Arrange a layer of salmon, then rice, then mango and avocado, and finish with a layer of tightly packed rice.
Fold the film over, press down by hand to compact. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Turn out onto a board, remove the film, and slice with a knife that has been dipped in hot water between each slice. Serve with the sweet and savory soy sauce on the side.

title: Coco Lagoon
intro: It all comes down to the ripeness of the fruit: a perfectly ripe mango is enough to sweeten the glass, the rest is just a matter of dosage.

ing.note: honey or sugar, according to taste

titane: No pan required here, but the same contact is necessary: pour the coconut mixture slowly over the ice cubes, using a spoon resting against the side of the pan. The syrup stays at the bottom, the fruity layer settles on top, and the gradient lasts for several minutes. Pouring it directly stirs everything up and you lose the effect.
steps: Peel the mango and cut the flesh into cubes. Peel the pineapple if needed and cut it into pieces.
Scoop out the flesh and seeds from the passion fruits with a spoon. Reserve one spoonful for garnish.
Blend the mango, pineapple and passion fruit pulp with the coconut milk until you obtain a smooth texture, without any visible fibres. Allow about one minute at full speed.
Taste it. Add the agave syrup, honey or sugar only if the fruits lack ripeness, then blend for three more seconds. If the mango was very fibrous, strain through a fine sieve before serving.
Pour a little blue syrup into a saucer and the grated coconut into another. Dip the rim of the glasses in the syrup, then in the coconut, turning by a quarter turn for an even border.
Pour the remaining blue syrup into the bottom of the glasses. Add the ice cubes on top without touching the sides.
Pour the coconut-fruit mixture in a slow stream along a spoon. The blue should rise up in a veil, not blend in.
Give it just one turn with a spoon to marble it, place the reserved passion fruit pulp on the surface and serve immediately.

title: Whisked mayonnaise
intro: A mayonnaise depends on two things: the temperature of the ingredients and the slowness of the oil stream.
titane: The trickle. The oil should fall in a continuous stream, barely thicker than a thread, while the whisk turns quickly and steadily. Until the emulsion (a stable dispersion of oil droplets in the aqueous phase) has formed, each spoonful poured at once risks losing it. Place a rolled-up damp cloth under the mixing bowl: it stabilizes the container and frees up your other hand for the oil.
steps: Take the egg, mustard, and oil out of the refrigerator at least thirty minutes in advance. Nothing should be cold: a yolk taken from the refrigerator will curdle the emulsion.
Pour the vinegar into a mixing bowl. Add the salt and pepper, and mix until the salt is dissolved. The salt will no longer dissolve once the oil is added.
Incorporate the mustard and mix to obtain a smooth base.
Add the egg yolk alone. Whisk for a few seconds, until the mixture is smooth and uniformly yellow.

Pour the oil in a very thin stream, whisking quickly and continuously. After about thirty milliliters, the sauce will whiten and thicken: you can then pour it in a little more steadily, without ever stopping the stream.
Keep an eye on the surface. If oil beads up and refuses to incorporate, stop pouring, whisk until smooth, then resume more slowly. The mayonnaise is ready when the whisk leaves a clean trail.
Taste, adjust the salt and vinegar. Transfer to a clean bowl and set aside at room temperature until serving.

title: Homemade mixed vegetables
intro: Everything hinges on the cooking time, which should be short, and on the drying time: a failed mixed vegetable salad is a wet one.
ing: a liter of water with about twenty ice cubes added
titane: Between ice water and mayonnaise, there's a step no one does that makes all the difference: spread the chilled vegetables in a single layer on a clean tea towel and let them drain for ten minutes. Roll up the towel without crushing them. The mayonnaise will stick to the vegetables instead of sinking to the bottom of the bowl.
steps: Prepare the ice bath: very cold water and ice cubes in a large salad bowl. Keep it within reach, as it will stop the cooking.
Peel the carrots, turnips and potatoes. Plunge the peeled potatoes into cold water to prevent them from oxidizing while you wait to cut them.
Cut the carrots, turnips and potatoes into 8 mm dice. Slightly larger than classic mixed vegetables: the cooking remains controlled and you save ten minutes of knife work.
Top and tail the green beans and cut them to the same size as the diced vegetables.

Bring the 2 liters of water to a boil with the coarse salt. You will cook à l'anglaise (in a large volume of boiling salted water, uncovered), vegetable by vegetable, so that each retains its color and texture.
Plunge the carrots for 4 minutes. Remove them with a slotted spoon and transfer them immediately to the ice water. Wait for the water to return to a boil before each new vegetable.
Continue in the same way: turnips 4 minutes, green beans 4 minutes, peas 3 minutes. The dice should remain firm to the bite.
Cook the potatoes last, drained of their soaking water, for 6 to 7 minutes, and refresh them as well. They cloud the water, which is why they go in last.
Drain everything, then spread the vegetables on a clean kitchen towel. Let them dry for 10 minutes. See the note.
Transfer the dry vegetables to a cold salad bowl. Add the mayonnaise in three batches, mixing with a spatula, until each dice is coated without excess.
Fold in the chopped herbs at the last moment. Adjust the seasoning and add a few grinds of pepper. Refrigerate for 30 minutes before serving.

title: Cloud eggs
intro: It all comes down to two contrasting textures cooked together: a whipped white that remains airy and a yolk that is still liquid in the center.
titane: Make a shallow indentation in the nest with a spoon, not your finger. A clean, deep indentation will hold the yolk in the center while the white rises; a hollow that is too wide will allow it to slide to the edge, where it will cook in two minutes.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Lightly oil four cavities of a muffin tin with a brush, extending into the bottom corners.
Separate the eggs one by one over a bowl, reserving each yolk whole in a small cup. A trace of yolk in the whites prevents them from whipping up properly.

Whip the egg whites to stiff peaks (whisk until the mixture stands straight on the whisk) with sea salt, pepper and nutmeg. Stop as soon as the texture becomes glossy and firm: beyond that, it would become grainy.
Place a generous tablespoon of whites in each cavity. Create a nest with the back of the spoon, up to halfway.
Slide a yolk into each hollow. Cover with a small spoonful of white, without pressing, barely smoothing the top.

Bake for 5 to 6 minutes at 180 °C. The top should be just set and barely coloured, the yolk still runny under the snow. Unmould with the tip of a knife and serve immediately: the clouds collapse within a few minutes.

title: Churros
intro: Three ingredients, no egg: everything depends on the cooking of the dough and the temperature of the oil.
titane: The titanium pan is ideal for making panade (a cooked dough made with water and flour): its wide base provides even heat, allowing the flour to hydrate quickly and dry without sticking. However, it's not suitable for deep frying. Transfer the oil to a tall saucepan or deep fryer, and keep the pan for working with the dough.
steps: Pour the water and salt into the titanium pan. Bring to a rolling boil over high heat.
Remove from heat. Add the flour all at once and mix with a spatula until you obtain a smooth, lump-free batter.
Return to medium heat for one minute and dry out the dough (evaporate excess moisture by working it against the bottom): it should detach in a compact mass.
Remove from the pan and place in a wide dish. Let cool for 15 minutes; the dough should remain soft but stop smoking.
Fill a piping bag fitted with a fluted nozzle. Pipe 12 cm sticks onto oiled baking paper squares, one per square.
Heat the oil to 180°C in a tall saucepan, filled to a maximum of one-third full. Check with a thermometer.
Dip the churros three at a time, turning the paper over above the oil: it will detach easily; remove it immediately with tongs. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until they are a uniform golden color.
Drain on absorbent paper for about thirty seconds, then roll the churros in sugar while they are still hot.

title: Cold cheesecakes with speculoos and red berries
intro: A cheesecake without gelatin and without an oven, whose entire structure comes from the very cold whipped cream and the time spent in the freezer.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: Melt the butter in a titanium pan over low heat, then stir in the speculoos powder and cook for 2 minutes off the heat: the residual heat will toast (dry out and intensify the flavors) the powder, and the base will remain crisp even under the creamy mixture. Remove from heat immediately to stop the cooking process.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecakes spend 4 hours in the freezer then 2 hours in the refrigerator before serving; factor in this time for your preparation.
Place the bowl and whisk in the refrigerator 15 minutes before starting, along with the liquid cream.
Process the speculoos into fine powder. Melt the butter over low heat in the pan, add the powder, stir for 2 minutes then remove from heat.
Divide the mixture among six silicone moulds and press with the back of a spoon until you have an even base. Keep refrigerated.
Whip the very cold cream with a whisk until it holds stiff peaks without flowing. Stop as soon as it is firm: beyond that, it will become grainy.
In a second bowl, whisk the mascarpone, fresh cheese, icing sugar and lemon juice. The mixture should be smooth and lump-free.
Fold in the whipped cream in three additions, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from bottom to top. The preparation should remain airy.
Fill the moulds to the brim, smooth the surface and tap the moulds lightly on the work surface to remove air bubbles.
Place in the freezer for at least 4 hours, until completely set.
Unmould the cheesecakes while still hard, by gently pulling on the silicone, and place them on the serving plates.
Let them come back in the refrigerator for 2 hours, then coat with red fruit coulis when serving.

title: Apricot mousse with rosemary
intro: Everything depends on the firmness of the egg whites: too soft, the foam collapses within an hour; tightly packed, it lasts three days.

ing.note: or Greek yogurt, or drained cottage cheese
to 3 tablespoons depending on the acidity of the fruit

titane: Gently warm the honey and rosemary in the titanium pan over very low heat for three minutes, making sure it never simmers. The coating distributes heat evenly, drawing the oils from the rosemary without burning the honey's sugars. Remove from the heat and let it infuse while you pit the fruit, then remove the sprigs.
steps: Wash the apricots, cut them in half, and remove the pits.
Steep the rosemary sprigs in the honey for a few moments, then remove the rosemary.
Blend the apricot flesh with the infused honey until you obtain a smooth puree. Taste it: it should remain distinctly fruity and slightly tart.
Set aside three spoonfuls of this puree for plating.
Whisk the remaining puree with the skyr until the colour is homogeneous.
Whip the egg whites with the pinch of salt. Whisk them vigorously (whisk briskly for the last few seconds) until they form stiff peaks on the whisk.
Fold the egg whites into the apricot mixture in three additions, using a spatula, with upward movements from the bottom. The first third serves to loosen the mixture, the next two to lighten it.
Place a spoonful of reserved puree at the bottom of each glass, then fill with the mousse.
Refrigerate for 2 to 3 hours, or serve immediately for a lighter, airier texture.

title: Banana, peanut and speculoos ice cream
intro: Everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas: well-spotted, they sweeten and bind the ice cream without adding anything.
titane: Before adding them, toast the peanuts for three to four minutes in a dry titanium pan over medium heat, stirring constantly. They should brown and release their aroma, not burn. The speculoos crumbs should be toasted for thirty seconds in the same spot, off the heat, on the still-warm pan: they will come out crispier and hold their shape better in the cold. Remove them from the pan (transfer them immediately to a cold plate) to stop the cooking process, then let them cool completely.
steps: Plan ahead: the banana slices will spend 2 hours in the freezer and then the ice cream will rest in the cold for at least 4 hours, a total of 6 hours of resting time.
Slice the bananas into regular rounds of half a centimetre. Spread them in a single layer on a sheet, without them touching.
Place in the freezer for 2 hours. The rounds must be hard to the touch.
In the meantime, toast the peanuts and speculoos as indicated above. Roughly crush them once cooled.

Blend the frozen rounds for about ten seconds, scraping down the sides once. You are aiming for a smooth and creamy texture, close to Italian ice cream. If using them, add the skyr and protein powder at this point and blend for two more seconds.
Fold in with a spatula the peanut butter, chocolate chips, crushed peanuts and speculoos. Mix briefly: streaks of peanut butter that remain visible are better than a uniform mixture.
Pour into a freezer-safe container, smooth the surface, cover with cling film to prevent ice crystals.
Return to the freezer for a minimum of 4 hours, until the ice cream is firm.
Remove it 5 minutes before serving, scoop into balls, finish with a drizzle of peanut butter and a few crushed peanut pieces.

title: Cookies filled with chestnut cream and chocolate
intro: Egg-free, with a flowing chestnut cream center: it all comes down to a lightly worked pastry and taking it out of the oven early.

ing.note: 100 g, melted and then brought back to room temperature
150g, of which 60g were set aside for the heart

titane: The filling seals when cold. Hollow out the center of the ball with the back of a spoon, add the chestnut cream, then top with a disc of dough, pinching it all around. If the seal is good, the cream will stay inside during baking. If it leaks, the dough was too warm: refrigerate for ten minutes and then try again.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), fan setting. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
In a bowl, combine the cooled butter, sugar, and 90g of chestnut cream. Mix with a spatula until smooth. Add the vanilla and Greek yogurt, and mix again.

Add the flour, yeast, and fleur de sel. Mix gently (bring the ingredients together without overworking) in just a few movements: stop as soon as the flour disappears. Overworked dough loses its softness.
Add the chocolate chips and give three or four turns of the spatula to distribute them.
Take twelve equal portions. Set aside a small third of each, roll the rest into a ball.

Hollow out each ball using the back of a teaspoon, fill with a spoonful of the reserved chestnut cream, cover with the reserved dough, and seal by pinching the edges. Place seam-side down on the baking sheet, spacing them 5 cm apart.
Bake for 12 minutes. The edges should be set and colored, the center still light and soft to the touch.
Allow to cool completely on the baking sheet: the cookies will firm up as they dry, while the center remains soft.

title: Instant banana ice cream
intro: It's all about the temperature: the bananas must come out of the freezer hard, and the liquid must be added drop by drop, otherwise you get a milkshake.

ing.note: cut into 1 cm slices and frozen at

titane: Scrape down the sides. Every twenty seconds, stop the motor and push the bits stuck to the sides towards the blades. It's this back-and-forth motion that makes the puree aerate (incorporates air) and gives it its ice-like texture, not the power of the blender.
steps: Slice the bananas into rounds **before** freezing. Whole bananas will clog the blades.
Pour the still-frozen slices into the blender bowl. Blend in short pulses until you obtain a fine semolina.
Add the milk one spoonful at a time, with the engine off between each addition. Wait until the mixture has thickened before adding more.
Blend at low speed for about 5 minutes, scraping down the sides regularly. The mixture will go from grainy to creamy all at once: stop at this precise moment.
Fold in the chocolate chips with a spatula, without remixing.
Serve immediately, in small portions. This ice cream doesn't wait.

title: Instant red fruit ice cream
intro: It all comes down to freezing: very cold and very dry fruit gives creamy ice cream, moist fruit gives crystals.
titane: Spread the fruit in a single layer, without the pieces touching. A tightly packed layer freezes slowly and forms large crystals; spaced-out pieces set quickly and remain soft when blended. The same principle applies as for searing: never overload the surface.
steps: Plan ahead: the fruit needs 2 to 3 hours in the freezer, organize accordingly.
Hull the strawberries and cut them in half. Peel the banana and slice it into 1-centimetre rounds.
Dry the fruit in a clean cloth. Surface water is the enemy of texture.
Line a baking sheet with baking paper. Distribute banana, strawberries and raspberries in a single layer, spaced apart.
Deposit the Greek yogurt in small touches between the fruit, with a spoon. These islands freeze separately and blend more easily than a block.
Place in the freezer for 2 h 30, until the fruit is firm when pierced with a knife tip.

Transfer everything to the blender with salt and sweetener if your fruit lacks ripeness. Blend in pulses, scraping the sides, until the mixture becomes light and fluffy (incorporating air) and turns smooth.
Serve immediately, in quenelles. The texture is at its best within two minutes.

title: Christmas shortbread cookies with royal icing
intro: It all comes down to two things: a dough rolled out to a constant thickness, and an icing whose texture changes depending on whether it is used for outlining or filling.
titane: Test the icing with the ribbon test: lift the spoon and let a thin stream of water fall back onto the mixture. If it disappears in five seconds without leaving a trace, the consistency is right for filling. If it remains visible longer, add water drop by drop. If it's too runny, it will overflow and nothing will fix it.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Whisk the softened butter with the sugar, salt and vanilla for 2 minutes. The mixture should lighten in color and become airy.
Add the egg, whisk again until the mixture is homogeneous.
Pour the flour in all at once. Incorporate it with a spatula, by hand or with the paddle attachment of a food processor, without overworking it: as soon as the dough comes together, stop.
Roll out the dough between two sheets of baking paper to a thickness of about 4 mm. Cut out shapes with cookie cutters and arrange them on a baking sheet.
Bake for 11 minutes. The edges should be barely colored.
Remove from the baking sheet and place on a wire rack to cool completely. A still-warm cookie will melt the icing.
Whisk the egg white with the icing sugar using a paddle attachment for 5 minutes, until you obtain a firm icing that holds its shape on the whisk.

Divide the mixture into four bowls. Leave one white, and color the other three red, brown, and black: a few drops at a time, mixing after each addition. It's easy to darken a color, but never to lighten it.
Reserve a portion of each color in its firm consistency for outlining. Dilute the rest with a few drops of water, mixing between each addition, until you reach a ribbon-like texture.
Fill piping bags and pipettes.
Outline the shape with stiff icing, let it set for a minute, then fill in the center with thinned icing. Smooth it out towards the edges with the tip of a toothpick.
Dry the shortbread cookies for 10 minutes in a 40°C oven between each layer. This creates distinct textures instead of blended colors.
Draw the details — eyes, mouth, fine lines — with black food coloring or firm black icing, once the surface is completely dry.

title: Vanilla rice pudding with pan-caramelized fruit
intro: It all comes down to the starch: a round rice that is never rinsed, never pre-cooked in water, which releases its cream into the milk for forty minutes.
titane: The pan is only used at the very end, on top of the fruit. Preheated empty, without any coating, it heats up quickly and browns evenly: the slices settle once, stay put, and release easily when the other side is set. It's this contrast—warm, caramelized fruit on fresh, creamy rice—that makes the dessert.
steps: Split the vanilla pod, scrape out the seeds. Put the seeds and pod in a saucepan with the milk. Heat over medium heat.
Pour in the dry rice without rinsing it. Bring to a simmer for one minute, then reduce to low heat.
Let cook for 30 minutes, stirring often, especially at the bottom. The rice should remain loose in the milk.
Add the sugar, stir, and continue cooking for 10 minutes. The mixture still looks quite liquid at this stage: this is normal.
Cover and remove from heat. The rice absorbs the remaining milk as it cools and develops its creamy texture. Remove the pod before serving.
Cut the fruit into thick slices, about one centimetre thick, and dust them with vanilla sugar.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Add the fat and wait until it is fluid and glossy.

Arrange the slices flat in a single layer without overlapping. Do not touch them. When they come away on their own and show a golden side, flip them and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes. The sugar browns quickly: stay by the pan.

Plate the rice pudding at room temperature, place the warm fruit on top, and coat with the caramelized juice left in the pan. If the rice has been refrigerated for a few hours, take it out about 30 minutes before serving: it will regain a softer texture this way.

title: Pecan pie
intro: It's all about the contrast: a really cooked shortcrust pastry underneath, a just-set filling, and roasted nuts that retain their crunch.
ing: Whole cane sugar or coconut sugar
titane: Dry-roast the pecans in a titanium pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring constantly. They should brown lightly and release their aroma, not smoke. Remove them from the pan immediately (transfer them to a cold plate): the residual heat will continue to cook them and make them bitter. Let them cool completely before arranging them on the tart.
steps: Plan ahead: the dough rests for at least 1 hour and the tart then cools for at least 1 hour, factor the resting time into your schedule.
Combine flour, nut powder, salt and brown sugar in a bowl. Add the cold butter and rub in (rub the butter and flour between your fingers until you obtain a coarse semolina texture).
Pour the cold water all at once. Gather without kneading, just enough to form a homogeneous ball. Flatten it into a disk.
Wrap in plastic film and refrigerate for a minimum of 1 hour. The butter must become firm again.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Toast the pecans according to the technique described above, then let them cool.
Whisk the whole sugar with the eggs. Incorporate the melted butter, cornstarch, honey and vanilla. The mixture must remain smooth, without cornstarch lumps.
Roll out the dough to 3 mm and line (cover the bottom and sides) a perforated 24 cm tart pan. Prick the bottom with a fork, trim the excess at the edge.
Pour the mixture into the tart shell, then distribute the cooled pecans over the surface. They float and form the crust.
Bake at 180 °C for 40 to 45 minutes. The filling must be set at the edges and still very slightly wobbly in the centre.
Let cool on a rack for at least 1 hour. The tart slices poorly when hot.
Whisk the very cold coconut cream with the sugar and vanilla until it holds on the whisk. Serve the tart lukewarm or cold, with a quenelle of Chantilly on the side.

title: Tiramisu-style iced latte
intro: It's all about the temperature: a scalding espresso, very cold milk, and a mascarpone mousse whipped just before serving.

ing.note: about 16, enough to fill both glasses
teaspoon, to be shared between the coffee and the
teaspoon, to be shared in the same way

titane: Pour the sweetened espresso in a thin stream, along the side of an inverted spoon resting against the glass. The coffee, hotter and lighter, remains suspended on the iced milk, creating a gradient effect. A direct pour will ruin everything in two seconds.
steps: Grind the beans at the last moment, fine and consistent grind, calibrated for espresso.
Extract two double espressos. Stop extraction when the crema on the surface remains dense and hazelnut-colored.
Divide into two small bowls half of the brown sugar and half of the vanilla.
Pour the hot espresso over and stir until the sugar dissolves completely. Let cool for two minutes.
Fill the glasses with ice cubes two-thirds full, then top up with very cold milk.
Pour the sweetened coffee using the titanium gesture, to achieve the separation of layers.
Combine in the frother pitcher the heavy cream, mascarpone, egg yolk, remaining brown sugar and remaining vanilla.
Start the cold program and let it rise (incorporate air until thickened): the foam should coat the spoon without running.
Spoon the foam onto each glass, sliding it from the back of a spoon to avoid breaking the gradient.
Dust with bitter cocoa through a small sieve.
Place a ladyfinger biscuit across the rim of the glass and serve immediately.

title: Potato, green apple and herb salad
intro: It's all about the contrast: a melting base that's still warm and soaks up the sauce, and raw elements cut at the last moment to keep some bite.
ing: New potatoes, ratte potatoes or Noirmoutier potatoes
titane: Take a third of the cooked potatoes, lightly crush them with the palm of your hand to open the flesh, then dry-fry them in a very hot titanium pan, crushed side down, for three to four minutes without touching them. This will create crispy bones that stay in the sauce instead of dissolving. Let them cool slightly before adding them back to the rest of the pan.
steps: Plan ahead: the salad rests for two to four hours in the refrigerator before serving; plan this time into your schedule.

Plunge the unpeeled potatoes into a large saucepan of cold salted water. Bring to a simmer and allow approximately 20 minutes from boiling: the tip of a knife should enter without resistance and come out on its own.
In a second saucepan, cook the eggs for 9 minutes in boiling water, then cool them immediately under running water. Shell them.
Drain the potatoes and let them cool for five minutes in the open air so they dry. Cut them in half or in quarters depending on size.
Perform the titanium technique on one third of them.
Cut the celery into fine bevel-cut slices, mince the spring onions, cut the cornichons into rounds.
Chop the dill and chives.
Cut the Granny Smith into thick batons, skin included. Work with it last so it does not oxidize and maintains its texture.
Combine the potatoes, celery, onions, cornichons, apple and herbs in a large salad bowl.
