In a bowl, combine the cold puree, oat flour, cocoa, maple syrup, melted coconut oil, vanilla, and salt. Mix until you have a smooth, pliable dough.
Line a 20cm square baking tin with baking paper, leaving two strips overhanging. Pour in the batter and press it down firmly with the back of a spoon, in an even layer all the way to the corners.
Place in the freezer for 10 to 15 minutes, until the base firms up.
Soften the cream cheese (whisk it until it becomes creamy), then stir in the honey and vanilla. Stop as soon as the mixture is smooth: if you over-whisk it, it will become runny.
Spread this layer on the cold base, smooth with a spatula.
Return to the freezer for 45 minutes. The surface should be firm to the touch.

Chop the chocolate finely. Combine it in a titanium pan with the condensed milk over very low heat. Stir continuously until the ganache (chocolate and liquid emulsion) is smooth and glossy. Remove from the heat as soon as there are no more lumps.
Let it cool for 5 minutes, then pour over the cheesecake layer and spread quickly before the ganache sets.
Freeze for 30 minutes.

Sprinkle with fleur de sel, remove the block using the paper strips, and cut into 9 bars with a blade that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry between each cut. Let it rest for 10 minutes at room temperature before serving.

title: Protein cookie and cream ice cream
intro: Everything hinges on the consistency of the egg whites: it is the air they trap that replaces the ice cream maker here.
ing: Cookie and cream flavored whey protein
titane: No pan is needed for this recipe, but the principle remains the same: the cold metal does the work for you. Place the metal container in the freezer thirty minutes before starting. Upon contact with an already frozen surface, the mixture sets from the outside immediately, and the crystals remain fine. A plastic container at room temperature will produce grainy ice.
steps: Place the empty metal container in the freezer at least 30 minutes before starting.
Pour the condensed milk into a bowl, add the protein in a steady stream and whisk until the mixture is smooth, with no lumps at the bottom of the bowl.
Whisk the egg whites until stiff peaks form (the whisk should leave a clean trail and the white should form a soft peak at the tip). Allow 3 to 4 minutes with a mixer.
Take a third of the egg whites and whisk them vigorously into the protein mixture to loosen it.

Incorporate the remaining egg whites in two batches, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from the bottom up and rotating the bowl a quarter turn with each pass. Stop as soon as the mixture is homogeneous.
Pour into the cold container, smooth the surface and place in the freezer for about 2 hours, until a spoon sinks in with slight resistance.

title: Madeleines with almond puree and dates
intro: With no added flour or sugar, everything relies on the balance between the egg which binds, the nut puree which provides the fat and the compote which sweetens.

ing.note: or the equivalent in raisins or dried apricots

titane: Lightly grease each mold with a little nut butter before pouring in the batter. It's less sticky than regular butter during baking and adds flavor to the shells. Fill them two-thirds full: the batter doesn't rise much but overflows easily.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Beat the egg in a bowl until it is smooth, with the white and yolk well mixed.
Add the nut puree. Mix by hand, without whisking: the dough should become smooth and slightly thick.
Stir in the applesauce. It loosens the mixture (the base mixture) and gives it its sweetness.
Cut the dates into small cubes, about the size of a grain of rice. If they are too big, they will sink to the bottom of the molds.
Mix the diced dates into the dough in two batches to distribute them evenly.
Fill the cavities of a small madeleine mold two-thirds full.
Bake for 15 minutes. The edges should be set and browned, the center still soft to the touch.
Let them cool for 5 minutes in the mold before unmolding: when hot, the madeleines tear.

title: Vegetable patty with feta
intro: It all comes down to how the vegetables are seared: brightly colored in the titanium pan, they arrive on the pastry with juices that the oven alone never gives.
ing: semi-salted butter taken out of the refrigerator

ing.note: or a few sprigs of thyme

titane: Preheat the pan empty, then work the vegetables in small batches. A full pan cools down, and the vegetables release their water instead of browning. Let each slice stick together, then release on its own: that's the signal to flip it without tearing it. The galette, however, ends up in the oven—34 cm of batter to brown on top; the pan can't help you with that.
steps: Place the titanium pan to heat up empty, over high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the eggplant and zucchini into even rounds. Halve the cherry tomatoes.

Pour the olive oil into the hot pan. Add a first batch of vegetables in a single layer, and season with salt. Let them brown without touching them, then turn them over when they begin to separate easily. Reduce the heat to medium if they are browning too quickly. Allow about fifteen minutes in total, batch after batch.
Remove the vegetables as they are cooked (transfer them to a separate dish to stop the cooking process).
While the dough is resting, combine flour, butter, egg, water, and salt in a bowl. Knead until a smooth ball forms, without overworking. Refrigerate.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Roll out the dough (roll it out with a rolling pin) on a sheet of parchment paper, into a disc of 32 to 35 cm. Prick it with a fork and slide it onto a baking sheet.
Spread the mustard on the base, leaving a 4 cm margin all around.
Crumble half the feta cheese over the mustard. Arrange the seared vegetables on top, then the remaining feta.
Fold the pastry margin over the filling, pleating at each fold.
Bake for 32 minutes, until the pastry is golden brown and firm to the touch.
Sprinkle with basil after removing from the oven, just before serving.

title: Shredded beef quesadillas with dried chilies
intro: It all comes down to two steps: the meat is simmered long enough to fall apart on its own, and then browned thoroughly in the pan to create the crust.
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. For quesadillas, use a high smoke point oil (like grapeseed oil), then do nothing more: the tortilla will stick at first, then release on its own once the crust has formed. That's the only sign you need to wait for. Simmering, however, is best done in a Dutch oven: more than a liter of sauce and four hours of cooking are not suitable for a pan.
steps: Peel the onions and slice them thinly. Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then pour a thin stream of grapeseed oil. Sweat the onions and garlic over medium heat (cook without browning until they become translucent and fragrant), 4 to 5 minutes.

Trim and seed the ancho and guajillo peppers. Transfer the onions to a Dutch oven, add the peppers, the tomatoes cut into quarters, the broth, the enchilada sauce, garlic salt, cumin, paprika, pepper and oregano. Bring to a light simmer and let cook for 15 minutes.
Blend the sauce until you obtain a smooth texture, then pour it back into the Dutch oven. Strain it through a fine mesh sieve if you want a finer sauce.
Immerse the beef in the sauce, cover and let cook over very low heat for 4 hours. Stir every 45 minutes and check the liquid level: the meat must remain submerged three-quarters.
Remove the meat, shred it with two forks (break it into strands along the grain), then return it to the reduced sauce. Chop the fresh cilantro and add it.
Fill each tortilla with shredded meat drained and mozzarella, then fold in half. Keep the remaining sauce aside for dipping.

Wipe the titanium pan, preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add a thin stream of grapeseed oil. Place the quesadillas and do not move them: they are ready to turn when they detach on their own and show an even crust. Allow 2 to 3 minutes per side.

For freezing: let cool completely, wrap individually in aluminium foil or a freezer bag, for up to 3 months. Reheat in the microwave for 3 to 4 minutes under a damp paper towel, then return to the preheated pan for 2 minutes to restore crispiness.

title: Sandwich with crushed white beans and dill pickles
intro: It's all about the texture: coarsely crushed beans, never pureed, so that the filling stays in the bread without collapsing.
titane: Toss the bread slices in a dry, hot titanium pan, without any oil or butter, for one minute per side. The surface will dry out and form a barrier, preventing the moist topping from soaking through the crumb. Transfer the bread to a wire rack, not a plate, to avoid condensation.
steps: Drain and rinse the beans, then pat them dry with a kitchen towel. The less water they retain, the better the filling will hold together.
Combine the beans, gherkins, celery, red onion and dill in a large bowl.
Add the yogurt, lemon juice, mustard and salt. Mash with a fork using short pressing motions: aim for a lumpy mixture where about a third of the beans remain whole.
Taste. Adjust the seasoning with salt, then lemon if the mixture lacks tang.
Toast the bread slices dry in the titanium pan, one minute per side, and let them cool slightly on a rack.
Spread a thin layer of mayonnaise on both inner sides. Distribute the filling, top with arugula, sprouts and pickled onions, close the sandwich. Press gently for a moment, then slice diagonally.

title: Peanut butter and white bean cookies
intro: It all comes down to the blending: a perfectly smooth bean puree leaves no trace in the mouth, and it is this that gives it its soft texture.
titane: Drain the beans, rinse them thoroughly in cold water, then dry them with a cloth. The canning liquid imparts a bitter, vegetal flavor that sugar won't mask. Blend them on their own for thirty seconds before adding anything else: the purée develops its smooth texture during this first pass, not subsequent ones.
steps: Drain and rinse the white beans under cold water before blending.
Preheat the oven to 175°C, fan setting. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Blend the white beans alone until you obtain a smooth puree without any grains. Scrape the sides of the bowl once during the process.
Add the peanut butter, sugar, vanilla, flour and baking powder. Blend again until you have a homogeneous and sticky dough. It should coat the spatula.
Transfer the dough out of the blender bowl into a mixing bowl. Fold in the chocolate chips with a spatula, without overworking the mixture.

Form ten balls using an ice cream scoop, place them on the baking sheet spacing them 4 cm apart, then flatten them slightly with your damp fingertips. The dough barely spreads during baking, so give them their final shape now.
Bake for 26 to 28 minutes. The edges should be golden and firm, the centre still soft to the touch.
Let cool for 10 minutes on the baking sheet, then on a cooling rack. The cookies will only hold their shape once cooled.

title: No-bake protein cookie dough
intro: It all comes down to hydration: oat bran absorbs a lot of water, and it is by watering it in stages that you obtain a dense paste rather than a porridge.
titane: Moisten in two stages. First, pour in the fromage blanc alone and work until the mixture is smooth and compact. Then, loosen (soften) the mixture with milk, spoonful by spoonful. Stop as soon as the mixture holds its shape on the spatula without running. If you mix everything at once, the bran will expand too quickly in the center and leave dry lumps.
steps: Plan ahead: an optional rest of 30 minutes in the cold may be necessary for a firmer consistency
Combine in a mixing bowl the oat bran, whey and peanut butter powder. Mix dry to distribute the powders evenly.
Add the cottage cheese. Work with a spatula until completely absorbed: the mixture becomes compact and slightly stiff.
Loosen with milk, in small amounts, stirring between each addition. Aim for a thick and creamy texture that holds the mark of the spatula.
Fold in the chocolate chips, lifting the mixture gently, without crushing, so that they remain whole and evenly distributed.
Divide between two bowls. Enjoy as is, or place in the cold for 30 minutes for a firmer consistency and a chew closer to cookie dough.

title: Shokupan with tangzhong, spicy tuna tartine
intro: It all comes down to the tangzhong: this cooked flour porridge retains water in the crumb and keeps the bread soft for three days.

ing.note: plus a little diluted yellow for the gilding

ing: Canned tuna in its own juices, well drained
titane: Tangzhong is made in a titanium pan, not a saucepan. The thin base reacts quickly: whisk continuously over medium heat and remove from the heat as soon as the whisk leaves a clear trail on the bottom. Two seconds too long and the porridge will clump. Remove immediately (transfer to a cold container) to stop the cooking process, then cover with plastic wrap, pressing it directly onto the surface.
steps: In a titanium pan, whisk the tangzhong flour into the water while cold. Heat over medium heat, whisking constantly, until you obtain a thick, smooth cream. Remove from heat, cover with plastic wrap, and let cool slightly.
Pour the flour, plant-based milk, egg, salt, yeast, and cooled tangzhong into the bowl of a stand mixer. Knead for 5 minutes on low speed, then 5 minutes on medium speed (3 or 4).
Add the olive oil. Knead for another 2 to 3 minutes: the dough should pull away from the sides and form a thin film when you stretch it between your fingers.
Cover. Let rise for 1 to 2 hours at room temperature, until doubled in volume.
Deflate the dough, divide it into three equal pieces. Roll each piece out into a rectangle, fold the sides towards the middle, rotate a quarter turn, roll out again, then roll tightly onto itself.
Place the three rolls side by side, seam underneath, in an oiled bread tin. Let rise for at least 1 hour: the dough should reach the edge.
Brush gently with egg wash. Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Bake for 30 minutes. The crust should be evenly golden and the bottom should sound hollow.
Turn out onto a wire rack. Wait until completely cool before cutting into nine slices.
For the filling, mix the cottage cheese, tomato paste and gochujang until evenly colored.
Stir in the flaked tuna, finely chopped spring onion, salt, and honey. Taste: the acidity of the tomato should remain subtle.
Spread over two slices, then drizzle with light mayonnaise at the last moment.

title: Morning cake with red lentils and oat flakes
intro: Coral lentils replace flour here: they provide softness and structure without being recognizable for a single second by their taste.
ing: and a half of agave syrup
titane: Before adding them, dry-roast the oats in a titanium pan over medium heat for two to three minutes, stirring constantly. They should be lightly browned and smell nutty. This dry toasting is what gives the cake its toasted cereal flavor, whereas a raw batter would remain flat. Immediately transfer them from the pan to a cold bowl; on hot metal, they would continue to cook and turn bitter.
steps: Rinse the red lentils under cold water. Plunge them into a large volume of boiling water and let them cook for 30 minutes at a gentle boil until they break apart under the pressure of a spoon.
Drain them in a fine strainer, then rinse under cold water to stop the cooking. Let them drain for a few minutes: a batter that is too wet will not rise.
Toast the oat flakes as indicated above, then let them cool.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Line a 22 cm mould with baking paper.
Blend the lentils with the coconut milk, eggs and agave syrup until you obtain a perfectly smooth batter. Add the toasted flakes and blend for a few more seconds, keeping some texture.
Fold in the bicarbonate of soda, then the lemon juice. The batter foams slightly: pour it immediately into the mould.
Peel the banana, cut it into slices, arrange them on the surface with the chocolate chips. Press them in only slightly, they will sink on their own.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes. A knife blade inserted in the centre should come out dry. Let it cool in the mould before turning out: the cake firms up as it cools.

title: Sweet potato squares with nut caramel and dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the base: a very dry and smooth sweet potato puree, otherwise the base remains soft under the caramel.
titane: The caramel and chocolate melt in the titanium pan, off the heat or on the lowest setting: the heat is distributed evenly enough to avoid a double boiler, and the surface can be rinsed with a sponge. However, roasting the sweet potato and cooking the base of the dish are best done in the oven, which is the only way to provide consistent, even heat.
steps: Roast a large, whole, unpeeled sweet potato for 60 minutes at 200°C (400°F), until a knife blade pierces it easily. Split it lengthwise, scoop out the flesh, and then purée it until smooth. Weigh out 200g and let it cool slightly.
Lower the oven to 180°C. Line a 20cm square baking tin (line it with baking paper, leaving two edges overhanging for easy removal).
Mix the puree, almond flour, melted butter and salt until you obtain a soft, cohesive dough.
Press the dough firmly and evenly into the mold. Smooth with a spatula: the thickness must be the same everywhere, otherwise the cut will be uneven.
Bake for 20 minutes at 180°C: the edges will brown, and the surface will become firm to the touch. Let it cool completely in the pan, without rushing.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then remove it from the heat. Pour in the nut butter, maple syrup, vanilla, and salt. Work with a spatula over the residual heat until the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Spread this caramel evenly over the cold base. Place in the freezer for 40 minutes, until firm.

Melt the dark chocolate with the coconut oil in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring constantly. As soon as the mixture is smooth, remove from the heat and pour over the firm caramel. Tilt the mold to spread.
Refrigerate until the chocolate is completely set. Unmold, then cut into 12 squares with a blade that has been dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: White cheese and whey milkshake
intro: It all comes down to temperature and duration: ice cubes rather than water, and a short blend, otherwise the foam will collapse.
titane: The whey protein goes in last, placed on top of the already cold cottage cheese. The blades first attack the ice; the powder is gradually drawn into the vortex and hydrates without forming lumps. The opposite results in a paste stuck to the bottom of the bowl.
steps: Pour the cottage cheese into the blender bowl. Add the ice cubes on top.
Place the whey protein dose last, on top, without mixing.
Blend for 30 seconds, no more. The mixture should be thick and frothy, with a visibly increased volume.
Transfer immediately into a tall glass and drink within a minute: the foam settles quickly.

title: Chocolate and cauliflower ice cream
intro: The cauliflower here brings neither taste nor color: it brings creaminess, and replaces cream without weighing down the chocolate.
titane: Before blending, dry out the cooked cauliflower in a titanium pan (evaporate its water over high heat, stirring constantly). Three to four minutes is enough: the purée should separate from the bottom of the pan in one piece. Without this step, the vegetable's residual water will crystallize in the cold and the ice cream will become grainy.
steps: Drain the cauliflower and press it between two sheets of absorbent paper.
Heat the pan dry over high heat. Add the cauliflower, mash it with a spatula and dry it out for 3 to 4 minutes, until the puree forms a compact and matte mass.
Roughly chop the milk chocolate. Pour it into the blender bowl with the still-hot puree and hot water.

Blend for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down the sides once. The heat from the puree will melt the chocolate. Stop when the mixture is perfectly smooth, glossy, and has the consistency of a thick smoothie.
Add the salt, blend for another 10 seconds.
Transfer (to another container) into a shallow tray, smooth the surface, cover with cling film.
Freeze for a minimum of 4 hours. Remove the ice cream from the freezer 10 minutes before serving and work it with a spoon to loosen it.

title: Cucumber and chickpeas, peanut sauce
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the sauce: thick enough to coat the chickpeas, yet flexible enough not to weigh them down.
titane: Before assembling, toast the sesame seeds for two minutes in a dry titanium pan over medium heat, without any oil. Stir continuously. They are ready when they turn golden and begin to pop. Transfer them immediately to a cold plate; otherwise, the residual heat from the metal will continue to cook them.
steps: Drain and rinse the cooked chickpeas.

Place the peanut butter in a bowl. Add two spoonfuls of plant-based yogurt and whisk until there are no lumps. Incorporate the remaining yogurt in three additions: the sauce should remain smooth and glossy.
Season this base with soy sauce, maple syrup and paprika. Salt cautiously, as soy sauce already provides salt. Pepper. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

Wash the cucumber. Split it in half lengthwise and remove the central seeds with a spoon if they are well developed: they would release water into the sauce. Cut into thick half-moons, about one centimetre thick.
Combine cucumber and chickpeas in a salad bowl. Pour the sauce and mix with a spatula, lifting from underneath, to coat without crushing the chickpeas.
Divide between two shallow bowls, building the salad into a dome rather than spreading it flat.
Crumble the lacto-fermented tofu over the top. Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, then drizzle with chilli oil over the surface. Serve immediately, before the cucumber releases its water.

title: Cookie and cream protein milkshake
intro: It all comes down to overrun (incorporating air into a preparation to give it volume): a shaker gives a flat drink, a blender gives a milkshake.
ing: whey protein cookie and cream flavor
titane: No pan here, so no need to worry about stirring: the trick is to start the blender at full power right away, without pausing. A gradual increase in speed circulates the liquid around the ice cubes. The full power creates a vortex that draws the foam down and then pumps it back in, and it's this cycle that thickens the texture in less than a minute. Turn it off as soon as the motor noise stabilizes and the mixture starts to climb the sides of the blender.
steps: Pour the almond milk into the blender bowl, then add the whey protein on top. In this order: the powder placed on the liquid will disperse without sticking to the bottom.
Add the ice cubes and a pinch of salt.
Blend at full power for 1 minute, until you get a frothy and airy texture, noticeably thicker than at the start.
Pour into a large glass and drink immediately: the foam will subside in a few minutes.

title: Date, peanut and chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to the consistency of the three layers: a tightly packed pressed base, a date caramel firm enough not to leak, and a chilling period between each layer.
titane: Roast the peanuts (dry-roast them to develop their aroma) in a titanium pan over medium heat, without any oil. Stir continuously for 4 to 5 minutes, until they turn golden brown and release their fragrance. Immediately transfer them to a cold plate: the pan retains heat and would continue to cook them. Warm, dry peanuts adhere better to the caramel than peanuts straight from the bag.
steps: Plan ahead: resting and freezing totalling approximately 1 hour 20, the bars must be very firm before unmoulding.
Line the loaf tin with parchment paper, leaving two tabs overhanging on the long sides: these will be used for unmoulding.
Mix the almond flour, maple syrup, coconut oil and salt until you obtain a moist sand that holds when you squeeze it in your hand.
Pour into the tin and press down firmly with your fingertips, then smooth with the back of a spoon. The base must be compact and of even thickness.
Place in the freezer for 10 minutes.
Toast the peanuts in a pan according to the method described above. Set aside.
Blend the dates, peanut butter, coconut oil, maple syrup and one tablespoon of hot water. Stop when the mixture is smooth, thick and sticky.
Add the remaining hot water one tablespoon at a time, blending between each addition. Aim for a soft caramel texture that falls in a ribbon without running.
Spread the caramel over the cold base in an even layer right to the edges. Return to the freezer for 10 minutes.
Melt the chocolate chips with the coconut oil in a bain-marie, or in the microwave in 10-second intervals, stirring after each stop. The chocolate must be smooth and never hot to the touch.
Remove the tin, distribute the peanuts over the caramel and press them gently to anchor them.
Coat with melted chocolate in drizzles, then sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Freeze for 1 hour, until the whole is firm.
Unmould by pulling on the tabs. Cut into 8 bars with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Pasta with seared beef and chipotle cream
intro: It all comes down to the beef crust: a really hot pan, fat that holds the temperature, and no hands on the meat during searing.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat before adding the oil or butter. The titanium coating withstands this heat without damage, resulting in a crisp crust in just a few minutes. The same pan is then used to combine the pasta and sauce, off the high heat: you only need one container for searing and assembling the pasta.
steps: Cut the beef into even pieces. Season with garlic salt and black pepper, mix by hand to distribute.
Peel the garlic. Blend the cottage cheese, parmesan, garlic, chipotles, garlic salt, pepper and milk until you obtain a perfectly smooth sauce. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook the pasta, drain it while keeping one ladle of cooking water.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes on high heat. Add the clarified butter or grape seed oil.

Place the beef in a single layer, without overcrowding. Do not move it: it will release from the pan on its own when the crust is formed. Flip, sear the other side, set aside (transfer to a separate dish).
Lower the heat to minimum. Pour the drained pasta into the pan, add the sauce and mix until it is coated. Loosen with a little cooking water if the sauce thickens too much.
Distribute the beef over the pasta, sprinkle with chives.
For meal prep: portion into 10 airtight containers. The portions can be frozen for up to 3 months.

When reheating, remove a container from the freezer and remove the lid. Add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a damp paper towel and allow 5 to 6 minutes in the microwave, stirring halfway through.

title: Oven-dried tomatoes
intro: Three hours in a gentle oven is enough to remove the water without cooking the flesh: all the sugar and acidity of the tomato remain, simply concentrated.
titane: Scoop out the insides of the tomato segments with a spoon, including the seeds and membranes, leaving only the petal (the firm outer layer of the tomato, covered in its moist pulp). It's this internal moisture that slows down drying and helps the petals stick together. Place them skin-side down: the skin protects, while the flesh opens up to the warm air.
steps: Preheat the oven to 100°C, fan-assisted if you have it.
Cut the tomatoes into quarters. Hollow out each quarter, leaving only the petal.
Arrange the petals on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, skin side down, without them touching each other.
Add salt, sprinkle with stevia, and scatter with herbes de Provence.
Bake for 3 hours. The petals should be soft, dark, distinctly shrunk, without the slightest bead of water on the surface.
Let them cool completely on the baking sheet. Then stack them, layering them with parchment paper, and freeze.

title: Protein mac and cheese that can be prepared in advance
intro: It all comes down to the sauce: when blended cold, it remains smooth when reheated instead of separating into grains and fat.
titane: When ready to serve, warm a portion in a titanium pan with a tablespoon of water over medium heat. Spread it evenly over the surface, then let it sit for thirty seconds. A thin, golden, and slightly brittle cheese crust will form on contact. Loosen it with a spatula and mix it into the portion: this toasted layer is what makes the difference between a simply reheated dish and a more substantial one.
steps: Plan ahead: mac and cheese freezes for up to three months and one portion must thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating in a pan, anticipate this resting time.
Combine in the food processor bowl the cottage cheese, cream cheese, cheese powder, grated cheddar, milk, garlic salt and pepper.
Process at full speed until you obtain a homogeneous sauce, with no visible cottage cheese grains. Scrape the sides once along the way. Allow two minutes: the texture should coat the blade.
Bring a large volume of salted water to a boil. Cook the protein pasta one minute less than the indicated time: they will finish softening during reheating.
Drain without rinsing, keeping a ladleful of cooking water aside.
Return the pasta to the saucepan off the heat, pour the sauce and mix until completely coated. If the mixture seems tight, loosen with a little reserved cooking water.
Transfer into ten portions in airtight containers. Let cool uncovered before sealing, to avoid condensation.
Freeze for up to three months.

To reheat: either in a titanium pan, according to the gesture described above, starting from the portion thawed overnight in the refrigerator; or in the microwave, removing the lid and adding one to two tablespoons of water to the portion still frozen, covered with a damp paper towel, five to six minutes stirring halfway through.

title: Cucumbers with plant-based yogurt and peanut butter
intro: It all comes down to the cucumber water: if you leave it in the bowl, the sauce will dilute and the peanut butter will disappear.
titane: Dry-roast the sesame seeds (without oil) in the cold titanium pan, then increase the heat to medium. Stir constantly. As soon as two or three seeds pop and a nutty aroma rises, transfer them to a cold plate: the residual heat from the titanium pan would continue to cook them.
steps: Slice the cucumbers into thin slices, approximately 2 mm. A mandoline provides the regularity that a knife cannot achieve.
Salt the slices with half of the herb salt and let them release their water in a colander for 5 minutes. Press lightly between your palms, without crushing.
In a bowl, dilute the peanut butter with a spoonful of plant-based yogurt until you obtain a smooth paste. Add the remaining yogurt and the grated garlic.
Pour the drained cucumbers into the bowl. Mix with a spoon, lifting gently, to coat each slice without breaking them.
Adjust the seasoning with the remaining herb salt and pepper. The sauce should remain creamy, not liquid.
Toast the sesame seeds dry in a pan, stirring, until they turn golden.
Arrange in a dome shape in a shallow dish and sprinkle with toasted sesame at the last moment, so it remains crispy.

title: Tarator, cold cucumber yogurt soup
intro: It all comes down to temperature: yogurt, water and cucumber must be taken from the cold, otherwise the soup becomes bland.
titane: Dry-roast the walnuts in the titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring constantly. No oil is needed: the coating is sufficient, and the dry heat releases the oil from the kernels. Remove them as soon as they become fragrant and transfer them immediately to a cold plate; otherwise, they will continue to cook and turn bitter.
steps: Toast the walnuts as indicated above, let them cool, then chop them roughly with a knife. Keep irregular pieces: it is the only texture of the recipe.
Peel the cucumber in alternating strips and cut it into small 5 mm dice. Avoid a grater, which releases too much water and dilutes the soup.
Strip the dill leaves and chop them finely. Reserve a pinch for serving.
In a bowl, thin the yogurt with cold water, in three additions, whisking. Pour all at once and the mixture will curdle.
Add the cucumber, dill, walnuts and salt. Mix with a spoon.
Pour in the lemon juice, taste, adjust the salt. The tarator should be distinctly tangy and salty: the cold will mute both.
Chill for 30 minutes in the refrigerator. Serve in cold bowls, with the reserved dill and a few walnut fragments on the surface.

title: Homemade almond milk
intro: It all comes down to soaking: plump almonds produce a dense and creamy milk, dry almonds a pale and thin juice.

ing.note: cl, enough to amply cover the almonds

titane: Don't throw away the pulp. Spread it in a dry, oil-free titanium pan over very low heat. Stir with a spatula every minute for 8 to 10 minutes, until it becomes sandy and no longer sticks. You will obtain almond flour ready to be toasted (dry-heated to develop the aromas), which you can store in a jar for up to a week.
steps: Plan ahead: the almonds soak overnight, 8 hours minimum, start the day before.
Place the almonds in a large bowl. Cover with cold water by about three good centimetres: they will absorb and swell.
Leave to soak in the refrigerator overnight, 8 hours minimum. The almonds should be soft to the touch and have lost their brittleness.
Discard the soaking water, which is cloudy and bitter. Rinse the almonds under clear running water until they are no longer slippery.
Put them in the blender bowl with one litre of cold water. Blend for 2 minutes at full power: the liquid should be uniformly white, with no visible sheen.
Strain the mixture through a fine cloth over a bowl and gather the edges, twist, then press firmly with both hands until the pulp yields nothing more.
Pour the milk into a bottle and keep it for 3 days in the cold. Shake before each use, it separates naturally. Reserve the pulp for the titanium gesture.

title: Banana and peanut ice cream, protein almond paste
intro: It's all about the texture: a very smooth blended base before freezing, and a dough that's soft enough to stay moist when cold.
titane: Place the empty titanium pan in the freezer for thirty minutes. When ready to serve, pour in the frozen ice cream and work it for twenty seconds with a spatula: the very cold metal breaks up the ice crystals without melting the mixture. You'll get a creamy texture, similar to churned sorbet.
steps: Peel the banana, cut it into chunks. Place it in the blender bowl with the cottage cheese and the first spoonful of peanut butter.
Blend until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture, without any banana grains. Allow about one minute, scraping down the sides once.
Pour into a wide, shallow container, cover with plastic wrap. Freeze for at least 4 hours. A thin layer sets more quickly and more evenly than a thick mass.
Meanwhile, mix the almond powder, whey, honey, the second spoonful of peanut butter and the chocolate chips.
Add the plant-based milk spoonful by spoonful, working by hand, until you have a homogeneous paste that rolls without sticking. Stop as soon as it holds together in a ball.
Shape small irregular pieces of paste, keep them in the cold while the ice cream sets.
Remove the ice cream, scrape it with a spoon or work it in the frozen pan, then fold in the paste pieces without stirring too much: you want distinct flakes, not a uniform mixture.
Divide among three bowls, drizzle with a little sugar-free topping and serve immediately.

title: Pan-fried chili sin carne
intro: Textured soy is only worthwhile if it is dry-colored before being added to the sauce: that's when it gets its flavor and texture.
titane: Rehydrate the soy protein, squeeze it firmly between your hands, then drop it into a very hot, lightly oiled pan. Let it sit for a full minute before stirring. It should brown in patches and sizzle. If you add it wet, it will boil and remain spongy. Titanium handles this dry heat better than a conventional coating: take advantage of this to achieve a deep hazelnut brown.
steps: Pour the boiling water over the soy protein. Let it soak for 10 minutes, then drain and squeeze firmly to remove as much water as possible.
Start the rice separately in a pan of salted water or until it reaches the absorption stage. It should be ready at the same time as the chili.

Heat a dry pan over high heat. Add a tablespoon of oil, then the pressed soybeans in a single layer. Leave for one minute, then stir and continue cooking for 3 to 4 minutes until browned. Remove from the pan (transfer to a plate to free up space).
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the second tablespoon of oil, the sliced red onion, and the minced garlic. Sauté for 4 minutes without browning, until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the paprika and cumin. Stir for 30 seconds in the hot oil: the spices should be fragrant but not smoking.
Add the soy sauce back in, pour in the tomato sauce. Scrape the bottom with a spatula to loosen the juices (the colored residues attached to the bottom, which carry the flavor).
Simmer uncovered for 20 minutes over low heat, stirring every 5 minutes. The sauce should coat the back of a spoon and leave a clean trail when a spatula passes through it.
Add the kidney beans and corn. Continue for 5 minutes, just long enough to warm them through without mashing them.
Season with salt and pepper, taste. Remove from heat and add the parsley. Serve over rice.

title: Pumpkin seed granola and small savory tahini brioches
intro: Two preparations, one pan that goes from the worktop to the oven: what matters here is the thickness of the granola layer, thin and even, otherwise the top will color while the bottom remains moist.
ing: Pumpkin seeds, or an assortment of nuts and seeds
titane: Spread the granola in a single layer, without packing it down, leaving a two-centimeter border against the edge of the pan. The metal heats up faster there, so the flakes resting on it will burn before the others. Halfway through cooking, gently fold the center towards the outside and vice versa.
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C, fan-assisted.
In a bowl, combine the oats, seeds, cinnamon, and raisins. Pour in the melted coconut oil and then the maple syrup. Mix by hand until each oat is coated and the mixture forms small clumps.
Transfer to the cold pan. Spread in a thin, even layer. Bake for 15 minutes, stirring after 7 to 8 minutes.
Transfer the granola from the baking container to a cold plate in a single layer. It hardens as it cools; that's when it becomes crunchy, not when it comes out of the oven.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. In a bowl, whisk together the tahini and egg until you have a smooth, thick paste, then gently fold in the pesto to keep some marbling.
Wipe the pan clean and lightly oil it. Place four heaped spoonfuls of batter in the pan, spaced apart: they will spread slightly in the heat.
Bake for 20 minutes. The brioches are cooked when the tops are set and dry to the touch, but the centers are still soft. Let them cool in the pan for 5 minutes before removing them from the pan.

title: Inside-out maki with smoked salmon, avocado and cucumber
intro: It all comes down to the rice: well seasoned, still warm when assembling, it holds the roll together without having to be squeezed like a vise.
titane: Dry-roast the sesame seeds in the titanium pan over medium heat for two minutes, shaking constantly. As soon as they pop and release their nutty aroma, remove them from the pan and transfer them to a cold plate; the residual cast iron would burn them in seconds.
steps: Rinse the rice in cold water until the water runs clear. Cook it in water in a dedicated pan over medium heat for about fifteen minutes, then let it rest covered. It should be sticky, never mushy.
Dissolve the sugar and salt in the rice vinegar. Pour over the hot rice and mix with a spatula, cutting through the mass rather than crushing it. Let it cool to room temperature.
Stretch a large sheet of plastic wrap on the board. Spread the smoked salmon slices over it, overlapping them slightly, to form a rectangle with no gaps.
Cover with a layer of rice one centimeter thick, with damp hands so it doesn't stick. Place a sheet of nori on top, then spread the cream cheese in an even layer.
Peel the avocado and remove the pit. Cut the cucumber into thin slices and the avocado into slices. Arrange them in tight bands on the cream cheese.
Add the second sheet of nori and press with the flat of your hand to remove any air.
Finish with a final layer of rice and compact the whole thing using the plastic wrap until you have a firm block. Chill for 10 minutes.
Unmold onto the board, remove the plastic wrap, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. Cut into portions with a smooth-bladed knife, wiped and moistened between each cut.

title: Buffalo breaded chicken and creamy mac & cheese
intro: It all comes down to the cornflake coating: it must remain dry and crunchy until the moment the buffalo sauce touches it, not a second before.
titane: Breaded chicken is cooked in a very hot titanium pan, not in the oven. Place the pieces loosely in the pan, leaving a finger's width between each one: the breading needs room to breathe. Don't move them for the first three minutes. The crust will release on its own once it's set; if you have to force it, it's too soon. Cook in four batches rather than two overcrowded ones.
steps: Cut the chicken into cubes of approximately 2.5 cm. Consistency is everything: equal-sized pieces cook together.
Mix the flour, garlic salt, 7 g black pepper and cayenne in a large shallow dish.
In a second dish, whisk the egg whites, pickle juice and hot sauce.
Crush the corn flakes by hand into coarse pieces rather than powder. Pour them into a third dish.
Coat the chicken cubes in the spiced flour, tap to remove excess, dip them in the egg white mixture, then press them into the corn flakes to coat. Reserve on a rack, never flat on a plate.

Heat the titanium pan over high heat, oil lightly. Sear the chicken in four batches, 3 minutes on the first side, 2 to 3 minutes on the second side. Remove from the pan and reserve on a rack between each batch.
Meanwhile, blend the cottage cheese, mac & cheese preparation, cream cheese, onion powder, 3 g black pepper and milk in a blender. Blend until the sauce coats the blade without graininess.
Cook the pasta in salted water, one minute less than the package instructions. Drain while reserving one ladle of cooking water.
Return the pasta to the saucepan off the heat, pour in the cheese sauce and mix. Loosen with the reserved cooking water until you reach a texture that flows slowly from the spoon.
Coat the chicken with buffalo sauce at the very last moment, turning it twice in a salad bowl. Plate over the pasta.

For storage, divide into 10 portions, pasta underneath, chicken on top without prolonged contact with the sauce. Keeps for 3 months in the freezer. When reheating, add a spoonful of water, cover with a damp cloth and allow 5 to 6 minutes in the microwave, stirring halfway through.

title: Beef stir-fried in garlic butter and fried rice
intro: It all comes down to the cutting of the beef and the discipline of the batches: thin slices, a hot pan, and the rice left to face the heat alone.
titane: Heat the dry skillet until a drop of water rolls in a ball on the surface instead of sizzling. This is the searing point. Cook the beef in three batches: an overcrowded skillet cools down, the juices run out, and the meat boils. Between batches, wipe away any burnt bits with a paper towel folded in a tong, and let the skillet reheat.
steps: Whisk together in a bowl the mayonnaise, ketchup, sugar, vinegar, garlic salt, smoked paprika, onion powder and pepper. The sauce should be smooth and glossy. Keep chilled.
Mix the beef strips with the soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic salt and pepper. Let marinate for 15 minutes at room temperature, then pat dry. Wet meat does not sear properly.
Break up the cold rice by hand, grain by grain. Drizzle it with the remaining soy sauce and sesame oil, mix until the color is even.

Heat the pan dry according to the indicator above. Sear the beef in three batches, in a single layer, 90 seconds on one side, 45 seconds on the other. Remove from the pan and keep covered after each batch.
Lower to medium heat. Beat the eggs, pour them into the pan and scramble them roughly in 40 seconds, still slightly runny. Remove with the beef.

Turn the heat back up. Add the frozen vegetables to the dry pan, let the water evaporate for 2 minutes, then add the rice. Spread it out, let it stick for 1 minute without stirring, then stir. Repeat three times: it is this still contact that gives the grains their crispness.
Push the rice to one side. Place the butter and minced garlic in the empty space, let the garlic turn golden for 30 seconds, add the honey and chili crisp. Stir this emulsion for 20 seconds.
Return the beef and eggs to the pan, mix everything with the garlic butter for 1 minute, no longer.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions. Serve with the yum yum sauce on the side.

title: Gluten-free blueberry cake
intro: A gluten-free cake depends mainly on two things: a dough rich enough to remain moist without a gluten network, and fruit that does not migrate to the bottom.

ing.note: or 50 g of additional gluten-free mix

titane: Roll the blueberries in a spoonful of flour before mixing them into the batter. The dry skin helps the batter adhere and keeps the fruit suspended while it rises. This batter, however, requires an oven: heat from the bottom alone would burn the underside of the crust before the center sets. Save the titanium pan for the variation at the end of the recipe.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a cake tin (line it with baking paper up to the edges).
Whisk the olive oil and eggs until the mixture is smooth and without any visible separation.
Add the skyr, maple syrup and salt. Mix well: the mixture should be smooth and homogeneous.
Incorporate the gluten-free flour mix and hazelnut powder. Mix just enough so that no dry lumps remain.
Add the baking soda and vanilla. Mix briefly one last time.
Roll the blueberries in the reserved spoonful of flour, shake off the excess, then fold them in with a spatula in two or three movements.
Pour into the mold, smooth the surface and bake for 45 minutes.

Check for doneness: the top should be golden brown and firm, and a knife inserted into the center should come out clean. Let it cool slightly in the pan before unmolding (removing the preparation from its container).

title: Noodles with gochujang and crispy beef
intro: It's all about the contrast: truly crispy meat placed on noodles coated in a creamy and spicy sauce.
titane: Only the beef should be seared in the titanium pan, and it benefits greatly from it. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, until a drop of water just begins to float. Work in small batches: an overcrowded pan will cause the meat to sweat instead of browning. Spread the meat out, press it against the bottom, then leave it alone. It will release on its own once a crust has formed. Noodles, on the other hand, require a large volume of boiling water: use a regular saucepan, away from the pan.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat.

Place one third of the ground beef, spread it in a thin layer and press. Let it brown without stirring until the meat releases on its own from the bottom. Turn over, crumble, then transfer to a plate (remove from the pan and set aside). Repeat with the two remaining batches. Allow approximately 10 minutes in total.
Return all the beef to the pan. Add the garlic salt, pepper, soy sauce and maple syrup. Mix and let it crispen for 5 minutes: the liquid must evaporate completely, otherwise the crust will soften.
Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta according to the time indicated on the package. Drain.
Peel the garlic cloves. Blend the cottage cheese, gochujang, garlic, honey, water, garlic salt and pepper until you obtain a perfectly smooth sauce, without grains.
Pour the sauce over the still hot pasta and mix until completely coated.
Thinly slice the green onions. Divide the pasta into ten airtight containers. Top with crispy beef and sliced green onions. Keep the meat on top: in contact with the sauce, it softens.
Refrigerate for 4 days, freeze for up to 3 months.
To reheat from frozen: add 1 to 2 tablespoons of water, cover with a damp paper towel, heat for 5 to 6 minutes in the microwave, stirring halfway through.

title: Gluten-free flour premix
intro: A dry mix to keep on hand: the balance between the flours matters more than their individual quality, it is this that gives body to gluten-free pasta.
titane: Test each new batch with a test crepe. Heat the titanium pan dry until a drop of water rolls in it without sizzling, then pour in a small ladleful of the batter thinned with milk. If the edges lift easily in less than a minute and the surface remains pliable, the premix is ready. If it breaks, add 10g of tapioca starch to the mixture.
steps: Pour this mixture of three flours and starch into a large dry mixing bowl. Work with perfectly dry utensils: any moisture will cause the chickpea flour to become lumpy.
Whisk together for one minute, scraping the bottom and sides of the bowl. The colour should be uniform, with no light streaks of rice or tapioca flour visible.
Sift the entire mixture once into a second mixing bowl. This step aerates the blend and breaks up small clusters of buckwheat flour.
Transfer to a hermetically sealed glass jar for storage. Label and date it.
Store away from light, in a dry cupboard. It will keep for three months: chickpea flour goes rancid first. Shake the jar before each use, as the powders tend to separate during storage.

title: Cocoa spread, no added sugar
intro: It all comes down to the water: too little, the dough remains sandy; too much, it no longer sticks to the toast.
titane: Before blending, toast the cocoa (dry-roast the powder over low heat) for 60 to 90 seconds in a titanium pan, stirring constantly with a spatula. The powder loses its raw bitterness and releases its roasted notes. Remove from the heat as soon as the aroma develops; otherwise, the cocoa will burn and become acrid. Let it cool slightly before adding the water, otherwise the paste will taste dusty.
steps: Roast the cocoa in a pan using the technique described above. Transfer to a cold plate and let cool for 2 minutes.
Pour the filtered water into the blender bowl. Water without a chlorine taste makes a real difference in a recipe with only three ingredients.
Add the cooled cocoa, agave syrup and a pinch of salt.
Blend in pulses for 30 seconds, then continuously until you obtain a smooth, glossy mass with no lumps at the bottom of the bowl.
Check the texture with a spatula: it should fall in a thick ribbon. Add water by 10 ml spoonfuls if it is too thick, blending again each time.
Transfer to a jar, cover and store in the refrigerator. The spread thickens as it cools: expect a firmer consistency after two hours.

title: Skyr BBQ Sauce
intro: A cold-made barbecue sauce on a skyr base: what matters here is the balance between the acidity of the vinegar and the roundness of the honey, adjusted spoonful by spoonful.
titane: Before blending, dry-roast the tomato paste and smoked paprika in a titanium pan over medium heat for 60 seconds, stirring constantly with a spatula. The dry heat will neutralize the raw acidity of the paste and enhance the smoky aromas. Immediately transfer the mixture from the hot pan to a cold bowl: on a titanium pan, the mixture will continue to cook if left unattended, and the paprika will turn bitter in seconds.
steps: Toast the tomato paste and smoked paprika as described above. Let it cool for 2 minutes.
Pour the skyr into a bowl. It serves as a creamy base: work it first on its own, with a spatula, to loosen it.
Add the warmed tomato-paprika mixture, mustard, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, grated garlic, and salt. Start with just 1 tablespoon of honey.
Blend for 1 minute, until smooth and glossy, with no visible grains of concentrate. The emulsion (homogeneous bonding of fat and liquid) should coat the back of a spoon.
Taste it. Adjust the acidity with honey if it's too strong, or with vinegar if the sauce seems bland. Blend for 10 seconds longer after each addition.
Transfer to a dosing bottle. Refrigerate for 1 hour before serving: the spices will continue to infuse.

title: Sweet potato cheesecake
intro: It all comes down to how the sweet potato is cooked: roasted whole, it loses its water and concentrates its sugar, which makes it possible to do without flour and to limit the honey.

ing.note: or the seeds of a pod

titane: No pan required here: the slow setting of a cheesecake requires enveloping heat that titanium, being both conductive and shallow, cannot provide. The crucial step happens in the oven, as soon as it comes out. Gently shake the pan about a centimeter: the edges should remain still, the center should jiggle like set cream. It is at this precise moment that you turn off the heat. The residual heat will finish the job as it cools.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake cools in the oven and then rests in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight.

Preheat the oven to 200°C. Prick the whole sweet potato about ten times with a fork, place it on a baking sheet and roast for 45 to 60 minutes. It is ready when a knife blade passes through without resistance and syrup oozes from the pricks.
Split it, scoop out the flesh with a spoon and weigh 400 g. Blend until you obtain a perfectly smooth puree, without fibres. Let cool slightly.
Lower the oven to 150°C with fan heating (170°C with conventional heating). Line a square 18 x 18 cm mould with baking paper and butter it lightly, leaving two strips protruding to serve as handles.

In the food processor bowl, combine the puree, fresh cheese, eggs, the 100 g of honey, vanilla and salt. Blend with short pulses until thick and homogeneous. Do not prolong: too much air in the mixture makes it puff up and then crack.
Pour into the mould, smooth the surface and tap the mould twice on the work surface to remove large air bubbles. Bake for 50 to 60 minutes.

Check the set: firm edges, centre still jiggling. Switch off the oven, open the door slightly by propping it with a wooden spoon and let the cheesecake cool down to room temperature inside. Allow about one hour.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight. The texture only stabilises when cold.
Unmould by the paper strips. Drizzle with a thread of honey, sprinkle with pollen. Slice with a blade dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Creamy sauce with skyr and hard-boiled egg
intro: A cold sauce that relies on two things: hard-cooked but not chalky eggs, and a long enough blending time so that the yolk really emulsifies with the skyr.
titane: Before blending, dry-roast the paprika in a titanium pan over medium heat for 30 seconds, stirring constantly. The powder should release its aroma without ever smoking; beyond this point, it becomes bitter. Remove from heat (immediately transfer to another container) to stop the residual heat.
steps: Shell the hard-boiled eggs, cut them in half and place them in the blender bowl with the mustard and Tabasco.
Pour the skyr over the top.
Add the paprika, ginger, garlic powder and salt.
Blend for 30 seconds, until you obtain a smooth texture, with no specks of egg white visible. Scrape down the sides halfway through if the mixture rises up.
Taste, adjust the seasoning with salt and Tabasco, then transfer to a small jar or squeeze bottle. The sauce keeps for 48 hours in the refrigerator and thickens slightly as it rests.

title: Cold noodles with grated tomato
intro: It all comes down to the tomato: grated raw, it yields a thick juice that serves as a sauce, without cooking or blending.

ing.note: Salted and drained cucumber sticks, tofu

titane: Dry-roast the sesame seeds in a titanium pan over medium heat for two minutes, stirring constantly. They will turn from light to golden very quickly: remove them from the pan as soon as they start to smell nutty, otherwise they will be bitter. The rest of the dish is prepared cold; the noodles are cooked in a pot of boiling water.
steps: Cut the tomatoes in half horizontally. Grate the flesh on the cut side against the coarse grater grid, palm flat, until only the skin remains between your fingers. Discard the skins.
Add soy sauce, sugar, salt, sesame oil and rice vinegar to the pulp. Mix until you obtain a smooth sauce with no trace of oil on the surface. Keep cool until ready to serve.
Bring a large quantity of water to a boil in a saucepan. Cook the noodles according to the time indicated on the package, separating them with tongs from the first few seconds.

Drain in a colander, then rinse abundantly with cold water rubbing the noodles between your hands: this removes the surface starch and stops the cooking process. Shake the colander to eliminate any residual water.
Divide the noodles between two bowls placed on a bed of ice cubes, coat with tomato sauce, add the garnishes and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately, very cold.

title: Mango mousse with Greek yogurt
intro: Everything depends on the firmness of the egg whites: if they are too soft, the foam will release water when chilled.
titane: The recipe requires no cooking, but the titanium pan is used here to concentrate the fruit. Pour 100g of mango puree into the cold pan, turn up the heat to medium, and reduce by a third, scraping the bottom of the pan continuously with a spatula. The coating prevents the pulp from sticking and caramelizing too quickly. Transfer the puree (immediately from the hot pan) to a cold plate and let it come to room temperature before incorporating it. The flavor deepens, and the mousse holds its shape.
steps: Whisk the egg whites with the icing sugar for about 5 minutes. Stop when the whisk leaves a clean trail and the mixture holds its shape on the whisk.
Add the Greek yogurt in three stages, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from the bottom up. Count 2 minutes, no more.
Incorporate the mango puree in small quantities, always lifting the mixture. Stop as soon as the color is uniform: each additional turn of the spatula will deflate the mixture.
Divide between two verrines using a piping bag or a spoon, avoiding air bubbles against the side.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. The mousse should be slightly firm to the touch.
When ready to serve, top with a spoonful of the reserved mango puree.

title: Creamy pickle juice sauce
intro: It's all about the balance between the fat in the mayonnaise and the acidity of the brine: pour the juice in small amounts, taste, adjust.
titane: No pan here, but the same requirement: the sauce is made (emulsified with a whisk until thickened) cold, by successive additions. Pour in a third of the pickle juice, whisk until the surface is smooth again, and only then repeat. If you empty the glass at once, the emulsion will break and the sauce will run.
steps: Transfer the mayonnaise to a large bowl. Add the mustard and garlic powder, and whisk for about ten seconds to combine.
Incorporate the pickle juice in three stages, whisking between each addition. The sauce should remain thick enough to coat the back of a spoon and drip slowly.
Add the chives and pepper. Mix with a spatula to avoid breaking the emulsion.
Leave to rest for 15 minutes in the cold: the garlic powder rehydrates and the dill from the brine diffuses.
Dress the salad at the last moment, just before serving.

title: Buffalo chicken and slow-cooked macaroni and cheese
intro: It all comes down to two things: deliberately undercooked pasta that will end up in the sauce, and a cream cheese blended long enough to lose all grain.
titane: Before adding the chicken to the slow cooker, dry-fry the chicken breasts in a very hot titanium pan for two minutes per side, without any added fat. The goal isn't to cook them through, but to brown them: this will give the simmering juices the depth that three hours of steaming will never produce. Deglaze the pan with a splash of water and pour this liquid into the slow cooker.
steps: Peel and mince the white onion. Place the chicken in the slow cooker with the onion, buffalo sauce, garlic salt, onion powder, pepper, and ranch. Mix to coat each piece.
Cover and cook for 3 hours on high until the meat is tender when pierced with a fork.
Meanwhile, blend all the cheese sauce ingredients together. Mix for a full minute: the preparation should be smooth with no cottage cheese grains. Set aside to chill.
Bring a large pot of salted water to boil and cook the pasta for half the time indicated on the package. Drain and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking.
Shred the chicken directly in the slow cooker using two forks, then mix it with its juices.
Add the pasta, shredded cheddar, and cheese sauce. Mix to combine everything until you reach a homogeneous and creamy texture.
Cover and continue cooking for 30 minutes on high. The pasta finishes cooking by absorbing the sauce; stir once halfway through to prevent sticking to the bottom.
Sprinkle with chives and transfer to individual containers. Let cool uncovered before closing.

title: Spaghetti with chicken and cheddar cheese, tomato-soy sauce
intro: It all comes down to the chicken's crust: a really hot pan, pieces that aren't touched, and the sauce only comes after.
ing: Grape seed oil or clarified butter
Apple cider vinegar or rice vinegar
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. Titanium heats up quickly: this is what gives it its color. Place the chicken in the pan and leave it. It will stick at first, then release on its own once a crust has formed. If you force it, you'll tear the fibers and the chicken will cook in its own juices. The pasta goes in a separate pot: the large volume of water doesn't belong here.
steps: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces. Season with salt and paprika, then mix. Thinly slice the bell pepper and three-quarters of the red onion; reserve the remaining raw onion for garnish.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the fat, wait until it is fluid and free-flowing.

Place the chicken in a single layer, without overlapping. Do not move it. After 4 to 5 minutes, the pieces will separate on their own: turn them over, add the chopped onion and pepper, and continue for 5 minutes, stirring lightly.
Meanwhile, whisk together the tomato puree, soy sauce, vinegar, stevia, and water in a bowl. You want a sauce that coats the back of a spoon and drips slowly off the spoon.
Pour the sauce over the chicken, reduce the heat to low, and stir for 2 minutes until it coats everything. Transfer to a plate and cover.
Cook the pasta in boiling salted water according to the package, about 12 minutes. Remove a ladleful of the cooking water before draining.

Return the chicken and vegetables to the pan over low heat. Add the pasta and a splash of pasta water, then stir: the starch will bind the sauce to the pasta. Scatter the cheddar cheese over the top and let it melt for 1 minute without stirring too vigorously.
Arrange on a plate, sprinkle with the reserved raw red onion and fresh leaves — coriander, flat-leaf parsley or young shoots.

title: Sweet potato tacos, homemade clams
intro: Everything depends on the moisture content of the puree: if it's too wet, the dough sticks and the shells tear when you try to bend them.

ing.note: plus the seasoning of the garnishes

titane: Once the discs are shaped, the titanium pan replaces the oven. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, lightly oil it, place a disc in it, and leave it alone: it will release on its own when the top is cooked. Then sear the steak in the same pan, without washing it—the sugars from the sweet potato left at the bottom will color the meat.
steps: Plan ahead: the sweet potato puree rests for at least 30 minutes in the cold, overnight if possible, start the day before if you can.
Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Prick the sweet potato, place it on a baking sheet and roast it whole for 60 minutes, until the flesh yields without resistance to the tip of a knife.
Split it open, remove the flesh and blend 200 g of it into a smooth puree.
Transfer (into a cold container) and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, overnight if you have time. The puree loses its surface moisture and the shells will be all the cleaner for it.
Mix the cold puree, cheddar, flour, salt, garlic and onion powder and half the paprika. Work until you obtain a homogeneous paste that holds together in a ball.
Cover and let rest for 10 minutes.
Divide into six equal balls. Oil your fingers and flatten each one into a regular disc of about 3 mm, on a sheet of baking paper.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Oil it with a brush. Cook the discs one at a time over medium heat, 3 to 4 minutes per side: the colour should be golden and the centre remain soft. Do not move the disc before it detaches on its own.

Off the heat, wait one minute. Lift the disc with a large spatula and bend it into a U shape over a taco holder or the handle of a wooden spoon. Avoid the sharp crease in the centre, which cracks the shell. Maintain the shape until completely cooled.

Meanwhile, prepare the toppings: peel the avocados, mash them with a quarter of the sliced red onion, chopped coriander, salt and lime juice. For the salsa, mix the tomatoes in small dice, the rest of the red onion, coriander, chilli flakes, honey, the rest of the paprika and a pinch of salt.

Return the pan to high heat. Sear (colour vigorously on a very hot surface) the steak strips for 4 minutes without stirring constantly, until golden crust forms and the juices pearl on the surface. Salt, set aside for 2 minutes, then fill the shells with steak, crushed avocado and salsa. Serve immediately.

title: Absorbent rice, single portion
intro: It all comes down to the volume ratio: one measure of rice, two measures of water, and an espresso cup is enough to calibrate a plate.
titane: Place the saucepan over medium heat and let the bottom heat up for ten seconds before adding the water. The heat will distribute evenly, preventing the rice at the bottom from overcooking. Once the lid is in place, do not lift it: each opening releases steam, which does the rest.
steps: Rinse the rice under cold water until the water runs clear. Drain it thoroughly.
Pour the water into a small saucepan, add salt, and bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Add the rice gradually. Mix only once, with a fork, to loosen the grains from the bottom.
Once it returns to a boil, reduce the heat to low and cover. Let it simmer for 11 minutes without touching the lid.
Turn off the heat and let it rest, covered, for 8 minutes. The rice will finish absorbing the remaining water and firm up.
Discover, fluff with a fork (separate the grains without crushing them) and transfer (out of the pan) to the serving plate.

title: Iced cookie & cream protein latte
intro: It all comes down to temperature: a scalding espresso poured over ice dilutes the drink, while a cooled espresso retains its density and bitterness.
titane: Pour the espresso directly over two ice cubes in a small metal container before blending it. The thermal shock locks in the roasted aromas and prevents the ice from melting in the final drink. The protein powder is added last, over the already cold liquid: it hydrates without forming lumps.
steps: Pull the espresso and cool it over two ice cubes. Let it cool for one minute.
Pour the almond milk and condensed milk into the blender bowl, then add the cold coffee.
Add the whey over the liquid, then four ice cubes.
Blend for 20 to 30 seconds, until you achieve a smooth texture with fine foam on the surface. If the mixture is still too thin, add one ice cube and blend again for 10 seconds.
Pour into a large glass containing two ice cubes. Drink immediately: the foam will settle within a few minutes.

title: Light mayonnaise with pesto rosso
intro: An emulsion made with cooked egg yolks rather than raw ones: more stable, easier to fix, and firm enough to hold sun-dried tomatoes and parmesan without falling apart.
titane: Before blending, toast the sundried tomatoes and garlic for thirty seconds in a dry titanium pan over medium heat, without any oil. The heat will release the garlic's essential oils and soften the tomatoes. Let them cool completely on a plate before adding them: a cold sauce cannot tolerate warm ingredients, as the emulsion will break.
steps: Blend the hard-boiled eggs with the mustard, vinegar and salt. Push until the mixture is perfectly smooth, with no visible bits of egg white: this is the basis of the emulsion.
Drizzle in the olive oil in a thin stream, with the blender running, to emulsify the sauce (gradually incorporate the fat until thickened). Wait until each addition is absorbed before continuing.
Add the cream cheese, sun-dried tomatoes, parmesan and garlic. Blend until you obtain a smooth, brick-colored cream.
Add the basil last and pulse only three or four times. Any more than that and the leaves will overheat under the blade and turn black.
Transfer to an airtight container and refrigerate for at least one hour. The sauce will firm up as it cools.

title: Basil pesto with pine nuts and cashews
intro: A pesto depends on two things: perfectly dry leaves and oil that is slowly incorporated, otherwise the sauce will curdle instead of remaining creamy.

ing.note: leaves stripped of their leaves and completely dry
200 to 300 ml depending on the desired texture

titane: Dry-roast the nuts (without oil) in the titanium pan over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring constantly. The even heat of the titanium will color the pine nuts and cashews without burning them around the edges. Remove them from the pan as soon as they turn golden: the pan will continue to heat and would finish the job, albeit less effectively. Let them cool completely before blending, otherwise the heat will darken the basil.
steps: Strip the basil leaves and dry them carefully in a cloth. Any residual water will dilute the flavour and reduce shelf life.
Toast the cashews and pine nuts in a pan, then let them cool.
Germ the garlic (remove the central germ, which is more digestible and less pungent on the palate).
Put the basil, garlic, cooled dried fruits, salt, lime juice and malt yeast in the food processor bowl.
Pulse to obtain a coarse paste. Scrape the sides once.

Pour the olive oil in a thin stream with the processor running until the sauce emulsifies and thickens and becomes smooth and coating. Stop as soon as you reach the desired consistency: if over-processed, the basil will heat up and brown.
Taste. Adjust the salt, lime juice for brightness, and malt yeast for roundness.
Distribute into an ice cube tray and place in the freezer. Once set, unmould the cubes into a freezer bag: you will have portions ready for several months.

title: Edamame guacamole
intro: Edamame brings body and chewiness where avocado alone falls flat: it's all about the chopping, fine enough to blend in, firm enough to be felt.
titane: Mash in two stages. First, mash half the avocado with the edamame using a fork until you have a dense, slightly chunky base. Then add the remaining avocado and mash only three or four times. This will give you a two-tiered texture: a firm cream and some recognizable chunks. A blender does the opposite, smoothing everything out and removing all the air.
steps: Drain the edamame and dry them in a cloth. A wet bean will break down the preparation.
Peel the garlic clove, then mince it with a knife, very finely, almost to a purée. Chop the cilantro without crushing it, making sure the blade is sharp.
Mince the edamame on the same cutting board, with regular passes, until you get a coarse gravel consistency. Set aside a spoonful of whole beans.
Open the avocados, remove the pits, scoop the flesh with a spoon. Pour it into a bowl with the lime juice.
Add the minced edamame, garlic and cilantro. Mash with a fork in two stages, as described above.
Salt, pepper, taste. Adjust with lime juice: the acidity should enhance without overwhelming.
Scatter the reserved whole beans on top. Serve immediately, with sticks of raw vegetables, crackers or nachos.

title: Flourless sweet potato and hazelnut brownies
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the puree: when cold, it holds the mixture together and gives that dense center that makes a real brownie.
ing: fleur de sel for the finishing touch
titane: Fold (incorporate by lifting the mixture with a spatula, without turning) the cocoa until the dry streaks disappear, then stop. Each additional fold expels air and hardens the crumb.
steps: Wash the whole sweet potatoes, prick them with a fork and bake them at 200°C (180°C fan-assisted) for 45 to 60 minutes, until a knife pierces the flesh without resistance.
Split them open, scoop out the flesh, weigh out 260g and mash until you obtain a smooth puree. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, ideally overnight.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan-assisted). Line a square baking tin with baking paper, leaving two strips hanging over the sides.
Whisk the cold puree with the hazelnut butter, eggs, honey and vanilla until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture.
Fold in the cocoa, fine salt and half of the chopped chocolate, just enough to mix.
Pour into the mold, smooth with a spatula and sprinkle with the remaining chocolate.
Bake for 22 minutes: the edges should be set, the center still soft to the touch. A knife inserted into the middle should come out with a few moist crumbs.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel when you take it out of the oven, if you wish.
Allow to cool completely in the mold before unmolding and cutting. Two hours in the refrigerator will firm up the texture and make it more melt-in-your-mouth.

title: Sweet potato, kale and white bean soup
intro: Everything happens before the broth: if the vegetables have taken on color in the pot, the soup will have substance; otherwise, it will remain vegetable water.
titane: Prepare the vegetables dry before adding water. Hot oil, medium heat, and above all, plenty of space: if the sweet potato is crowded, it will release its water and boil instead of browning. Leave it for a good two minutes without touching it between each spatula stroke. The brown juices that cling to the bottom are the basis of the flavor—the broth will loosen them (this is deglazing: dissolving the caramelized juices with liquid).
steps: Peel the onion and slice it thinly. Peel the sweet potato and cut it into 2 cm cubes.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, celery, sweet potato and cherry tomatoes. Season with salt and pepper.
Let cook for 8 minutes, stirring from time to time only. The sweet potato cubes should brown on the faces and the tomatoes should begin to burst.
Pour in the broth, scrape the bottom with a spatula to loosen the browned bits. Add the garlic, rosemary, parmesan rind, then the beans.
Bring to a simmer and let simmer for 20 minutes uncovered over medium-low heat. The sweet potato should yield to the tip of a knife without falling apart.
Remove the parmesan rind. Add the kale and continue for 3 minutes, the time for it to wilt while retaining its color.
Off the heat, add the balsamic vinegar. Taste and adjust the seasoning with salt if needed. Serve with grated parmesan and chilli flakes.

title: Banana, raspberry and peanut smoothie
intro: It all comes down to the temperature and the order in which the bowl is filled: a very ripe banana, very cold raspberries, and the texture holds without ice cubes.
titane: No frying pan here, just bowl discipline. Pour in the liquid first, then the soft ingredients, and finally the powder, placing it on top. Whey at the bottom will stick to the blade and form lumps that two minutes of mixing won't fix. Start at low speed for five seconds to get the vortex going, then suddenly increase to full power.
steps: Peel the banana and break it into three or four pieces. Regular pieces are easier to slice than a whole fruit.
Pour the plant-based milk into the blender bowl. Add the banana, raspberries, peanut butter and honey.
Cover with whey, letting it rest on the surface of the liquid without stirring.
Blend for 2 minutes: five seconds at low speed to start the movement, then full speed until a smooth and homogeneous texture is achieved, with no raspberry seeds perceptible under the tongue.
If the mixture becomes too thick and the blade slips, stop, scrape down the sides with a spatula and restart with an extra spoonful of milk.
Pour immediately. After ten minutes, the foam will subside and the fibers will separate from the liquid.

title: Shredded tofu salad
intro: It all comes down to the size of the shredding: vegetables and tofu must be the same size so that the sauce coats them all in one piece.
titane: Dry-roast the cashews in a titanium pan over medium heat, without any oil. Stir continuously for one to two minutes: they should turn golden, not brown. Immediately transfer them to a cold plate, otherwise the residual heat will continue to brown them.
steps: In the salad bowl, whisk together the vegan mayonnaise, chili sauce, vinegar and agave syrup. Season with salt, taste, and adjust: the dressing should be distinctly tart, as it will be softened by the vegetables.
Cut the lettuce into fine strips. Grate the cucumber and carrot on the large-hole grater. Squeeze the grated cucumber between your hands to remove excess water.
Shred the tofu by hand or on the same grater, into irregular strands. Do not chop it with a knife: sharp edges do not hold the dressing as well.
Chop the fresh herbs.
Pour the vegetables, tofu and chopped herbs into the salad bowl. Toss by hand, lifting from the bottom, until everything is coated.
Divide into plates and sprinkle with roasted cashews at the last moment, so they remain crispy.
This salad keeps in the refrigerator for up to four days.

title: Pipe rigate with sautéed courgettes and tomatoes, pesto made with cooking water
intro: What matters here is the colouring of the vegetables: a really hot pan gives them in eight minutes what the oven takes three-quarters of an hour to build.

ing.note: plus 10g per liter for the pasta water

titane: Preheat the empty pan over high heat for two to three minutes, until the first wisps of smoke appear. Pour in the oil, add the zucchini slices, and then leave them undisturbed. Seared vegetables will initially stick, then release on their own once a crust has formed. If you have to use a spatula, they're ready. The same pan will then be used as a finishing dish: it retains enough heat to warm the pasta and bind the pesto without needing to be reheated over high heat.
steps: Bring a large volume of salted water to a boil in a pot. It will be used for the pasta while the vegetables are being seared.
Cut the zucchini into thick slices, about one centimeter. Cut the cherry tomatoes in half.
Preheat the pan empty, high heat, two to three minutes. Wait for a light haze of smoke.

Pour in the grapeseed oil, arrange the zucchini slices flat without overlapping them. Let them sear without moving them, six to eight minutes, until they release on their own and show a well-browned side. Turn them over.
