Add the cherry tomatoes cut side down against the pan for the last two minutes. Salt.
Transfer the vegetables out of the pan into a bowl and cover to retain heat. Set the pan aside, off the heat.
Cook the pasta in the boiling water according to the time indicated on the package. Before draining, remove a small ladleful of cooking water.
In a bowl, thin the pesto with two to three tablespoons of this cooking water. Whisk: the starch and oil combine into a homogeneous sauce.

Drain the pasta. Return the pan to low heat, pour in the pasta, vegetables, and thinned pesto. Mix for two minutes, until the sauce coats each piece. Add a spoonful of cooking water if the mixture becomes too dry.
Grate the parmesan on top, grind pepper, scatter the basil torn by hand. Serve immediately.

title: Chocolate-peanut rice cakes
intro: It all comes down to the cold: a well-frozen galette solidifies the peanut butter and allows the chocolate to crack cleanly.
titane: Dry-roast the peanuts in the titanium pan for 3 to 4 minutes over medium heat, stirring constantly until they turn golden and release their aroma. Remove them from the pan (immediately transfer them to a cold plate) to stop the heat, then remove the pan from the heat, let it cool for thirty seconds, and add the chopped chocolate. The titanium's thermal inertia will melt the chocolate gently, without a double boiler and without burning it. Stir with a spatula until smooth.
steps: Plan ahead: the rice cakes need at least two hours in the freezer, so organize accordingly.
Toast the peanuts as shown in the step above, then break them up coarsely with a knife. Set aside.
Arrange the rice cakes on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, smooth side facing up.
Spread the peanut butter in an even layer on each rice cake using a small spatula. Leave 5 mm margin around the edge: the filling will spread when dipped.
Sprinkle with broken peanuts and press them lightly with your fingertips to secure them.
Place the baking sheet in the freezer for at least 2 hours. The surface must be firm to the touch, with no marks.
Melt the chocolate in the warmed pan. It should be fluid but not hot: a drop placed on your lip should not burn.
Remove the rice cakes three by three and dip them filled side into the chocolate, or coat them with a spoon. Scrape off excess on the edge of the pan.
Place them back on the parchment paper, sprinkle with fleur de sel while the chocolate is still glossy, then let set for 10 minutes in the cool.

title: Buckwheat chia pudding
intro: It all comes down to the resting time: the chia seeds must swell completely, otherwise the texture remains sandy instead of creamy.
titane: Before adding them, dry-roast the buckwheat flakes in a titanium pan over medium heat for two minutes, stirring constantly. They will turn from beige to golden and release a nutty aroma. Immediately transfer them to a cold plate; the residual heat from the metal would continue to cook them. Let them cool completely before mixing, otherwise they will become soggy and lose their crunch.
steps: Pour the almond milk into a bowl or a jar with a lid.
Add the chia seeds and buckwheat flakes.
Incorporate the almond protein powder gradually, sprinkling it in to avoid lumps.
Add the soy yogurt and agave syrup.
Mix until you obtain a homogeneous mixture, with no dry powder at the bottom.
Let it rest for at least 15 minutes, ideally overnight in the refrigerator. The seeds should have absorbed all the liquid and formed a gel.
Mix one last time, then cover with a layer of yogurt and fresh fruit.

title: Pulled chicken burritos with chipotle queso
intro: Everything hinges on the bottom of the pan: the chicken must release its juices during searing, then draw them back up during braising with the lid on.
titane: Sear the chicken breasts in a very hot, dry pan, without any added fat, until they release easily from the pan. The juices (the brown deposits left by the meat) will stick to the bottom: this is the foundation of your flavor. Then reduce the heat to low, pour in the liquid, and cover. The pan will maintain a low, steady heat, allowing the chicken to confit without drying out. Cook for 35 to 40 minutes, no longer: the meat will relax and should not fall apart.
steps: Pat the chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Rub them with garlic salt and 28 g taco seasoning.
Heat the pan empty over high heat. Place the breasts without crowding, in two or three batches. Leave 3 minutes per side: they will release on their own once the crust has formed.
Return all the chicken to the pan. Add the green peppers, chipotle peppers, lime juice and water. Scrape the bottom with a spatula to loosen the drippings.
Cover, reduce to low heat. Leave for 35 to 40 minutes. The chicken is ready when a fork opens it without resistance.
Meanwhile, blend together the cottage cheese, 15 g seasoning, enchilada sauce, chipotle peppers, salsa and milk. Blend until no grains remain: the sauce should coat the spoon.
Remove the chicken (take it out of the pan) onto a cutting board. Shred it with two forks, then return it to the pan off the heat, with its cooking liquid.
Incorporate the mozzarella, pepper jack, queso sauce, pico de gallo and cilantro. Mix: the residual heat is enough to melt the cheeses.
Warm the tortillas 20 seconds per side in the wiped pan. Place 40 g rice in the center, then a generous spoonful of chicken. Fold the sides, then roll tight.
Wrap each burrito in an aluminum foil sheet, well fitted. You can freeze them this way for up to 3 months.
To reheat a frozen burrito, wrap it in a damp paper towel and microwave it on a plate for 5 to 6 minutes. To crisp it, finish for a few minutes in the pan or air fryer.

title: Cucumber boats with crushed chickpeas
intro: It's all about the texture: the chickpeas should remain irregular, never reduced to a puree.
titane: No cooking is involved here, and a pan adds nothing to a cold dish. There's only one useful exception: briefly fry the nori sheet in a dry pan over medium heat for 20 seconds, just before crumbling it. It will become brittle and its briny aroma will be clearly released. Remove it immediately (take it off the heat) to prevent it from burning.
steps: Mash the chickpeas with a fork in a bowl. Stop as soon as the mass holds together while keeping some whole pieces: it is this irregularity that gives the bite.
Add the mustard and mayonnaise. Mix with a spoon until the mixture is smooth, without overworking it.
Crumble the nori sheet between your fingers and mix it in. Taste, add salt and pepper. The nori already provides salt: adjust at the end.
Cut the cucumbers in half lengthwise, then into 8 cm pieces. Scoop out the center with a small spoon, leaving 5 mm of flesh on the edges so that the boat will hold together.
Generously fill the hollows with a spoon. Serve immediately, as the cucumber will release water after about twenty minutes.

title: Coriander and cherry tomato sauce
intro: A raw sauce that holds together thanks to the balance between acid and sweet: taste before serving, and correct with a drop of syrup if the vinegar dominates.
titane: Nothing cooks here, but everything happens right after searing. When the plant-based steaks come out of the pan, remove it from the heat, wait thirty seconds, then pour the sauce over them. It warms up from contact with the still-hot metal and absorbs the juices (the golden deposits left by cooking). Stir once, coat, and serve. Titanium cools down quickly: no risk of cooking the herbs.
steps: Strip the cilantro leaves. Chop them finely with a knife, with a sharp blade, without crushing the leaves: they would blacken and lose their flavor.
Wash the cherry tomatoes, then cut them into quarters. Keep the juice and seeds, they are part of the sauce.
Combine herbs, tomatoes, vinegar, maple syrup, oil and salt in a bowl. Mix with a spoon until the oil and vinegar emulsify.
Let rest for 5 minutes, giving the salt time to draw out a little water from the tomatoes. Taste and adjust the salt if needed.
Serve on vegetable steaks, vegetable skewers or legume patties that have just been seared. The sauce keeps for 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator, in a closed container.

title: Shredded beef burritos with dried chilies
intro: Six hours of simmering gives the meat, two minutes in the pan gives the crust: the rest is just assembly.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the filling

titane: The slow cooking process happens elsewhere—the volume of liquid and the cooking time eliminate the need for a pan. It comes into play at the end. Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add a drizzle of high-smoke-point oil (sunflower, grapeseed), and place the burrito underneath. Don't move it. It will release on its own once the shell has formed. Forcing it beforehand will tear the tortilla and ruin the cheese.
steps: Peel and thinly slice the white onions. Mince the garlic.
Stem and seed the ancho and guajillo peppers. Keep the flesh.
Sauté the onions and garlic over medium heat in a pot until fragrant and the onion becomes translucent.
Add the peppers, tomatoes, broth, enchilada sauce, garlic salt, cumin, smoked paprika, pepper and oregano.
Bring to a simmer and let the peppers rehydrate for about ten minutes: they should bend without resistance.
Blend until you obtain a smooth sauce. Pass through a fine sieve if you want a cleaner texture.
Place the steak in the slow cooker, coat with sauce, cover. Cook for 6 hours on low heat.
Remove the meat and shred it using two forks, pulling in the direction of the fibres. Return it to a little sauce: it should remain moist, never drowned.
Fill each tortilla in this order: rice, shredded meat, mozzarella, raw onion, cilantro. Fold in the sides, then roll tightly.
To store: wrap each burrito in aluminium foil or a freezer bag. Three months in the freezer.
To serve: wrap the frozen burrito in a damp paper towel, 5 to 6 minutes in the microwave. Then place it in a titanium pan, seam side down, 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden crust forms.

title: Roast chicken and creamy orzo with sun-dried tomatoes
intro: Everything hinges on searing the chicken: it is this that deposits the juices at the bottom of the pan which will give the broth, and then the orzo, its depth.
titane: Heat the empty skillet until a drop of water forms a bead on the surface, then oil it. Sear the chicken in three batches, in a single layer, never covering more than two-thirds of the pan. An overcrowded pan will release water, causing the chicken to boil instead of browning. Between batches, transfer the chicken to a serving dish and allow the pan to return to its normal temperature.
steps: Mix the diced chicken with the garlic salt, Italian seasoning, and smoked paprika. Let it rest for 10 minutes at room temperature.

Heat a dry skillet, add a drizzle of oil, and sear the chicken in three batches, 3 to 4 minutes per batch, without stirring for the first minute. Remove from the pan. The chicken is not cooked through at this stage.
Reduce heat to medium. Add the remaining oil, onions and garlic, cook for 2 minutes, until translucent.
Stir in the tomato paste and sundried tomatoes. Stir for 1 minute: the paste should brown slightly and lose its acidity.
Pour in the orzo and toast it (coat the grains in fat until they become shiny), 1 minute.
Deglaze with a third of the stock, scraping the bottom with a flexible spatula to loosen the browned bits. Add the rest of the stock.
Simmer uncovered for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring every 2 minutes to prevent the orzo from sticking. The grain should be tender, and the liquid almost absorbed.
Return the chicken and its juices to the pot. Continue cooking for 3 minutes, until it is fully cooked.
Remove from heat and stir in the blended cottage cheese, Parmesan, spinach, and lemon juice. Mix well: the spinach will wilt in 1 minute from the residual heat.
Adjust the seasoning and serve, or divide into ten containers for the week.

title: Tuna and avocado rice cake
intro: It all comes down to how it holds together: sticky rice, tightly packed layers, and four hours of cold before unmolding.
titane: Dry-roast the black sesame seeds in a titanium pan over medium heat for one minute, stirring constantly. The smooth surface heats up quickly and evenly: the seeds pop, release their aroma, and won't burn as long as you keep them moving. Remove from the pan (immediately transfer to a cold plate) to stop the cooking process.
steps: Cook the rice according to the package instructions. Spread it out on a wide dish and let it come to room temperature, without chilling it: it should remain soft and sticky.

In a bowl, mash the tuna with a fork. Add the mayonnaise, cream cheese, mustard, lemon juice, and chives. Season with salt and pepper, and mix until you have a smooth paste that holds its shape on a spoon.

Slice the avocados into thin strips. Peel the cucumber into ribbons with a vegetable peeler or into very thin rounds, then pat them dry with absorbent paper: the water from the cucumber is the enemy of unmolding.
Line a springform pan with cling film, leaving plenty of overhang (cover the bottom and sides so you can pull it down later). Arrange the avocado slices tightly in the bottom, without any gaps.

Cover with a layer of rice, pressing down with the back of a damp spoon. Spread the tuna mixture, then the cucumber, and finish with a final layer of rice. Press down firmly with the palm of your hand.
Fold the film over the top and place in the refrigerator for 4 hours. This time is non-negotiable: it's what seals the layers.
Turn out onto a serving dish and remove the film. Coat with a tangy mayonnaise, sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds, and slice with a knife dipped in hot water between each slice.

title: Dried fruit bites with honey, coated in dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to packing: the more the mixture is compacted in the circle, the longer the bite will hold without crumbling.
ing: Mixed dried fruits and nuts, as desired
titane: Before mixing, toast the nuts (dry-roast to release their aromas) in a titanium pan over medium heat for three to four minutes, stirring occasionally. The almonds should smell toasted and the seeds should begin to pop. Transfer the mixture to a cold plate and let it cool slightly before incorporating the egg white; pouring it over hot nuts would cause it to curdle immediately.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper and place the cookie cutters on it.
Roughly chop the larger dried fruits. Keep some texture: a completely crushed bite loses its appeal.
Combine the dried fruit, egg white and honey in a bowl. Mix until each piece is coated with a shiny film.
Fill the cookie cutters to the level of two large spoonfuls each.
Pack firmly into the bottom of a glass. The mixture should form a dense disc, without air pockets.
Bake for 10 minutes at 180°C, until golden brown and crispy edges.
Let them cool completely on the baking sheet, then remove the rings. The pastries will crumble when hot.
Melt the dark chocolate in a double boiler. Dip each bite halfway into the chocolate, place on baking paper and let set at room temperature.

title: Cheesecake in a chocolate egg
intro: Everything depends on the consistency of the mixture: a cream that is too runny will soak the biscuit base and the egg will not hold its shape when cut.
titane: Melt the butter over low heat in the titanium pan, then remove it from the heat. Pour the crushed biscuits directly into the pan and stir: the residual heat from the bottom is enough to coat them and bring out their toasted aroma, without ever browning them. Transfer them immediately to a cold plate to stop the heat.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake must rest for at least 4 hours in the cold, leaving it overnight gives a better result.
Crush the biscuits with a rolling pin inside a sealed freezer bag until you obtain a coarse semolina. A few larger pieces add texture.
Mix them with the melted butter using the titanium method, then let cool completely. A crumbly mixture still warm would cause the cream to break.

Work the fresh cheese with a whisk with the icing sugar and vanilla until it is perfectly smooth. Add the cold cream and whisk for another thirty seconds: the mixture should thicken and hold on the whisk.
Cut the chocolate egg in half with a serrated knife heated under hot water and wiped dry. Place each half-shell in a ramekin to hold it in place.
Press the biscuit mixture to the bottom of each half-egg over a good centimetre, using the back of a spoon. Fill with cream up to the edge and smooth.
Reserve in the cold for 4 hours minimum. Leaving it overnight gives a noticeably firmer texture, which can be cut with a spoon without collapsing.

title: Small pot of sweet potato, courgette and whiting
intro: A salt-free, diversified puree, where the fish is added at the end of cooking to remain tender and retain its clean taste.

ing.note: g, peeled and cut into cubes

ing: Cereals, in a quinoa and bulgur mix

ing.note: about 400 ml, at the level of the vegetables

titane: Sweat the chopped onion and garlic in the titanium pan, dry, for two minutes over medium heat (sweat: cook gently to release the water from the vegetables without browning). The coating is very well suited to cooking without oil, and this step adds depth to the purée without adding salt or stock. Then transfer to the saucepan for boiling.
steps: Dice the sweet potato into 1.5 cm cubes. Cut the courgette into thick slices, leaving the skin on if it is young. Slice the onion thinly, crush the half clove of garlic.
Sweat the onion and garlic in the titanium pan for two minutes, without browning. Transfer the preparation to a saucepan.
Add the sweet potato, courgette and cereals. Pour the water just to level: the less liquid there is, the more fragrant the puree will be.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 15 minutes over low heat. The sweet potato must crush without resistance under the fork.
Place the hake on the vegetables, cover again and allow 4 to 5 minutes. The flesh becomes opaque and breaks into flakes.
Remove a ladle of cooking liquid and set it aside. Blend everything, adding liquid spoon by spoon until you reach the desired texture: smooth for the start of weaning, thicker afterwards.
Add the chopped dill at the last moment, away from the heat. Do not salt.
Portion the preparation according to your needs. You can freeze the unused portions to have them always on hand.

title: Hollowed-out cucumber, sushi style
intro: It all comes down to how the rice is packed: if it's not compressed properly, it will fall apart at the first bite.

ing.note: or the sauce of your choice

titane: Toast (dry-heat to release their aromas) the sesame seeds in the titanium pan, without oil, over medium heat. Stir continuously. As soon as the first seed pops and the aroma rises, transfer (remove from the pan) to a cold plate: the titanium cast iron retains heat and the seeds would continue to brown.
steps: Wash the cucumber and dry it.
Toast the sesame seeds as indicated above. Set aside.
Split the cucumber in half lengthwise, without peeling it.
Hollow out each half with a small spoon along the seed line. Carve out a regular groove, leaving at least 5 mm of flesh on the sides.
Fill the grooves with rice. Press firmly with the back of the spoon, in small quantities, until the surface is smooth and dense.
Arrange smoked salmon strips over the rice, then add chives.
Drizzle with a line of mayonnaise, then hot sauce if using.
Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds. Slice into 2 cm bite-sized pieces with a sharp knife, blade moistened.

title: Cannelloni with green asparagus and ricotta
intro: It all depends on how well the asparagus holds its shape: they must remain firm to the filling, because the oven will cook them a second time.
titane: Before adding the filling, fry the asparagus tips for two minutes in a very hot titanium pan, dry and without oil. They will brown slightly and release their surface moisture: the filling will remain dense and the gratin won't release any liquid. Remove from the heat and transfer to a cold dish immediately to stop the cooking process.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Peel the base of the asparagus, break off the fibrous part. Cut the stems into small pieces and set the tips aside whole.
Sear the pieces and tips in a titanium pan for two minutes, then remove and let cool slightly.
Wash the spinach, squeeze dry thoroughly, chop coarsely.
In a bowl, work the ricotta with the egg until you obtain a smooth mixture. Fold in the spinach and asparagus pieces. Season with salt and pepper, grate over nutmeg.
Fill the cannelloni using a piping bag or small spoon, without pressing. Arrange them side by side in the gratin dish.
Mix the milk and cream, season lightly, pour over the pasta until completely covered. The tubes should be submerged: this liquid is what will cook them.
Cover with aluminum foil, sealing tightly around the edges. Bake for 35 minutes.
Remove the foil, distribute the grated cheese and asparagus tips on top. Continue for 10 minutes, until lightly browned.
Let rest for 5 minutes outside the oven before serving: the filling sets and the portions hold together.

title: Instant icing sugar made in a blender
intro: Commercial icing sugar contains starch: this one does not, which changes the consistency of an icing and the fineness of a coating on a cake.
titane: Nothing heats up here; it's all about the seal. Stretch the cling film over the bowl like a drumhead, then fold it down with two fingers against the outer wall before sliding the blender foot underneath. A loose film will release a cloud of sugar that settles everywhere; a taut film will give you a fine powder.
steps: Pour instant powdered sugar in the bowl of the immersion blender. Do not exceed one third of the height: the powder needs space to rotate.

Cover the opening of the bowl with plastic wrap stretched taut and pressed against the sides. Pierce it at the centre just enough to pass the immersion blender head through, which must touch the bottom.
Blend at full power for 30 seconds, moving the head up and down slightly to mix all the powder. Stop when the powder is fine and homogeneous, with no grains detectable between your fingers.
Let the dust settle for about ten seconds before removing the plastic wrap, then transfer through a fine sieve into another container.

title: Instant kiwi-banana ice cream
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the fruit: cold enough to make ice cream, soft enough for the knife to grip.

ing.note: peeled, sliced into rounds and frozen

ing: The juice of half a lime
titane: Remove the fruit from the freezer five to six minutes before blending. The surface frost melts, the slices yield to the touch, and the blade cuts through a smooth, homogeneous mixture instead of breaking it apart. This short waiting time is what makes the difference between a grainy snow and a smooth cream.
steps: Plan ahead: the fruits freeze for 6 hours or overnight, start the day before or several hours in advance.
Peel the kiwis and banana, cut them into 1 cm slices. Spread them flat on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, without them touching.
Place in the freezer for 6 hours, or overnight. The slices should come away one by one. If you blend them after approximately 6 hours of freezing, you can blend them directly without tempering.
If the fruits have been in the cold overnight, let them temper for 5 minutes on the work surface. They should resist slightly to the pressure of your finger.
Pour the fruits into the bowl of the blender with the honey and lime juice. Blend using short pulses, scraping the sides between two passes.
Continue until the mixture sets: the mass stops jumping, gathers around the blade and becomes coating consistency. Allow one to two minutes.
Serve immediately, or transfer into an airtight container and place back in the freezer for 20 minutes for a firmer consistency.

title: Fresh tuna and tomato tart, sesame pastry baked upside down
intro: It all comes down to the pastry: blind baked (baked alone, without filling) on the back of an upturned cake tin, it dries all over and remains perfectly flat, which allows it to be filled when cold.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the mold

titane: This one comes out of the pan. The curved base of the titanium pan will never provide a flat, unmolding surface: you need an inverted loaf pan, generously oiled, onto which the batter will press like a lid. The pan is used again to dry-roast the sesame seeds for two minutes over medium heat, until they pop and turn golden. Remove them (take them out of the hot pan immediately) before incorporating them into the flour.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Toast the seeds in a frying pan, then let them cool slightly.

In a salad bowl, combine the flour, seeds, and a generous pinch of salt. Pour in the water and oil, mix with a fork then by hand until you obtain a smooth, homogeneous dough. It should not stick: if needed, add a tablespoon of flour.
Turn a loaf tin upside down on a baking sheet. Generously oil the back and sides.
Roll out the dough to 3 mm thickness, then place it on the inverted tin. Press it well against the bottom and sides, cut off any excess, prick the top with a fork.
Bake for 30 minutes, until the dough is golden and firm to the touch.
Remove and let cool completely on the tin. Never force a warm dough: it would break. Then detach it by lifting a corner, then flip it over.
Drain the tuna, then crumble it with a fork. Mix it with the fresh cheese and mayonnaise until you obtain a smooth cream. Season with pepper, taste before salting.
Spread the cream in the cooled tart base, in an even layer.
Slice the tomatoes into thin rounds, lightly salt them and let them drain for 5 minutes on paper towels. Arrange them overlapping, add the chiffonade basil at the last moment, a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Creamy crozets with mushrooms
intro: It all depends on the colouring of the mushrooms: if they release their water without ever turning golden, the dish will remain flat.
titane: The titanium pan is used here for searing, not for cooking. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, sear the mushrooms in a single layer until nicely browned, then transfer them to the pan. The 80 cl of stock requires a deep sauté pan: beyond 500 ml, the lower sides of a pan become empty and the pasta cooks unevenly.
steps: Clean the mushrooms and slice them into thick rounds. Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then pour in half the oil.
Sear the mushrooms over medium-high heat without stirring for the first minute. Stir, then continue until the water has evaporated and the slices are golden. Remove and set aside on a plate.

Peel and mince the shallot, peel, remove the germ and chop the garlic if not already done. In a large sauté pan, sweat the shallot and garlic in the remaining oil for 3 minutes over medium heat, without browning.
Add the raw crozets, stir for 1 minute to coat them in fat.
Pour in the hot stock, cover and cook for 20 minutes over medium heat. Stir every 3 or 4 minutes: the friction releases the starch and creates the creamy binding.
Return the mushrooms to the sauté pan for the last 5 minutes, just long enough for them to heat through without breaking apart.
Off the heat, stir in the cream and parmesan. Season with pepper and mix until you reach a coating consistency. Serve immediately: the crozets continue to absorb liquid.

title: Sesame corn hummus
intro: Corn provides the sugar, chickpeas the structure: it's all about the balance between the two and the amount of oil you add at the end.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: Toast (dry-heat to develop the aromas) the sesame seeds in the titanium pan, without oil, over medium heat. Two to three minutes, shaking the handle regularly. As soon as the seeds turn golden and release their aroma, transfer them (out of the hot pan) to a cold plate: the titanium retains heat and they would continue to brown otherwise.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a pan according to the technique described above. Set aside.
Peel and remove the germ from the garlic. Combine in the food processor bowl the corn, chickpeas, garlic, lemon juice, salt and pepper. Pour in 4 tablespoons of olive oil.
Blend with short pulses first, to break up the grains, then continuously until you obtain a smooth mass. Scrape down the sides once or twice.
Taste. Add the remaining oil one tablespoon at a time, blending between each addition, until you reach the desired consistency: the hummus should fall slowly from the spatula.
Adjust the salt and acidity. Spread it out, creating a groove with a spoon, drizzle with oil, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.

title: Iced banana latte
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the coffee: lukewarm, it drowns the ice cream and dilutes the banana.

ing.note: or another milk of your choice

titane: Heat a dry titanium pan over high heat and cook the banana slices for the topping for one minute per side, without any oil. The sugars will caramelize on contact, while the flesh remains firm. Transfer the bananas from the pan to a cold plate and let them come to room temperature before adding the topping.
steps: Pull the espressos first. Pour them into a small cup and place in the freezer while you prepare the other ingredients: they should be thoroughly cold.
Peel the bananas, cut them into chunks and put them in the blender bowl with the oat milk, cane sugar and vanilla.
Blend for around thirty seconds, until the mixture is smooth and coats the sides of the bowl. No lumps should remain.
Fill a large glass with ice cubes right to the top. Pour the banana mixture over it, leaving two centimetres free at the top.
Add the cold coffee in a thin stream down the centre. Let the layers form naturally, or stir once with a spoon if you prefer a uniform colour.
Top with banana slices and sprinkle with cinnamon.

title: No-bake red berry yule log
intro: Everything depends on the consistency of the cream: too soft, the log collapses when cut; firm enough, it slices cleanly after a night in the cold.
ing: Very cold, full-fat liquid cream (30% fat).
titane: Combine the mascarpone and cream in a chilled bowl. Whisk slowly at first to loosen the mascarpone, then gradually increase the speed until the mixture forms stiff peaks (it should hold its shape on the whisk and form a soft, glossy peak that doesn't collapse). Stop whisking; beyond this point, the mixture will become grainy and brittle.
steps: Plan ahead: the log should rest for a minimum of 5 hours in the refrigerator, ideally overnight; start the day before.
Combine the mascarpone, jam and very cold cream in a large bowl. Whisk until you obtain a firm and smooth cream. Reserve in the cold, setting aside two good spoonfuls for decoration.
Pour the milk into a shallow dish. Dip a ladyfinger biscuit for one second per side, no more: it should remain firm in the center.
Spread a large sheet of plastic wrap on the work surface. Align six ladyfinger biscuits side by side, rounded side facing down.
Place a second row of ladyfinger biscuits on top, this time flat side facing up: you obtain a regular base, easier to roll and to slice.
Spread a thin layer of cream over the entire surface to bind the biscuits together.
Deposit a strip of cream along the center, then press raspberries and blueberries into it in a continuous line.
Cover with a final layer of cream, then close the log by pulling the plastic wrap towards you to roll the ladyfingers around the filling.
Tighten the plastic wrap at both ends like a sweet. Press gently over the entire length to compact the log and remove any air pockets.
Reserve in the refrigerator for a minimum of 5 hours, ideally an entire night.
Remove the plastic wrap, place the log on a cold serving plate. Smooth the remaining cream over the top, distribute the remaining fruit and dust with icing sugar at the last moment.

title: Cold mint syrup
intro: No cooking: it is the sugar and lemon that draw the essential oil from the mint, and this is what gives a green color and a bright aroma where a cooked syrup turns brown.
titane: No pans here; the heat would spoil the aroma. The crucial step is the final pressing: squeeze the leaves against the sieve until they release no more juice. The last third of the juice, the most concentrated, is still in the leaf.
steps: Plan ahead: the syrup macerates for 72 hours in the refrigerator, start three days before serving.
Strip the leaves from the mint stems. Rinse the leaves in cold water, then dry them carefully in a cloth: residual water shortens shelf life.

Place a layer of leaves at the bottom of a clean jar. Cover with sugar. Press down lightly with your fingertips to bruise the leaf (crumple the leaf to release its oils). Alternate mint and sugar until the jar is full, ending with sugar.
Squeeze the lemons, strain the juice from the pips, pour it over the layers. Close the jar.
Place in the refrigerator for 72 hours. Turn the jar upside down morning and evening: the sugar dissolves gradually and must soak all the leaves.
Pour the contents into a fine strainer lined with cloth, set over a bowl. Let drain, then press firmly on the leaves, several times, until completely extracted.
Transfer to a sterilized bottle. Keep in the refrigerator and consume within three weeks.

title: Burrata stuffed with pesto, tomato and arugula
intro: It all depends on the freshness of the burrata and the tomato, which must be perfectly ripe and thinly sliced.

ing.note: Remove from the fridge 10 minutes before

titane: No cooking required here: the pan stays in the cupboard. The key is the injection. Pierce the burrata only once, from the top, where the creamy layer is thickest. Push the pesto in slowly so it settles in the center without breaking the skin. Just one point of entry, and the burrata will hold up until serving.
steps: Remove the burrata from the refrigerator and let it return to room temperature for a few minutes before filling it.
Slice the tomato thinly, barely 3 mm, with a sharp knife. Arrange the slices in a rosette pattern (in a spiral, slightly overlapping) at the bottom of the plate.
Season with salt and pepper. Drizzle with a thread of olive oil, then a few drops of balsamic vinegar.
Distribute the arugula in the center, without pressing down.
Fill a kitchen syringe or piping bag fitted with a fine nozzle with the pesto. Fill the burrata (inject the filling into the center) until you feel slight resistance.
Place the burrata on the bed of arugula, injection side facing up. Serve immediately, with bread for dipping.

title: Yogurt and chocolate chip cake, cooked in a pan
intro: A snack cake whose moistness comes entirely from the yogurt: the dough remains soft, the chocolate melts in pockets inside.
titane: The covered pan works like a small oven: the heat rises from the bottom, and the steam trapped under the lid cooks the top. Maintain a constant low heat, and never lift the lid for the first fifteen minutes. If you hear sizzling, it's too hot.
steps: In a bowl, whisk the yogurt with the sugar, egg and liquid vanilla until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous mixture (basic mixture).
Pour the oil in a thin stream, whisking constantly. The mixture should remain glossy.

Separately mix the flour, yeast, and salt. Incorporate them in three additions, using a spatula, without overmixing: stop as soon as all the dry flour is incorporated. Scrape down the sides of the bowl to gather the dough.
Add the chocolate chips. Two turns of a spatula are enough to distribute them.
Butter the cold titanium pan, bottom and sides. Pour in the batter, smooth the top, and tap the pan once on the work surface to remove any large bubbles.
Cover and place over low heat. Cook for 20 minutes without uncovering.
Remove the lid and check with the tip of a knife in the center: it should come out dry. If not, cover and continue for 5 minutes.
Let it cool for 10 minutes in the pan before turning it out onto a wire rack. Cut into portions.

title: Melon-apricot sorbet with ginger
intro: Without an ice cream maker, everything hinges on the double freezing process: you freeze the raw fruit, blend it, refreeze it, and the texture becomes smooth.

ing.note: deseeded and hollowed out (approximately 450g of flesh)

titane: Blend the fruit while it's still very cold, never thawed. The blender breaks up the ice crystals instead of melting them: this cold shearing is what gives a churned sorbet its tight texture. If the mixture starts to run down the sides of the bowl, put it back in the freezer for ten minutes before continuing.
steps: Plan ahead: the sorbet spends approximately 4 hours then 6 hours in the freezer, start the day before or early in the day.
Cut the melon flesh and apricots into regular pieces of approximately 2 cm. The smaller the pieces, the shorter the blending time.
Combine the fruits in a mixing bowl with the sugar, honey, lemon zest and juice, grated ginger. Mix to coat: the sugar should begin to draw the juice from the fruits.
Spread everything in a thin layer in a dish or on a baking sheet, then place in the freezer for 4 hours. Spread flat, the fruits freeze quickly and detach easily.

Pour the well-frozen pieces into a powerful blender or food processor. Blend in pulses, then continuously, until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture, without fragments. Scrape the sides one or two times.
Transfer to another container in a bowl covered with cling film and return to the freezer for 6 hours.
Remove the sorbet 10 minutes before serving, to allow it to become creamy under the spoon.

title: Cold box of tuna, corn and risoni
intro: It all comes down to the sauce: flexible enough to coat, thick enough not to drown the pasta at the bottom of the can.
titane: Here, the pan remains cold: nothing cooks, everything comes together. Only the risoni pasta goes through a pot of salted water beforehand. If you still want a bit of char, pour the drained corn into the dry, very hot titanium pan and let it brown for 2 minutes without touching it. Transfer it (remove it from the pan to stop the cooking) to a cold plate before adding it to the rest of the dish, otherwise it will make the sauce too warm.
steps: In the bottom of the airtight container, combine the fromage blanc, mayonnaise, and mustard. Mix until you obtain a smooth sauce.
Season with lemon juice, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Taste now, not later — once the ingredients are added, correction is approximate.
Cut the cucumber into thin half-slices. Mince the red onion (cut it into very thin slices, along the grain so it remains crisp).
Drain the corn and tuna.
Layer over the sauce: the vegetables, the corn, the tuna roughly crumbled, then the risoni.
Close the container and shake firmly, two or three times. The sauce should rise and coat everything.
Keep refrigerated until the meal. A second round of shaking just before eating refreshes the mixture.

title: Vegan waffles, red fruit jam with chia seeds
intro: It all comes down to two things: a dough acidified with vinegar, which gives it a soft texture without eggs, and a jam made with chia seeds, without long cooking or added sugar in bulk.
ing: Soy-based plant drink enriched with fiber

ing.note: non-alcoholic apple cider or white vinegar

titane: Jam is made in a frying pan, not a saucepan. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes: the heat rises quickly and spreads evenly, the fruit softens more rapidly, and the mixture thickens without sticking, even over low heat. The wide base accelerates evaporation, which a narrow pan doesn't allow.
steps: Pour the plant-based milk into a bowl, add the vinegar and let it sit for 5 minutes: the mixture will curdle slightly. Stir in the melted butter and sugar.
In a bowl, combine the flour, yeast and salt. Make a well in the center.

Pour the liquid into the well and whisk until you have a smooth, lump-free batter. Don't overmix: excessive mixing develops gluten and makes the waffles elastic. Let the batter rest while the jam cooks.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the frozen berries, maple syrup, and chia seeds. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring regularly, until the berries have broken down and the mixture coats the back of a spoon. Transfer to a separate container and let cool slightly; the seeds will continue to expand off the heat.

Preheat the waffle iron. Pour a ladleful of batter into each mold and cook for approximately 3 minutes 30 seconds over medium heat, until the waffles are golden brown and crispy on top. Place them on a wire rack, never flat on a plate: the steam will soften the waffle pattern.

title: Tiramisu in a ramekin, for one person
intro: It all comes down to the soaking of the biscuits: two seconds too long and the structure collapses when it's time to serve.
titane: Dry-fry the biscuits in the hot titanium pan for thirty seconds per side, without any oil. They will dry slightly and absorb the coffee without falling apart. While they're cooking, reduce the coffee by a third over high heat: this intensifies the aroma, allowing for a shorter soaking time.
steps: Plan ahead: the tiramisu requires three to four hours in the refrigerator; allow this time before serving.
Whisk the egg yolk with the two sugars (work with a whisk until the mixture pales and doubles in volume). Allow three good minutes.
Fold in the cream cheese, cream and vanilla. Whisk until you obtain a smooth batter with no lumps, that holds on the whisk.
Dip each biscuit in the coffee for one second per side, no more. Line the bottom of the ramekin, breaking the biscuits to fit the shape.
Spread a layer of cream, then repeat: soaked biscuits, cream. Smooth the surface with a spatula.
Sift the cocoa in an even layer on top, just before setting aside.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for three to four hours minimum. The layers will firm up and the flavors will meld.

title: Mascarpone doughnuts with no resting time
intro: A dough that can be assembled in three minutes and fried immediately: it all comes down to the minimal work required and the temperature of the bath.
titane: Deep frying is not done in the titanium pan: you need a stable oil level, so a tall saucepan or a deep fryer is necessary. Save the pan for the next day. A drizzle of neutral oil over medium heat, and the leftover doughnuts will regain their crust in two minutes per side, whereas the oven would dry them out.
steps: Heat the oil to 170 °C in a tall saucepan, filled to mid-height at most. Without a thermometer: a small piece of dough dropped in should float back up in three seconds while crackling gently.
In a bowl, whisk the mascarpone with the eggs and caster sugar until you obtain a smooth batter.
Add the white vinegar. It slightly acidifies the batter, which limits oil absorption during cooking and produces less greasy doughnuts.
Mix the flour and baking powder, then incorporate them all at once. Stop as soon as the batter is combined (no dry flour visible). Overworked batter produces compact doughnuts.
Lightly oil your palms to prevent the batter from sticking. Take portions the size of a large walnut and roll them without insisting, just enough to obtain an irregular ball.
Immerse five or six at a time, no more: an overloaded batch causes the oil temperature to drop. Allow 3 to 4 minutes, turning them halfway through cooking for even browning.
Remove and drain on paper towels to remove excess oil. Leave to cool for two minutes, dust with icing sugar at the last moment.

title: Cucumber, avocado, radish and shrimp verrines
intro: It all comes down to the cutting and the water: regular cubes, dried vegetables, and the verrine stays neat until serving.
titane: Drain the cucumber (let it release its water with salt) for ten minutes in a colander, then press it between two sheets of paper towel. Otherwise, the water will seep to the bottom of the glass within an hour and dilute the sauce. The same principle applies to radishes: dry them after trimming.
steps: Peel the cucumber in alternating strips, split it lengthwise in half, remove the seeds with a spoon. Cut it into 3 mm dice, salt lightly and let it drain for ten minutes in a colander. Press, set aside.
Cut the radishes into julienne (thin sticks), then cut the julienne into dice. Pat dry.
Set aside six whole large shrimp for plating. Cut the rest into pieces the same size as the vegetable dice.
Cut the avocados into dice just before assembly. Squeeze lemon juice over them immediately so they do not darken.
Combine cucumber, radishes and shrimp in a bowl. Add a drizzle of lemon juice, the spices, a pinch of salt. Toss gently without crushing.
Whisk the fresh cheese with the fromage blanc and grated lemon zest. The sauce should be smooth and firm enough to hold in a piping bag: if it runs, chill it for ten minutes.
Fill a piping bag. Place a base of sauce on the bottom of each verrines, then layer the avocado, radishes, shrimp, pressing down gently. Finish with a layer of sauce.
Top with a dollop of sauce, a whole shrimp and a sprig of dill.
Chill for at least one hour, but no more than four hours to keep the avocado looking fresh. You can prepare these verrines in advance and keep them chilled until ready to serve.

title: Puff pastry folded with pesto, smoked salmon and mozzarella
intro: It all comes down to moisture: if the filling is too soggy, the central puff pastry won't rise.
titane: Cut the dough only halfway through, never all the way through. These four sections remain attached and act as hinges when folding: the pastry then rises as a single unit, without falling apart. Next, seal the edges by pressing firmly with the back of a fork to enclose the filling.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C (conventional setting). Unroll the pastry onto its baking sheet and slide it onto a baking tray.
Pat the tomato and mozzarella slices dry between two sheets of absorbent paper. This step is crucial for the puff pastry to hold its shape.
Make cross cuts in the dough, halfway through its thickness, to delimit four rectangles joined together.
Spread the pesto over each area, leaving a 1 cm border. Distribute the mozzarella, then the smoked salmon, then the tomatoes.
Fold the rectangles over each other along the notches to create a four-layer sandwich.
Seal the edges with a fork. Brush the surface with egg yolk, sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 25 minutes, until the pastry is golden brown and distinctly crispy on the sides. Let it rest for 5 minutes before slicing, allowing the mozzarella to soften.

title: Greek yogurt ice cream without an ice cream maker
intro: It all comes down to the size of the crystals: frozen in small cubes and then blended, the mass remains fine and creamy, whereas a full container would give a grainy block.
titane: Pulse the mixture, not continuously. Three or four pulses, scrape down the sides, and repeat. The milk should only be added on the second pass, drop by drop: just enough for the blades to cut through, never enough to loosen the mixture. If the mixture becomes shiny and runny, it's too late; put it back in the refrigerator for ten minutes.
steps: Plan ahead: the ice cubes freeze for 8 hours or overnight, start the day before.

Whisk together the Greek yogurt, honey, vanilla and salt until the honey is completely dissolved. Taste and adjust the sugar at this stage: after freezing, the cold diminishes the perception of sweetness.
Pour into an ice cube tray, filling each cavity to the brim. Tap the tray on the work surface to release air bubbles.
Freeze for 8 hours, or overnight.
Unmould the cubes and let them temper (bring back to temperature) for 15 minutes on a cold plate. They should yield slightly under your fingernail.
Blend in short pulses, adding the milk gradually, until you obtain a smooth and stable texture.
Serve immediately in quenelles, or place back in the freezer for 20 minutes in a flat container if you want a firmer consistency.

title: Vanilla white icing for shortbread cookies
intro: It all comes down to consistency: if it's too runny, the icing will drip from the edges and leave the designs blurry; if it's too thick, it will break when dipped.
titane: Before incorporating it, gently warm the plant-based cream for ten seconds in the titanium pan over very low heat, then remove it from the heat. The icing sugar will dissolve easily, and the glaze will dry with a shinier finish. The pan should remain warm to the touch, never hot: if it gets too hot, the cream will bubble and the glaze will lose its opacity.
steps: Sift the icing sugar over a bowl. A single lump is enough to jam a toothpick in the middle of the marbling.
Pour the warmed plant-based cream in three stages, mixing with a spatula between each addition. The mixture will appear sandy, then bind together all at once.
Work until you obtain a smooth ribbon (the icing falls from the spatula in a continuous strip and takes three seconds to close on the surface). Adjust with a few drops of cream if the strip breaks.
Add vanilla flavoring and mix without incorporating air.
Take a small portion of the icing in a bowl and color it with gel. Avoid liquid food coloring: it dilutes the mixture and you'll be back to square one with icing sugar for ten minutes of fixing it.
Dip the shortbread cookies face down in the white icing, turn them flat, and scrape off the excess on the edge of the bowl.

Immediately place three dots of colored icing on the still-damp surface, then use a toothpick to draw a line through the dots to create a marbled effect. Let it set for 2 hours at room temperature, uncovered.

title: Strawberry and mascarpone whipped cream roll
intro: It all comes down to two things: a biscuit cooked just enough to remain flexible, and rolling done while still hot, before the dough sets.
titane: As soon as it comes out of the oven, turn the biscuit out onto a clean, lightly sugared tea towel, remove the parchment paper, and roll it up immediately, towel and all. It will take shape as it cools. Unrolled while still warm, it will retain the shape of the roll and won't crack when you add the filling.
steps: Plan ahead: the roll should rest in the refrigerator for a minimum of 2 hours before serving; please allow for this time.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper, bringing it up the sides.
Whisk the yolks with 70 g of sugar and vanilla until the mixture turns pale and doubles in volume. Incorporate the oil.

Whip the egg whites with the lemon juice. When they become frothy, pour in the remaining 30 g of sugar in a thin stream and beat them firmly (whisk faster towards the end to obtain a dense and glossy texture).
Loosen the yolks with a third of the whites, then incorporate the rest using a spatula, lifting the mixture. Sift the flour over the top and fold together until no dry streaks remain, no more.

Spread the batter on the sheet in an even layer approximately 1 cm thick. Smooth with an offset spatula. Bake for 11 minutes: the sponge cake should be golden and spring back when pressed with a finger.
Unmould immediately onto a sugared kitchen towel, remove the parchment paper, and roll lengthwise using the towel. Let cool for 20 minutes.
Whisk the mascarpone with icing sugar, then pour in the cold cream and whip the mixture to stiff peaks. Reserve in the refrigerator.
Hull the strawberries, slice two-thirds of them into strips, and set aside the remaining ones whole for the top.
Unroll the sponge cake. Spread the jam in a thin layer, then the mascarpone cream leaving 2 cm free on the opposite edge. Scatter the strawberry strips.
Roll firmly, without crushing. Wrap tightly in cling film and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours. Decorate with whole strawberries when serving, trim both ends with a serrated knife.

title: Pistachio and raspberry center muffins
intro: It all comes down to the pistachio center: frozen before being enclosed in the dough, it remains runny when the muffin is cooked.

ing.note: g, of which 120 g were frozen in 12 small piles on a

titane: Dry-roast the crushed pistachios in a titanium pan over medium heat for two to three minutes, stirring constantly. They should smell toasted before browning. Remove from the pan (transfer immediately to a cold plate): residual heat would burn them. This step brings out the pistachio's natural oils and gives the garnish a crisp texture that the oven alone cannot achieve.
steps: Plan ahead: the pistachio filling must freeze for at least three hours, or preferably overnight.
The day before or at least three hours in advance, place twelve small dollops of pistachio cream on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Place in the freezer until they are firm.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Butter the cups of the muffin tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar in a bowl until the mixture turns pale and doubles in volume: it should fall in a soft ribbon.
Pour in the oil, milk and raspberry jelly. Whisk to obtain a smooth and homogeneous base.
Sift the flour with the baking powder over the bowl. Fold in with a spatula, without overworking: as soon as there is no more dry flour, stop. Overmixed batter produces rubbery muffins.
Place a spoonful of batter at the bottom of each cup. Set a dollop of frozen pistachio cream in the centre, then cover with batter until three quarters full.
Sprinkle with roasted pistachios.
Bake for 20 minutes at 180 °C. The muffins are puffed, golden, and a skewer inserted at the edge (not in the centre, where the filling remains runny) comes out clean.
On removal from the oven, let cool for 5 minutes in the tin. Top each muffin with a knob of pistachio cream and a fresh raspberry.

title: Watermelon mint lemonade
intro: It all comes down to filtering: a blended watermelon produces a cloudy and thick juice, it is the sieve that gives it its consistency and freshness.

ing.note: that's about 1.5 kg of flesh without the skin

titane: No pan needed here; heat has no place in this recipe. The crucial step happens over the sieve: let the juice drain on its own, without pressing the pulp with the back of a ladle. Pressing it releases fibers that cloud the drink and make it pasty after ten minutes. Wait one to two minutes, then remove the pulp remaining in the sieve (transfer the mixture to another container).
steps: Remove the rind from the watermelon and cut the flesh into large cubes. Remove the most visible seeds; the others will be removed during straining.
Blend the cubes with the lime juice until smooth, about thirty seconds. Don't over-blend, the juice will heat up.
Pour the mixture into a fine sieve placed over a bowl. Let it drain without pressing, then discard the pulp.
Fill a carafe with ice cubes and pour the filtered juice over them.
Add the lime slices and mint leaves, crushed between your palms to release their oils. Top up with sparkling water just before serving, not before: the bubbles dissipate quickly.

title: Carrot tagliatelle, smoked salmon and Greek yogurt
intro: It all depends on the thickness of the carrot ribbons: too thick, they remain hard; too thin, they sink in the yogurt.
ing: with 3 nice slices of smoked salmon
titane: No pan required here, but the same need for contact. Run the peeler along the entire length of the carrot in one smooth motion, applying consistent pressure. A hesitant movement will create uneven ribbons that will cook unevenly under the lemon's acidity. Rotate the carrot a quarter turn after each set of strokes to ensure an even peel all the way through.
steps: In a bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, pressed garlic, and a squeeze of lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper. Whisk for a few seconds to loosen the mixture (to soften it until smooth and pliable). The texture should coat the back of a spoon without running.
Spread this base evenly across the bottom of the plate using the back of a spoon. Leave a one-centimeter border around the edge.
Peel the carrots, then slice them into tagliatelle-like strips using a peeler, pressing down evenly along the entire length. Stop when you reach the fibrous core.
Place the ribbons on the yogurt without packing them down, allowing them to fall back into volume.

Arrange the smoked salmon strips among the carrots. Add a drizzle of olive oil, the roughly chopped dill and basil. Give it a final grind and serve within minutes: the salt is already starting to draw out the carrot's moisture.

title: Chocolate-hazelnut cupcakes with mascarpone whipped cream
intro: It all comes down to two things: butter that is really soft to the touch at the start, and cupcakes that are perfectly cold before filling.

ing.note: to fill the center of the cupcakes

titane: Dry-roast the chopped hazelnuts in a titanium pan over medium heat for three to four minutes, stirring constantly. They should brown lightly and release their aroma. Remove them immediately (transfer them from the pan to stop the cooking process): if left in the hot pan, they will continue to brown and turn bitter. Set aside for finishing.
steps: Beat the soft butter with the sugar and vanilla sugar until you reach a creamy texture (soft, smooth, without any cold butter lumps). Remove the butter from the refrigerator an hour in advance if necessary.
Add the egg and mix until the batter becomes homogeneous again.
Fold in the flour, baking powder and salt, then the milk. Mix without overworking: the batter should be smooth, not overworked.
Preheat the oven to 170 °C.
Divide the batter among fifteen cupcake moulds, filling them two-thirds of the way up. The batter rises significantly during baking.
Bake for 15 minutes at 170 °C. A knife point should come out clean.
Turn out and let cool completely on a rack. A warm cupcake would melt the cream.
Whip the whipping cream and mascarpone until the mixture thickens and holds its shape on the whisk. Stop as soon as it forms soft peaks: beyond that point, it will become grainy.
Core each cupcake (make a well about 2 cm deep with a knife point or using an apple corer), fill it with cream using a piping bag, then pipe a rosette on top.
Sprinkle with hazelnuts and refrigerate for a few moments before serving.

title: Strawberry and chocolate rolled crepes
intro: A rested batter and a well-handled pan produce crepes that are flexible enough to be rolled tightly without cracking.
titane: Heat the pan dry, over medium heat, until a drop of water dances on the surface and then evaporates. Reduce the heat slightly, pour the batter into the center, and tilt the pan in a circular motion: titanium pan needs no oil or butter, and the first crêpe will turn out perfectly, as will all the others. If the batter sets before reaching the edges, the heat is too high.
steps: Combine flour, sugar and salt in a bowl. Make a well in the center, crack the eggs into it, and whisk together, bringing the flour from the edge towards the center.

Thin the mixture with the warm milk, adding it in three stages, then the oil. The dough should coat the back of a spoon (it should be covered with a layer that holds its shape). Let it rest for 15 minutes.

Heat a dry pan. Pour in a small ladleful of batter, spread it out by swirling it, and cook for 1 minute 30 seconds until the edges start to lift. Flip the pancakes and cook for another 40 seconds. Transfer them to a plate and stack them flat: the steam will keep them soft.
Hull and slice the strawberries. Set aside a dozen for decoration.

Place a crepe on your work surface. Spread a thin layer of chocolate spread, leaving a 1 cm border, then arrange the strawberry slices on top. Roll up tightly, starting from the edge. Repeat with the remaining crepes.

Arrange the rolls side by side on a long platter. Cover with a ribbon of whipped cream, grate dark chocolate over the top, arrange the reserved strawberries and finish with icing sugar, sifted just before serving.

title: Chocolate cookies with a pistachio center
intro: It all comes down to two temperatures: a pistachio center frozen in the cold, a rested dough, and a baking time short enough that the center remains runny.

ing.note: g, plus a handle for finishing

titane: Here, the titanium pan stays in the cupboard: the risen dough requires gentle, enveloping heat, and direct contact would burn the base before the center melts. The technique shifts to the cold. Portion the pistachio cream into balls and freeze them for at least an hour. A hard ball will be neatly coated in dough and hold its shape until the cookie comes out of the oven. A soft ball will sink to the bottom and seep through the cookie.
steps: Plan ahead: the pistachio balls freeze for one hour and the cookies then rest for two hours in the refrigerator, allow time before serving.
Using a small spoon, scoop the pistachio cream and roll six regular balls, place them on a film-wrapped plate and put them in the freezer for one hour.
Cream the softened butter with the two sugars (beat with a whisk until the mixture becomes pale and fluffy).
Add the egg and then the vanilla. Mix just enough for the mixture to become homogeneous again.
Sift the flour with the baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and salt on one side, and sift the cocoa separately: it forms tight lumps that a single pass does not break.
Pour the dry ingredients over the mixture, add the 85 g of chocolate chips and fold with a spatula until all dry streaks disappear. Stop here, the dough should not be worked further.

Scoop the dough with an ice cream scoop. Make a hollow in each portion in the palm of your hand, place a frozen pistachio ball in the centre, seal it closed and roll to seal. The layer of dough should be even all around.
Arrange the balls on a baking sheet, cover and leave to rest for two hours in the refrigerator. The butter firms up, the cookies spread less.
Press a few chocolate chips on the top of each ball.
Preheat the oven.
Bake at 180 °C for 12 minutes. The edges are set, the centre still appears soft and slightly puffed. Do not extend the baking time: it is what determines the runny centre.
Let cool on the baking sheet for ten minutes before removing the cookies, they continue to set as they cool.
At serving time, add a drizzle of pistachio cream and a few crushed pistachio pieces.

title: Feta dip with green olives
intro: It all comes down to texture: a short blend keeps the olives grainy, too long a blend turns the dip into a soft paste.
titane: Heat the titanium pan dry over medium heat, without any oil or butter. Place pita bread triangles or thin slices of country bread in the pan and cook for one minute per side, until the surface is marked and crisp. Dry titanium produces a crisp, clean crust, without the soggy texture of bread cooked in oil. Remove from the pan and let cool on a wire rack to allow the steam to escape.
steps: Peel the garlic and remove the central germ, which is more bitter. Drain the olives if they are in brine.
Place the olives, garlic, cheese crumbled roughly by hand, oil and lemon juice in the bowl of a food processor. Blend for one minute, stopping once to scrape down the sides.
Taste. If the mixture remains compact, pour in a thin drizzle of olive oil and run the processor for a few seconds.
Add the basil and give three or four short pulses: the leaves should remain visible, not disappear into the mixture.
Spread the dip into a wide bowl, lightly hollow out the center with a spoon. Cut the sun-dried tomatoes into strips and place them in this hollow. Serve with warm toasted bread.

title: Fresh cheese balls in balloon-like shapes
intro: It all depends on how well the cheese holds its shape: if it's too soft, the ball sinks onto the biscuit and the pattern gets blurry.
titane: Toast the biscuits dry in a very hot titanium pan for 30 seconds per side, without any oil or butter. They will regain their crispness and hold their shape under the cheese without becoming soggy. Let them cool completely on a wire rack before assembling: a warm biscuit will melt the cheese ball.
steps: Place the fresh cheese in the refrigerator for 20 minutes, bowl included. Very cold cheese rolls cleanly without sticking to your hands.
Heat the titanium pan dry over medium heat. Toast the crackers for 30 seconds per side. Remove them (transfer out of the pan to stop the heat) onto a rack and allow to cool.
Season the cheese with salt and pepper, mix briefly. Take portions of approximately 8 g and roll them between your palms, lightly dampened, to obtain regular balls.
Reserve the balls in the cold on a plate while you prepare the decoration.
Cut the olives into small diamonds and pentagons of 3 to 4 mm, using a well-sharpened paring knife.
Apply the olive pieces to each ball by pressing lightly: one pentagon at the top, the others all around. The ball pattern should be readable at a glance.
Place each ball on a cooled cracker at the time of serving. Beyond 30 minutes at room temperature, the cracker absorbs moisture from the cheese.

title: Smoked salmon and avocado domes
intro: It all comes down to the presentation: a salmon stretched taut in the mold, a packed filling, and the dome unmolds cleanly.
titane: Dry-toast the bread slices in a titanium pan over medium heat, without any oil or butter. Place them in the pan, press down firmly for a second with the back of a spatula to ensure good contact, then let them brown for 60 to 90 seconds per side. The bread should dry completely, not just brown: it will form a base and absorb the moisture from the avocado without becoming soggy.
steps: Plan ahead: the dome must rest in the refrigerator for a minimum of one hour; factor in this time before serving.
Cut the bread slices with a cutter to the exact diameter of the opening of your silicone moulds. Keep the offcuts for another use.
Toast the discs dry in the titanium pan, 60 to 90 seconds per side. Remove from the pan and set aside on a rack so they don't sweat.
Line the mould cavities (coat the walls) with smoked salmon, strips slightly overlapping, leaving the ends protruding outside.
Spread the cream cheese in an even layer against the walls, about half a centimetre thick. Build it up to the top: this layer is what holds everything together.
Mix the diced avocado with lemon juice, season with pepper, add chilli and dill. Fill the centre of the dome.
Fold the salmon ends over the filling, place the toasted bread disc on top, press firmly to compress.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 1 hour. Unmould onto a plate at service time, bread side down.

title: Vegan marbled waffles
intro: It all comes down to contrast: two liquid preparations of the same density, placed side by side without ever being mixed.
titane: The marbling is achieved with a spoon, not in the bowl. Spoon the two batters onto the waffle iron in a staggered pattern, each in its own quarter, then immediately close the iron: the pressure of the waffle iron will cause them to merge naturally and create the vein. One too many turns of the spoon and you'll end up with a uniformly brown waffle. If you don't have a waffle iron, cook the batter in thick pancakes in a titanium pan over medium heat, two minutes per side; the marbling will remain distinct.
steps: Pour 1 litre de boisson végétale, versez-la dans un saladier, ajoutez le jus de citron et laissez reposer 5 minutes : le mélange épaissit légèrement et prend une texture de lait fermenté.
Incorporez le beurre végétal fondu et le sucre. Fouettez pour dissoudre.
Ajoutez la farine, la levure et le sel. Mélangez jusqu'à obtenir une pâte lisse, sans plus : un appareil trop travaillé donne une gaufre élastique.
Répartissez la pâte à parts égales dans deux bols.

Versez le chocolat fondu dans l'un des deux et mélangez jusqu'à une couleur uniforme. Les deux pâtes doivent rester de même consistance ; si la chocolatée s'épaissit, détendez-la avec une cuillère de boisson végétale.
Préchauffez le gaufrier. Déposez 2 càs de pâte claire et 2 càs de pâte chocolatée en alternance sur la plaque, sans les remuer.
Fermez et cuisez 3 minutes, jusqu'à ce que la vapeur se raréfie sur les bords. Débarrassez (retirez du feu et déposez) sur une grille, jamais sur une assiette : le dessous resterait mou.
Servez tièdes, nappées de pâte à tartiner.

title: Creamy corn hummus
intro: A hummus without tahini, where corn provides sweetness and chickpeas provide structure: everything depends on the oil added in a thin stream, never all at once.
titane: First, dry-blend the legumes and corn alone until you obtain a grainy paste. Only then, with the motor running, do you slowly pour in the oil in a thin stream to emulsify the mixture (incorporate the fat gradually so that it emulsifies instead of floating on top). The creaminess comes from this, not from the amount of oil.
steps: Drain the corn and chickpeas. Rinse the chickpeas in cold water and let them drain for one minute: residual water dilutes the hummus.
Pour corn and chickpeas into the blender bowl. Pulse until you obtain a thick and uneven paste.
Add the lemon juice, salt and pepper. Pulse again for 15 seconds.
With the motor running, pour the olive oil in a thin stream. Stop as soon as the mixture forms a supple ribbon that falls slowly from the spatula.
If the mass remains compact or sticks to the sides, add the oil one spoonful at a time, pulsing between each addition. Adjust the salt and acidity.
Transfer to the serving dish, making a furrow with a spoon. Drizzle with a thin stream of oil, sprinkle with paprika.

title: Soufflé doughnuts with fresh cheese
intro: A dough without resting, without rising, which swells on its own in the oil: everything depends on the temperature of the bath, 170 °C, not one degree more.

ing.note: taken out of the refrigerator an hour in advance

titane: This is done in a deep fryer, not a pan: the oil needs to be at least 6 cm deep so the doughnuts float and turn on their own. Use a heavy-bottomed pot or a deep fryer. The titanium reflex remains the same, it simply shifts to the oil: let it heat up slowly, check it with a little batter (it should rise to the surface in three seconds, sizzling), and wait for it to return to its normal temperature between batches. Warm oil soaks into the doughnuts, oil that's too hot browns them before the center is set.
steps: Work the fresh cheese with a spatula in a bowl until it is softened (smooth, without lumps or hard clumps). If it's straight from the refrigerator, it will resist and the mixture will remain grainy.
Add the sugar, vanilla and eggs. Mix until you obtain a smooth and creamy mixture.

Sift together the flour and baking powder (pass them through a sieve to avoid lumps and aerate), add the salt. Incorporate in two stages: you are looking for a runny batter that falls from the spoon in a thick ribbon.
Heat the oil to 170°C in a tall saucepan. Dip a tablespoon into the hot oil before each scoop: the dough will detach easily.
Place the quenelles of dough in the bath, four or five at a time, without overcrowding it. They will puff up and turn themselves over once the first side is set; use a skimmer if necessary.
Cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until a deep, even golden color is achieved. Transfer to a wire rack, not paper towels, to maintain a crispy surface.
Sprinkle with icing sugar at the last minute. To fill them, pierce the side with the tip of a knife and pipe in the spread while the doughnuts are still warm.

title: Creamy winter vegetable soup
intro: A soup thickened with milk rather than cream alone: everything depends on the cooking of the roux and on a fairly low heat so that nothing sticks to the bottom.

ing.note: g, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

titane: This preparation remains in a saucepan or stockpot: nearly a liter and a half of liquid, with high sides essential. The key here is thickening the sauce. Cook the butter-flour mixture for a good two minutes before adding the milk, otherwise the soup will retain a raw flour taste. Then pour in the cold milk in three stages, whisking between each addition: the first third forms a smooth paste, the subsequent additions loosen it without lumps.
steps: Heat the olive oil with 15 g of butter in a large saucepan. Add the diced onion, carrot and celery. Sweat (cook without browning) for 6 to 7 minutes over medium heat, stirring.
Add the garlic, let it open for 30 seconds, no longer.
Pour in the potatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer, cover half-way, then cook for 15 minutes: a knife point should pass through a cube with no resistance.
Meanwhile, melt the remaining 55 g of butter in a small saucepan. Add the flour all at once and whisk. Cook for 2 minutes over low heat: the roux should remain pale blonde and smell of hazelnut.
Incorporate the cold milk in three additions, whisking until you obtain a smooth sauce. Leave to thicken for 3 minutes without ceasing to stir.
Pour this liaison into the vegetable saucepan. Mix, then add the broccoli and drained corn. Continue for 5 minutes over low heat, scraping the bottom with a spatula.
Off the heat, add the cream. Season with salt and pepper, taste. If the soup seems too thick to you, thin it with a little hot stock.

title: Mango and coconut kefir chia pudding
intro: It all comes down to the ratio of seeds to liquid: too tight, the pudding becomes compact; properly measured, it remains creamy and the seeds retain their chewiness.
titane: Toast (dry-roast, without oil) the coconut flakes in a titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir constantly and remove from the heat as soon as they turn golden brown around the edges: the residual heat of the metal finishes the job. This is the only hot step in the recipe, and it's what gives the dish its unique character.
steps: Plan ahead: the pudding needs to rest for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator; factor in this time before serving.
Pour the coconut milk, plant-based kefir and maple syrup into a bowl. Whisk to combine: the coconut milk tends to separate into two phases and needs to be re-emulsified.
Add the chia seeds. Stir, wait 2 minutes, then stir again. This second pass breaks up the clumps of seeds that have gathered at the bottom.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. The mixture is ready when a spoon stands upright in it for a second before tipping over.
Meanwhile, toast the coconut flakes in a pan. Transfer them to a cold plate to stop the cooking.
Cut the mango into 1-centimetre cubes. Slice along the flat pit, score the flesh in a crosshatch pattern without piercing the skin, turn the mango half over and scoop out the cubes with a knife.
Divide the pudding among 4 bowls. Top with mango cubes, sprinkle with warm coconut flakes and serve immediately to maintain the contrast of temperatures.

title: Banana and double chocolate cake
intro: It all comes down to the ripeness of the bananas and a very brief final mixing: the more you work the dough, the tighter the crumb becomes.

ing.note: g, plus a handle for finishing

titane: Before mashing them, place the halved bananas in a very hot titanium pan, cut-side down, for two minutes without moving them. The sugars will caramelize on the surface and the puree will thicken. Remove from the heat and transfer to a cold container immediately to stop the cooking process.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), conventional setting. Grease the cake tin and line it with baking paper.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl. Keep some pieces whole: they will melt during baking and create moist pockets in the crumb.
Pour the warm melted butter, cream and eggs over the mixture. Whisk until you obtain a smooth base liquid mixture.
Add both sugars. Mix for about twenty seconds, until they dissolve.
Combine flour, cocoa and baking powder in a small container, then sift (pass through a sieve to aerate the powder and crush any lumps) directly over the mixture.
Mix with a spatula, without overworking, until the streaks of flour disappear. Incorporate the chocolate chips in three or four movements.
Pour into the mold, smooth the surface, distribute the remaining handful of chocolate chips.
Bake for 50 to 60 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out with a few moist crumbs and melted chocolate, never completely dry.
Allow to cool for 15 minutes in the mold before unmolding onto a wire rack.

title: Cucumber sticks topped with smoked salmon
intro: It all comes down to the cucumber: it must be firm and well hollowed out, otherwise the water it releases will make the rice soggy in a few minutes.
titane: Dry-roast the sesame seeds in a very hot titanium pan, without any oil. Shake the pan continuously for one minute, remove from the heat as soon as the seeds turn golden and transfer them immediately (to a cold plate): the residual heat from the coating would be enough to burn them.
steps: Toast the sesame seeds as described above. Set aside.
Split the cucumber lengthwise. Using a small spoon, scrape out the center to create a neat groove on each half. Pat the inside dry with paper towels.
Cut the smoked salmon into half-centimeter strips. Finely chop the chives.
Pack the cold rice into the grooves, without compacting it excessively: it should remain pearly. Smooth the surface with the back of a spoon.
Spread the salmon over the rice, then add the chives.
Drizzle with mayonnaise, add hot sauce if using, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.
Slice each half into three-centimeter pieces with a sharp knife. Serve immediately.

title: Buckwheat crozets with mushrooms, cooked by absorption
intro: It all depends on the colouring of the mushrooms: if they release their water without turning golden, the dish will remain flat.
ing: Button mushrooms or mixed forest mushrooms
titane: First, place the mushrooms alone in a very hot, lightly oiled titanium pan: in a single layer, without stirring for the first minute, until a golden crust forms. Remove them from the heat and place them on a plate, then transfer everything to a deep-sided sauté pan. The 80 cl of stock requires depth: the pan is for searing, not absorption.
steps: Finely slice the shallot, mince the garlic. Clean the mushrooms with a dry brush or cloth, then cut them into thick quarters.
Heat the titanium pan over high heat with a drizzle of oil. Sear the mushrooms in a single layer, without salt, until well browned. Remove from the pan.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the remaining oil to a deep sauté pan and sweat the shallot (cook without browning until translucent) for 4 minutes. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Return the mushrooms to the pan, add salt, pour in the crozets and mix for a minute to coat them in fat.

Moisten with the hot stock, scrape the bottom to loosen the browned bits, cover and cook for 15 minutes over medium heat. Stir two or three times: the crozets should be tender and the liquid almost completely absorbed.

Remove from boiling and, over low heat, stir in the cream, Parmesan cheese, and pepper. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, then stir: the sauce should coat the back of a spoon without floating. Adjust the seasoning and serve immediately.

title: Greek salad with marinated tofu
intro: It all comes down to the marinade: the tofu needs to soak up the marinade while you're chopping the vegetables, otherwise it will remain bland in the center.

ing.note: of which you will keep half

titane: No fire is needed for this recipe. The pan acts as a press: place the drained block of tofu between two sheets of paper towel, then lay the titanium pan on top, bottom against the tofu. Its weight and flat surface will expel the water in five minutes, without crushing the tofu. The drained tofu absorbs the marinade instead of repelling it.
steps: Press the tofu (see above), then cut it into cubes of about 1 cm.
In a bowl, whisk together the malted yeast, olive oil, vinegar and salt until well blended.
