Place the tofu cubes in the bowl, coat them with the marinade, then top up with cold water. The cubes should be submerged, not floating on the surface. Set aside while you cut them.
Remove the seeds from the tomatoes if they release a lot of juice, then cut them into thick wedges. Cut the cucumber into half-moons, the pepper into short strips, and the red onion into thin petals.
Combine the vegetables in a large bowl. Add the olives, then the drained tofu with two tablespoons of its marinade. Mix gently by hand, keeping the cubes intact.

title: Water-based chocolate marble cake
intro: Without a drop of milk, the crumb remains soft for several days: it is the water, combined with the oil, that keeps it soft.
titane: Chocolate is cut with a knife, never into chips. Lay the block flat, attack it from an angle, keeping the blade straight: you'll get irregular shards, thin shavings, and a few thick pieces. The thin ones melt and streak the dough, while the thick ones remain gooey in the center. Chips, on the other hand, are formulated to hold their shape—exactly what we don't want here.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a cake tin with baking paper, leaving it overhanging on the long sides.
Whisk the eggs with the sugar until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous mixture, with no visible grains under the whisk.
Pour the oil in a thin stream, mix, then add the water. Continue until the mixture is perfectly smooth — it will seem very liquid, that's normal.
Incorporate the 320g of flour, the yeast and the salt all at once. Mix gently: stop as soon as the dough is smooth.
Weigh the dough and divide it into two equal portions in two bowls.

In the first bowl, add the remaining 35g of flour. In the second, sift in the 35g of cocoa powder. Smooth each mixture separately: the lighter batter will be slightly thicker, the cocoa batter slightly denser.
Cut the chocolate with a knife (see above).

Pour a ladleful of the light batter into the center of the mold, then a ladleful of the chocolate batter on top, always in the same spot. Alternate until all the batter is used up: the weight of each layer will spread the previous one and create the marbled effect on its own. Do not stir.
Scatter the chocolate chips over the last layer of cocoa, barely pressing them in.
Bake for 40 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean, except for the melted chocolate. Let cool for 10 minutes before unmolding, then cool completely on a wire rack.

title: Tortellini salad with cherry tomatoes and mozzarella
intro: A leftover salad that works as long as the pasta is very cold and the dressing is prepared separately, never poured haphazardly.

ing.note: half a piece, cut into cubes

titane: Before assembling, toast the cold tortellini for three minutes in a very hot, dry titanium pan, without stirring them immediately. They will develop a golden, crispy crust that contrasts beautifully with the cucumber and mozzarella. Transfer them from the pan to a cold plate and let them come to room temperature before mixing them with the other ingredients: warm pasta will cause the tomato to release its moisture.
steps: Drain the mozzarella balls and place them on paper towels while preparing the rest.
Peel the half cucumber, then cut it into dice.
Combine in a salad bowl the tortellini, the halved cherry tomatoes, the diced cucumber and the mozzarella.
In a bowl, thin the pesto with olive oil. Whisk with a fork until you obtain a homogeneous sauce, without basil lumps remaining at the bottom.
Pour the sauce over the salad. Mix by hand or with two spoons, lifting rather than stirring, to avoid tearing the stuffed pasta.
Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve within the hour.

title: No-bake lemon and blueberry squares
intro: It all depends on the firmness of the base: a well-compacted crust holds up when cut, a soft crust collapses under the cream.
titane: Melt the butter over very low heat directly in the titanium pan, then remove from the heat. Sprinkle the breadcrumbs over the butter and mix in the still-warm pan: the residual heat will coat each crumb without browning. This saves you a bowl and gives you a homogeneous mixture, ready to be pressed down.
steps: Line a 20cm square mold with baking paper (line the base and sides, leaving two strips hanging over; these will be used for unmolding).

Mix the breadcrumbs and melted butter until the mixture resembles damp sand. Pour into the mold and press down firmly with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass, paying particular attention to the corners.
Place in the refrigerator for 15 minutes, allowing the butter to solidify and seal the base.

Beat the cream cheese alone until perfectly smooth and lump-free. Add the lemon pudding mix, stir, then slowly pour in the cold heavy cream in a thin stream while whisking. Continue whisking until the mixture is thick and holds its shape on the whisk.
Remove the base and spread the lemon mixture in an even layer. Smooth with a spatula.
Spoon the blueberry topping over the top, then spread it out without pressing down so as not to mix it with the lemon layer.
Cover with whipped cream, smooth it out, and sprinkle with fresh blueberries.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour, preferably 3 hours. Unmold by pulling on the paper, then cut into 9 squares with a blade that has been dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Coconut, cranberry and orange bars
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the sauce must have cooled down before meeting the base, otherwise the coconut oil melts and the two layers mix.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan for the sauce. Its rapid heat-up makes the cranberries burst in minutes, and its large flat surface accelerates evaporation: the sauce thickens without prolonged reduction, therefore without caramelizing the maple syrup.
steps: Plan ahead: the bars must refrigerate for at least 3 hours before unmolding, allow for this time before serving.

In a mixing bowl, combine the shredded coconut, coconut milk, coconut oil, maple syrup, vanilla and salt. Mix until you obtain a homogeneous mixture that holds together when pressed between your fingers.

Line a square mold with parchment paper. Pour the mixture and pack firmly with the back of a spoon, pressing especially into the corners. Place in the refrigerator while you prepare the filling, so the base can firm up.

In the titanium pan, combine the cranberries, water, maple syrup, orange juice and zest, and cinnamon. Heat over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring from time to time. The berries should burst and the sauce should coat the spatula (leaving a film that does not run off immediately).
Off the heat, stir in the chia seeds directly into the pan. Let rest for 5 minutes: the sauce thickens and becomes sticky.
Let cool to room temperature, then transfer to the coconut base. Spread in an even layer.
Refrigerate for at least 3 hours, until the whole mixture is firm. Unmold and cut into bars with a blade dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: No-bake Oreo cheesecake verrines
intro: It all comes down to two things: a really firm whipped cream, and a lukewarm, never hot, ganache when it's time to coat it.
ing: Whole or half Oreos for decoration
Oreo crumbs for the finishing touch
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan for ganache. Its conductivity rises quickly: preheat it empty for one minute over low heat, pour in the milk, then work the chocolate off the heat, briefly returning the pan to the flame for a few seconds. The mixture remains smooth and shiny, without ever sticking.
steps: Plan ahead: refrigeration for 3 to 4 hours before serving.
Mix the finely crushed Oreos with the melted butter until you obtain a moist, homogeneous sandy mixture with no dry patches.
Divide among six glasses of 150 ml. Press down the bottom firmly with the back of a spoon.
Keep the glasses in the refrigerator while you prepare the filling.
Whip the whipped cream preparation with the ice-cold water until thick and firm. The water must be very cold: it gives the mixture its structure.
Add the cream cheese. Beat gently, just enough to smooth the mixture.
Fold in the 30 g crushed Oreos with a silicone spatula, lifting the preparation to avoid deflating it.
Fill the cooled bases with a spoon or pastry bag. Smooth the surface.
Return to the cold while you prepare the topping.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 1 minute over low heat.
Pour the milk, remove from heat, add the chocolate. Stir off the heat, with very brief returns to low heat, until you obtain a smooth and glossy ganache. Allow 3 minutes.
Let the ganache cool in the pan off the heat. It should still flow without effort. Coat each glass with a thin layer.
Decorate with a whole Oreo or a half, then add crumbs.
Refrigerate for 3 to 4 hours, until the surface is firm to the touch. Serve well chilled.

title: Crushed Brussels sprouts, lemon-tahini sauce
intro: It's all about moisture: steamed cabbage that's well dried before frying is the difference between a crispy coating and a soft coating.

ing.note: Brown rice for a gluten-free version
or the same amount of breadcrumbs plus

titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat when the choux pastry is added: the breading crisps on direct contact with the metal, and the Maillard reaction (the browning that creates the toasted flavor) occurs in just a few minutes, without preheating or sticking. Never load the pan with more than one layer; sear in two batches if necessary.
steps: Trim the cabbages, removing any damaged leaves. Steam them for 10 minutes in a covered steamer basket over medium-high heat. A knife should pierce them easily without the cabbage collapsing.
Remove the cabbages from the pan and place them on a board. Slide them between two sheets of baking paper and flatten each piece at the bottom of a jar until you obtain a disc about 1 cm thick.
Thoroughly blot both sides with paper towels. The surface should be dry to the touch.

Mix together the breadcrumbs, nutritional yeast, paprika, garlic powder, oregano, and salt in a bowl. Lightly oil the crushed cabbage with 2 tablespoons of oil, then press it into the dry mixture on both sides.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the remaining oil: it should simmer and coat the bottom in a moving film.

Place the choux pastries in a single layer, without overlapping them. Leave them undisturbed for 8 minutes. The choux pastry will detach itself from the metal once the first side is set and golden brown.
Turn them over with a flick of the wrist, reduce the heat to medium, cover and continue for 6 minutes to brown the second side and heat through.
While the pan is cooking, whisk together the yogurt, tahini, lemon juice, grated garlic, salt, and pepper. Thin with water, spoonful by spoonful, until you reach a coating consistency.
Serve directly from the pan, with the sauce on the side. These cabbage rolls don't keep well: they soften in the refrigerator.

title: Pistachio-crusted salmon, mango-avocado salsa
intro: The whole recipe hinges on one detail: the crust must stick to the fish, and for that you don't touch anything until it comes off by itself.
titane: The lid transforms the titanium pan into a sealed chamber. The pistachio crust browns through direct contact with the hot base, while the heat retained beneath the lid finishes the meat from above. Do not turn the fillet until it releases itself: if you force it, the breading will stick to the metal.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Grind the pistachios in a food processor until they reach a fine, irregular texture, similar to coarse sand. Do not grind them into a paste.
In a bowl, combine the pistachios, mustard, lemon juice, garlic, honey, salt and pepper. Mix well: you should obtain a compact mass that holds its shape on a spoon.
Pat the salmon fillets dry with paper towels on both sides. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread the pistachio paste over the top of each fillet and press firmly with the palm of your hand. The more you press it down, the less the crust will detach during cooking.
Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan. Place the fillets crust-side up, cover, and leave for 6 minutes without touching them. The indicator: the fish will release itself from the bottom.
Reduce heat to medium, replace the lid and continue for 8 minutes, until the crust is golden and the flesh is just pearly (opaque on the surface, still translucent in the center).
Meanwhile, mix the mango, red onion, bell pepper, avocado, cucumber and coriander in a salad bowl.
Drizzle with olive oil, squeeze in the lime, add salt and stir without crushing the avocado.
Remove the salmon from the pan and place it on a warm plate, then let it rest for 5 to 10 minutes. The residual heat will finish cooking it evenly.
Place the salsa on the bottom of the plate, then place the fillet on top, crust side up. Serve.

title: Mini strawberry and lemon cheesecakes
intro: It all comes down to undercooking: the dish should come out of the oven still wobbly in the center; it is the cold that finishes the setting.
ing: and a half of maple syrup or honey
pure maple syrup or raw honey
titane: Before assembling the tart shells, toast the biscuit crumbs in a dry titanium pan over medium heat for two to three minutes, stirring constantly. They should smell like brown butter and darken slightly. Remove from the heat and transfer to a cold container immediately, otherwise the residual heat of the titanium pan will continue to cook the crumbs and they will turn bitter. Add the melted butter only once the crumbs are lukewarm.
steps: Preheat the oven to 163°C. Line a 12-cavity muffin tin with paper baking cups.
Mix together the cooled toasted breadcrumbs, melted butter, and maple syrup. The mixture should hold together when you press it in the palm of your hand.
Place a tablespoon of mixture into each cavity and press down firmly with the back of a spoon or a small flat-bottomed glass.
Bake the bases for 5 to 6 minutes. Remove them and let them cool while you prepare the filling.
Beat the cream cheese and Greek yogurt until perfectly smooth. Scrape down the sides of the bowl twice: any cold lumps will remain visible after baking.
Incorporate the maple syrup, egg, salt, and lemon zest. Beat at low speed until combined. Too much air at this stage will cause the cheesecakes to rise and then collapse.
Distribute the mixture over the cooled bases, about 2 tablespoons per cavity.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes. The edges are set, the center still jiggles slightly when you shake the mold.
Let it cool for 30 minutes at room temperature, in the mold.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight. The texture will firm up and the lemon flavor will become more pronounced.
Remove from the molds, take out the baking cups and place a dollop of whipped cream on each chilled cheesecake.
Top with a strawberry point upwards, then place a small dot of cream on top.
Sprinkle with grated coconut or icing sugar when serving, not before: the humidity from the cold melts the sugar.

title: No-bake chocolate-cocoa cheesecake
intro: It's all about temperature: soft cheeses, ice cream, and a long rest that transforms a soft mixture into a clean slice.

ing.note: in large shards and in quarters

titane: Melt the butter in the titanium pan over very low heat, taking your time. The even heat distribution of the titanium prevents the hot spot that browns the butter and imparts a toasted nutty flavor to the crust, which is not desired here. Remove from the heat as soon as the last solid particles disappear: the butter should be liquid and clear, never hot to the touch. If poured too hot onto the biscuits, it will make them soggy instead of binding them.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake sets in the cold for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight, so start the day before.
Line the bottom of a 23 cm springform pan with parchment paper. Blitz the 20 whole biscuits, filling included, until you obtain a fine powder.
Melt the butter over low heat, let it cool slightly, then pour it over the biscuit powder. Mix until it reaches the texture of damp sand: the mixture should hold when pressed in your palm.
Press firmly into the bottom of the pan, using the bottom of a glass to achieve a flat, dense surface. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.

Meanwhile, beat the cream cheese and mascarpone until the mixture is perfectly smooth, without grains. Pour in the sweetened condensed milk and vanilla, beat for another 2 minutes: the mixture thickens and becomes glossy.
In a cold bowl, whip 240 ml of cream to soft peaks (the cream forms a peak that droops slightly at the whisk tip). Stop there; cream that is too stiff will make the mixture grainy.
Fold in the whipped cream and the 8 crumbled biscuits into the mixture using a spatula, with broad sweeping motions from the bottom to the surface. Do not work with the whisk.
Spread two-thirds of this mixture over the cold crust, smooth with an offset spatula. Set aside (reserve separately) the remaining third.

In this remaining third, sift the cocoa and icing sugar. Whisk briefly, adding the remaining 120 ml of cream by spoonfuls if the mixture becomes stiff. You are aiming for a smooth, thick cream with a pronounced beige-cocoa colour.
Deposit this layer onto the white layer by spoonfuls spaced apart, then connect them with the spatula without pressing, to avoid mixing the two layers.

Sprinkle with biscuit shards and pieces. Cover without touching the surface and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight. The cake is ready when the centre no longer trembles under finger pressure.
Run a thin blade along the edge before opening the clasp. Cut with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each slice.

title: Avocado mousse with cocoa, dark chocolate shell
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the avocado: if it's too firm, the mousse remains grainy and the cocoa flavor dominates.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Over very low heat, its even temperature rise melts the chocolate without hot spots or sticking. Turn off the heat as soon as the mixture is glossy: the residual heat finishes the job.
steps: Cut the avocado in half lengthwise and remove the pit. Scoop out the flesh with a spoon, keeping the two halves of the skin intact to use as serving dishes. Set them aside.
Combine the pulp, cocoa, maple syrup, coconut milk, cinnamon, and salt in a small blender. Blend until perfectly smooth, scraping down the sides once or twice.
Fill the half-skins with mousse, or transfer (into another container) into two ramekins. Smooth the surface.
Place the dark chocolate in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously for about 3 minutes, until it is shiny and runny. Remove from the heat immediately.
Coat the mousse with melted chocolate, add a pinch of fleur de sel.
Place in the refrigerator for 5 to 10 minutes, until the shell sets. Serve with a spoon, breaking the chocolate into pieces.

title: Flourless chocolate-strawberry fondant
intro: It all comes down to two things: eggs beaten long enough to support the batter, and cooking stopped before the center is completely set.
titane: The pan goes directly from the countertop to the oven without any temperature precautions. Its metal mass heats up quickly and dries the surface: a thin, slightly crispy crust forms, while the center remains gooey. The low rim then allows you to slide in a knife and flip the cake in one smooth motion.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake cools and then rests for 2 hours in the refrigerator before being unmolded.
Preheat the oven to 175 °C. Generously butter a 20 cm springform pan and line the bottom with a disc of baking paper cut to its size.
Melt the chocolate and butter in a double boiler over low heat, or in the microwave in short bursts. Mix until you obtain a smooth and glossy mass, then let cool slightly away from heat.
Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla for 4 minutes with a mixer. The mixture should become pale, thicken and double in volume.

Pour the lukewarm chocolate over the whipped eggs, add the cocoa, salt and strawberry purée. Fold in with a spatula, lifting the mass from bottom to top to preserve the air in the mixture, without overmixing. Stop as soon as the batter is homogeneous.
Pour into the pan, smooth the surface and bake for 33 minutes. The centre should remain just set: a knife tip inserted at the edge should come out with a few moist crumbs.
Let cool completely in the pan. The centre sinks into a hollow, which is normal. Then refrigerate for at least 2 hours.
Run a thin blade along the edge, turn out onto a plate, remove the paper. Garnish with strawberry slices and serve chilled.

title: Crunchy sesame bars
intro: It all comes down to thickness: a thin, even layer gives a plate that breaks cleanly, a thick layer gives a soft bar.

ing.note: or the same quantity of black sesame

titane: Dry-roast the seeds in a titanium pan over medium heat before binding them. Two minutes is enough: stir constantly, wait for the crackling and the first nutty aroma, then remove from the pan (immediately transfer to a cold container). The seeds will continue to cook in a hot pan and turn bitter.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170 °C. Cut two sheets of parchment paper to the dimensions of your baking tray.
Toast both sesame seeds dry in a pan over medium heat for 2 minutes. Transfer to a bowl and let cool slightly.
Melt the coconut oil with the honey for a few seconds over low heat until you obtain a fluid and homogeneous mixture.
Pour over the seeds, add the salt, mix until each seed is coated and shiny.

Place the mixture on one sheet of parchment, cover with the second sheet, then flatten with a rolling pin to 3 mm thickness. Work from the centre towards the edges to maintain an even thickness: the thinner the layer, the crispier the result.
Remove the top sheet, slide the whole thing onto the baking tray. Bake for 16 to 18 minutes: the edges should be golden, the centre still pale.
Remove and let cool completely on the tray without touching it. The sheet hardens as it cools.
Cut into bars with a large knife, using a single vertical motion. If the sesame crumbles, it was not cold enough.

title: Quinoa and crispy tofu salad
intro: It all comes down to the tofu's crust: pressed, coated with starch, placed in an already hot pan and left alone until it detaches on its own.

ing.note: pressed and cut into 2 cm cubes
cut into julienne strips (thin, even strips)

titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat before adding the first drop of oil. The temperature rises quickly: the tofu will stick at first, then release itself once a crust has formed. That's the signal. As long as a cube resists, it's not ready to be flipped—and each premature attempt will tear the crust. Two batches are better than one overcrowded pan, which would cause the tofu to sweat instead of sear.
steps: Press the tofu between two cloths under a weight for 10 minutes, then cut it into cubes. Mix the cornstarch, smoked paprika, ginger, and pepper in a bowl, add the cubes, and stir to coat them evenly.
Cook the quinoa in a saucepan with a small amount of water, according to the package instructions. Drain and let it cool uncovered so the grains remain separate.
Blanch the edamame for 2 minutes in a pot of boiling water, drain and refresh under cold water. Cut the carrot into julienne strips, shred the red cabbage, and chop the cilantro.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.

Arrange the tofu cubes in a single layer, without crowding them. Leave them undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes. Turn them over as soon as they begin to release from the pan, reduce the heat to medium-high, and continue cooking on both sides for a total of 12 minutes, until a golden crust forms on all sides. Transfer to a plate.
Whisk together in a bowl the peanut butter, soy sauce, honey, minced garlic and water added one spoonful at a time, until you have a smooth, coating sauce.
Combine the quinoa, carrot, red cabbage, edamame, and coriander in a large bowl. Add the still-warm tofu, pour over the sauce, and mix thoroughly.
Sprinkle with crushed peanuts and serve immediately, while the tofu is still crispy.

title: Cranberry-orange chia pudding with vanilla cream
intro: The sharp acidity of cranberries needs the sugar of citrus fruits to hold up: mix the two together, never separately.
titane: Chia seeds gel in two stages. Whisk once upon adding them, then a second time ten minutes later, when the mixture begins to thicken. This second whisking breaks up any clumps of seeds stuck to the bottom and creates a smooth texture, free of dry pockets.
steps: Plan ahead: the pudding requires at least 2 hours in the refrigerator, or even overnight.
Soak the cashew nuts in cold water during the pudding preparation. They will blend more finely.
Blend the cranberries, mandarins and 120 ml of hemp milk until you obtain a smooth purée, without skin fragments.
Pour into a bowl. Add the honey, taste, adjust: the mixture should be slightly sweeter than what you are aiming for, the chia will tone it down.
Fold in the chia seeds with a whisk. Wait ten minutes, whisk again.
Cover and let set in the refrigerator for 2 hours, or overnight.
Drain the cashew nuts. Blend them with the 30 ml of hemp milk, vanilla and honey until you obtain a smooth cream. Add milk a spoonful at a time if the blender is struggling.
Plate by alternating pudding and vanilla cream in two glasses. Serve chilled.

title: Chocolate, nut and date bars
intro: It all comes down to compaction: a mixture pressed roughly produces clean bars, a mixture placed loosely crumbles under the knife.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, without a double boiler. The even heat distribution prevents hot spots that can cause the coating to become grainy. Stir continuously and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth: the residual heat of the pan finishes the job. A quick wipe with a cloth is all it takes to clean.
steps: Plan ahead: the chocolate must set in the refrigerator for approximately 2 hours before you can cut the bars.

Mix the peanut butter, honey and cinnamon in a large bowl until you obtain a homogeneous and supple mass. If the peanut butter comes straight from the refrigerator, work it for a few seconds with a spatula to soften it.
Incorporate the dates, then the walnuts, almonds and cashews. Finish with the pumpkin and sesame seeds. Stir until each fragment is coated.

Line a rectangular mould with parchment paper, leaving two sides overhanging. Pour in the mixture and press firmly with the back of a spatula, pressing into the corners. The surface should be flat and compact.
Place the chocolate broken into pieces in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously for approximately 3 minutes. Remove from heat as soon as the chocolate is smooth and glossy.
Coat the nut mixture with the melted chocolate. Spread with a spatula to the edges.
Refrigerate until the chocolate is completely set, approximately 2 hours.
Unmould by pulling on the paper. Cut into rectangular bars with a smooth-bladed knife, wiping it between each cut.

title: Blueberry and toasted coconut froyo
intro: Three ingredients, but everything depends on the water content: if it's too liquid, the mass clumps together and remains sandy after turning.
titane: Dry-roast the topping. In a very hot titanium pan, without any oil, spread the coconut flakes and pumpkin seeds in a single layer. Stir constantly: the coconut will go from white to golden in thirty seconds, and from golden to burnt in ten. Remove from the pan as soon as it starts to brown, and transfer to a cold plate; otherwise, the residual heat of the metal will finish the job for you.
steps: Plan ahead: the froyo goes in the freezer for 24 hours, start the day before.
Combine the still-frozen blueberries, yogurt and stevia in the ice cream maker bowl. Mix until you obtain a homogeneous mass, violet in colour, without any pockets of white yogurt.
Smooth the surface with a spatula. A flat surface ensures even freezing and prevents hollow areas that resist the blade.
Place in the freezer for 24 hours, bowl upright, lid in place.
Churn (whip the frozen mass under a rotating blade) on the light ice cream program. On the first pass, the texture remains powdery: this is normal.
Add water or plant-based milk to the centre of the bowl. Run another pass, or two if necessary, until the mass closes on itself and becomes creamy.
Meanwhile, toast the coconut and pumpkin seeds in a titanium pan. Set aside.
Serve as a quenelle, sprinkle the warm topping over the cold froyo.

title: Semolina cake with rose syrup
intro: It all comes down to two things: the resting time of the dough, which allows the semolina to absorb the yogurt, and the temperature difference between a hot cake and a cold syrup.
titane: Before mixing, toast (dry-heat to develop the aromas) the shredded coconut in the titanium pan over medium heat, without any oil. Stir continuously for two to three minutes, until it turns golden and smells nutty. Remove from the heat and transfer to a cold container immediately: on a hot pan, it will continue to brown and become bitter in seconds. While the pan is still warm, toast the almonds for garnish for one minute, then set them aside.
steps: Plan ahead: the dough rests for 30 minutes before baking.
Combine the sugar, water and lemon juice in a saucepan. Whisk while cold to dissolve some of the sugar, then place over medium-high heat.
Bring to a rolling boil.
Reduce to low heat and let simmer for 10 minutes, stirring from time to time. The syrup should coat the spoon lightly without running off.
Off the heat, add the rose water. Let cool completely: this point is non-negotiable, a warm syrup does not penetrate in the same way.
In a large bowl, mix the semolina, toasted coconut, sugar, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda.
Add the ghee, yogurt, milk and vanilla. Work by hand until you obtain a homogeneous and thick dough, without dry lumps at the bottom of the bowl.
Cover and let rest for 30 minutes minimum. The semolina swells and the texture changes from sandy to supple.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Grease a large baking dish, or two medium ones, with tahini, including the sides. It flavours the crust and prevents the cake from sticking.
Pour in the dough and press it by hand or with the back of a wet spoon, to a thickness of 2 to 3 cm regular.
Score with a knife into diamonds or squares, pressing down to the bottom of the dish.
Place a golden almond in the centre of each portion.
Bake for 35 minutes, until a uniform golden colour and edges that pull away.

Remove the dish and pour the cold syrup immediately, in a regular shower over the entire surface. Start with three-quarters, wait a minute for it to be absorbed, then complete according to the desired result: more or less syrupy.
Let cool completely in the dish before detaching the portions. The cake holds together better the next day.

title: Orange and poppy seed muffins with cream cheese frosting
intro: It all comes down to the zest: rubbed in sugar, it perfumes the entire dough instead of remaining on the surface.
ing: The zest of an untreated orange

ing.note: butter worked until it has the texture of a cream

titane: The muffins are baked in the oven in paper cases. The titanium pan is used beforehand: pour in the poppy seeds dry, over medium heat, and stir for one minute until they smell nutty. The even heat distribution of the titanium will toast them without burning. Remove from the pan (immediately transfer to a cold container) to stop the heating process.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175 °C. Line nine muffin cups with paper cases.
In a large bowl, combine the sugar and orange zest. Rub them together with your fingertips for about thirty seconds, until you have a moist, fragrant sugar.
Add the eggs, milk, olive oil, orange juice, yogurt and vanilla. Whisk until the mixture is smooth. Set aside.
In a second bowl, combine the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, poppy seeds and cinnamon. Whisk to distribute the dry ingredients.
Pour the dry ingredients over the wet ingredients. Mix with a spatula until the flour traces disappear, without overworking: overworked batter makes dense muffins.
Divide the batter among the paper cases, filling them three-quarters full.
Bake for 24 minutes. The tops should be golden and a skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean.
Turn out onto a wire rack and let cool for at least 20 minutes. A warm muffin would melt the frosting.
Meanwhile, beat the softened butter and cream cheese with a whisk. Add the icing sugar, vanilla and orange juice. Whisk until you have a smooth, lump-free frosting.
Spread the frosting on the cooled muffins with a small spatula.
Grate a little orange zest over the top just before serving.

title: Dark chocolate and coconut milk panna cotta
intro: Everything happens below the boiling point: past this threshold, the gelatin loses its strength and the cream becomes grainy.
titane: The pan serves as a saucepan from start to finish. Cold-swollen gelatin in it, melted chocolate in it, lukewarm mixture in it. The wide surface distributes heat without hot spots, and the low thermal inertia of titanium allows you to cut the heat cleanly at the first sign of simmering: you regain control in two seconds, something a thick pan cannot forgive.
steps: Plan ahead: panna cotta sets in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, allow for this time before serving.

Pour the coconut milk into the cold pan, away from the heat. Sprinkle the gelatin evenly over the entire surface, without stirring. Let it bloom for 5 minutes: the powder must absorb the liquid and form a thick veil.
Lightly oil the ramekins if you plan to unmould them. Wipe the excess with paper towels, only a thin film should remain.

Place the pan over low heat. Add the chopped chocolate and cinnamon. Stir continuously with a spatula, bringing the edges towards the centre, until the chocolate is melted and the gelatin is completely dissolved. The mixture should barely steam. If it begins to tremble, remove the pan from the heat for a few seconds.
Away from the heat, let it cool for 5 to 10 minutes in the pan. Taste: at 80%, the chocolate is bitter and clean. Add the maple syrup only if you deem it necessary, one spoonful at a time.
Pour into the ramekins. Refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours, until firmly set — the surface must resist under your finger.

To unmould, dip the bottom of the ramekins into a bowl of warm water for 1 to 2 minutes, making sure the water does not touch the panna cotta. Run the tip of a knife around the edge to loosen it, turn onto the plate and tap the bottom with a sharp blow.
Sprinkle with crushed pistachios, arrange the raspberries and mint. Serve immediately.

title: White chocolate, puffed quinoa and pistachio bites
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the cocoa butter: melted gently, it remains smooth and gives a clean bite in the mouth; heated too quickly, it grains (separates into small grains) and the texture becomes sandy.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its thin walls transmit the heat from the low flame without concentrating it: the cocoa butter melts evenly, without any hot spots. You then proceed with the mixing and incorporation in the same container, off the heat, without transferring anything.
steps: Plan ahead: the bites must chill for 1 hour in the refrigerator to set.
Line a mini-muffin tin with paper cases, or use a silicone mold with impressions. Place it near your work surface: the preparation sets quickly.

Put the cocoa butter in the cold pan, then place it over very low heat in a bain-marie. Stir continuously with a spatula for approximately 3 minutes, until you obtain a clear liquid with no lumps. Never leave the pan unattended.
Remove from heat. Add the cashew butter, maple syrup and vanilla. Mix for 2 minutes: the mixture should become smooth, glossy and perfectly homogeneous, with no greasy streaks on the surface.
Fold in the puffed quinoa. Mix gently to coat it completely without crushing it.
Divide the preparation among the impressions using two spoons. Press down lightly, then sprinkle with crushed pistachios and rose petals.
Refrigerate for 1 hour, until the bites are firm to the touch. Unmold.
Store the remaining bites in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to two weeks, or in the freezer for up to six months.

title: Apple-cinnamon ice cream with date caramel
intro: It all comes down to the pan: the apples must be really stewed and golden, otherwise the ice cream will remain flat.
ing: Greek yogurt or thick plant-based yogurt
titane: Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 minutes over medium heat before adding the oil. The diced apples will stick just enough to caramelize their juices, then release easily when they're ready. It's this slight sticking, impossible to achieve in a saucepan, that gives them that pie-filling flavor.
steps: Plan ahead: the ice cream freezes for 24 hours in an ice cream maker (or 2 to 4 hours in a regular container), start the day before.
Blend the dates, almond butter and water until you obtain a smooth cream. Set aside.
Peel the apple then cut it into dice.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 minutes over medium heat. Add the grape seed oil, then the apple dice, water and half a teaspoon of cinnamon.
Let cook for 15 minutes, stirring regularly. The apples are ready when they come away from the bottom on their own and yield under the spatula.
Remove 1 tablespoon of apples and set aside for plating.
In the ice cream maker bowl or a hermetic container, mix the remaining apples, yogurt, collagen, remaining cinnamon and 3 tablespoons of date caramel. Taste and adjust the sugar.
Smooth the surface and freeze for 24 hours in an ice cream maker (churn in a sorbet maker), or 2 to 4 hours in a regular container.
Churn, add a splash of water or plant-based milk, then restart one or two cycles until a creamy texture is reached. Without a machine, scrape with a fork every 45 minutes.
Plate with the date caramel, reserved apples and pecans.

title: Cinnamon marble banana bread with cream cheese frosting
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the bananas: black-spotted skin, almost liquid flesh, it is at this stage that they really sweeten and flavor the crumb.
titane: The butter for the marble cake is first cooked in a titanium pan. Heat it over medium heat until it foams, then until the milk particles brown at the bottom: this is beurre noisette (melted butter cooked until it turns a hazelnut color, with a nutty aroma). Immediately pour it over the sugar and cinnamon, off the heat. The thin, responsive pan allows you to see the color change perfectly.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C using the fan setting. Line a 28 x 13 cm cake tin with baking paper, leaving two strips hanging over the sides.
Prepare the marbled cake: melt the butter until it turns a hazelnut brown, then mix it with the brown sugar and cinnamon. Set aside at room temperature; the mixture should remain runny.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl. Keep some pieces, they will melt during cooking.
Add the eggs, milk, olive oil, yogurt, honey and vanilla. Whisk until smooth and homogeneous.
Pour the flour, cinnamon, baking powder and baking soda over the top. Mix with a spatula just enough so that no dry flour remains: beyond that, the crumb will become dense.
Pour the batter into the mold and smooth the surface.

Drizzle the cinnamon mixture along the entire length of the mold. Insert a fork to the bottom and trace three or four figure-eights lengthwise to create a marbled effect. Two passes are sufficient, otherwise the design will disappear.
Bake for 45 to 50 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean. If the top is browning too quickly, cover with aluminum foil after 30 minutes.
Let it cool in the pan for 20 minutes, then unmold onto a wire rack and let it cool completely. A cake that's still warm will absorb the glaze instead of holding it.
Work the softened butter with the cream cheese, icing sugar and vanilla until you obtain a smooth cream.
Spread the icing over the cold cake in waves using a small spatula.
Slice into ten thick pieces and serve.

title: Coconut bars coated in milk chocolate
intro: It all comes down to the firmness of the center: a coconut that has been chilled properly dips cleanly, without falling apart in the chocolate.
titane: The chocolate melts in the pan over very low heat, and the bars are dipped directly into it. The rapid temperature rise of the titanium requires constant stirring, but eliminates the need to transfer the melting and coating containers.
steps: Plan ahead: the coconut mixture goes into the freezer for one hour before being cut into bars.
Combine the shredded coconut, condensed milk and vanilla in a bowl. Mix until the mixture is homogeneous and no dry coconut remains visible.
Line a mold with parchment paper. Pour the mixture and press it firmly with a spatula or the back of a spoon, in a regular layer of approximately 2 cm.
Place in the freezer until the mixture is firm to the touch, approximately 1 hour.
Unmold and cut into twelve bars. Return them to the cold while preparing the chocolate.

Pour the chocolate chips and coconut oil into the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously with a silicone spatula until you obtain a smooth and shiny mixture, 3 minutes. Remove from heat as soon as melting is complete: residual heat finishes the work.
Dip each bar in the chocolate, directly in the pan, turning it over with a fork. Drain against the edge and place on parchment paper.
Let it set at room temperature, 20 minutes. In the refrigerator, the chocolate develops a white bloom.

title: Batata harra, mashed potatoes and garlic yogurt
intro: It all comes down to the crust: potatoes first boiled in water, then crushed and left alone on the hot metal until they detach on their own.

ing.note: the juice, for the spicy sauce

titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven for the second cooking. Preheated empty, it gives a cleaner and faster crust on direct contact than roasting, and you can then make the spicy sauce in the same pan without washing it: the potato juices are released with the garlic and tomato paste.
steps: Place the new potatoes in a saucepan of cold, salted water. Bring to a simmer and cook for about 15 minutes: a fork should pierce them easily. Drain and let them cool in the open air until the steam has evaporated.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should bead and run down the bottom.
Place the potatoes in the hot pan, well spaced apart. Crush them one by one with the bottom of a glass or the back of a fork, until they are about 1.5 cm thick.
Drizzle with olive oil and season with sea salt. For a more intense sear, replace some or all of the oil with grapeseed oil, which has a higher smoke point.

Cook for about 20 minutes, covering them for the first 10 minutes if you want to speed up the cooking process. Do not move them: they will release from the metal on their own once a crust has formed. Then turn them over and brown the second side.
Meanwhile, in a bowl, combine the Greek yogurt, tahini, parsley, garlic, and lemon juice. Thin with a spoonful of water until it reaches a coating consistency. Refrigerate.
Remove the potatoes (take them out of the pan and set them aside in a warm dish).
In the same pan, over medium heat, pour in the olive oil and sauté the garlic for 1 minute, until fragrant but not browned.
Add the tomato paste, chili flakes and paprika. Stir for 2 minutes: the mixture should darken and lightly pick up the juices from the bottom.
Remove from heat and stir in the lemon juice and coriander. Adding them over the flame will diminish their freshness.
Return the potatoes to the pan and roll them in the sauce to coat them without breaking the crust.
Serve in a pan, with the garlic yogurt on the side or in swirls on top.

title: Buckwheat mixed with raspberries
intro: It all comes down to the mixing: the raw buckwheat must disappear completely, otherwise the texture remains sandy.
ing: Greek yogurt or plain plant-based yogurt
titane: The pan serves only one purpose here: to melt the chocolate. Uncoated, titanium heats up quickly and conducts heat evenly. Use a very low heat, and remove the pan from the heat as soon as the chocolate pieces begin to sizzle. The residual heat finishes the job.
steps: Plan ahead: buckwheat soaks overnight, start the day before.
The day before, cover the buckwheat with cold water, add the lemon juice and let soak overnight. Rinse thoroughly the next day until the water is clear, then drain.

Put the buckwheat, dates, 65 g of raspberries, yogurt, plant-based milk and cinnamon into the blender. Blend for a long time, scraping down the sides once or twice. Stop when the mixture is perfectly smooth, with no grains under the tongue.

Place the titanium pan on very low heat. Pour the chopped chocolate and coconut oil into it. As soon as the edges of the pieces round off, remove from heat and stir until you obtain a fluid and coating mixture (that flows in a regular veil over the spatula). Allow 2 minutes in total.
Distribute the remaining raspberries at the bottom of two jars. Cover with the buckwheat mixture, then pour the melted chocolate in a thin stream over the top.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight: the chocolate must have set into a thin shell and the cream must have firmed up.

title: Banana, oat and dark chocolate bites
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the banana: if it is very spotted, almost black, it sweetens the dough on its own and makes it unnecessary to add sugar.
titane: No double boiler required. Heat the empty titanium pan over low heat for one minute, remove it from the heat, then add the chocolate and coconut oil. The metal's thermal inertia is enough to melt it slowly, without ever overheating or causing it to seize. The chocolate remains in the pan: it becomes the dipping container.
steps: Plan ahead: the balls are placed in the freezer for 1 hour before coating, organize accordingly.
Mash the banana with a fork in a bowl until you obtain a puree without lumps.
Add the oat flour, almond powder, honey, peanut butter and melted coconut oil. Mix until you have a homogeneous and supple paste. If it sticks too much to your fingers, add a spoonful of oat flour.
Take the paste with a spoon and roll twelve regular balls between your palms. Place them on a plate lined with baking paper.
Place in the freezer for 1 hour. They should be firm to the touch: this allows the chocolate to set sharply.

Heat the titanium pan empty, over low heat, for 1 minute. Remove it from the heat. Add the chocolate broken into pieces and the coconut oil, stir constantly. In about 3 minutes, the mixture becomes smooth and glossy.
Take out the balls. Dip them one by one in the chocolate remaining in the pan, turning them with a spoon, then drain against the edge.
Sprinkle with chopped walnuts while the chocolate is still fluid.
Return to the freezer for 10 minutes, the time it takes for the coating to set.
Take them out 5 minutes before serving: the center should become tender again, not frozen.

title: Blueberry and chocolate frozen bites
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the mixture must be well set, the chocolate barely melted, otherwise the coating will slide instead of setting.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Over very low heat, it diffuses an even heat without any hot spots: the chocolate melts without sticking or graining, and you can monitor the texture visually. Its wide surface then serves as a dipping basin, off the heat, to coat the chocolates before they begin to bead.
steps: Plan ahead: the bites spend 3 hours in the freezer and then 20 additional minutes after coating, for a total of more than 3 hours of waiting time.
Blend the yogurt, 100 g of blueberries and the protein until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture, with no fruit skin pieces.
Pour into a silicone mold with small round or cubic indentations. Tap the mold on the work surface to remove any air bubbles.
Freeze for 3 hours, until the bites are firm in the center. Unmold and return them to the cold while you prepare the chocolate.

Melt the chopped chocolate in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring constantly. Allow approximately 3 minutes. Add coconut oil if the mixture remains thick. You are looking for smooth, fluid chocolate that coats the spatula without hiding it.
Remove the pan from the heat. Take out the bites and dip them one by one in the chocolate, using a fork, letting them drain for two seconds. Place them on a cold baking sheet.
Decorate with the remaining blueberries while the chocolate is still soft, then return to the freezer for 20 minutes to set the coating.
Store in the freezer for up to 3 months. Remove them 10 to 15 minutes before serving: beyond that, they will collapse.

title: Tahini, black sesame and macadamia cookies
intro: The whole recipe lies in the cooking: covered, over low-medium heat, so that the bottom browns while the center remains soft.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes, remove it from the heat, then wipe the bottom with a paper towel soaked in oil. The film of oil will then be minimal and even, much thinner than a cold-oiled pan. Once the lid is on, the heat becomes enveloping, like in an oven, but direct contact browns the food more quickly: trust your eye, not the timer.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Remove it from the heat. Wipe the bottom with a folded paper towel soaked in grapeseed oil, then set aside off the heat.

In a bowl, whisk together the tahini, black sesame paste, maple syrup, coconut oil, egg, and vanilla. Mix until the batter (the mixture of liquid and oil ingredients) is smooth and glossy. Make sure the coconut oil is lukewarm, not hot; if it's too hot, it will curdle the egg.
Add the almond flour and baking soda. Mix until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous dough.
Incorporate the macadamia nuts and white chocolate chips by folding with a spatula (bottom-up motion, so as not to crush the dough).

Shape into 12 portions. Arrange them in the pan in a single layer, spaced apart, and flatten them slightly with your fingertips. Cook in two batches if the pan is small: consistent thickness is more important than quantity.

Sprinkle with fleur de sel. Cover and cook over low-medium heat for 14 to 16 minutes, without moving the cookies. They are ready when the edges are set, the center is still soft, and they easily pull away from the bottom of the pan.
Remove (transfer from the pan) onto a wire rack and let cool for 10 minutes: it will firm up as it cools.

title: Crispy gnocchi with yogurt-basil dip
intro: It all comes down to drying the gnocchi before frying: a dry surface, a really hot pan, and the crust forms on its own.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two minutes and replaces the air fryer: it creates the crust in just a few minutes instead of a full convection cycle. Preheat it empty, pour in the oil, and then leave it alone. The gnocchi will release on their own once the crust has formed. Immediately afterward, the same pan, still hot, is used to toast the pine nuts.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to the boil. This volume will not fit in the pan, which is why this is the only step that requires a pot.

Add the gnocchi to the water. Remove them as soon as they float to the surface. Drain, then spread them on a clean kitchen towel and let them dry for a few minutes: this will make all the difference when searing.
Transfer the gnocchi to a bowl. Coat them with the Parmesan, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, thyme and salt.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should shimmer without smoking.
Place the gnocchi in a single layer, without crowding them. Work in two batches if necessary, as direct contact with the metal is essential. Leave them to sear without stirring for 3 to 4 minutes.
When the gnocchi release easily and are golden, turn them over and reduce the heat to medium. Continue cooking until all sides are golden, about 10 minutes in total. Keep warm.
In the still-hot pan, toast the pine nuts over medium heat, stirring, until lightly coloured. Remove them immediately and let them cool, as they burn quickly.
Peel and remove the germ from the garlic clove. Blend the basil, Parmesan, pine nuts, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, salt and pepper until smooth.
Stir this pesto into the yoghurt in a bowl. Taste and adjust the salt if needed.
Plate the gnocchi straight from the pan, sprinkle with parsley and serve immediately with the dip on the side. They will lose their crispness within a few minutes.

title: Chocolate fondant cake
intro: A cake that remains moist in the center because it is not whipped enough: the air you incorporate into the eggs is the enemy of a moist texture.
ing: instant coffee dissolved in 2 tablespoons of hot water
titane: The titanium pan doubles as a saucepan and then a mold. You melt butter and chocolate in it over the stovetop, prepare the batter elsewhere, pour it back in, and bake. No transferring, no extra washing up. The metal heats up slowly and evenly: the surface cracks, the center remains dense and moist.
steps: Preheat the oven to 165°C. Butter the titanium pan and line the bottom with a disc of baking paper.
In the pan, over medium heat, melt the butter with the oil. Remove from heat as soon as the butter is liquid.
Add the chopped chocolate off the heat. Stir until the mixture is smooth and lump-free. Pour the cocoa in a stream and whisk: the mixture should become shiny. Let it cool slightly.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs with the muscovado sugar and sugar just long enough to combine them. No foam, no ribbon: too airy a batter would give a dry crumb.
Incorporate the buttermilk and vanilla, then the cooled chocolate mixture.
Sift the flour, bicarbonate, baking powder and salt over the bowl. Fold (mix by lifting the batter with a spatula, without stirring) until all flour traces disappear.
Add the dissolved coffee, then the chocolate chips. Two or three turns of the spatula are enough.
Pour the batter into the lined pan, sprinkle with a few chocolate shards and bake for 60 to 70 minutes. A skewer inserted in the centre should come out clean, possibly with a little moisture.
Let it cool in the pan for about twenty minutes, then turn out onto a rack. Wait for it to cool completely before slicing: the cake holds together better when cold.

title: Cocoa, chickpea and date truffles
intro: It all comes down to the fineness of the mixing: the paste must be perfectly smooth, without any chickpea grains or pieces of date.
titane: Before coating, dry-roast (heat to develop the aromas) the finishing cocoa in a titanium pan. Use a dry pan over medium heat for 60 to 90 seconds, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon. As soon as the aroma develops, transfer (immediately from the hot pan) to a cold plate. Cocoa continues to cook in a hot pan and turns bitter within seconds.
steps: Plan ahead: the truffles need to firm up for one hour in the refrigerator before coating.
If the dates are dry, cover them with very hot water for 10 minutes, then drain them carefully.
Combine chickpeas, pumpkin puree, dates, 36 g cocoa, almond butter, cinnamon and salt in the food processor bowl.
Mix for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down the sides two or three times. Stop when the mixture is smooth and glossy, with no graininess on the tongue.
Scoop out regular portions with an ice cream scoop, roll them between your palms and place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Refrigerate for 1 hour. The balls must be firm to the touch before coating, otherwise the cocoa will become soggy.
Roll each truffle in the cocoa, then tap them to remove the excess.

title: Refrigerated speculoos cake
intro: It all depends on the firmness of the whipped cream: if it's too soft, it won't hold the biscuits upright and the slice will collapse.

ing.note: 220g for the filling and the rest for

titane: The spread melts in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula. The heat distributes quickly and without hot spots: the sugar doesn't stick to the bottom, and the spread remains smooth and pourable. As soon as it coats the spatula, remove from the heat—it will continue to soften off the flame.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake must chill for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight; start in advance.
Line a loaf tin with cling film (cover the interior, leaving plenty of overhang on all four sides). This overhang will help you unmould the cake.
Pour 220 g of spread into the titanium pan. Heat over very low heat, stirring constantly, for 30 seconds to one minute, until smooth and runny. Transfer to a bowl and let it cool slightly.
Whip the plant-based cream with an electric mixer until you obtain stiff peaks: the cream should stand upright on the whisk when lifted.
Fold the cooled spread into the cream using a spatula, with folding motions. Stop as soon as the mixture is homogeneous.
Spread a thick layer of filling on the bottom of the tin. Stand the biscuits vertically, 6 rows of 7, leaving a slight gap between each one.

Fill a piping bag with the remaining cream and pipe between the biscuits to fill all the gaps. Smooth the surface, then lay a final row of biscuits flat. Press down lightly with the flat of your hand: this is what gives you a neat cross-section.
Cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight.

Unmould onto a serving plate by pulling on the film, then remove it. Reheat the remaining spread in the titanium pan over very low heat and coat the cake. Sprinkle with biscuits coarsely crumbled. Slice with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped dry between each slice.

title: No-bake cheesecake verrines with cocoa biscuits
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate when it's poured over the top: if it's too hot, it melts the cream and the marbled effect disappears.
ing: Whole or halved filled cocoa biscuits
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its thinness conducts heat instantly: over very low heat, the chocolate and milk blend into a smooth emulsion, without steam or an intermediate pan. Remove from the heat as soon as the mixture becomes glossy; the pan continues to heat for a few seconds off the flame.
steps: Crush the 170g of biscuits into coarse crumbs. Mix with the melted butter until the mixture is evenly moist and holds together between your fingers.
Divide the mixture into six small glasses. Firmly press down the base with the back of a spoon.
Refrigerate for 10 minutes.
Whisk the whipped cream mix with the ice water until you obtain a firm mass that clings to the whisk.
Add the cream cheese. Beat at low speed, just until you get a smooth cream. Beyond that, it will loosen up.
Incorporate the 30g of crumbs with a spatula, in just two or three movements, to marble (leave visible veins rather than mix).
Pipe or place the cream onto the cold bases. Smooth the surface.
Put the verrines back in the fridge.
Pour the chopped chocolate and milk into the titanium pan. Heat over very low heat, stirring continuously. Remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy, without lumps.
Let it cool in the pan, off the heat. The chocolate should be fluid but warmer than lukewarm to the touch.
Cover each glass with a thin layer.
Place a whole biscuit or half a portion on top, sprinkle with crumbs.
Refrigerate for 3 to 4 hours, until completely set.

title: Raspberry cheesecake-style verrines
intro: It all comes down to the consistency of the cream: firm enough to support the compote, yet supple enough to remain light in the mouth.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: The compote is made in a frying pan, not a saucepan. The heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without creating hot spots, so the raspberries release their juices and reduce them rapidly, without sticking. Preheat the empty pan for a minute before adding the still-frozen fruit: this speeds up the thawing process and reduces excess water. Use a spoon, never a whisk, to keep some chunks.
steps: Crush the biscuits into fine crumbs, using a mortar or rolling pin, in a bag.
Mix the crumbs with the melted butter. The texture should be that of wet sand that holds together when pressed in your hand.
Divide into 12 small glasses and press down with the back of a spoon to form a regular base.
Whisk together the quark, mascarpone, icing sugar, lemon juice and vanilla until you obtain a perfectly smooth, grain-free mixture.
Whip the liquid cream into stiff peaks (whipped until it holds its shape on the whisk).
Incorporate the whipped cream into the mixture in three stages, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from underneath. Stop as soon as the mixture is homogeneous.
Pipe or spread the cream onto the biscuit bases. Refrigerate.

Preheat the titanium pan over medium heat for one minute without any liquid. Add the frozen raspberries, sugar, and cornstarch. Stir with a spoon for about ten minutes: the compote is ready when it coats the back of the spoon and the bubbles become shiny.
Transfer the mixture from the cooking container to a bowl and let it cool completely. Warm compote would melt the cream.
Top each glass with cold compote.
Place a fresh raspberry and a mint leaf on each one.
Refrigerate for at least two hours before serving.

title: Red velvet cupcakes
intro: A successful red velvet cake depends on two things: a very fine crumb, obtained by the acidity of buttermilk and vinegar, and a glaze firm enough to stay on the piping bag without collapsing.
titane: The decorative crumbs dry out in a pan, not in the oven. Crumble a leftover piece of cake, pour it into a cold titanium pan, turn up the heat to low, and stir constantly for two to three minutes. The crumbs will lose their moisture, remain soft in the center, and won't brown. Transfer them immediately from the pan to a cold plate to stop the residual heat.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C. Line the mould with paper cases, one per cupcake.
Whisk together the flour, cocoa, baking soda and salt. Set aside.
Cream the butter and sugar with an electric mixer (work them until the mixture turns pale and doubles in volume), four to five minutes at medium speed.
Add the egg, vanilla and food colouring. Beat until you obtain a smooth mass that is evenly red.

Incorporate one third of the dry ingredients at low speed, then half of the buttermilk, then a second third of dry ingredients, the remaining buttermilk and finally the last third. Stop as soon as the batter is homogeneous: beyond that, the crumb becomes tight.
Add the vinegar with a spatula, in just a few folds. The batter rises slightly, which is a sign that the reaction is starting.
Fill the paper cases two thirds full, no more.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes. The tops should be domed and spring back under your finger; a skewer inserted comes out clean.
Turn out of the mould as soon as they come out of the oven and let cool completely on a wire rack. A warm cupcake will melt the frosting.
Beat the cream cheese and butter for two minutes, until the mixture is smooth and lump-free.

Add the vanilla then the icing sugar in three additions, at low speed first, then medium, until you achieve an airy texture that holds on the whisk. If it lacks firmness, place in the refrigerator for 15 minutes.
Fit a piping bag with a fluted nozzle and pipe a spiral on each cupcake, from the outside towards the centre.
Sprinkle with crumbs and keep in the refrigerator for 20 minutes before serving.

title: Chocolate, seed and puffed quinoa bars
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: if it's too hot, it curdles and releases fat, and the bars never set properly.
titane: The titanium pan heats up evenly, without hot spots: it replaces the double boiler. Melted chocolate, seeds incorporated, mixture transferred (out of the pan) into the mold — all in one container from start to finish.
steps: Plan ahead: the slab is refrigerated for one hour before cutting.
Line a 23 x 13 cm mold with parchment paper, leaving two edges overhanging. Set aside.
Heat the pan over very low heat, empty, for a few seconds. Reduce if it becomes warm beyond comfortable.
Pour the chocolate into the pan. Stir continuously with a spatula, bringing the edges toward the center. Allow approximately 3 minutes: the chocolate should be smooth and glossy, never smoking.
Off the heat, add the tahini. Mix until the mixture becomes homogeneous and supple again.
Fold in the puffed quinoa, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, and sesame seeds. Mix to coat each seed.
Pour into the mold. Pack down with the back of a spoon to remove air pockets and even out the surface. Sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Refrigerate for 1 hour, until the slab is firm to the touch.
Unmold by pulling on the paper. Cut into eight bars with a smooth-bladed knife, lightly heated under warm water and dried.

title: Frozen yogurt, hazelnut and chocolate bites
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the device must come out of the freezer completely firm, and the chocolate must be melted and then only lukewarm at the time of dipping, otherwise the coating will slide instead of sticking.
titane: A titanium pan replaces a double boiler. Preheat it for one minute over low heat, then remove it from the heat source: the heat retained in the thin metal is enough to melt the chocolate slowly, without a hot spot or an additional pan of water. If the chocolate cools too much, a ten-second pass over the lowest heat will restart the melting process.
steps: Plan ahead: the bites take 1 hour in the freezer; factor in this time before you can coat them.
In a bowl, combine the yogurt, hazelnut butter, cocoa and maple syrup. Mix until you obtain a smooth, uniformly dark mixture. Taste and adjust with syrup if the cocoa is too dominant.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Spoon ten small, even mounds, spacing them two centimeters apart.
Place the baking sheet in the freezer. Let set for 1 hour: the bites must be firm to the touch, with no fingerprints.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over low heat, then remove from heat. Pour the chopped chocolate into it and stir gently with a silicone spatula until completely melted, about 3 minutes. The chocolate should be smooth and shiny. Add coconut oil if it remains too thick to coat.
Let the chocolate cool for a minute off the heat. Remove the bites, dip them one by one using a fork, then let the excess drain against the edge of the pan.
Place them back on the parchment paper and immediately sprinkle with crushed hazelnuts and fleur de sel: the coating sets in a few seconds upon contact with the cold, you must garnish right away.
Return the baking sheet to the freezer. The bites keep for 3 months. Allow 1 hour in the refrigerator or 15 minutes at room temperature before serving.

title: One bowl of fudgy chocolate cake
intro: It all comes down to the hot coffee poured last: the batter becomes very liquid, almost worryingly so, and that's exactly what gives it that tight and moist crumb.
titane: The frying pan replaces the baking pan. Oil it completely, including the edges, with a neutral, high-smoke-point oil—no parchment paper. It goes straight from the countertop to the oven, and its metal mass conducts heat to the center without drying out the edges. When cool, the cake releases cleanly.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Generously oil the titanium pan, base and sides.
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, cocoa, baking powder, baking soda, and salt. Break up any cocoa lumps well, as they won't dissolve later.
Add the milk, oil, sour cream, eggs, and vanilla. Whisk until you have a thick, smooth batter with the consistency of brownie batter.
Pour the hot coffee in a thin stream while continuing to whisk. The batter will loosen and become very fluid: this is the correct consistency.
Pour into the pan and bake directly. Allow 35 minutes. A knife blade or toothpick inserted into the center should come out clean or with a few moist crumbs.
Let it cool completely in the pan. Remove from the pan, then glaze — on a still-warm cake, the glaze would slide off.

title: Raw date, peanut and dark chocolate bars
intro: Everything depends on the pressing: a tightly packed mass holds up to cutting, a soft mass crumbles.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the bain-marie. Its even heat distribution allows dark chocolate to be melted over very low heat, without hot spots or sticking, for a smooth coating in three minutes.
steps: Plan ahead: the preparation will rest in the refrigerator for 2 hours before being sliced.
Coarsely chop the dates and break the walnuts, almonds and cashews with a knife. Keep visible pieces: this is what gives the bar its bite.
In a mixing bowl, work the peanut butter with the honey and cinnamon until you obtain a homogeneous paste.
Fold in the dates, the broken dried fruits, the pumpkin seeds and the sesame. Mix with a spoon, pressing against the side of the bowl, until no piece remains dry.

Line a rectangular mould with baking paper (cover the bottom and sides, leaving two tabs hanging over the edge). Pour the mixture and press firmly with the back of a spoon or a glass with a flat bottom, until the surface is very even.

Break the chocolate into pieces in the cold titanium pan. Heat over very low heat and stir continuously for 3 minutes. Remove from the heat as soon as the chocolate is smooth and shiny: if heated too strongly, it seizes (its sugar crystals separate and the mass becomes grainy).
Pour the chocolate over the pressed mixture and spread in an even layer with a spatula.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until the whole is firm to the touch.
Unmould using the paper tabs and cut into rectangles with a knife with a smooth blade, passed under hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: No-bake coffee tiramisu verrines
intro: It all comes down to two things: really cold coffee and biscuits soaked for one second, not two.
titane: No pans here, no heat source: the dessert is assembled cold and built up in the refrigerator. The key is in the dipping. Allow one dip per side for one second, holding the biscuit flat between two fingers. The ladyfinger should emerge soft on the surface and still firm in the center: it's the six-hour rest that will soften it completely, not the coffee bath.
steps: Plan ahead: the verrines must rest for 5 to 6 hours minimum, preferably overnight; begin in advance.
Dissolve the instant coffee and sugar in hot water. Pour into a shallow, wide dish, then let cool completely. Warm coffee softens the biscuits too quickly.
Whip the very cold cream with an electric whisk (whip: beat until the cream traps air and thickens). Stop when it is mousy and coats the back of a spoon.
Incorporate the cold sweetened condensed milk in a thin stream, whisking continuously, until you obtain a smooth cream that holds its shape on the whisk tip. It must be firm enough to pipe.
Dip each biscuit in the cold coffee, one second per side. Drain it for half a second over the dish. Do not let it soak too long, it would fall apart.
Place 2 soaked biscuits side by side at the bottom of each container. Trim them with scissors or a serrated knife so they fit the bottom perfectly.
Pipe or spread a generous layer of cream on top, pressing well into the corners.
Repeat: 2 soaked biscuits, then a final layer of cream thicker than the first.
Smooth the surface with the back of a spoon or an offset spatula. Do the same for all 6 verrines.
Cover and refrigerate for 5 to 6 hours minimum, preferably overnight. The biscuits soften, the cream firms up.
Just before serving, dust the cocoa through a fine sieve, in an opaque and even layer.
Serve with a spoon, going straight down to the bottom to catch all the layers.

title: Date peel, pistachio and dark chocolate
intro: It's all about contrast: a compact date base, a layer of toasted coconut that crunches, a chocolate thin enough to break cleanly between the teeth.
titane: One pan is all you need for this recipe. It toasts the coconut dry, without any hot spots or burning corners, thanks to a rapid and even heat distribution. It then serves as a double boiler (gently melting the chocolate in the steam) placed over a pan of simmering water. Always preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the coconut: this ensures even browning from the very first seconds.
steps: Open the dates in half lengthwise and arrange them flat, tightly packed, on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Cover with a second sheet of paper and roll over with a rolling pin until you obtain a continuous and even layer of approximately 5 mm. Remove the top sheet of paper.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat.

Pour the coconut into the pan and toast it dry (without oil), stirring regularly, for about 5 minutes. Stop as soon as the strands are golden and the aroma is released: the coloring process will continue off the heat.
Remove from heat and stir in the pistachio butter directly into the pan. Mix until the coconut is completely coated.
Spread this mixture over the layer of dates, in an even thickness all the way to the edges.
Rinse and dry the pan, then place it over a pan of simmering water. Melt the chocolate over low heat, stirring constantly, until smooth and glossy.
Coat the dates with chocolate and smooth with a spoon to cover the entire surface.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel and refrigerate for about 22 minutes, until the chocolate is set and matte.
Cut into irregular bite-sized pieces, either by breaking or with a warm knife.

title: Falafel wrap cooked in pita bread
intro: Here, the falafel is not fried: it is cooked in a thin layer directly on the bread, and everything depends on the crust.

ing.note: soaked overnight then cooked in water

ing: a good pinch of sea salt
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. Place the pita, falafel-side down, and don't move it. As long as the batter adheres, the crust will form. Once it's set, the bread will release easily: that's the signal to flip it, not before.
steps: Drain the chickpeas thoroughly. Blend them with the parsley, cilantro, quartered onion, garlic, cumin, pepper, paprika, and salt. Add a tablespoon of grapeseed oil while blending. Process until you obtain a smooth paste with no visible lumps.

Prepare the tarator: mix the tahini with the lemon juice; it will thicken initially. Stir in the yogurt, then add the water one spoonful at a time until you reach a coating consistency. Season with salt.
Spread a thin layer of falafel paste on one side of each pita, about 3 mm thick, up to the edges.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Place a pita, falafel side down, in the pan. Do not touch it. After about 3 minutes, it will detach on its own and the crust will be golden brown.

Flip it over with a quick, firm motion. Let the other side toast for 1 minute, until the bread is golden brown but not dry. Remove from the pan and set aside on a wire rack, then repeat, one pita at a time: an overcrowded pan loses heat and the crust becomes soggy.
Garnish with mixed greens, pickled turnip and cherry tomatoes. Top with tarator sauce, roll up tightly, and serve immediately.

title: Black sesame matcha latte
intro: It all depends on the relaxation of the sesame paste: if it remains lumpy, the glass will be grainy until the last sip.
ing: raw honey or pure maple syrup
titane: No pan here, but an equally precise cooking technique: loosen (soften a thick mixture by gradually incorporating the liquid) the sesame paste with only a small amount of milk, stirring tightly, before adding more. The opposite—pouring in all the milk at once—hardens the paste into small, impossible-to-remove lumps.
steps: In a large glass, combine the black sesame paste and honey. Add a teaspoon of milk, whisk or stir with a spoon until you obtain a homogeneous cream, then incorporate the rest of half the milk. The texture should be smooth and coating.
In a separate bowl, pour the matcha, then the hot water. Whisk with a rapid W motion until completely dissolved and a fine foam appears on the surface. No grains should remain at the bottom.
Fill the glass with ice cubes over the sesame base. Pour the remaining milk.
Add the matcha very slowly, in a thin stream, along a piece of ice or the back of a spoon: the layers remain distinct. Stir and serve immediately.

title: Chocolate mousse and silken tofu
intro: Everything hinges on the melting of the chocolate: gentle, monitored, never rushed, otherwise the mousse loses its velvety texture.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its rapid and even heat distribution melts the chocolate without any hot spots, provided you keep the heat very low and stir continuously. This prevents it from curdling (the cocoa butter separates and the mixture becomes grainy).
steps: Plan ahead: the mousse must rest at least 2 hours in the refrigerator before serving.
Break the chocolate into regular pieces and place them in the cold titanium pan. Set over very low heat.
Stir continuously with a spatula for about 3 minutes, until you have a smooth and glossy mass. Remove from heat as soon as the last piece has melted.
Pour the melted chocolate into the mixer bowl. Add the drained silken tofu, honey, cocoa, and peanut butter.
Blend for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down the sides once, until you reach a perfectly homogeneous texture with no tofu grains.
Divide among three glasses or small bowls. Smooth the surface with the back of a spoon.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours. The mousse should be firm to the touch yet creamy when eaten with a spoon.
Just before serving, top each with a spoonful of yogurt, then sprinkle with crushed peanuts and grated chocolate.

title: Focaccia with za'atar
intro: A highly hydrated dough, two short rises during the day, and pan cooking which gives the base a crust that no high-sided dish produces.

ing.note: Allow 390 to 420 ml depending on the absorption of your flour.

ing: olive oil for mixing with za'atar
titane: The titanium pan serves as a mold here. With no coating, there's no temperature limit: it goes straight from the countertop to a 220°C oven without any precautions. The direct contact of the oiled dough with the bare metal fries the base while the crumb finishes rising. That's the contrast we're aiming for.
steps: Whisk the lukewarm water, 15 ml olive oil, honey and yeast in a bowl. The honey gives the yeast something to get started quickly.
Mix the flour and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the liquid and work by hand until no dry flour remains. The dough is sticky, which is normal.
Cover. Let rest for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Stretch and fold (grasp one edge of the dough, pull it upward, fold it back to the center) eight times while rotating around the bowl.
Cover again. Rest for 15 minutes.
Repeat the series of stretches and folds. The dough should be noticeably smoother and more resilient than on the first round.
