Cover and let rise for 1 hour 15 minutes at room temperature, until the volume has increased well and the surface is covered with bubbles.
Generously oil the titanium pan, bottom and sides. Pour the dough into it and fold it in three on itself, like a letter.
Cover the pan. Let rise a second time for 1 hour 15 minutes, still at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 220 °C. The pan goes in as is.
Mix the zaatar and 1.5 tbsp olive oil in a bowl.
With oiled fingertips, gently stretch the dough to the edges of the pan. If it resists, wait five minutes and try again.
Drizzle with the zaatar mixture, then dimple the dough by pressing your fingers down to the bottom, regularly across the entire surface. These dimples hold the oil and create the relief.
Distribute the olives by pressing them lightly into the dimples.
Bake on the lowest rack for 21 minutes. The focaccia is golden on top, the base distinctly seared from contact with the titanium, the crumb soft.
Unmold onto a rack and wait 15 minutes before cutting, allowing time for the steam to escape and the crust to remain crispy.
Serve with the labneh.

title: Pistachio cheesecake with kataifi and milk chocolate ganache
intro: It's all about the contrast: a cold and dense mixture, a layer of pan-roasted kataifi that must remain crisp to the bite, and a ganache poured lukewarm so as not to soften it.

ing.note: or clarified butter, or grapeseed oil

titane: Kataifi burns easily if the heat is uneven. Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the fat: the even heat will brown the strands in a single layer, without any black spots. Do not stir while the kataifi is still sticking. It will release easily when it's ready. The same pan, simply wiped with paper towels, is then used to heat the ganache cream without imparting any buttery flavor.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake takes a full night in the refrigerator; start the day before.

Mix the crumbled cookies with melted butter. Press firmly into the bottom of a 20 cm springform pan, bringing the mixture slightly up the sides. Press with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass: a poorly packed crust will crumble when unmolded.
Whip the cold cream until mousy and smooth, just barely holding its shape on the whisk. Reserve in the cold.
Beat the cream cheese with the sugar until smooth. Add the melted white chocolate, then the pistachio cream, and beat again until you have a homogeneous mass with no grains.
Fold in the whipped cream in three additions, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from bottom to top (this motion prevents the air from deflating).
Spread the mixture over the crust and smooth the surface. Refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hours: the filling should be firm to the touch, with no fingerprints.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes. Melt the butter in it over medium-high heat, add the kataïfi and toast for about 8 minutes (toasting: cooking in fat until golden to develop flavor). Wait for it to release naturally from the pan before stirring, then stir regularly. It should be evenly golden and crispy.
Transfer to a bowl, let cool for two minutes, then mix with the pistachio paste. Spread over the cheesecake removed from the cold in an even layer.
Wipe the pan with paper towel. Heat the cream in it over medium heat for 3 minutes, until it steams: in a pan, the temperature rises quickly, keep watching.

Pour the hot cream over the chopped milk chocolate. Let sit for 2 minutes, then stir from the center outward until the ganache is smooth and shiny (the emulsion forms in the center and spreads outward).
Let the ganache cool until it coats the spoon without running quickly. Unmold the cheesecake, pour the ganache in the center and let it spread to the edges on its own. Serve.

title: Pan-fried shish tawouk, fries and Greek salad
intro: Everything happens in the same pan: dry-fried golden fries, then yogurt-marinated skewers that are left to color without ever being disturbed.
ing: sweet chili paste or tomato paste
titane: The titanium pan is high enough to replace the oven for fries and the grill for kebabs. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add the oil or butter, place the food inside, and wait. As long as it's sticking, it's not ready: the crust that forms will release the food on its own. Forcing it with a spatula will tear off the color and leave it at the bottom.
steps: Peel the garlic cloves and thinly slice them.
Cut the potatoes into regular batons of 6 mm per side. Consistency determines the cooking.
Cover them with hot water in a bowl and let soak for 10 minutes: surface starch is removed, crispness comes.
Drain, then dry the batons in a clean cloth. They must be completely dry before touching the pan.
Place the chicken cubes in a bowl. Add yoghurt, chilli paste, garlic, oil, lemon juice and all the spices. Mix by hand to coat each side.
Wrap and keep in the cold for 15 to 20 minutes.
In the meantime, prepare cucumber, tomato and olives, and keep them chilled.
Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add the clarified butter.

Arrange the batons in a single layer, without overlapping. Season with salt and pepper. Let them brown without touching until they release by themselves, then turn them regularly. Allow 20 minutes for a crust on all sides. Do this in two batches if the pan is full.
Transfer the fries to a dish, sprinkle with parsley and cover with aluminium foil.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers at the last moment, pressing the cubes without packing them.
Heat the pan empty again for 1 to 2 minutes, add a drizzle of fat.

Sear the skewers for 5 to 8 minutes on the first side without moving them. Turn when they release, and continue for 5 to 8 minutes: the yoghurt marinade should show brown spots and the centre remain pearly with juices.
Season the salad with lemon, olive oil, salt and pepper, add the feta and mix just before serving.
Plate the skewers, fries and salad together, and serve without delay.

title: Pan-fried almond and banana muffins
intro: Muffins without a mold: it all comes down to the ripeness of the bananas and a properly buttered pan, which gives a nice golden base and a clean release from the mold.
titane: Generously butter the titanium pan, drop the batter into spaced mounds, then place the pan directly in the oven. Without a coating or parchment paper, the bottom conducts heat directly: the base caramelizes while the top remains soft. Work in two batches if the mounds are touching.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C, fan-assisted.
In a bowl, mix the almond spread, almond flour, honey, and milk until you have a smooth cream. Add a spoonful of milk if it's too firm. Set aside.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl until you have a smooth puree with no large pieces.
Incorporate the eggs, milk, olive oil, honey and vanilla. Whisk to combine.
Add the flour, cinnamon, and baking soda. Mix until all traces of flour have disappeared, but no more.
Generously butter the titanium pan. Place the batter in twelve even, well-spaced mounds.
Place a spoonful of almond cream in the center of each mound.
Sprinkle with flaked almonds.
Place the pan in the oven and bake for 24 minutes. The muffins are cooked when the tops are golden brown and firm to the touch.
Let it cool in the pan, then remove (transfer to a rack) using a thin spatula.
Sprinkle with icing sugar when serving.

title: Chocolate-coffee pan cheesecake
intro: It all comes down to the degree of cooking: a center that is still mobile when it comes out of the oven will, after a night in the cold, give a dense and creamy texture rather than a sandy one.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the springform pan. Preheated empty for two to three minutes, then coated (with a thin layer of fat) with clarified butter, it goes directly from the hob to the oven without transfer: the appliance begins to cook in already hot metal, and the direct contact lightly caramelizes the base.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake cools then rests for at least 8 hours in the refrigerator; start the day before.
Preheat the oven to 163 °C.

Combine in the blender the cottage cheese, yogurt, eggs, cocoa, maple syrup, flour, vanilla and ground coffee. Blend until the mixture is perfectly smooth, with no residual cottage cheese grains. Scrape the sides halfway through if necessary.

Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat. The bottom must be distinctly hot. Off the heat, brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter: the surface must remain shiny, without excess.
Pour the batter into the hot pan and smooth the top. Cover and bake for 45 minutes. If you don't have an oven, continue on the stovetop over very low heat, lid closed.
Check the cooking: the edges are set and shrink back from the sides on their own, the center still trembles slightly when you shake the pan. This is the right moment to stop.
Let cool in the pan, off the heat, without lid, until completely cooled. Run a thin blade along the edges, turn out onto a plate, then refrigerate for at least 8 hours before slicing.

title: Red Berry Crumble Bars
intro: It all depends on how well the crumble mixture holds its shape: if it compacts between your fingers, the base will cut cleanly once cold.
titane: The pan performs two functions in the same recipe. First, it reduces the berries dry, without any added fat: the preheated titanium handles the fruit's acidity and evaporation without sticking. Then, it acts as a mold: you press the base directly into the pan and bake it as is. No transfer required, only one piece to wash.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C using the fan setting.
In a bowl, combine the almond flour, oat flakes, baking powder and cinnamon. Mix together dry ingredients.
Pour in the melted coconut oil and three-quarters of the honey. Work with your fingertips until you obtain a moist, crumbly mixture that holds its shape when squeezed in your hand. Set aside.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 minutes over medium heat.
Pour in the still-frozen berries, without any fat. Let it reduce for 8 minutes over medium heat, stirring regularly: the fruit will break down and the mixture will coat the spoon.
Remove from heat and add the lemon juice, chia seeds, and remaining honey. Stir, then transfer to a cold container to stop the cooking process. Let it thicken for 5 minutes.
Rinse and dry the pan, line it with baking paper. Press three-quarters of the almond sand into it, pressing firmly and slightly up the sides.
Spread the berry topping over the base in an even layer.
Crumble the rest of the mixture on top, without packing it down, to keep the texture.
Bake the pan for 24 minutes at 180°C: the top should be golden and crispy.
Allow to cool completely in the pan before unmolding and cutting into bars. When warm, the base crumbles.

title: Coconut-chocolate bars with almonds
intro: It all comes down to the consistency of the base: enough fat and binder so that it cuts cleanly, never soggy.
ing: dark chocolate with no added sugar
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its rapid heat distribution melts chocolate and almond butter in three minutes over very low heat, without preheating, since it's melting, not searing. Stir continuously: the heat rises quickly and the chocolate will stick as soon as you take your eyes off it.
steps: Blend the coconut, coconut milk, coconut oil, maple syrup and vanilla in a food processor for about 1 minute. The mixture should stick between your fingers without falling apart.
Line a 13 x 18 cm baking tin with baking paper. Press the mixture into the base, making sure it's flat, using the back of a spoon to create an even layer.
Place in the freezer while preparing the chocolate.
Place the chopped chocolate and almond butter in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir constantly for 3 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and glossy. Remove from the heat immediately.
Pour the chocolate over the cold base and spread it into an even layer.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel, then distribute the almonds in a staggered pattern, one per portion to come.
Refrigerate for 1 hour 30 minutes, until firm to the touch.
Remove the preparation from its mold by pulling on the paper, then cut into bars with a blade that has been rinsed under hot water and wiped dry.

title: Mini chocolate-coated cookies
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: too hot, it remains matte and sticks to the silicone; just lukewarm, it sets cleanly and releases a shiny shell.
titane: A titanium pan replaces a double boiler. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then reduce the heat to very low and place the chocolate inside. The thermal mass of the base is enough to melt it. Stir continuously with a spatula and remove the pan from the heat as soon as the mixture is fluid: the titanium continues to radiate heat for a good minute.
steps: Cream the butter and brown sugar (work them together until the mixture lightens in color and becomes fluffy), using a whisk or mixer.
Incorporate the egg and vanilla. Add the flour, then the chocolate chips. Stop as soon as the batter is thick and smooth.
Preheat the oven to 180°C. Roll balls the size of a hazelnut and place one in each cavity of a miniature half-sphere silicone mold.
Bake for 13 minutes, until the edges are barely golden and the center is still soft.
Allow to cool completely in the mold, then unmold. Wash and dry the mold: even the smallest crumb will spoil the shine of the shell.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over very low heat. Melt the milk chocolate, stirring constantly, and remove it from the pan as soon as it is smooth. Wipe the pan clean and repeat with the white chocolate.
Pour a spoonful of melted chocolate, milk or white, into the bottom of each cavity.
Press a cooled cookie into the chocolate so that it rises up the sides and coats the bottom and sides. Smooth the edges with your finger.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, until the shell is perfectly firm to the touch.
Remove from the mold by pushing the silicone from underneath, without forcing the shell. Serve at room temperature.

title: Night oats, banana and speculoos shell
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the speculoos paste must be poured hot onto a cold bowl to set into a thin, brittle shell.

ing.note: or the milk of your choice

titane: Melt the speculoos spread and coconut oil over very low heat in the titanium pan rather than in the microwave. The heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots: you can visually monitor the consistency of the mixture and turn off the heat the second it coats the spoon with an even layer.
steps: Plan ahead: the shell takes at least 1 hour in the refrigerator, or overnight; start in advance.
In a glass jar or bowl, combine the oats, protein powder, milk, flax and chia seeds, cinnamon and salt. Mix until you obtain a thick and homogeneous base.
Smooth the yogurt in an even layer over the oats. Arrange the banana slices on top, tightly packed, leaving no gaps.
Place the jar in the refrigerator while you prepare the shell: the temperature contrast does all the work.

In the titanium pan, combine the speculoos paste and coconut oil. Heat over low heat for 2 min, stirring, until you obtain a smooth and fluid mixture. Remove from heat as soon as it runs from the tip of the spoon in a continuous stream.
Remove the jar and immediately pour the hot mixture over the bananas, covering the entire surface to the edges. Sprinkle with crumbled biscuit.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 1 hour, or overnight, until the shell is completely set.
To serve, break the shell with a spoon and mix the layers as you go.

title: Chocolate, peanut and marshmallow cups
intro: It all depends on the thickness of the shell: too thin and it breaks when unmolding, too thick and it crushes the filling.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a melting pot. Preheated empty for two minutes over low heat, it distributes heat evenly without any hot spots: the chocolate melts without sticking or graining. Its thin base and narrow sides allow for direct pouring into the baking cups, without transferring to an intermediate bowl. The same pan is used for both coating and sealing the chocolate.
steps: Plan ahead: the cups require at least 1 hour in the refrigerator after glazing, plan for this time before serving.
Arrange the paper cups on a baking sheet, placed closely together so they stay upright.

Preheat the empty pan for 2 minutes over low heat. Turn off the heat, add half the chocolate chips and stir with a spatula. The residual heat is enough to melt them into a smooth, fluid mass. If the chocolate remains grainy, turn the heat back on for a few seconds on minimal setting.
Pour a spoonful of chocolate into each cup, then line (coat the bottom and sides) by turning the cup or spreading with the back of a small spoon. Make sure to go all the way up to the rim.
Place the baking sheet in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. The shell must be firm and matte to the touch.
Place a heaping teaspoon of peanut butter in the centre of each shell, without touching the sides: the sealing chocolate must be able to seal the edges.
Cover with a spoonful of marshmallow cream. Smooth it barely, the layer must remain below the rim level.
Melt the remaining chocolate chips in the pan, using the same method. Coat each cup to the level of the paper, making sure the chocolate joins the shell all around the edge.
Refrigerate for 1 hour, or 20 minutes in the freezer, until completely set.
Remove the paper at serving time. Keep the cups chilled, they soften quickly at room temperature.

title: Triple chocolate cookie-style dip
intro: A spoon dessert that plays with cooking: everything is decided by the texture, therefore by the temperature of the fats and the toasting of the oats.

ing.note: in a block, at room temperature
ointment (very soft to the touch, without being

titane: Dry-roast the oats in a titanium pan (heat without oil to develop the aromas) over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring continuously. The oats will turn from pale to golden and smell nutty: immediately transfer them from the pan to a cold plate, otherwise the residual heat will make them bitter. Let them cool completely before incorporating them, or they will melt the butter and liquefy the mixture.
steps: Plan ahead: the dip must rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Toast the oat flakes as indicated above. Set aside on a flat surface and let cool.

Check that the butter and cream cheese are at room temperature before beginning. Beat the cream cheese and icing sugar with an electric mixer at medium speed for 2 to 3 minutes. Stop when the mixture is perfectly smooth, with no graininess or white streaks.
Add the softened butter, peanut butter, brown sugar, milk, vanilla and salt. Beat until you obtain a homogeneous and glossy mixture. Scrape the sides of the bowl halfway through.
Fold in the cooled oat flakes using a flexible spatula, lifting the mixture rather than stirring.
Fold in the same way the chocolate chips and dragées, setting aside a handful of each.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 30 minutes. The mixture will firm up and the oats will absorb some of the milk.
Transfer to a serving bowl, smooth the surface and sprinkle with the reserved chocolate. Serve well chilled.

title: Kadayif iced cake with hazelnut and milk chocolate
intro: It all comes down to the kadayif: if it is toasted thoroughly and cooled completely, it remains crispy under the cream for several days.
titane: Kadayif is toasted in a pan, not an oven. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes: the heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots, and the strands brown in a few minutes instead of 15 minutes in the oven for 250g. Then wipe the same pan clean to warm the ganache cream. Use only one pan from start to finish.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake goes into the freezer for 30 minutes then approximately 3 more hours to set, allow for this time before serving.
Separate the thawed kadayif with your fingers and cut the strands to lengths of 3 to 4 cm. Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.

Lower to medium heat, add the clarified butter then the kadayif by handfuls. Stir regularly for approximately 8 minutes: the strands should be golden all over and smell of roasted hazelnut. Do not overcrowd the pan, work in two batches if needed.
Transfer to a cold plate and let cool completely. While still warm, the kadayif would soften on contact with the spread.
Mix the cooled kadayif with the spread until each strand is coated.
Line a 24 x 24 cm square mould with parchment paper leaving two sides overhanging. Dip 12 biscuits briefly in the milk and arrange them at the bottom, edge to edge.
Spread the kadayif-hazelnut mixture over the biscuits and level without compressing.
Whisk the cold cream with the vanilla pudding, icing sugar and vanilla extract until thick and fluffy texture that holds a peak.
Spread this cream over the kadayif layer, smooth with a spatula.

Wipe the pan. Chop the milk chocolate. Over low heat, warm the 125 ml of cream until the first simmer, pour it over the chopped chocolate, wait one minute then stir from the centre outward until you have a smooth and glossy ganache.
Let the ganache cool for two minutes, then pour it over the vanilla cream and tilt the mould to spread it.
Place in the freezer for 30 minutes, while the ganache sets.
Dip the remaining 12 biscuits in the milk and arrange them on the set ganache.
Return to the freezer for approximately 3 hours, until the cake is firm in the centre.
Unmould by pulling on the paper, cut into 9 squares with a blade passed under hot water and wiped between each cut. Serve after 10 minutes at room temperature.

title: No-bake cheesecake with blueberries and white chocolate
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the compote must be perfectly cold before assembly, otherwise the layers will blur.
titane: The compote cooks directly in the titanium pan, without a saucepan. The base heats up quickly, and the large surface area accelerates evaporation: the starch sets in a few minutes, and the compote becomes glossy instead of remaining liquid. Stir constantly with a flexible spatula; the volume is small and it sticks easily if left undisturbed.
steps: Crush the biscuits into fine crumbs. Pour in the melted butter and mix until the mixture resembles damp sand. Press firmly into the bottom and up the sides of a 20cm springform pan using the back of a spoon. Refrigerate.
Dissolve the cornstarch in cold water. Place the frozen blueberries, sugar, lemon juice, and salt in a titanium pan. Heat over medium heat until the fruit releases its juices.

Pour in the dissolved cornstarch. Continue cooking for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until the compote coats the back of a spoon and becomes glossy. Immediately transfer it from the pan to a wide, cold dish and let it cool completely to room temperature.
Melt the white chocolate in a double boiler over low heat, stirring constantly. Let it cool slightly: it should remain fluid but not hot.
Whip the cream (whip it until it holds its shape on the whisk but is not stiff). Refrigerate.

Beat the cream cheese with the sugar until perfectly smooth. Stir in the melted chocolate and vanilla, then gently fold in the whipped cream in three additions, using a spatula and lifting the mixture to retain air.
Spread half of the filling over the cold crust. Spread the cooled compote evenly, leaving a border around the edges. Cover with the remaining filling and smooth the surface. Refrigerate overnight.
Run a thin blade along the side before opening the hinge. Serve chilled.

title: Honey and nut bars
intro: It all comes down to roasting: properly browned dried fruit makes for a bar that holds together and tastes good, the honey just binds them together.
titane: The pan heats up quickly and evenly: it dry-roasts the nuts without any added fat, then immediately adds the honey, without rinsing. A single utensil is used from start to finish, and the juices left by the almonds infuse the syrup with their flavor.
steps: Plan ahead: the slab must chill for at least 2 hours in the refrigerator before being cut.
Heat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. It must be thoroughly hot before the first contact.

Pour in almonds, walnuts, sunflower seeds and pumpkin seeds. Toast dry (without any fat) for approximately 6 minutes, stirring regularly. They are ready when they are golden, fragrant, and detach on their own from the bottom.
Remove from the pan and transfer into a salad bowl. Set aside.
Place the still-hot pan back over medium heat and pour in the honey. Bring to a boil.
Let simmer for 1 minute, without taking your eyes off the pan: honey turns from golden to burnt very quickly.
Off the heat, pour the hot honey and cinnamon over the dried fruits. Mix until everything is coated.
Transfer to a dish lined with parchment paper. Cover with a second sheet and press firmly with the bottom of a glass: the more you press, the less the bars will crumble.
Remove the top sheet. Refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours, until the slab is firm to the touch.
Cut into bars. Store them in an airtight container, in the refrigerator.

title: Banana, peanut butter and dark chocolate bites
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: if it's melted too quickly or is too hot, it loses its shine and turns grey when cold.
titane: A titanium pan replaces a double boiler. Preheat it empty for one minute over low heat, remove it from the heat, pour in the chocolate, and stir constantly: the heat retained at the bottom is enough to melt it in seconds. Never put it back on the flame once the chocolate is inside.
steps: Mash the bananas with a fork, or slice them into 5mm rounds. Spread them in the bottom of a twelve-cavity silicone mold, to a depth of about one centimeter.
Place a spoonful of peanut butter on top. Smooth the top without trying to reach the edges: the chocolate will seal everything together.
Place the mold in the freezer while you prepare the chocolate. The filling layer needs to firm up, otherwise the hot chocolate will sink into it.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for one minute over low heat. Remove it from the heat. Pour in the chopped chocolate and honey, then stir continuously with a spatula. Allow two to three minutes: the mixture should be smooth and fluid, never smoking.
Remove the mold. Coat each cavity with melted chocolate, slightly overflowing to seal the edges.
Immediately sprinkle with crushed nuts, while the chocolate is still liquid.
Return to the freezer for at least two hours, until the bites are completely frozen. Unmold by pushing on the base of the silicone mold, and serve immediately: they soften quickly.

title: No-bake coconut-almond cheesecake
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the white chocolate: if it's too hot, it will liquefy the whipped cream and the cake will never set.
ing: coconut-almond bites coated in white chocolate
titane: The butter melts in the titanium pan over low heat, then you crumble the biscuits directly into it, off the heat. The residual heat and its even distribution are enough to soak each crumb without browning the butter. All in one place, no saucepan or bowl in between.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake requires at least 4 hours in the refrigerator, preferably overnight.
Melt the white chocolate in a bain-marie, then let it cool to room temperature. It should remain fluid but no longer be warm to the touch.
Line a 22 cm springform pan with parchment paper, covering the bottom and sides.
Melt the butter in the titanium pan over low heat. Remove from heat as soon as it is liquid, without letting it foam.
Crumble the biscuits directly into the pan. Mix until the mixture resembles damp sand and no crumb remains dry.
Pour into the pan and press firmly on the bottom with the base of a glass. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Whip the cold cream and fresh cheese together until you obtain a smooth and firm mixture that shows the mark of the whisk.
Add the cooled white chocolate and almond extract. Fold with a spatula (incorporate by lifting the mixture from the bottom to the top) to avoid deflating the volume.
Pour half of the mixture onto the cold crust. Smooth. Distribute the almond purée in small touches, then the crushed almonds. Cover with the remaining mixture and smooth again.
Refrigerate for 4 hours minimum, preferably overnight. The center should no longer jiggle.
Unmold, generously cover with coconut flakes and arrange the chocolates on top. Slice with a blade dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Pistachio-chocolate clusters
intro: Three ingredients, one pan: everything hinges on the melting temperature of the chocolate, which must remain low and constant.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its gradual heat-up and even distribution melt the chocolate without hot spots or lumps, in the same pan that will also be used for the final glaze. Turn off the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth: the pan itself will continue to heat up.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty, for 1 minute over very low heat. It should be lukewarm, never hot to the touch when held a few centimeters away.
Pour the chocolate chips and coconut oil into the pan. Let it melt for 3 minutes over very low heat, stirring continuously. Stop as soon as the mixture is smooth and shiny, without any lumps.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the whole pistachios and stir until each piece is coated.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, forming round and even mounds.
Sprinkle with crushed pistachios while the chocolate is still soft.
Refrigerate for 25 minutes, until the clusters are firm to the touch.
Melt the remaining 30g of chocolate in the same pan over very low heat. Drizzle the clusters with a thin line of chocolate (drawn with a spoon) and serve.

title: Cottage cheese flatbread
intro: It all comes down to the thinness of the layer and patience: a mixture that is too thick remains moist in the center, a thin layer sets into a soft and golden pancake.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven here. With the lid on, the trapped steam poaches the center, allowing the eggs to set without drying them out. Once the lid is removed, a quick flip puts the other side in direct contact with the hot metal for a deep brown color. Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding oil: on a surface that's already hot, the food will sear instead of sticking.
steps: Combine the cottage cheese, eggs, oregano, garlic and onion powder in a blender. Blend until perfectly smooth, with no visible lumps of cheese.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the grapeseed oil and spread it evenly with a brush or paper towel. It should simmer gently without smoking.
Pour the mixture into the center and immediately spread it in a thin, even layer over the entire surface, tilting the pan.
Cover and cook for 15 minutes over low to medium heat. The top should be set, the edges golden. Test with the edge of a spatula: do not try to lift until the galette releases easily.
Remove the lid. Flip with a flick of the wrist and continue cooking uncovered for 2 to 3 minutes, until the second side is golden brown and firm.
Remove the mixture from the pan onto a board and let it rest for 1 minute before cutting: the pancake will firm up as it cools.

title: Crispy peanut butter and dark chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to the melting of the chocolate: a few seconds too long and it starts to curdle, whereas the residual heat of the pan is enough to finish the job.
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty, over low heat, for 2 minutes. Add the chocolate and coconut oil, then remove from the heat as soon as the first pieces begin to sizzle and soften. Finish melting off the heat, stirring constantly: no double boiler, no burnt chocolate. Titanium heats up quickly and retains heat, so never leave the pan unattended during this step.
steps: Plan ahead: the chocolate must set in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour (or 20 minutes in the freezer) before unmolding.
Crumble the rice cakes by hand in a large bowl into irregular pieces the size of a fingernail. Fine fragments will provide binding, the larger pieces will give the crunch.
Add the peanut butter and honey. Mix with a spatula until each fragment is coated. The mixture should hold when you squeeze it in your hand: if it remains crumbly, add a spoonful of peanut butter.
Line a rectangular baking dish with baking paper, leaving two edges overhanging as they will be used for unmolding.

Pour the mixture and press down firmly with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass. A smooth and compact surface prevents the bars from crumbling when sliced. Set the dish aside while you prepare the chocolate.
Preheat the titanium pan empty over low heat for 2 minutes. Add the chopped chocolate and coconut oil.
As soon as the chocolate begins to shine at the edges, remove the pan from the heat and stir constantly until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture. Allow 3 minutes in total.
Pour the chocolate over the pressed base and spread it in a single motion, tilting the dish rather than passing the spatula back and forth.
Refrigerate for 1 hour, or 20 minutes in the freezer, until the chocolate is set and dull to the touch.
Unmold by pulling on the paper. Cut into ten bars with a large knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Baked oats with raspberries
intro: It all comes down to the moisture of the dough: liquid enough when putting it in the oven so that the center remains soft when the edges have browned.
ing: clarified butter to coat the pan
titane: The pan goes from the worktop to the oven without transition. Preheated empty and then buttered, it replaces the dish and the parchment paper: the metal conducts quickly, the dough takes immediately on contact and develops a slightly crispy edge, impossible to obtain in a cold mold.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until it heats up.
Remove the pan from the heat and brush the bottom and sides with a thin layer of clarified butter. Clarified butter can withstand oven heat without burning.
Mash the banana with a fork in a large bowl until you obtain a smooth puree without any lumps.
Add the oats, protein powder, honey, milk, vanilla, baking powder, chia seeds, and cinnamon. Mix thoroughly: the batter should be smooth and flow from the whisk in a thick ribbon.
Incorporate the raspberries with a spatula, in just two or three movements. If overworked, they will color the entire batter.
Pour the mixture into the hot pan, smooth the surface and bake immediately for 35 minutes. Check after 30 minutes: a knife inserted into the center should come out dry.
Remove the pan and let it cool for 15 minutes before unmolding. The preparation doesn't hold its shape well when hot.
Serve in slices, with a spoonful of yogurt and a drizzle of peanut butter softened for a few seconds in a bain-marie.

title: Chocolate bars, toasted coconut and pistachio
intro: It all comes down to the coconut: too pale it remains soft, too dark it is bitter; you have to aim for a deep blond that retains its crunch under the chocolate.
ing: dark chocolate with no added sugar
titane: Toast the coconut in a dry pan, without any oil. Preheat the pan empty for one minute over medium-low heat: the titanium will heat up quickly and evenly, without any hot spots that would burn the finest flakes. Stir as soon as the coconut starts to pull away from the bottom of the pan. Off the heat, stir the pistachio butter into the same still-warm pan: the residual heat will soften it, and the mixture will be ready without any extra dishes.
steps: Melt the plant-based white chocolate in a double boiler over low heat. Divide it between two small bowls.
Color the first bowl with a hint of matcha to obtain a light green. Add the remaining matcha and spirulina to the second bowl for a deeper green.
Draw green swirls at the bottom of the silicone mold cavities with a spoon or piping bag.
Place the mold in the freezer for 12 minutes, until the swirls are firm to the touch.
Melt the dark chocolate in a double boiler over low heat.
Pour a thin layer of dark chocolate over the swirls. Rotate the mold to coat (line the sides with an even layer) each cavity up to the top.
Refrigerate until the shell sets. Keep the remaining dark chocolate warm.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over medium-low heat. Pour the shredded coconut and toast for 4 minutes dry, stirring regularly. It is ready when it is golden, fragrant, and comes away on its own from the bottom. Watch carefully from the third minute.
Remove the pan from the heat. Add the pistachio butter to the warm coconut and mix until you obtain a homogeneous paste. Let it cool to room temperature.
Fill the shells with this mixture, pressing lightly to remove air. Leave 2 mm free under the edge.
Seal with the remaining melted dark chocolate and smooth the surface with a spatula.
Let it set for 30 minutes in the refrigerator, until everything is completely set.
Unmold. Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to two weeks.

title: Chicken fajitas with three peppers
intro: It all comes down to the starting temperature: a really hot pan caramelizes the edges of the chicken and peppers instead of making them sweat.

ing.note: deseeded and cut into small cubes

titane: Preheat the empty skillet over high heat for two to three minutes, until a wisp of smoke rises. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat when the vegetables are added: this is what gives them the browning that a baking sheet never achieves. At the end of cooking, cover and reduce the heat to low for two minutes to melt the cheese, without using a second dish.
steps: Cut the chicken and vegetables into pieces of the same size. Over high heat, preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes: it should be smoking slightly.

Pour in the grapeseed oil, then add the chicken, the three bell peppers, and the red onion all at once. Sprinkle with the spices, salt, pepper, and minced garlic, and stir briefly to coat. Cook for 2 minutes.
Squeeze half a lime over the mixture and place the two squeezed halves in the pan, cut side down.

Let it sear without touching, for about 8 minutes, over medium-high heat. The chicken will detach itself from the bottom when the crust has formed: this is the signal to turn it over and spread everything out in a layer.
Continue cooking for 8 minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally. The chicken should be opaque throughout, and the peppers tender but still firm to the bite.
Remove from heat and sprinkle the grated mozzarella directly into the pan.
Cover and let it rest for 2 minutes over low heat, until the cheese melts.
Meanwhile, mash the avocado with the tomato, red onion, squeezed half a lime, salt and pepper.
Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds per side in a dry pan. Serve the filling directly from the pan, along with the guacamole, yogurt, and chopped cilantro.

title: Ricotta toast with crispy garlic mushrooms
intro: It all comes down to the water content of the mushrooms: if it evaporates on contact with the hot pan instead of stagnating, you get a golden crust and not a soggy fricassee.
ing: flat-leaf parsley, leaves removed and chopped
titane: Preheat the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes before adding any oil or butter. The rapid heat-up of the titanium pan allows you to sear the mushrooms quickly: direct contact is a much better alternative to the forced air of a deep fryer. Once the mushrooms are removed from the pan and set aside, wipe the bottom clean and toast the bread in the same pan. Use only one pan, from start to finish.
steps: Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth. Avoid rinsing them under water, as they absorb it.
Slice them thinly and evenly so that they all color at the same rate.
Combine them in a bowl with the olive oil, soy sauce, garlic, parmesan cheese, parsley, thyme, ginger, pepper, and chili. Mix well to coat them thoroughly.
Preheat the empty pan over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the clarified butter or grapeseed oil: the fat should simmer gently.
Spread the mushrooms in a single layer. Work in two batches if the pan is full: if packed tightly, they release their water instead of browning.
Leave them untouched for about 8 minutes. They will peel off on their own once a crust has formed. Then turn them over and finish the coloring process.
Remove the mushrooms. Wipe the pan with paper towels, reduce the heat to medium and dry-toast the rye slices for 1 minute per side, until golden brown.
Spread the ricotta generously over the still-warm bread.
Scatter the crispy mushrooms on top, sprinkle with chives and serve immediately.

title: Eggplant caviar with tahini and yogurt
intro: It all comes down to the searing: well-colored meat against the metal gives the smokiness that the oven cannot produce.

ing.note: plus a little bit for cooking

titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil, then place the eggplant halves cut-side down and leave them untouched. They will stick at first, then release on their own when caramelized: this is the signal, not a timer. The lid then takes over to tenderize the center without drying it out.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the grapeseed oil. Place the eggplant halves skin-side down while you organize your work surface.
Turn them flesh-side down and salt the exposed side.
Leave them to set for about 5 minutes without moving them. They will detach on their own once the color has set: do not force them before then.
Turn skin-side down, reduce heat to medium, cover and continue cooking for 15 minutes. The tip of a knife should pierce the flesh without resistance.
Remove from the pan and set aside, let cool slightly, then scoop out the flesh with a spoon, leaving the skin on.
Chop the meat into small pieces on a board. Let it rest for 5 minutes and drain off any excess water.
Combine the eggplant in a bowl with the tahini, yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, salt, and pepper. Mix until you obtain a smooth but still slightly rustic texture.
Spread on a shallow dish, making a furrow with a spoon.
Drizzle with olive oil, sprinkle with parsley and pomegranate seeds.
Serve with warm Lebanese bread.

title: Thick cookies filled with white chocolate and cocoa biscuits
intro: A New York-style cookie hinges on two things: a very cold dough when baking, and a properly sealed filled center.
ing: white chocolate with cocoa biscuit pieces

ing.note: plus 10 whole biscuits for the filling

titane: This one doesn't require a pan. The dough is too thick for direct contact cooking: the bottom would burn before the filling was hot. So the technique shifts to shaping—hollow out the ball into a cup shape, add the filling, close it by folding the dough over, and roll it between your palms until the seam is no longer visible. Then it goes in the freezer overnight. It's this deep cold that keeps it from freezing for the twelve minutes in the oven.
steps: Plan ahead: the dough balls freeze overnight, start the day before.
Cream the butter and both sugars (beat them until you obtain a smooth, pale mixture with no visible grains).
Add the whole egg, the yolk and the vanilla. Mix until the batter becomes homogeneous again.
Incorporate the flour, baking soda, baking powder and salt, then the crushed biscuits. Stop as soon as the dough comes together: it should remain thick and barely worked.
Divide into ten portions and roll them into balls.
Open each ball into a cup shape, place a piece of white chocolate and a whole biscuit, close and seal carefully. Roll again.
Arrange the balls on a baking sheet, cover and place in the freezer overnight.

Preheat the oven to 188 °C. Bake in the middle of the oven, without thawing, for 12 minutes: the edges should be set, the center still pale and soft. If the bottoms brown too quickly, lower to 177 °C.
Let rest 10 minutes on the baking sheet before transferring to a wire rack. The center finishes setting during this time.

title: Frozen clusters with yogurt, almond butter and dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to how well it holds up in the cold: a mixture thick enough to form mounds that don't collapse, and chocolate that's just melted and sets on contact.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Preheated empty for one minute over low heat and then removed from the heat as soon as the base is lukewarm, it melts the chocolate by thermal inertia, without ever burning it. You then dip the clusters directly from the freezer into it: the smooth surface allows the excess to slide off, the chocolate sets cleanly, and you only dirty one utensil.
steps: In a bowl, mix the yogurt, almond butter, maple syrup and vanilla until you obtain a perfectly homogeneous mixture, without any clear streaks.
Taste. Adjust the maple syrup now: once frozen, the mixture will taste less sweet.
Drop regular dollops of a good tablespoon onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Space them two centimetres apart.
Freeze for 1 hour, until the mounds are firm to the touch.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over low heat. Pour in the chopped chocolate, remove from heat and stir. Add the coconut oil if the mixture remains thick. You are aiming for smooth, glossy chocolate, never hot to the touch.
Remove the clusters in small batches. Dip them in the chocolate remaining in the pan, leave them for a few seconds: the cold sets the coating almost immediately.
Transfer onto the parchment paper, sprinkle with fleur de sel while the chocolate is still dull.
Return to the freezer. The clusters keep there for 3 months. Remove them 15 minutes before serving, in the refrigerator or at room temperature.

title: Chocolate bars, dried fruit and cocoa biscuits
intro: It all comes down to heat: chocolate melted too quickly becomes grainy, and no topping can save a dull, grainy slab.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Placed over very low heat, it distributes heat evenly, without any hot spots under the chocolate. A single container, no water, no steam to cause the fat to curdle. Keep a close eye on it: the pan heats up quickly if you take your eyes off it.
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Place it flat; it should fit in the freezer without wobbling.
Roughly chop the almonds, cashews and walnuts. Keep some uneven pieces; they add texture when broken.

Place the chocolate and coconut oil in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously with a spatula for about 5 minutes, until smooth and glossy, without any lumps. Remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is homogeneous: the residual heat will finish the job.
Pour the chocolate onto the parchment paper. Spread it with a spatula to a thickness of 4 to 5 mm, keeping the edges irregular.
Immediately distribute the dried fruit, crushed biscuits, and cranberries. Press lightly with the back of a spoon to embed them in the still-soft chocolate.
Place in the freezer for 20 minutes, until the plate is completely frozen and matte to the touch.
Peel off the paper, break or cut into neat rectangles with a knife. Serve immediately, or store in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
Clean the pan while it is still warm, with hot water: the chocolate melts easily before it hardens.

title: Cottage cheese and date caramel ice cream
intro: Everything hinges on the first minute of mixing: if the cottage cheese is not perfectly smooth before adding the dates, the ice cream will remain grainy.
titane: Blend the cheese alone, without anything else, until it forms a glossy ribbon on the sides of the bowl. Scrape down the sides once, then blend again. The grains must be completely gone before any sugar enters the bowl: the dates thicken the mixture and clog the blades.
steps: Pour the cottage cheese into the blender bowl. Blend at full speed for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping down the sides halfway through, until you have a smooth, lump-free cream.

Add the dates, honey, vanilla and fine salt. Blend again until the mixture becomes thick and silky, with a uniform beige colour. If the dates resist, let them soak for 10 minutes in warm water and drain them.
Transfer to an airtight container. Smooth the surface with a spatula to remove any air pockets.
Freeze for 3 hours 30 minutes, until the centre is firm when pierced with the tip of a knife.
Remove the container 5 minutes before serving, to allow the surface to become pliable under a spoon. Form the scoops, finishing with fleur de sel at the last moment.

title: Creamy pasta with purple sweet potato and roasted cauliflower
intro: The entire consistency of this dairy-free sauce comes from the roasting: vegetables that are truly golden brown, never steamed, and cashews soaked for the fat.

ing.note: soaked for 4 hours in cold water
up to 1 and a half lemons depending on the acidity
plus the water from the pasta

titane: The final coating is done in the titanium pan, away from direct sunlight. Pour the sauce over the drained pasta, stir for one minute over low heat, adding the reserved pasta water one spoonful at a time: the starch binds the sauce instead of letting it run off. The smooth surface of the titanium prevents the pasta from sticking, which is essential for maintaining a vibrant purple color rather than browning.
steps: Preheat the oven to 205 °C.

Slice off the top of the garlic head to expose the cloves. Place it on a baking sheet with the cauliflower florets and the whole purple sweet potato, pricked twice. Drizzle the cauliflower and garlic with olive oil, season lightly with salt.
Bake for 30 minutes. The cauliflower should be golden at the edges, and the sweet potato should be pierced without resistance by the tip of a knife.
Split the sweet potato, scoop out the flesh with a spoon and weigh 450 g. Press the garlic head to extract the pulp.
Drain the soaked cashews.
Bring a large volume of water to the boil, season generously with salt, cook the pasta al dente (firm to the bite). Reserve 250 ml of cooking water, then drain.

Blend together the sweet potato, cauliflower, garlic pulp, drained cashews, nutritional yeast, miso, onion powder, lemon juice, plant-based milk and stock. Work until no grain of cashew is felt under the tongue. Season with salt and pepper.
Adjust the texture with stock or cooking water: the sauce should fall from the blender in a thick ribbon, without flowing like a liquid cream.
Combine the pasta and sauce in the pan over low heat, and stir for 1 to 2 minutes until everything is glossy and each piece is coated.
Transfer (to the serving dish) without delay, sprinkle with chopped herbs and serve.

title: Pan-fried almond French toast crumpets
intro: It all comes down to the balance between a distinctly caramelized surface and a still-soaked center, which requires a very hot pan and a batter thick enough to stay on the surface of the crumpet.
titane: The pan replaces the oven. Direct contact with the hot metal caramelizes the dish in minutes, whereas a fan oven would take half an hour, and the slivered almonds toast in the same motion, placed on their still-raw side. The result: a more pronounced crust and a soft interior.
steps: In a bowl, whisk together the egg, almond butter, honey, vanilla, cinnamon, almond flour, and milk. Mix for 2 to 3 minutes, until the almond butter is completely dissolved and the mixture is smooth.
Cut the crumpets in half lengthwise to obtain six half-discs.
Dip each half into the mixture, honeycomb side first. Let it soak for a few seconds, then drain thoroughly: a dripping crumpet will splatter in the pan and cook poorly.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour in the clarified butter and tilt the pan to coat the entire bottom.

Place the crumpets loosely on the pan—in two batches if necessary—ensuring even contact with the metal. Let them cook for 4 minutes without touching them: the top is ready when it easily releases from the bottom.

Flip with a flick of the wrist, reduce the heat to medium, and immediately sprinkle the slivered almonds on top. Continue cooking for 3 minutes, until the second side is golden brown and the egg is set.
Remove (transfer from the pan to stop the cooking) onto a warm plate and sprinkle with icing sugar.

title: No-bake lemon-poppy seed balls
intro: It's all about the balance between the acidity of the lemon and the fat of the coconut: weigh the juice, don't just eyeball it.

ing.note: plus a little something for the finishing touch

titane: Before mixing, dry-roast (heat without oil) the shredded coconut and poppy seeds in the titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir constantly. The coconut should turn golden at the edges, not brown. Immediately transfer (from the hot pan) to a cold plate: the pan retains enough heat to continue cooking and turn the poppy seeds bitter.
steps: Plan ahead: the balls need 1 hour in the freezer to firm up, allow for this resting time.
Toast the coconut and poppy seeds as indicated above. Let cool completely.
Combine almond flour, coconut, poppy seeds, hemp seeds and zest in a large bowl. Mix dry to distribute the seeds.

Add lemon juice, maple syrup and coconut butter. Work with a spatula then by hand until you obtain a homogeneous and sticky paste that holds in a ball when pressed. If it remains crumbly, add one teaspoon of juice; if it sticks too much, one tablespoon of almond flour.
Scoop the paste with an ice cream scoop or tablespoon, roll between your palms. Roll half of the balls in additional poppy seeds.
Arrange them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, without them touching. Place in the freezer for 1 hour: they should be firm to the touch.
For the coated version, melt the vegan white chocolate in a double boiler, dip the ice-cold balls, let set on the parchment paper.
Store in an airtight container, 1 week in the refrigerator or 3 months in the freezer.

title: Chocotorta
intro: It all comes down to dipping the biscuits: one second per side, no more, otherwise the structure collapses in the cold.

ing.note: Removed from the refrigerator 1 hour before
of cold coffee, or half and half

titane: No cooking involved here, but one opportunity to use the pan: gently warm the milk and coffee mixture in it over low heat for 1 minute, just until steam rises. The titanium coating heats up quickly and without hot spots, ensuring the liquid remains evenly distributed. Then pour it into a wide bowl and let it cool to room temperature before dipping. Warm liquid penetrates the biscuit too quickly and breaks it; cold liquid requires a second longer. Aim for room temperature.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake rests for at least 6 hours in the refrigerator, ideally a whole night.

Whip the softened cream cheese with the dulce de leche. Work vigorously for 2 to 3 minutes until you have a smooth, thick cream with a light caramel colour. Not a single grain should remain. Set aside a good third of the mixture for finishing.
Warm the coffee milk in a pan, transfer it into a shallow bowl and let it return to room temperature.
Dip each biscuit for one second per side. It should remain firm to the touch: it is the cream and the resting time that will finish softening it.
Line the bottom of a 20 cm square mould with a tight layer of biscuits, edge to edge. Break a few to fill the corners.
Spread a layer of cream with a spatula, even, right to the edges. Repeat biscuits then cream until you have five layers of biscuits, ending with the biscuits.
Cover with clingfilm and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours, preferably overnight. The biscuit should have taken on a cake-like texture.
Unmould. Pipe (deposit from a piping bag) the reserved cream on top, scatter with dark chocolate shavings. Cut with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each slice.

title: Strawberry cheesecake verrines
intro: A no-bake cheesecake hinges on two things: a base that's still crunchy after a night in the fridge, and a filling firm enough to support the weight of the frosting.
ing: white chocolate ganache tinted with strawberry puree
titane: Dry-toast the biscuit crumbs in a titanium pan over medium heat before adding the melted butter. Cook for two to three minutes, stirring constantly: the heat dries the crumb, evaporates any remaining moisture, and releases the biscuit's caramel notes. This dehydration prevents the base from becoming soggy when it comes into contact with the cream. Remove from the heat and pour in the butter, stir, and immediately transfer to another container to stop the cooking process.
steps: Toast the crumbs in a pan, bind them with melted butter, then press them firmly into the bottom of six verrines using the back of a spoon. The base should be compact and of even thickness. Refrigerate while preparing the filling.
Whisk the cream cheese with the icing sugar and vanilla until perfectly smooth and grain-free. Do not over-whip, or the mixture will become runny.
Whip the heavy cream into soft peaks (it should hold its shape on the whisk but the peak should droop slightly). If it's too stiff, it will curdle when you fold it in.
Fold in the whipped cream in three stages, using a spatula and lifting the mixture from the bottom up. Add the diced strawberries at the end, with just two turns of the spatula.
Fill the verrines using a piping bag or a spoon, smoothing the surface. Leave half a centimeter free below the rim for the icing.
Pour the lukewarm, not hot, ganache into the glass in a thin, even layer. Tilt each glass slightly to spread it to the edges.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour 30 minutes. The filling should be firm to the touch and the glaze matte on the surface.

title: Soba noodles, crispy tofu and peanut sauce
intro: It all comes down to the tofu: pressed thoroughly, then seared without being disturbed, it retains a crisp crust even when placed on cold noodles.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the tofu is added. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, add the oil, place the cubes in a single layer, and then leave it alone. The tofu will stick at first, which is normal: it will release on its own once a crust has formed. If you try to remove it before then, you'll leave the crust in the pan.
steps: Press the tofu for 15 to 20 minutes between two cloths, under a weight. Cut it into 2 cm cubes, then coat them with cornstarch, crushed pepper and a drizzle of grapeseed oil.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in the remaining oil: it should ripple slightly.

Place the cubes in a single layer, without crowding them. Let them brown without touching them. As soon as they detach on their own, turn them face by face and reduce to medium heat. Allow 10 to 12 minutes in total, for golden and dry-to-the-touch faces.
Remove the tofu from the pan and set it aside on a warm plate.
Bring 1 litre of water to the boil in a medium saucepan.
Cook the soba noodles for 1 to 2 minutes. Drain them, rinse them under cold water until they are completely cooled, then let them drain.
In the same boiling water, cook the edamame for 5 minutes. Drain.

Peel the garlic cloves before mincing them, then whisk the peanut butter with the soy sauce, sesame oil, chilli flakes, garlic and water. Add the water in small touches until you have a smooth and coating sauce.
Prepare the vegetables: cucumber cut into dice, spring onion and coriander finely chopped, cabbage grated, rinsed and well drained.
Mix the cold noodles with the cabbage, cucumber, edamame, spring onion, coriander and three quarters of the sauce.
Divide among the plates, place the tofu on top, drizzle with the remaining sauce, then finish with the crushed peanuts and sesame seeds.

title: Chocolate-banana skillet brownies
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the bananas: they should be very speckled, almost black, otherwise the paste lacks sugar and flavor.
titane: The pan replaces the mold. The dough cooks covered over low to medium heat, which allows the heat to rise from the sides as well as the bottom, preventing the dry crust of a conventional oven. A few minutes in the oven to finish sets the center. The result: crisp edges and a soft, melt-in-your-mouth center.
steps: Plan ahead: the brownie must cool and rest in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight, before serving.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Blend together bananas, cottage cheese, eggs, maple syrup, cocoa, baking powder and salt until you obtain a perfectly smooth batter with no visible cheese grains.
Generously oil the titanium pan, bottom and sides, with grapeseed oil. Pour in the batter and smooth the surface.

Place on medium-low heat, cover and cook for 35 minutes. Lift the lid only halfway through: the edges should be set, the centre still slightly trembling. A knife inserted into the centre should come out almost clean.
If the top remains wet, place the pan (oven-safe, handle included) in the oven for 5 to 7 minutes at 180 °C. The centre sets without the edges drying out.
Loosen the edges with a spatula, turn out onto a wire rack and let cool completely. Then refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight: this is when the texture becomes dense and melting.
Cut into 12 squares. Sprinkle with shredded coconut when serving.

title: Ice cream made with ube without an ice cream maker
intro: Three ingredients, no cooking: it all comes down to the amount of air you trap in the cream, because that alone will prevent crystals from forming in the freezer.
titane: No need for heat here, but the same principle applies as for searing: the starting temperature is key. Place the mixing bowl and whisk in the freezer for twenty minutes before you begin. Cream at 4°C in a cold container will expand (rise by trapping air) almost twice as much as lukewarm cream, and it's this increased volume that gives you a smooth, creamy ice cream without churning.
steps: Plan ahead: the ice cream freezes for at least 6 hours, ideally overnight, start the day before.
Pour the cream into the chilled bowl. Whisk at medium then high speed until it holds on the whisk and forms a soft peak. Stop here: overwhipped cream becomes grainy and will release water.
Add the salt to the sweetened condensed milk, then pour one third of this mixture onto the cream. Loosen with a spatula to even out the textures.

Incorporate the remaining condensed milk in two stages, using upward folding motions while turning the bowl a quarter turn with each pass. The goal is to preserve the volume, not to achieve a perfectly smooth mixture in three seconds.

Add the ube extract. Mix until the purple is uniform, without any clear streaks. If you are using powder, dilute it first in 2 tablespoons of cream to avoid lumps; the colour will be more matte and more earthy.

Transfer to a shallow container, smooth the surface, cover with plastic wrap directly on the mixture. Freeze for at least 6 hours, ideally overnight, until it reaches a firm texture that slightly resists the spoon.
Remove the container 5 minutes before serving, then form the scoops with a spoon dipped in hot water.

title: Raw brownie bars, cranberry-orange compote
intro: A dense, uncooked base and a tangy compote reduced in the same pan: it all comes down to the firmness of the pressing and the degree of reduction of the cranberries.
ing: cooked and mashed sweet potato or butternut squash

ing.note: adjust according to the acidity of the fruit

titane: The cold pan serves as a mold: the base is pressed directly into the bottom, without grease or parchment paper. Once rinsed, the same pan is placed on the stovetop for the compote. Its rapid temperature rise shortens the reduction time, so keep an eye on it from the eighth minute onward.
steps: Plan ahead: the base cools for 30 minutes then the whole assembly sets for at least 2 hours in the refrigerator; allow extra time.

In a bowl, combine the coconut flour, cocoa, nut butter, maple syrup, cooked sweet potato or butternut squash puree that you have mashed, and salt. Work with a spatula until you obtain a homogeneous and supple dough that holds together when you press it between your fingers.

Pour the dough into the cold titanium pan. Press down firmly with the back of a spoon or the palm of your hand, working from the center toward the edges, to achieve an even thickness. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Unmold the cooled base onto a plate or a square mold lined with parchment. Rinse and dry the pan.

Return the pan to medium heat with the cranberries, water, maple syrup, orange juice, zest, and cinnamon. Allow 10 minutes: the fruits should burst and the preparation should coat the spoon (the mixture holds on the back of the spoon without running off immediately).
Off the heat, fold in the chia seeds. Let thicken for 5 minutes in the pan, stirring once.
Spread the warm compote over the base. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until the whole is firm, then cut into bars with a blade dipped in hot water.

title: Chocolate-banana cottage cheese ice cream
intro: An ice cream without an ice cream maker where everything depends on one point: the mixture must be perfectly smooth before going into the freezer, otherwise the cottage cheese remains grainy when served.
titane: No pan here, and that's intentional: the recipe is entirely cold-processed. The decisive step takes place in the blender. Blend longer than necessary, two to three full minutes, scraping down the sides once. The goal is to eliminate the graininess of the cream cheese and aerate the mixture (incorporating air, which lightens the texture and reduces crystals). A mixture that feels warm to the touch when you take it out of the bowl is a good sign: it's been sufficiently blended.
steps: Plan ahead: the ice cream needs to freeze for 4 to 6 hours, or even a full night, before it can be served.
Peel the bananas and break them into chunks in the blender bowl.
Add the cottage cheese, maple syrup, sifted cocoa, protein powder if you are using it, and salt.

Blend for two to three minutes at full power. Stop halfway through, scrape down the sides with a spatula, and resume. The mixture should be uniform, with no perceptible grains between the tongue and the palate.
Pour into a shallow, wide freezer container: the thinner the layer, the more even the freezing. Smooth the surface and cover it directly.
Freeze for 4 to 6 hours.
Remove the container 15 to 20 minutes before serving. After a full night in the freezer, allow 30 to 45 minutes.
Run the ice cream scoop under hot water, wipe it dry, form the scoops and serve immediately.

title: Peanut-chocolate bites
intro: Everything depends on the firmness of the dough before coating: if it's too soft, it won't absorb the chocolate shell.
titane: The pan becomes a bain-marie. A simmering water bath, a bowl placed on top without touching the water: the even diffusion of titanium melts the chocolate without hot spots, therefore without graininess (chocolate separating and becoming grainy). The result is a smooth and shiny shell.
steps: Combine the peanut powder and apple puree in a bowl. Work the mixture by hand until you have a smooth, firm dough that no longer sticks to your fingers. If it remains sticky, add a spoonful of powder.
Divide into 12 equal portions. Roll each into a ball between your palms.
Place the balls on a plate and refrigerate for 15 minutes. Do not skip this step: on warm dough, the chocolate will slide off instead of sticking.

Pour the water into the pan and bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. Place a heatproof bowl on top, making sure it doesn't touch the water. Melt the chocolate in the bowl, stirring gently, for about 3 minutes, until completely smooth. Keep the heat low.
Dip each cold ball in the chocolate, turn it over with a fork, then tap the handle against the edge of the bowl to remove the excess.
Remove from the work container and place on a sheet of baking paper. Let set for 10 minutes, until the shell is firm to the touch.

title: No-bake peanut butter oatmeal cookies
intro: It all comes down to the boiling of the syrup: one minute too long and the cookies become crumbly, one minute less and they will never set.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan for the butter-sugar-milk syrup. The volume remains under 500 ml, the large surface heats up quickly and evenly, and the sugar has fewer points of sticking. It boils in less than a minute, and the mixture remains smooth. The peanut butter and vanilla are then incorporated in the same pan: just one pan on the stove.
steps: Plan ahead: the cookies need approximately 1 hour at room temperature before refrigeration; factor this time into your schedule.
Mix the oat flakes and salt in a large mixing bowl. Set aside.
Combine the butter, sugar, and milk in the titanium pan. Heat over medium-high heat, whisking continuously: the whisk prevents the sugar from sticking to the bottom.
Bring to a rolling boil — small bubbles regularly across the entire surface — and time exactly 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Add the peanut butter and vanilla to the still-hot pan. Whisk until you obtain a perfectly smooth and glossy mixture.
Pour the hot mixture over the oat flakes. Mix with a spatula until no dry flakes remain. Work quickly, as the mass sets as it cools.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper using a cookie scoop. Space them slightly apart.
Let set at room temperature for approximately 1 hour. Once the surface is dry to the touch, transfer to the refrigerator in an airtight container.

title: Coffee jelly and cheesecake verrines
intro: It's all about the contrast: a bold, barely sweet coffee jelly placed on a soft and airy cream.
titane: Crumble the biscuits directly in the titanium pan (using the "sanding" method means working the flour with the butter until you get a damp, sandy texture). Over medium heat, melt the butter, add the crumbs, and cook for two to three minutes, stirring constantly. The crumbs will dry out, toast, and retain their crispness under the cream instead of becoming soggy after an hour. Transfer the mixture from the pan immediately to a cold plate: the titanium base retains heat and would continue to cook.
steps: Plan ahead: the coffee jelly and assembled verrines must chill in the refrigerator for at least three hours total; start well in advance.

Dissolve the gelatin and sugar in hot coffee, off the heat, whisking until the liquid is perfectly smooth and free of grains. With agar-agar, bring the coffee to a simmer for thirty seconds before removing it from the heat.
Pour into a shallow dish to a depth of one centimetre. Refrigerate for at least two hours, until the surface is firm and shiny to the touch.
Cut the jelly into regular cubes of one centimetre, using the tip of a thin knife wiped between each cut. Sharp edges catch the light in the glass.
Toast the biscuit crumbs with butter in the titanium pan, then allow them to cool completely.
Distribute the crumb base at the bottom of the verrines and press with the back of a spoon. An even layer, not too compact.
Whisk the cream cheese with icing sugar and vanilla until you obtain a smooth texture, without any lumps.

Whip the cold cream to stiff peaks, then fold it into the mixture in three batches using a spatula (flexible scraper), lifting the mixture from the bottom to the top. Stop as soon as the mixture is uniform.
Pipe the cream onto the crumb base, smooth it, then top with jelly cubes. Set aside a few to insert halfway up.
Refrigerate for one hour. Dust with cocoa using a sieve just before serving, not before: it would absorb moisture and dull the appearance.

title: Chocolate, seed and sesame crunch
intro: It all comes down to thickness: the thinner the layer of seeds in the pan, the crispier the crunch.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the chocolate

titane: The titanium pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty, it toasts (dry-roasts to develop the aromas) the seeds evenly in fifteen minutes, without added fat or a baking sheet. To check if it's cooked, loosen an edge with a spatula: when the layer of seeds detaches easily and shows an amber color underneath, it's ready. The glaze is applied and the mixture is set in the same pan.
steps: Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. It must be evenly heated before adding the mixture.
In a bowl, combine seeds, cashews, coconut, maple syrup, coconut oil and tahini. Mix until each seed is coated.
Pour the mixture into the hot pan. Press down with a spatula to spread it in a thin, even layer over the entire surface.

Reduce heat to medium-low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes. Every 4 to 5 minutes, gently loosen the edges and check the color. The mixture is ready when it is golden brown and easily pulls away from the sides of the pan.
Meanwhile, melt the chocolate in a double boiler over low heat. If it remains thick, add half a teaspoon of coconut oil to thin it out.
Remove the pan from the heat. Coat the crisp with melted chocolate and smooth with a spatula to cover the entire surface. Sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Allow to cool to room temperature in the pan, then refrigerate for at least 15 minutes, until the chocolate sets.
Remove from the mold in one piece and break into irregular pieces.

title: Carlota at the cafe
intro: Everything hinges on the cold night: the biscuits absorb the cream and become a cake, provided the cream is liquid enough to pass through them.

ing.note: taken out of the cold an hour before

titane: Before assembling, dry-fry the biscuits in a titanium pan over medium-low heat for one minute per side, without any oil or butter. This awakens the buttery flavor of the biscuits, bringing out their toasted cereal notes and standing up to the coffee. Let them cool completely on a wire rack: a warm biscuit will soften too quickly and the coating will collapse.
steps: Plan ahead: the carlota must chill for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight; start in advance.
Remove the cream cheese from the cold 1 hour before you start, so it is soft when mixing.
Toast the biscuits in a pan as indicated above. Set them aside on a flat surface, well cooled.
Mix the cream cheese alone for a few seconds, until it is perfectly soft. It will create lumps if added cold.
Pour in the sweetened condensed milk, evaporated milk and well-chilled coffee. Mix until smooth, fluid cream that coats a spoon without sticking.
Line the bottom of the dish (coat it with an even layer) with two good spoonfuls of cream. This first layer prevents the biscuits at the bottom from drying out.
Arrange a layer of biscuits edge to edge, breaking the last ones to fill the gaps.
Alternate cream and biscuits until the top of the dish. Finish with the cream, smoothed with a spatula.
Cover with plastic film in direct contact and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, preferably overnight. The biscuits should cut with a spoon without resistance.
When serving, dust cocoa over the entire surface and sprinkle with chocolate shavings. Serve very cold, in square portions.

title: Cold chocolate biscuit cake with milk ganache
intro: It all depends on how well the cream holds up: if it's not whipped enough, it collapses; if it's whipped too much, it curdles; and prolonged cold does the rest of the work.
ing: scoops of instant vanilla pudding mix
titane: No cooking required here, but the ganache deserves better than the microwave. Place a titanium pan over very low heat, turn off the heat as soon as it's lukewarm, and pour in the cream and chopped chocolate. The pan's residual heat will melt the chocolate without ever burning it. Stir in the center, using small circles, until the mixture is smooth and glossy.
steps: Break the biscuits by hand into medium-sized pieces. Keep some irregular shards: they will add texture when cut. Set aside.
Combine the very cold cream, cream cheese, pudding mix, icing sugar and vanilla in the bowl of a mixer.

Whisk for two minutes at low speed until the mixture is homogeneous, then gradually increase the speed. Stop as soon as the cream is firm, smooth, and airy, and holds its shape on the whisk without falling off. Do not over-whip (do not work it until it becomes grainy): it will become grainy.
Incorporate the biscuit pieces with a spatula, lifting the mixture from the bottom to the top. Stop as soon as they are distributed.
Pour into a round, square or rectangular mold. Tap the bottom on the work surface to remove air pockets, then smooth the surface.
Refrigerate for 6 to 12 hours, ideally overnight. It must be completely set: a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Prepare the ganache as described above, then let it cool until it coats the back of a spoon and leaves a clear trace on the finger.
Pour it over the completely cold cake and spread it in one smooth motion, from the center to the edges.
Chill for 30 minutes. Slice with a knife that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry between each slice. Serve very cold.

title: Chocolate-mint verrines, brownie crumbs
intro: It all comes down to temperature: a lukewarm pudding would melt the whipped cream and turn the mint green gray.
titane: The pudding cooks directly in the pan, without a saucepan. The heat spreads quickly and evenly across the entire surface, so there are no hot spots where the cocoa would stick to the bottom. Whisk flat, sweeping the edges.
steps: Plan ahead: the verrines should rest for at least one hour in the cold before serving.
Pour the milk, cocoa, 40 g sugar and cornstarch into the pan while still cold. Whisk until completely dissolved before turning on the heat: this prevents lumps from forming.

Heat over medium heat while whisking continuously, approximately 8 minutes. The mixture thickens suddenly at the end. Stop when it coats the back of a spoon and the imprint of your finger holds clearly.
Divide the hot pudding into three verrines. Leave to cool to room temperature, then place in the cold. The surface must be noticeably cold to the touch before proceeding.
Crumble the brownies between your fingers, keeping irregular pieces. Grate the dark chocolate into shavings.
Whip the cream (whisk it to incorporate air until it holds) with 2 tablespoons sugar, mint extract and food colouring. Stop as soon as the whisk leaves a firm trail.
Place the brownie crumbs on the cold pudding, then the chocolate shavings.
Pipe the mint whipped cream in a spiral on top, starting from the edge towards the centre.
Refrigerate until serving, 1 hour minimum.

title: Chocolate, coconut and pecan cheesecake
intro: Everything hinges on two temperatures: a gently cooked mixture so that it remains creamy in the center, and a glaze brought to a coating consistency without ever exceeding a simmer.
titane: The coconut-pecan glaze is best cooked in a wide skillet rather than a tall saucepan. The larger surface area distributes the heat more evenly and allows you to watch the glaze thicken. Stir constantly with a flexible spatula, scraping the bottom and sides of the pan. As soon as the glaze coats the back of the pan (it will coat the spatula and leave a fingerprint), remove it from the heat: the egg yolks will continue to coagulate for a few more seconds from the residual heat of the pan. Once off the heat, spread the glaze onto a cold baking sheet to stop the cooking process immediately.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake cools and then rests in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight; start the day before.
