Blend the whole cookies, including the filling, until you obtain fine, even crumbs.
Pour the melted butter over the crumbs and mix until the mixture holds together when pressed in your hand.
Press firmly onto the bottom and sides of a 23 cm springform pan. Use the bottom of a glass to compact the base.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes while the butter sets.
Preheat the oven to 163 °C.
Whisk the cream cheese alone until it is perfectly smooth with no lumps. Scrape the sides of the bowl.

Incorporate the sour cream, sugar, then the eggs and egg yolk one at a time, the vanilla, and finally the cooled melted chocolate. Work at low speed: too much air causes the mixture to puff up during baking, then crack as it cools.
Pour into the pan over the cold crust. Tap the pan twice on the work surface to release air bubbles.
Bake for 60 minutes. The edges should be set, the center still slightly jiggly over a 5 cm disc.
Remove and let come to room temperature, 1 hour, oven off with the door slightly ajar if possible.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight.

In a saucepan, combine the condensed milk, brown sugar, butter and egg yolks. Cook over medium-low heat while stirring constantly until the cream coats the back of a spoon, 8 to 10 minutes. Do not boil.
Off the heat, stir in the vanilla.
Let cool to room temperature: the cream will thicken further.
Mix in the pecans and coconut.
Unmold the well-chilled cheesecake, then coat it with the glaze in a thick, uneven layer. If it is still warm, the glaze will slide off.
Slice with a blade dipped in hot water and wiped between each slice.

title: Apple and almond muffins with date caramel
intro: A gluten-free dough holds together thanks to its fat and moisture content: the compote and olive oil do all the work here, and the date caramel is blended during cooking.
titane: Mix the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with about twenty turns of a spatula, no more, then scrape down the sides of the bowl to bring the dough back to the center and stop. Almond flour doesn't develop gluten, but it releases its oil if overworked: the crumb becomes dense and greasy instead of remaining soft.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line a muffin tin with ten paper cases.
Peel the apple, then cut it into small cubes.
Whisk the eggs in a large bowl until foamy. Incorporate the compote, maple syrup and olive oil, then the apple cubes.
Add the almond flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, baking powder and salt. Mix with a spatula just until no flour is visible.
Distribute the batter into the cases, filling them three-quarters full. It does not spread on its own: smooth the top with the back of a spoon.
Bake in the centre of the oven for 23 to 25 minutes. A toothpick inserted in the centre should come out clean, with no raw batter.
Meanwhile, blend the dates, almond butter, coconut milk and salt until you obtain a smooth cream. If the dates are dry, soak them for ten minutes in hot water before blending.
Leave the muffins to rest for 5 minutes in the tin, then turn them out (remove them from their baking container) onto a wire rack. Wait for complete cooling before coating with date caramel.

title: Pumpkin, peanut and dark chocolate truffles
intro: It's all about the temperature: a really cold dough, a barely warm chocolate, and the coating sets cleanly instead of running.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Placed directly over very low heat, it melts the chocolate in one to two minutes thanks to its rapid and even heat distribution. It then becomes the coating bath: you dip the truffles in it, drain them on top, nothing else to get out of the cupboard. Keep a close eye on the pan; the chocolate will melt quickly.
steps: Plan ahead: the truffles spend 30 minutes in the freezer before coating.
Combine in a bowl the pumpkin puree, peanut butter, maple syrup, cinnamon, vanilla and salt. Mix until homogeneous.

Add the almond flour. Work with a spatula until you obtain a thick paste that holds together and no longer sticks to the sides. If it remains soft, add 10 g of almond flour and wait two minutes before judging.
Scoop the equivalent of a tablespoon, roll between your palms, place on a tray lined with parchment paper. You will obtain about a dozen balls.
Place the tray in the freezer for 30 minutes. The truffles must be firm to the touch: this is what will prevent them from falling apart in the hot chocolate.
Put the chocolate and coconut oil in the titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously with a flexible spatula. Stop as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy, in one to two minutes.
Remove from heat. Let cool for 2 to 3 minutes in the pan: the chocolate should thicken slightly while remaining runny.
Pierce each truffle on a fork, dip it in the chocolate, turn to coat, then let the excess drain above the pan. Return to the parchment paper.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes, until the coating is firm and matte to the touch.
Store the truffles in an airtight box in the refrigerator for up to a week, or freeze them flat on a baking sheet before transferring them to a closed box.

title: Frozen blueberry-yogurt bites with dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to the temperature difference: hard-centered bites, barely melted chocolate, and the coating sets in a second.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Preheated empty for one minute over low heat, it heats up quickly and retains its heat once removed from the heat: the chocolate melts without ever cooking. Its smooth surface then serves as a dipping basin; the frozen treats won't stick.
steps: Plan ahead: the bites freeze for 2 hours, factor in this time before serving.
Mix the blueberries and drained yogurt in a bowl. The fruit should be coated, not drowned.
Drop small spoonfuls onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, spacing them apart.
Place in the freezer for 2 hours, until the bites are firm and distinctly cold to the touch.

Preheat the titanium pan empty, over low heat, for 1 minute. Off the heat, pour in the chocolate broken into pieces and the coconut oil. Stir continuously: the residual heat is enough, the chocolate should become smooth and glossy in about 3 minutes. If the melting stalls, place the pan back on the turned-off heat or on a very low burner, for a few seconds only.

Remove the bites from the freezer and dip them one by one in the chocolate, directly in the pan. A quick dip is enough: the coating sets within seconds on contact with the cold. Place them back on the parchment paper.
Serve immediately, or return to the freezer for 5 minutes if you want to find a well-frozen center.

title: Whipped white chocolate ganache
intro: It all happens in two stages: a strong hot emulsion, then a long enough cold rest so that the fat crystallizes and holds up to the whisk.
titane: The frying pan replaces the saucepan for heating the 100g of cream. The heat rises quickly and evenly, without hot spots or sticking to the bottom: you turn off the heat at a simmer, not at a boil, and the cream reaches the chocolate at the right temperature without having reduced.
steps: Finely chop the white chocolate and place it in a heatproof bowl. The more uniform the pieces, the more evenly it will melt.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 1 minute over low-medium heat. Pour in the 100g of cream and heat for about 2 minutes, until it just begins to simmer: small bubbles at the edge, no boiling.
Immediately pour the hot cream over the chocolate. Let it sit for 2 to 3 minutes without touching it, allowing the heat to penetrate the pieces.
Whisk from the center, using small circles, gradually widening the circles. You are looking for a smooth and glossy mixture, without any graininess.
Add the cold cream, whisking until fully incorporated. The mixture should be smooth and perfectly homogeneous.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, ideally overnight. This resting period is what makes the ganache whippable.
Whisk with an electric mixer at medium speed until the mixture lightens in color and forms stiff peaks. Stop as soon as the texture holds: beyond that point, it will become grainy.
Transfer to a piping bag and pipe onto entremets, cupcakes or tarts.

title: Oatmeal blended with raspberries
intro: It all comes down to the hydration of the seeds: chia and flax must swell before blending, otherwise the preparation remains grainy and falls apart when chilled.
ing: soy milk or other plant-based milk
titane: Blend the chia and flax seeds with the plant-based milk in a blender and let it sit for five minutes before adding the remaining ingredients. The seeds release their mucilage (a natural gel that forms upon contact with liquid), which gives the mixture its creamy texture, without the need for thickeners or cooking.
steps: Pour two cups of plant-based milk into the blender, add chia seeds and flax seeds. Let rest for five minutes.
Add oats, raspberries, Greek yogurt, cinnamon and dates.
Blend using short pulses first, then continuously, until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous texture. If the blender struggles, add one tablespoon of milk, no more: the preparation must remain thick.
Divide between two bowls or two jars. Garnish with whole raspberries, refrigerate, then serve well chilled.

title: Sweet potato ice cream, cheesecake and maple
intro: Ice cream without an ice cream maker either holds or collapses on one point: the whipped cream must remain airy when the base is incorporated, otherwise the mixture sets into a hard block in the freezer.
ing: crushed pine nuts or pecan nuts
titane: The titanium pan is used only once, at the end, and it's irreplaceable: heated empty for one minute, it dry-roasts the nuts in two or three minutes, without any oil, resulting in a more even color and a more pronounced aroma than in the oven. Don't touch the nuts until they've started to turn golden; if stirred too soon, they'll stick.
steps: Plan ahead: the ice cream must be frozen for at least 6 hours, ideally a full night.
Blend the sweet potato purée with the cream cheese, maple syrup, vanilla, cinnamon and nutmeg. Stop as soon as the texture is perfectly smooth, without any graininess.
Whip the cold cream until soft peaks form (the whisk leaves a trail that gently falls back). Don't go further: cream that is too stiff produces grainy ice cream.
Fold the sweet potato base into the cream in three additions, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from bottom to top. Stop as soon as it is homogeneous.
Pour into a loaf pan, alternating layers with diced cheesecake and crumbled biscuits. Run the tip of a knife in a spiral pattern, two passes maximum, no more.
Cover with cling film and place in the freezer for a minimum of 6 hours, preferably overnight. The ice cream must be firm when pressed with your finger.

When ready to serve, heat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over medium heat. Add the pine nuts or pecans and leave them untouched until the first golden spots appear, then stir for 2 minutes. Transfer immediately to a cold plate (remove from the pan): residual heat would burn them.
Form scoops in bowls that have been chilled in the refrigerator for ten minutes, drizzle with a thin stream of maple syrup and sprinkle with warm nuts.

title: Dark chocolate mousse
intro: It's all about the temperature: a lukewarm chocolate mixture, a very cold cream, and you get a mousse that is dense in taste but light in the mouth.

ing.note: very cold (120 ml for melting, 240 ml for

titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. It heats up instantly: over very low heat, the chocolate and cream melt in just a few minutes. The lack of a coating makes the surface completely neutral, so nothing sticks as long as you stir continuously. As soon as the mixture is smooth, transfer it from the pan to a cold bowl: the pan retains heat and would continue to warm the chocolate.
steps: Plan ahead: the mousse must rest for at least 4 hours in the refrigerator; allow for this time before serving.
Place a bowl and the whisks in the refrigerator 15 minutes before you begin. Cream whips poorly above 6 °C.

In the titanium pan, combine the chopped chocolate and 120 ml of cream. Heat over very low heat, stirring constantly with a spatula, 3 to 5 minutes, until the mixture is smooth and glossy. Remove from heat and pour immediately into a bowl. Let cool until the mixture is just slightly warmer than body temperature.

In the cold bowl, whisk the remaining 240 ml of cream with the sugar, vanilla and salt until soft peaks form (the cream forms a soft peak that droops when you lift the whisk). Stop there: overwhipped cream would make the mousse grainy.
Fold one third of the whipped cream into the cooled chocolate by mixing firmly. This first addition is meant to loosen the mixture, not to lighten it.

Add the rest in two additions, this time using a folding motion (scooping from bottom to top with a spatula, rotating the bowl a quarter turn with each stroke). Stop as soon as the colour is uniform, not a second longer.
Divide among four glasses or ramekins. Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, until the texture is firm enough to hold on a spoon.
Just before serving, garnish with chocolate shavings, a quenelle of whipped cream or red berries.

title: Açaí bowl with frozen fruit
intro: It all comes down to the amount of liquid: too little, the blender struggles; too much, the bowl becomes a drink.

ing.note: (reduce by half for a softer profile)

titane: Pour the liquid last, along the side of the bowl, and set aside 30 ml. First, pulse the blender to break up the frozen fruit, then increase to a continuous speed. If the blade spins freely, stop, scrape down the sides, and add just a spoonful of the reserved liquid. The perfect consistency should hold its shape on an inverted spoon for three seconds.
steps: Run the açaï packet under cold water for a few seconds, then break it into pieces between your hands before opening it. It will blend without straining the blade.
Place the mango, berries and açaï in the blender bowl. Pour 70 ml of coconut water along the side of the bowl.

Blend using short pulses until the large pieces disappear, then continuously for about 2 minutes, gradually increasing the speed. Add the remaining liquid one spoonful at a time, only if the mixture stops moving, until you obtain a thick and smooth texture.
Transfer to a cold bowl, taken out of the refrigerator ten minutes earlier. Smooth the surface with the back of the spoon.

Peel the banana, then slice the strawberries and banana into rounds. Arrange them in parallel bands, add the blueberries, passion fruit pulp, then the granola and hemp seeds at the last moment so they stay crispy. Serve immediately.

title: Seed and dark chocolate bites
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the dough: pressed enough to hold its shape when cut, oily enough to remain melt-in-your-mouth under the chocolate.
titane: No double boiler required. Preheat the empty titanium pan for one minute over low heat, remove it from the heat, then add the chopped chocolate. The metal mass provides gentle, even heat, enough to melt the chocolate without it becoming grainy. The bare, uncoated surface is non-stick: simply stir, dip, and rinse with hot water.
steps: Plan ahead: the block goes into the freezer for 1 hour, then the bites go into the refrigerator for 15 minutes after coating.
Line (cover with parchment paper) a small rectangular mold, leaving the paper overhanging on two sides.

Process in a food processor the pumpkin seeds, hemp seeds, pitted dates, softened coconut oil, cardamom and salt. Stop as soon as the paste clumps between your fingers: it should stick without being smooth.
Pour into the mold. Press firmly with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass, to an even thickness of about 2 cm. Smooth the top.
Place in the freezer for 1 hour, until the block is firm to the touch.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over low heat. Remove from heat, add the chopped chocolate and coconut oil. Stir continuously with a spatula. Allow 3 minutes: the chocolate should be smooth and glossy, never hot to the touch.
Unmold the block by pulling the paper. Cut it into 12 rectangles, blade rinsed in hot water and wiped between each cut.
Dip each bite into the chocolate, directly in the pan off the heat. Drain against the edge, place on a sheet lined with parchment paper.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes. The chocolate should snap cleanly between your teeth.
Drizzle with remaining chocolate, sprinkle with hemp seeds before it completely sets.
Keep in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week, or in the freezer for up to three months.

title: Cranberry and pomegranate salsa
intro: A raw salsa where the crisp acidity of the cranberry holds all the balance: the sweetness of the pomegranate molasses is there to round it out, not to cover it.
ing: The juice of half a lime

ing.note: plus a little something for the finishing touch

titane: Before chopping, toss a handful of cranberries into a very hot, dry titanium pan (no oil needed). Let them sizzle for thirty seconds, just until they split and brown. Transfer them to a cold plate (remove them from the pan to stop the cooking process), then stir them in at the end. You'll have two cranberry textures in the same bowl: crisp and crunchy, and meltingly tender.
steps: Rinse the cranberries and dry them. Cut the green onions into pieces, halve the jalapeño and remove the seeds and white ribs.

Combine the cranberries, cilantro, green onions, jalapeño, and garlic in a food processor bowl. Pulse five to six times: you want a coarse, even chop, definitely not a purée. Chop each ingredient separately with a knife, then combine them.
Transfer to a salad bowl. Add the pomegranate molasses, lime juice, and salt. Mix well.
Taste it. If the acidity dominates, add a spoonful of molasses; if it thickens in the mouth, add more lime.
Incorporate the pomegranate arils with a spatula, lifting the mass so as not to crush them.
Let it rest for 15 minutes in the fridge before serving: the salt makes the cranberries release their juices and the mixture binds itself.
Serve chilled in a bowl, garnished with extra arils. Leftovers will keep for 7 to 10 days in an airtight container in the refrigerator, as the acidity acts as a preservative.

title: Nut and seed discs, chocolate finish
intro: It all comes down to the thickness of the patties: thin and well packed, they take on a golden crust in the pan and keep a soft center, without ever going in the oven.

ing.note: (It can withstand higher heat without burning)

titane: The titanium pan acts like an oven floor. Preheated empty, it provides direct heat that caramelizes the seeds on contact and forms a crust beneath the egg. The lid traps the egg's moisture and cooks the center from above. Don't touch anything during the first cooking time: the egg will release itself once the crust is set. If you force it with a spatula beforehand, it will fall apart.
steps: Combine the almonds, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, cashews, sesame seeds and cranberries in a bowl. Mix to distribute the cranberries evenly.

Crack the egg on top. Work with a spatula until the mixture becomes sticky and holds its shape when you press it in your hand. If the mixture remains dry, let it rest for 5 minutes: the seeds will absorb the liquid and the mixture will bind together.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush it with a thin layer of clarified butter.
Shape into round patties about 7 cm in diameter and 7 mm thick, firmly pressed between your palms. Place them directly into the hot pan, without packing them tightly together.
Cover and reduce the heat to low-medium. Let it cook for 7 to 8 minutes without touching it. The patty is ready to be flipped when it easily releases from the pan and the bottom is golden brown.
Gently flip with a thin spatula. Continue covered for 4 minutes to brown the second side.
Remove from the pan to stop the cooking process and place on a wire rack. Let cool completely: the patties harden as they cool, which is when they become crispy.
Drizzle melted chocolate over the top in thin zigzags. Let it set at room temperature.

title: Baked oats, banana and speculoos
intro: Everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas: when they are very speckled, they sweeten and bind the mixture on their own; the syrup only adds to it.
titane: Before mixing, toast (dry-heat to develop the aromas) the oat flakes for two to three minutes in the titanium pan over medium heat, stirring constantly. The coating will heat up quickly and evenly: the flakes will turn a uniform hazelnut color without sticking. Immediately transfer them to a cold bowl, otherwise the residual heat will make them bitter.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C. Line (cover the sides of) a baking dish with baking paper.
Toast the oat flakes in a pan, then let them cool.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl until you have a smooth puree with no large pieces.
Add the cooled oats, protein powder, honey, milk, vanilla, yeast, chia seeds, and cinnamon. Mix until the powder is completely dissolved, with no lumps at the bottom of the bowl.
Pour into the dish and smooth the surface.
Sprinkle the crushed speculoos on top.
Bake for 38 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean; the top should remain soft to the touch but no longer sink in.
Let it cool for at least 20 minutes in the dish: it will hold its shape as it cools. Cut into portions.
Serve with a spoonful of yogurt and a drizzle of speculoos spread lightly softened in a bain-marie.

title: Chocolate cups with puffed quinoa
intro: Everything hinges on the crispness of the quinoa: if it is soft when the chocolate coats it, the bite is ruined.

ing.note: or 60g of raw quinoa to puff

ing: dark chocolate in pistoles or crushed
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and evenly: it steams the quinoa dry (without oil, the grain bursts from the heat alone) in fifteen seconds without sticking. The same pan, cleaned and cooled, is then filled with simmering water to create a bain-marie. One pan, from raw grain to molded bite.
steps: Line a mini-muffin tin with paper baking cups, or use a silicone mold. Keep it handy: the mixture sets quickly.

If you're puffing the quinoa yourself: Heat an empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the raw quinoa in a single layer, without any oil. Stir for 10 to 15 seconds, until the first bursts appear. Remove from the pan immediately as soon as the grains puff up; they will burn in a few seconds. Let cool.
Wipe the pan clean. Pour in a 1 cm layer of water, bring to a simmer over low heat, and place a bowl containing the chocolate on top. Stir continuously for 3 minutes, until perfectly smooth.
Remove the bowl, drain the water, and wipe the pan clean. Pour in the melted chocolate off the heat, stir in the almond butter, then the puffed quinoa. Mix until each grain is coated.
Divide the mixture among the molds, fill to the brim, and press down with the back of a spoon. Sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Place in the refrigerator for 30 minutes, or in the freezer for 15 minutes, until the chocolate is firm to the touch.
Remove from the mold and store in an airtight container: two weeks in the refrigerator, three months in the freezer.

title: Orange-vanilla salad with mandarins
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the gelatin when you work with it: too hot, it liquefies the cream; too set, it forms lumps that are impossible to fix.

ing.note: drained (two cans), including a small handful
plus ¼ cup reserved for finishing

titane: No frying pan here; the titanium one stays in the cupboard. The technique is to fold it in with a flexible spatula: cut the mixture vertically, slide it under the mixture, and then fold it back towards you while turning the bowl a quarter turn. Six to eight movements, no more. Each extra turn forces the air out of the whipped cream, and you end up with a flat salad instead of a mousse.
steps: Plan ahead: the salad must rest for at least 2 hours in the cold, preferably overnight; start in advance.
Pour the boiling water over the orange gelatin powder. Whisk until completely dissolved: there must not be a single grain grinding against the bowl walls.
Add the cold water, mix, then place in the refrigerator for 15 minutes. The preparation should thicken slightly without setting, to the consistency of a cold syrup.

Remove the bowl, sprinkle the vanilla custard powder over the surface and whisk vigorously for 1 minute. Cover with cling film and refrigerate for 20 minutes. The mixture becomes opaque and holds on a spoon.
Drain the mandarins carefully, then spread them out for a few minutes on paper towels: the residual water loosens the cream.
Fold the whipped cream in with a spatula, in three stages. Then add the mandarins and marshmallows, lifting the mixture gently without crushing the segments.
Transfer to a serving dish or individual cups. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
When ready to serve, distribute the reserved mandarins and marshmallows over the top. The surface should be cold and firm to the touch.

title: Rolled log cake with bananas and shortbread cookies
intro: Everything depends on the moisture content of the biscuits: too dry, they break when rolled; too soaked, the log collapses.
titane: Crumble a handful of biscuits and toast them dry (without oil) in a titanium pan over medium heat for two minutes, stirring constantly. Transfer them to a cold plate. These toasted crumbs will serve as a coating, providing the crunch that a chilled assembly cannot achieve.
steps: Plan ahead: the log requires 30 minutes of resting then 1 to 2 hours of freezing, allow plenty of time.
Lay a large sheet of plastic wrap on the work surface.
Dip each biscuit for one second in the milk, no more. Line them up side by side on the film forming a regular rectangle, on two rows that overlap slightly.
Let rest for 30 minutes. The biscuits must be tender throughout, without crumbling under your finger.
Whip the dessert preparation with the cold milk until you obtain a firm and fluffy mixture, that holds on the whisk.
Spread the cream over the entire surface of the biscuits, in an even layer, leaving two centimetres free on the edge opposite you.
Peel the bananas and place them end to end along the entire length, in the centre of the rectangle.
Lift the film from the closest side and roll in one continuous motion, pulling tight to remove air. Seal the film like a bonbon at both ends.
Place in the freezer for 1 to 2 hours: the log must be firm under finger pressure, without being completely frozen.
Unroll the film, roll the log in the toasted crumbs and slice diagonally, passing the blade under hot water between each cut.

title: Crispy tofu bowl with gochujang
intro: It all comes down to the water content of the tofu: pressed and then crumbled, it develops a crust in the pan which the sauce glazes without softening it.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat before adding any oil. The rapid heating works like an air fryer: the tofu will stick at first, then release on its own once a crust has formed. This is the signal, the only one. If you move it before then, you'll tear off the crust. The same pan, simply wiped clean, will then be used to reduce the sauce.
steps: Drain the tofu, wrap it in absorbent paper and press it under a weight for 10 to 15 minutes. Change the paper if it becomes waterlogged.
Crumble the tofu roughly into irregular pieces. Drizzle with a little oil, mix, then sprinkle with cornstarch, salt, and pepper. Stir to coat without mashing.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Pour in a drizzle of grapeseed oil: it should ripple slightly.

Place the tofu in a single layer, without overcrowding the pan. Let it cook undisturbed until the pieces separate easily, then turn them over to brown all sides. Cook for a total of 12 minutes, reducing the heat to medium-high if it's browning too quickly.
Remove (transfer from the pan) the tofu into a bowl.
While searing, mix together in a bowl the gochujang, soy sauce, rice vinegar, maple syrup, garlic, lime juice, chili flakes, ginger and 2 tbsp of water.
Separately whisk the cornflour and 60 ml of water until you obtain a homogeneous white liquid, without any sediment.
Wipe the pan clean, pour in the sauce and heat over medium heat until it just begins to simmer.
Whisk in the slurry. Cook until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
Return the tofu to the pan, stir to coat, and simmer for 3 minutes over low-medium heat. The pieces should be evenly glossy.
Sauté the broccolini in the rinsed pan for 4 minutes over high heat. Arrange the rice, tofu, and vegetables on a plate, then sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.

title: Shredded tofu wrap with gochujang sauce
intro: It all comes down to two things: tofu pressed long enough to lose its water, and strips seared in a single layer that are not touched until they detach on their own.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: The titanium pan replaces the air fryer here. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then oil it: the dry heat accumulated in the metal immediately attacks the surface of the tofu and creates a crust. Wait until each strip releases easily before flipping it—if it resists, the crust hasn't formed. The same pan is then used to make the sauce and coat the tofu in it, without transferring it.
steps: Drain the tofu, wrap it in paper towels and place a weight on top. Leave it to press for 10 to 15 minutes until it releases its water.
Cut the pressed block into fine shreds using a vegetable peeler or grater. The more irregular the shreds, the more the texture will resemble shredded meat.
In a salad bowl, mix the shreds with smoked paprika, cumin, garlic and onion powder, pepper, chili and cornstarch. Stir until each shred is coated with a dry layer.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.

Spread the tofu in a single layer. Do not stir. Leave to sear for about 5 minutes, until the shreds release themselves and are golden, then flip them over and continue for 5 minutes. Work in two batches if the pan is full.
Transfer the tofu to a plate.

Lower the heat to medium. In the same pan, combine the gochujang, soy sauce, minced garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, honey and water. Stir for 2 to 3 minutes: the sauce should become smooth and coating, and the pan juices dissolve into it.
Return the tofu to the pan and mix for 2 minutes, until it is glossy and completely coated.
Meanwhile, peel the cucumber if needed, chop the lettuce and cucumber, drain the pickled turnips.
Spread the breads with garlic yogurt sauce, top with tofu, then with vegetables. Roll tightly and serve immediately.

title: Chocolate-granola cheesecake in a glass
intro: A no-bake dessert where everything hinges on texture: the cottage cheese must be blended until it completely loses its grain, otherwise the layers remain sandy.
titane: Dry-fry the granola in a titanium pan over medium heat for three minutes, without any oil or butter. Stir continuously. The flakes will turn a nutty color and release their aroma: this is what makes the difference between a decent topping and one that's truly crunchy. Transfer it immediately to a cold plate, otherwise the residual heat will continue to cook it and it will turn bitter.
steps: Blend the cottage cheese alone in a blender until perfectly smooth. Scrape down the sides once during the process.
Whisk in the 10g of vanilla mixture. Mix for thirty seconds: the mixture will thicken and become glossy. Refrigerate.
In a tall bowl, whisk the 28g of chocolate mix into the cold protein drink. Gradually sprinkle in the powder to avoid lumps.
Place this mixture in the refrigerator for 10 minutes, until it sets.
Blend it again with an immersion blender for a few seconds, until it has the texture of a dessert cream, without bubbles or lumps.
Toast the granola as described above, then let it cool completely.

Assemble the verrines: a layer of cheesecake mixture, a layer of chocolate, then a final layer of cheesecake. Use a piping bag or a spoon, placing the mixture in the center so that each layer spreads on its own.
Sprinkle with granola at the last moment and chill for 15 minutes before serving.

title: Granola and yogurt ice cream bars
intro: It's all about the texture: dry-roasted dried fruit for crunch, a yogurt mixture dense enough to hold up in the cold without crystallizing.
titane: Dry-roast the nuts and seeds in a titanium pan over medium heat, without oil. Stir continuously for 3 to 4 minutes, until the almonds are golden brown and the sesame seeds begin to pop. Remove from the pan (transfer immediately to a cold plate): the pan retains heat and would continue to cook the seeds. Let them cool completely before chopping, otherwise they will release moisture into the mold.
steps: Plan ahead: the bars need 1 hour 30 minutes in the freezer, allow for this time before serving.
Toast the nuts and seeds dry, let them cool, then chop them roughly with a knife. Keep irregular pieces: this is what gives texture.
Distribute the dried fruit in the impressions of a silicone bar mould, up to halfway. Press lightly with your fingertips.

Whisk the yogurt with the nut butter, maple syrup and vanilla until you have a smooth mixture with no streaks. Incorporate the instant coffee or cocoa depending on the version you choose. Taste and adjust the maple syrup.
Pour the mixture over the dried fruit and press lightly to coat them well. Tap the mould on the work surface to remove air bubbles, then smooth the surface with a spatula.
Place in the freezer for 1 hour 30 minutes, until the bars are firm in the centre. Unmould by turning the silicone inside out.
Remove the bars 10 minutes before serving: they should give under the knife without melting.

title: Tahini-sesame cookies
intro: A dough without egg or butter, held together by tahini alone: everything depends on the gentleness of the fire, which must cook the center before the sesame browns.

ing.note: for the pan and the glass

titane: The preheated pan browns the bottom in minutes, while the lid traps the heat and steams the top. It's like an oven replaced by two heat sources: the baking sheet in direct contact with the food and the hot air trapped above. Hence the low heat as soon as the cookies are in place.
steps: Combine the tahini, honey, flour, almond flour, cinnamon, and baking soda in a bowl. Mix with a spatula until you obtain a smooth, pliable dough that pulls away from the sides of the bowl.
Divide into 9 equal portions and roll them into balls between your palms.
Pour the sesame seeds into a shallow dish and roll each ball in it, pressing lightly so that the seeds adhere to the entire surface.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush it with a very thin film of grapeseed oil.
Place the balls, spacing them about three centimeters apart. Don't overcrowd the pan: two batches are better than one full pan, which cools down and cooks unevenly.
Oil the bottom of a glass and flatten each ball to about 1 cm thick.

Reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook for 14 minutes. Do not touch the cookies during this time; they will release from the pan on their own when the bottoms are set. The edges should be just golden, the bottoms amber.
Remove from the pan and place on a wire rack. Let cool for at least 10 minutes: the texture only sets upon cooling.

title: Banana and double chocolate muffins
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the bananas: the more discolored the peel, the less sugar you will need and the more moist the crumb will remain.
titane: Before mashing them, slice the bananas in half lengthwise and place them cut-side down in a dry titanium pan over medium heat. Two minutes is all it takes: the sugars caramelize, the water evaporates, and the flavor intensifies. Mash them while still warm with a fork. This is the crucial step that separates a decent banana muffin from a truly great one.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), fan-assisted. Line a twelve-cup muffin tin with paper baking cups.
Caramelize the bananas in a pan as described above, then roughly mash them in a large bowl. Let them cool slightly.
Add the eggs, milk, olive oil, yogurt, honey and vanilla. Whisk until smooth and homogeneous.
In a second bowl, mix the flour, sifted cocoa powder, baking soda, baking powder, and salt. Sifting the cocoa powder is essential: it forms lumps that won't separate later.

Pour the dry ingredients into the liquid ingredients. Mix with a spatula, in about fifteen movements, until the streaks of flour disappear. Stop there. Overmixing will result in dense, rubbery muffins.
Incorporate three-quarters of the chocolate chips, still using a spatula.
Divide the batter among the cupcake liners, filling them three-quarters full. Sprinkle the remaining chocolate chips on top.
Bake for 18 to 22 minutes. A knife inserted into the center should come out dry, except for a melted nugget.
Let it rest in the pan for 5 minutes, then remove it from the baking container and place it on a wire rack. Cooling on the rack prevents the base from becoming soggy.

title: Caramel apple ice cream cake
intro: A dessert without an oven, where everything depends on patience: the biscuits need to hydrate long enough to become soft like a ladyfinger biscuit.

ing.note: or 2 sachets mixed with 1 liter of milk

titane: Toast the graham crackers for two minutes in a dry, hot titanium pan, cast-iron side down, before stacking them. This releases the butter and honey, enhancing their aroma and making the layer easier to cut. Gently warm the caramel in the same pan, off the heat, so it drips without breaking the pudding.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake must rest for at least 6 hours in the refrigerator, preferably overnight; begin the day before.
Heat the titanium pan dry over medium heat. Toast the biscuits for two minutes in batches, without browning them, then remove them (take them out of the pan and set aside flat) on a rack.
Off the heat, pour the caramel syrup into the still-warm pan. Stir until it becomes fluid, then set aside.
Line the bottom of a rectangular dish with a layer of biscuits, edge to edge. Break some to fill any gaps.
Spread half of the apple filling, distributing the quarters evenly right to the corners.
Coat with (cover with a smooth and even layer of) half of the vanilla pudding. Smooth with an offset spatula.
Drizzle one-third of the warm caramel in thin lines over the entire surface.
Repeat: biscuits, apples, pudding, caramel. Finish with a layer of biscuits, the remaining caramel and fleur de sel.

Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours, preferably overnight. The dessert is ready when a knife blade passes through without resistance and the biscuits have lost their crispness.
Cut into square portions, using a knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Broccoli wrap patty
intro: Two ingredients, one pan: it's all about the thinness of the layer and the patience before turning.
ing: turns of the black pepper mill
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat before adding the oil. The heat will rise evenly across the entire surface: the pancake will develop a thin, even crust and release easily from the pan. There's no risk of tearing when flipping.
steps: Blend the broccoli, eggs, garlic and onion powders, salt and pepper until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture (ready-to-cook liquid mixture) with no visible pieces.
Heat the empty pan over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the avocado oil: it should ripple slightly without smoking.
Pour the mixture into the center and spread it into a thin disc using the back of a spoon, spiraling from the middle. Let it cook for 3 minutes without touching it.
Wait until the edges retract and peel away on their own. Then flip it over smoothly in one go.
Continue cooking for 2 minutes, until the pancake is firm to the touch. Transfer to a plate.
Fill and roll immediately, while the galette is still pliable.

title: Chocolate bars, yogurt mousse and red berries
intro: It all comes down to the texture: a well-packed oat base, a mousse firm enough to cut cleanly, and cold, lots of cold.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a mold from start to finish. You press the base into it, bake it at 180°C, let it cool inside, spread the mousse on top, and then freeze it. No transfer, therefore no cracked base.
steps: Plan ahead: the assembly chills in the freezer for 2 hours before cutting, plan this time before serving.
Preheat the oven to 180 °C. Line the bottom of the titanium pan with parchment paper, leaving two edges overhanging: they will serve as handles for unmolding.
Mash the bananas with a fork until you obtain a puree without lumps. Add the oat flakes, the 60 ml of cocoa and 1.5 tablespoons of maple syrup. Mix until the mixture is homogeneous and sticky.
Pour the batter into the pan and press it firmly with the back of a spoon or your palm, to a regular thickness. The more you compact it, the cleaner the cutting will be.
Bake for 22 minutes. The base must be set in the center and dry to the touch.
Remove the pan and let cool completely at room temperature, without unmolding. A warm base would cause the mousse to melt.
In a bowl, whisk the Greek yogurt with the 2 tablespoons of cocoa and 1 tablespoon of maple syrup until you obtain a smooth texture, without cocoa grains.

Fold in the cooled melted chocolate in three batches, using a spatula, lifting the mixture (motion from bottom to top, so as not to crush the mixture). It should be barely warm: if too hot, it liquefies the yogurt; if too cold, it sets in filaments.
Spread the mousse over the cold base, smooth it. Arrange the strawberry slices and blueberries in tight rows.
Place the pan in the freezer until the whole thing is firm to the touch, about 2 hours.
Lift the block by the parchment edges, place it on a board and cut into 9 bars with a knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut. Keep refrigerated, well chilled.

title: Speculoos and white chocolate truffles
intro: It all comes down to the fineness of the biscuit powder: if it's too coarse, the dough remains grainy and the balls crack when coated.

ing.note: cream cheese type, taken out 30 minutes in advance

titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Preheat it empty for 2 minutes, then reduce the heat to very low and place the white chocolate inside. The heat is evenly distributed, preventing hot spots: the chocolate melts without graining. The pan then serves as a draining tray for the coating, and you won't get anything else dirty.
steps: Mix the 250 g of biscuits until you obtain a fine, sandy powder (with no perceptible grit under your fingers).
Add the softened fresh cheese. Work with a spatula until you have a thick, homogeneous paste that pulls away from the sides of the bowl.

Use an ice cream scoop to portion out regular amounts. Roll them between your palms to obtain smooth balls. Place them on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Chill for 10 minutes in the refrigerator: they will hold up better when dipping.

Preheat the titanium pan dry for 2 minutes. Lower to very low heat, pour in the chopped white chocolate and stir continuously for 3 minutes, until it is smooth and fluid. Turn off the heat as soon as there are no more lumps.
Pierce each ball with a fork, dip it in the chocolate, then let the excess drain over the pan by tapping the handle. Place back on the parchment paper.
Drizzle with a line of caramel in a zigzag pattern using a piping bag. Crumble the remaining biscuits and sprinkle them on the truffles before the chocolate sets.
Refrigerate for 35 minutes, until the coating is set and crispy when bitten.

title: Baked oats, coffee and cocoa
intro: It all comes down to cooking: the surface must be set while the center remains moist, otherwise the oats become dry and mealy.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, brush it with oil, pour in the batter, and then place it directly in the oven. The pan withstands 180°C without flinching, produces more browned edges than a baking pan, and releases the cake itself once it has cooled slightly.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Dissolve the instant coffee in boiling water. Let it cool while you continue.
Mash the banana with a fork in a large bowl until you obtain a smooth puree without any lumps.
Add the oat flakes, protein powder, honey, milk, coffee, vanilla, yeast, and chia seeds. Mix thoroughly (spread evenly, without lumps or pockets of dry powder).
Heat the empty pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes, then brush it with a light coating of oil, including the bottom and sides.

Pour the mixture into the pan, smooth the surface, cover, and bake for 37 minutes. The surface should be set, the edges golden brown, and the center still slightly soft. A wooden skewer inserted into the center should come out almost dry.
Remove the pan from the oven and let it cool slightly. The cake will pull away from the sides of the pan on its own: this is the signal to unmold.
Top with vanilla yogurt and sprinkle with cocoa using a sieve, either in the pan or on the plate.
Store the remainder in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to three days.

title: No-bake speculoos cheesecake bars
intro: It's all about the temperature: a cold ice cream to aerate (incorporate air by whipping), a barely warm topping to remain smooth.
titane: The topping melts in the titanium pan over very low heat, never in the microwave. The heat conduction is rapid and even: no overheating point, no crust burning at the edges while the center remains firm. Stir continuously with a spatula and remove from the heat as soon as the batter flows in a ribbon. If it starts to smell of caramel, it's already too hot and will burn the topping.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake chills for 4 to 6 hours, ideally overnight, so start the day before.
Line a 15 cm square mould with baking paper, leaving two bands overhanging on the sides so you can unmould without effort.
Reduce the 200 g of biscuits to fine crumbs using a food processor or a rolling pin in a freezer bag.
Mix the crumbs with the melted butter until you obtain the texture of damp sand: the mixture must hold together when you squeeze it in your hand.
Pack firmly into the bottom of the mould with the back of a spoon or a glass with a flat bottom. Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Whisk the cream cheese at room temperature with the 200 g of spread until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture, without lumps.

Pour in the very cold cream and whisk with an electric mixer until soft to medium peaks form (the cream falls back slightly when you lift the whisk). Stop there: beyond this point, the texture becomes grainy.
Spread the filling over the chilled crust and smooth it with an offset spatula.
Melt the remaining 125 g of spread in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring constantly, until it is runny and glossy. Remove from heat immediately into a bowl to stop the cooking.
Pour the warm topping over the filling and spread it in an even layer by tilting the mould.
Arrange the whole or crumbled biscuits on top, marking out the future portions.
Refrigerate for 4 to 6 hours, ideally overnight. Unmould, then cut into nine squares with a blade rinsed in hot water and wiped clean between each cut.

title: Chocolate squares, tahini and popcorn
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: if it's too hot, it curdles and loses its shine, so keep it on a very low heat and never stop stirring.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Preheat it empty for one minute, then reduce the heat to very low and melt the chocolate directly on it. Its heat conduction is immediate: the slightest inattention and the chocolate will stick. On the other hand, the same pan can then be used to coat all the toppings, without the need for a mixing bowl or extra dishes.
steps: Plan ahead: the baking sheet should chill for at least 30 minutes before cutting.

Preheat the skillet on high for one minute, then reduce to very low heat. Pour in the chocolate and stir continuously with a spatula for about 3 minutes, until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture with no lumps.
Remove from heat. Add the tahini and mix until the whole is homogeneous.
Add the puffed quinoa, slivered almonds and popcorn to the skillet. Coat with the spatula, lifting the mixture rather than crushing it, to preserve the crunch.
Line a rectangular mold with parchment paper (line the bottom and sides). Transfer the mixture into it (pour out from the skillet), press down lightly to a thickness of 1.5 cm.
Coarsely crush the pretzels and scatter them over the top. Press gently with your fingertips to set them.
Chill for a minimum of 30 minutes, until the baking sheet is firm to the touch.
Unmold and cut into squares of approximately 3 cm with a smooth-bladed knife.

title: Pineapple and mint sorbet
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the pineapple must come out of the freezer rock hard, otherwise you'll get a lukewarm puree instead of a sorbet.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: No frying pan here, and that's intentional. The key lies elsewhere: blend in short bursts, never continuously. A blender running constantly heats the container and melts the ice crystals you're trying to keep. Five seconds of blending, a pause, scrape down the sides with a spatula, and repeat. The mixture goes from grainy to creamy in just a few pulses.
steps: Plan ahead: the sorbet takes 1 hour 30 minutes in the freezer; allow this time before serving.
Remove the pineapple from the freezer at the last moment. If it has frozen into a block, separate the pieces by hand before pouring them into the food processor bowl.

Add the mint, lemon juice, coconut milk and honey. Process using short pulses, scraping the sides between each addition, until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous mixture. Allow about one minute of actual processing time, no more.
Taste. Pineapple varies greatly from one fruit to another: adjust with a few drops of lemon if it lacks punch, a drizzle of honey if it is too sharp.
Transfer to an airtight container, smooth the surface and place in the freezer for 1 hour 30 minutes. The sorbet should be firm but yield under the spoon.
Beyond two hours of freezing, leave the container at room temperature for 30 minutes before serving. The spoon should enter without resistance.

title: Banana, chocolate and walnut skillet muffin cake
intro: The entire muffin batter is cooked in the pan at once: what matters here is the contrast between a golden and crispy bottom and a moist crumb, achieved by starting on the stovetop and then baking in the oven.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before pouring in the batter. Titanium heats up quickly and retains heat: upon contact, the base of the batter sears immediately and forms a sweet crust all around, something a cold muffin tin will never achieve. The pan then goes directly into the oven without transferring the batter.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a large bowl. Leave some chunks: they will melt during cooking and retain moisture.
Add the eggs, milk, olive oil, honey and vanilla. Whisk until smooth.
Add the flour, cinnamon, ginger, baking soda, and baking powder. Mix until all traces of flour have disappeared, but no more: overworking the dough will result in a dense crumb.
Fold in the nuts and chocolate (incorporate them by lifting the mixture with a spatula, without whisking).
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then brush the bottom and sides with grapeseed oil.
Pour all the batter in at once, smooth the surface with a spatula. Cover and let it cook over low heat until the edges are firm and the top is almost dry, about 8 minutes.
Place the pan uncovered in the oven for 16 minutes, until golden brown and dry to the touch. A knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let it cool in the pan, then unmold and cut into 12 pieces.

title: Marbled blondies with black sesame
intro: It all comes down to cooking with the lid on: the edges set, the center remains soft, and the marbling doesn't move if you wait for it to cool before cutting.
titane: The covered pan acts as an oven. The titanium base transmits direct, even heat, forming a thin crust under the pastry, while the lid traps steam and keeps the center moist. Heat gently and check the bottom: in a pan, the heat rises faster than in a covered oven.
steps: Heat a 20-22 cm frying pan empty for 2-3 minutes over medium-low heat. Brush the base and sides with clarified butter, then line the inside with a disc of baking paper cut to the diameter of the pan. Remove from the heat while you prepare the batter.
Whisk the tahini and 60 ml of maple syrup until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture.
Add the egg, vanilla, and plant-based milk. Whisk until fully emulsified: the mixture should thicken slightly and take on a uniform color.
Incorporate the almond flour, baking powder and salt. Mix with a spatula, without overworking, until you obtain a thick dough.
Add the chocolate chips and spread them out with one or two movements.
In a bowl, loosen the black sesame paste with the 2 teaspoons of maple syrup until it reaches a soft cream consistency.
Pour the batter into the lined pan and smooth it out with a spatula.

Place the black sesame seeds by small spoonfuls on the surface, then marble (create ribbons by pulling one layer of dough into the other) with the tip of a knife. Three or four passes are enough: beyond that, the lines will become blurred.

Cover and cook for 24 minutes over low heat. Lift the lid halfway through cooking and slide a spatula under the parchment paper to check the color underneath. It's ready when the edges are set, the center is still soft to the touch, and the bottom is golden brown.
Remove from the heat, let it cool slightly in the pan, then transfer it to a wire rack by pulling the parchment paper over it. Allow it to cool completely before cutting it into nine squares.

title: Chocolate cake and M&M's cooked in a skillet
intro: A soft cake that bakes, cools, glazes and cuts in the same pan: it's all about the cooking, which is stopped when the crumb is still moist.

ing.note: and a little more if needed

titane: The titanium pan acts as a 23 x 33 cm baking pan and can go from countertop to oven at any temperature. Line the bottom with parchment paper, butter the sides, and use the same pan for everything from the first batch to the last. Before making any final batch, check that the handle is oven-safe.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Line the bottom of the titanium pan with baking paper and lightly butter the sides.
Whisk together the melted butter, sugar and cocoa until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture.
Add the eggs one at a time, then the milk and vanilla. Whisk between each addition.
Incorporate the flour, yeast, bicarbonate and salt. Stop as soon as the dough is smooth: beyond that point, the crumb will become denser.
Pour the batter into the pan, smooth the surface and bake for 25 minutes. A toothpick inserted into the center should come out with a few moist crumbs.
Remove the pan from the oven, place it on a wire rack, and let it cool completely. Never glaze a warm cake; the butter will melt.
Meanwhile, beat the softened butter with the cocoa until smooth and creamy.
Add the icing sugar in three additions, then the cream, vanilla, and salt. Beat until you have a thick, smooth frosting. Thin with a spoonful of cream if it resists the spatula.
Spread the icing over the cold cake in the pan, swirling it with a spatula.
Immediately sprinkle with M&M's, pressing them lightly to anchor them in the icing before it sets.
Cut into 12 thick squares directly in the pan and serve at room temperature.

title: Raw dark chocolate cheesecake
intro: It all comes down to the fineness of the mixing: the topping must be perfectly smooth, without the slightest cashew grain, otherwise the texture remains sandy in the mouth.

ing.note: soak for a minimum of 2 hours if your blender

ing: coconut oil or raw cocoa butter
titane: Dry-roast the almonds (without oil) in the titanium pan before grinding them. Over medium heat, for three to four minutes, stirring constantly. Wait until the almonds begin to smell toasted and the skins start to darken. Remove them immediately from the pan to stop the heat: the titanium base continues to release its heat after the heat is turned off. This roasting process gives the crust a depth that raw almonds will never achieve.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake takes two hours in the freezer; allow this time before serving.
Line the bottom of a 20 cm springform pan with parchment paper.
Toast the almonds in a pan as indicated above, then let them cool completely. While still warm, they would release their oil when blended and the crust would become greasy.
Blend the almonds with the dates and cinnamon until you obtain a mixture that holds together when you press it between two fingers. Add water one spoonful at a time if the mixture remains powdery.
Press this preparation onto the bottom of the pan in an even layer. Pack it down with the back of a spoon, pressing firmly on the edges.
Place the pan in the freezer while you prepare the filling.
Rinse and drain the cashews if you have soaked them.

Blend the cashews with the yogurt, cocoa, maple syrup, melted coconut oil, vanilla and salt. Allow at least one minute of continuous blending, scraping down the sides once or twice. The mixture must be completely smooth and glossy.
Taste it. Add one spoonful of maple syrup if you want a sweeter note, then blend for a few seconds.
Remove the pan, pour the filling over the hardened crust, smooth the surface and tap the pan lightly on the work surface to remove any air bubbles.
Return to the freezer for at least 2 hours, until the surface is firm to the touch.
Take the cake out 15 minutes before serving, unmold it, and grate the chocolate over the top.

title: Roasted purple sweet potato, crispy chickpeas and miso-tahini sauce
intro: It all comes down to the crust: a good searing before baking gives the sweet potato a contrast that baking alone never produces.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before adding any oil or butter. The titanium surface heats up quickly and retains heat: the slices stick, caramelize, and then release easily. The same pan can go in the oven, then be reheated for the chickpeas, and you only need to wash one container.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes.
Prick the sweet potato with a fork, cut it into 2cm thick slices. Coat them with a tablespoon of avocado oil and season with salt.
Pour a drizzle of oil into the hot pan, arrange the slices flat. Sear for 5 minutes without touching them: they will detach themselves once a crust has formed.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 30 minutes. A knife tip should pierce the flesh without resistance.
Meanwhile, dry the chickpeas between two cloths as thoroughly as possible. Mix them with the salt, paprika, and the second tablespoon of avocado oil.
Remove the pan from the oven. Transfer the slices to a serving plate and cover to keep them warm.
Return the pan to high heat. Spread the chickpeas in a single layer and stir-fry for 10 minutes, shaking regularly, until golden brown and sound hollow when pierced with a spoon.
In a bowl, whisk together the miso, tahini, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and maple syrup until smooth and coats the back of a spoon. Thin with a tablespoon of warm water if it's too thick.
Coat the sweet potato with sauce, top with chickpeas, sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions.

title: Speculoos and red fruit verrines
intro: It's all about the contrast: a very airy speculoos cream, a tangy red fruit puree, and a biscuit that must remain dry until serving.

ing.note: taken out early and very soft

ing: whipped cream stabilizer or instant pudding mix
titane: The speculoos spread melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirred continuously with a flexible spatula. No hot spots, no graininess: you see exactly when it becomes runny and you remove it from the heat. Overheated spread solidifies into a thick, brittle layer on the glass; just-melted spread spreads out smoothly.
steps: Distribute the 100g of crumbled biscuits into the bottom of six dessert glasses. Press down lightly with the back of a spoon.
Blend the strawberries, raspberries, and tablespoon of icing sugar until smooth. Pass it through a sieve if you want a seedless texture.
Beat the cream cheese with the 50g of speculoos paste, the 40g of icing sugar and the vanilla, until the mixture is perfectly smooth and lump-free.
Whip the cold cream into stiff peaks, adding the stabilizer if using. Stop as soon as the whisk leaves stiff peaks.
Incorporate the whipped cream into the cream cheese mixture by folding (lifting the mass with a spatula, without turning, to keep the air).
Assemble the verrines: a layer of cream on the biscuit, a layer of fruit puree, then a second layer of cream. Smooth the surface.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, until the cream is set and no longer moves when you tilt the glass.

Place the titanium pan over very low heat, pour in the 100g of speculoos spread and stir continuously with a flexible spatula. Remove from the heat as soon as it is smooth and runny, about 2 minutes. Let it cool slightly, then spread a thin layer on each verrine.
Sprinkle with 30g of crumbled biscuits, arrange the strawberries and raspberries, and place a whole biscuit on top of each glass. Serve immediately.

title: Chocolate, hazelnut and banana skillet cake
intro: Everything hinges on the gentleness of the fire: a flame that is too intense will burn the base before the heart catches.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, then grease it with a thin layer of oil or butter. The thick titanium base distributes heat evenly, without hot spots, and can withstand long, covered cooking times without damage. The cake will easily release from the sides of the pan when it's ready.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a large bowl until it's almost smooth.
Whisk together the spread, eggs, milk, oil and vanilla. The mixture should be creamy and smooth.
Incorporate the flour, cocoa, baking powder and salt. Mix just enough to obtain a smooth dough, without overworking.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, then spread the clarified butter over the entire surface, including the sides. The fat should sizzle slightly on contact.

Pour the batter into the pan, cover tightly, and cook for 38 minutes over very low heat. Do not stir, and lift the lid as little as possible: the cake is cooked when the center is set and the edges have pulled back on themselves.
Meanwhile, gently heat the milk, spread and butter in a small saucepan until it just begins to simmer.
Remove from heat, add the chocolate chips and stir until the sauce is smooth and glossy.
Pour the hot sauce over the warm cake, directly in the pan. Sprinkle with hazelnuts and mini chocolate chips, then cut and serve straight from the pan.

title: Seared corn ribs, creamy chili sauce
intro: Everything hinges on the first side: the corn must stick, caramelize, and then free itself from the metal.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and retains heat reliably. Place the wedges cut-side down in the very hot pan and leave them undisturbed: the flesh will brown in just a few minutes, well before it's fully cooked. The lid then takes over to finish cooking gently, without an oven and without drying out.
steps: Preheat the empty pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. A drop of water should bead and dance on it.
Remove the leaves and awns from the ears of corn (remove them completely, they would burn when handled).
Cut each ear of corn in half lengthwise, then cut each half in half again: you get four quarters per ear, each with a flat cut face.
Place the wedges in a bowl, pour over the grapeseed oil and coat them by hand.
Mix smoked paprika, garlic, cumin, onion, thyme, chili pepper, and black pepper. Sprinkle over the corn and toss the pieces until the spices are evenly coated.

Place the wedges cut-side down on the metal, without overlapping. Place over high heat and leave undisturbed for 5 minutes: the corn will release on its own once a crust has formed. Cook in two batches if the pan is too full.
Reduce heat to medium, cover and continue for 13 minutes, turning the pieces every 3 to 4 minutes, until all sides are golden brown and crispy.
Meanwhile, whisk together the Greek yogurt, mayonnaise, juice of half a lime, and sriracha in a bowl. The sauce should be smooth and coat the back of a spoon. Adjust the spiciness to taste.
Remove from heat, melt the butter on the still hot ribs, add the lime juice and parsley.
Serve immediately, with the sauce on the side.

title: Labneh with dill, capers and red onion
intro: It all comes down to draining: the more water the yogurt loses, the better the spread sticks to the bagel without making the crumb soggy.
titane: Before filling, toast the bagel halves cut-side down in a dry titanium pan over medium heat for 60 to 90 seconds. No oil is needed: the crust will brown, the crumb will remain soft, and the cold labneh will retain its contrast. Press lightly with the back of a spatula for even contact.
steps: Plan ahead: the labneh drains in the refrigerator for 24 to 48 hours, start the day before or two days before.
Mix the yogurt and salt. Line a fine strainer with cheesecloth, pour the yogurt in the center, gather the corners and tie.

Place the strainer over a deep bowl, place in the refrigerator and let drain for 24 to 48 hours (longer for firmer labneh). You obtain a labneh (yogurt drained to the texture of firm fresh cheese). Discard the whey or keep it for bread dough.
Transfer the labneh to a bowl without the liquid. Drain the capers then chop them coarsely. Fold in the dill, capers and pepper. Taste, adjust the salt: the capers already provide some.
Slice the red onion into vertical slices, along the grain. Soak them for 10 minutes in ice water to mellow their sharpness, then drain and pat dry.
Open the bagels, toast them as described above. Spread the labneh in a thick layer, distribute the onion and, if you wish, the smoked salmon.

title: Mini blueberry cheesecakes with a pan-fried speculoos base
intro: It all comes down to the biscuit base: browned dry in the pan, it retains its crispness under the creamy mixture instead of becoming soggy.

ing.note: taken out of the freezer 1 hour in advance

titane: The pan is used twice. First, empty and piping hot, to toast the biscuit discs as if they were a crust: the butter melts, the sugar barely caramelizes, and the base releases itself when it's ready. Then, with a little water in the bottom and a lid, it becomes a covered bain-marie where the cheesecakes gently set. The same pan is used from start to finish; no oven is needed.
steps: Mix the speculoos crumbs, melted butter and 2 tablespoons of sugar. The mixture should have the texture of damp sand that holds together when pressed between your fingers.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Place the mixture in eight small, spaced-out mounds, then flatten each one with the back of a spoon to form even discs half a centimeter thick.
Let it brown in a dry pan for about 3 minutes, without touching it. The base is cooked when it easily releases from the pan. If you have to force it, continue cooking for another 30 seconds.
Remove the bases from the heat and place them in eight pastry rings on a baking sheet. Wipe the pan clean.

Whisk together the cream cheese, yogurt, 45g of sugar, vanilla, and egg until perfectly smooth. Work gently, being careful not to incorporate too much air; the goal is a smooth, pliable mixture, not a voluminous one.
Distribute the mixture into the circles, on the cooled bases. Tap the tray to remove any bubbles.

Pour 1 cm of water into the pan, place the filled pastry rings inside, cover, and maintain a low heat: the water should simmer, not boil. Cook for 20 minutes. The centers will be set but will still jiggle slightly when the pan is moved.
Remove the rings from the refrigerator, let them come to room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours. This time is crucial: it's what gives them their shape.
Remove the ring mold with the tip of a knife, spread with blueberry jam and arrange the fresh blueberries on top. Serve chilled.

title: Zucchini ejjeh, tahini sauce
intro: It all depends on the water in the courgette: if it's not drained properly, the batter loosens and the patties steam instead of browning.
ing: The juice of half a lemon
titane: Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. Titanium heats up quickly and evenly, forming a crisp crust as soon as it touches the pan. After that, don't touch it. A pancake that sticks isn't ready; once the crust has formed, it will release easily.
steps: Grate the courgette, salt it lightly and let it drain (release its water) for 10 minutes in a colander. Then press it between your hands, firmly, until it releases nothing more.
Peel the garlic and mince it. Mince the green onion stem and finely chop the parsley and mint.

In a large bowl, whisk the eggs. Add the pressed courgette, parsley, mint, green onion, flour, baking soda, cumin, salt and pepper. Mix until you obtain a homogeneous preparation, without working the batter more than necessary.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour a thin stream of grapeseed oil and tilt the pan to coat the entire bottom. The oil should ripple without smoking.
Place spoonfuls of preparation, spacing them out. Three or four per batch, no more: an overloaded pan loses its heat and the crust becomes soft.
Let cook for approximately 2 minutes without touching it. When the pancake detaches on its own from the bottom and the edges are golden, flip it. Count 2 more minutes.
Transfer (remove from the pan and set aside) onto a rack rather than on paper towels, to keep the underside crispy. Add more oil between each batch.

For the sauce, whisk the tahini with the lemon juice and garlic. The mixture will first stiffen: this is normal. Add the water in small quantities, whisking, until you reach a coating consistency. Adjust the seasoning with salt.
Serve the ejjeh warm, with the sauce on the side.

title: Crispy quesadilla with egg and cottage cheese
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the pan: too low, the egg sticks and the tortilla remains soft; too hot, the egg sets in a clean layer and the bread browns in a shell.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes before adding the oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat on contact with the cold egg: coagulation is immediate, the base releases easily, and the tortilla browns without ever sticking.
steps: Whisk the eggs in a bowl, just enough to homogenize the yolk and the white.
Preheat the pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Melt the clarified butter, pour in the eggs and tilt the pan to spread them in a thin layer. Season with salt and pepper.
While the surface is still damp, spread the cottage cheese and crushed chickpeas, if using. Place the tortilla on top and press down lightly with the palm of your hand.
Let it cook for 1 to 2 minutes without touching it, until the egg is almost set and detaches itself from the bottom.
Flip the whole thing over with a flick of the wrist: the tortilla ends up against the metal.
Sprinkle the grated cheese over one half of the egg layer, then fold the other half over it.
Continue for 2 to 3 minutes, until the tortilla is golden brown and crispy and the cheese is melted.
Cut in half. Serve with avocado and cherry tomatoes.

title: Cocoa porridge with caramelized banana
intro: It all comes down to the banana: a real caramel crust, obtained in the pan that has just been used for the porridge.
titane: Titanium heats up quickly and evenly across its entire surface. After preheating empty for 2 to 3 minutes, the banana browns in just a few minutes without falling apart, in the same pan as the porridge. One pan, two cooking methods.
steps: Combine the oats, milk, water, chia seeds, cocoa, and honey in a pan. Heat over medium-low heat, stirring regularly, for about 6 minutes. The mixture is ready when it coats the back of a spoon (leaving a layer that doesn't drip).
Remove the porridge from the cooking container and place it in a bowl. Set aside.
Cut the banana into pieces of about 2 cm, or in half lengthwise.
Wipe the pan clean. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat, then add the clarified butter. It should simmer without smoking.

Arrange the banana slices, drizzle with honey, and sprinkle with cinnamon. Leave them undisturbed for 2 to 3 minutes: the slices will detach easily once the surface is caramelized. Turn them over and caramelize the other side.
Place the banana on top of the porridge, grate the dark chocolate over it, and sprinkle with hemp seeds.

title: Salted caramel and peanut cheesecake
intro: It all comes down to two cooking stages: a dish removed from the oven still wobbly in the center, and an amber caramel cooked without a second too long.
titane: The caramel is made in a titanium pan, not a saucepan. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the sugar in a thin layer: the heat rises quickly and spreads evenly without hot spots, resulting in a clean and consistent amber color. However, this high heat conductivity makes the butter explode if it reaches the stovetop. Remove the pan from the heat before adding the butter. The cheesecake filling, on the other hand, stays in the oven: 55 minutes of consistent heat in a springform pan is not the same as on a baking sheet.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake cools and then refrigerates for several hours, account for resting time in your schedule.
Preheat the oven to 160 °C. Line (coat with parchment paper) the bottom of a 22 cm springform pan.
Reduce the biscuits to fine crumbs. Mix them with the melted butter until you obtain a moist sand that holds when pressed in your hand.

Line the pan (coat it): press the mixture firmly on the bottom, then bring it up 3 to 4 cm high. Tamp it down with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass. Keep it cold while preparing the filling.
Beat the cream cheese and sugar until the mixture is perfectly smooth, without lumps. Work at moderate speed: too much air causes cracks during baking.
Add the eggs one by one, then the cream. Mix just enough to obtain a thick and creamy batter.
Pour over the crust, smooth the surface, tap the pan on the work surface to release air bubbles.

Bake for 55 minutes. The edges should be set, the center still trembling on a coin. Let cool completely at room temperature, oven off with door slightly ajar if possible, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours.

Prepare the caramel: empty titanium pan, medium heat, 2 to 3 minutes. Pour the sugar in a thin layer and let it melt without stirring. As long as the crystals are not completely liquefied, no spoon touches the pan, otherwise the sugar clumps. When the colour is amber and uniform, remove from heat.

Off the heat, incorporate the butter in pieces while whisking, then the warm cream poured in a thin stream. The mixture bubbles, that is normal. Whisk until you obtain a smooth sauce, add the fleur de sel, then transfer to another container to stop the cooking. Let cool slightly.
Distribute the peanuts over the well-chilled cheesecake. Coat with 200 ml of lukewarm caramel, not hot: it should spread without running down the sides. Sprinkle with fleur de sel.
Return to the cold for 30 minutes. Slice with a blade passed under hot water and wiped between each portion.

title: Matcha and white chocolate Christmas trees
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the cocoa butter: too hot, it separates and the matcha becomes bitter; just melted, it retains its shine and sets cleanly when cold.
titane: The titanium pan becomes your double boiler. A little simmering water in the pan, a bowl placed on top, and the heat rises evenly across the entire surface, without any hot spots. The cocoa butter melts without ever exceeding the point where it would curdle.
steps: Pour one centimeter of water into the titanium pan and bring it to a simmer over low heat. Place a heatproof bowl containing the cocoa butter on top. Let it melt for about 3 minutes, until it is completely liquid and transparent.
Remove the bowl from the heat. Add the cashew butter, maple syrup, sifted matcha, and vanilla. Mix with a spatula until smooth, with no lumps of matcha remaining.
Line a flat dish with baking paper. Arrange the pretzel sticks flat, spaced three centimeters apart, with the coated part facing up.
Transfer the mixture to a piping bag. Pipe (apply with even pressure) increasingly shorter zigzags onto the upper half of each stick, from bottom to top, to draw the silhouette of a Christmas tree.
Immediately place the pomegranate arils on the branches, then sprinkle with grated coconut. The mixture should still be soft so that the decoration adheres.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. The surface should be firm and matte to the touch. Carefully peel off the paper.

title: Sourdough toast, avocado and soft-boiled eggs with cottage cheese
intro: It all comes down to two things: timing the eggs to the second and a slice of bread that's really golden brown, not just dry.
ing: turns of the black pepper mill
titane: Forget the toaster. Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes, then place the lightly buttered slice of sourdough on it: the crust will form by direct contact, becoming dense and even. Don't move it until it detaches on its own—this is the signal that the Maillard reaction (browning of sugars and proteins under the effect of heat) has done its work. Only one slice at a time.
steps: Bring a small saucepan containing approximately 500 ml of water to a boil.
Place the eggs one by one using a spoon, without dropping them into the water.
Allow 6 minutes 30 seconds for a very runny yolk, 7 to 7 minutes 30 seconds for a semi-runny yolk. Maintain a steady boil.
Immediately transfer the eggs to an ice bath. The cooking process stops abruptly and the shell peels off more easily.
Peel the eggs and set them aside.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. A drop of water should sizzle on contact.
Brush the slice of sourdough with clarified butter and place it in the pan. Leave it for about 3 minutes, without touching it, until it releases easily and is golden brown.
Mash the avocado with a fork and spread it on the still-warm bread.
Season: lemon juice, grated zest on top, salt, pepper.
Scatter the hemp seeds over the top, spoon the cottage cheese over the top, and add the chili crisp if using.
Cut the eggs in half lengthwise, place them on the toast and serve immediately.

title: Spelt bagels with Greek yogurt
intro: A dough without baker's yeast, without resting and without an oven: everything depends on the regularity of the fire and on patience before turning.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the worktop

ing: sesame seeds or everything bagel mix
