titane: The covered pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat, it builds a crust by contact while the steam trapped under the lid cooks the crumb. You maintain control over the browning of each side, something a conventional oven doesn't allow.
steps: Place the empty titanium pan on medium-low heat and let it heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Keep the lid within reach.
Mix the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl. Drain the Greek yogurt well, add it all at once and work with a spatula until the mixture comes together.
Flour the work surface and knead for 1 to 2 minutes, no more: the dough should become smooth without firming up.
Divide into 4 equal portions. Roll each into a strip, seal the ends into a ring, then open a large hole in the center with your finger. It will close during cooking.
Brush the top with milk or water.
Pour the oil into the hot pan, spread it, then place the bagels with space between them. Brush again and sprinkle with seeds.
Cover and cook for about 10 minutes on medium-low heat. The bagel is ready to be flipped when it detaches on its own from the pan. If it resists, leave it.
Flip gently, cover and continue for 10 to 12 minutes. A skewer inserted in the center should come out dry.
Transfer onto a rack and wait 10 minutes before slicing. The crumb finishes setting as it cools.

title: Edamame and avocado hummus
intro: It all comes down to texture: edamame should just be defrosted, never cooked, otherwise the puree turns greenish and loses its bite.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the salad bowl for defrosting. Place the still-frozen edamame in the cold pan, cover with boiling water off the heat: the metal mass absorbs the heat in seconds and stabilizes the water at around 60°C. The beans relax without turning white. One pan, zero extra washing up.
steps: Pour the frozen edamame into the cold titanium pan, off the heat. Cover with boiling water and let stand for 2 to 3 minutes. The beans should remain firm to the bite.
Drain thoroughly, then transfer (out of the working container) onto a clean cloth. Pat dry: any remaining water would dilute the purée.
Combine the edamame, avocado, herbs, tahini, olive oil, lime juice, garlic, salt and pepper in the blender bowl.
Blend for 3 minutes, adding cold water by spoonfuls, until you obtain a smooth cream. Scrape down the sides twice during this process.
Taste it. Adjust with salt, pepper or lime: the acidity should remain clear behind the fat of the avocado.
Arrange in a bowl, make a groove with a spoon, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

title: Moist cottage cheese and blueberry cake
intro: A flourless cake that holds together only by the egg and drained cottage cheese: everything depends on the gentleness of the heat, otherwise the center remains liquid while the base browns.
titane: The covered pan replaces the oven. Direct contact with the titanium browns the bottom, and the lid traps the steam, which cooks the top. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes before greasing: a preheated surface will sear the batter instead of letting it seep through.
steps: Blend the banana, cottage cheese, egg, sweetener and vanilla. Push until no more cheese grains remain: the texture should be smooth and spreadable.
Preheat the pan empty, over medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Brush the bottom with clarified butter. It should simmer without smoking.
Pour the batter, spread it with a spatula, cover.

Reduce the heat to low and cook for 22 minutes. The cake is ready when the center no longer sticks to your finger and the edges shrink back on their own. Turn off the heat and let it cool slightly in the pan, uncovered: the texture will firm up as it cools.

Remove the cake from the pan and wipe it clean. Heat the blueberries in the pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, until they burst and release a syrupy juice. Spoon the blueberries over the cake and top with whipped cream.

title: Dark chocolate shells, puffed quinoa and pistachios
intro: It all comes down to the thickness of the first layer of chocolate: too thin, it breaks when unmolding; too thick, it crushes the filling.
titane: Stir the puffed quinoa and crushed pistachios into the dry titanium pan over low heat for two minutes, stirring constantly. The pan will heat up evenly, allowing the grains to pop without burning. Immediately transfer the mixture to a cold plate, otherwise the residual heat will continue to affect the pan.
steps: Melt the chocolate in a double boiler over low heat, stirring regularly. Remove from the heat as soon as it is smooth and shiny: overheating will make it dull and grainy.
Pour a thin layer of chocolate into two bubble-shaped silicone molds. Coat (line the sides) to the top with a pastry brush or the back of a small spatula.
Place the molds in the refrigerator and let them set while you prepare the filling. Keep the remaining chocolate warm, away from the double boiler.
Toast the puffed quinoa and pistachios using the titanium gesture, then let cool completely.
Mix the quinoa and pistachios with the tahini and 1 teaspoon of maple syrup. Taste. Add the second teaspoon if the tahini flavor is too strong.
Divide the filling between the two hardened shells and press it down flat, without touching the edges of the chocolate.
Coat with the remaining chocolate. Tap the mold on the work surface to remove any bubbles and smooth the surface.
Allow to harden for 1 hour in the refrigerator, or 20 minutes in the freezer. Unmold by turning the silicone over in one smooth motion.

title: Thick oat and cottage cheese pancakes
intro: Without a waffle iron, everything depends on the thickness of the dough and the ten-minute rest: this is what gives a tight crumb and a surface that browns nicely.

ing.note: the only sweetener in the dough
plus a drizzle between each cooking

titane: The titanium pan heats up in two or three minutes when empty and retains that heat even after the cold batter is added. The surface of the pancake sets instantly, creating a crust where a waffle iron would require a lengthy preheating process. There's only one rule: don't touch the pancake while it's still sticking. As soon as it releases easily from the spatula, it's ready to be flipped with a quick, clean motion.
steps: Blend the oat flakes alone, 5 to 10 seconds, until you obtain a coarse flour.
Add the banana, eggs, cottage cheese, collagen and cinnamon. Blend until the batter is perfectly smooth.
Fold in the baking soda and lemon juice with a spatula, without pressing. Let rest 10 minutes: the batter thickens and the bubbles distribute evenly.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat.

Pour a thin stream of oil, then a small ladle of batter, approximately one quarter of the volume. Aim for a thick disc rather than a wide one. Do not touch it as long as it does not release on its own, approximately 2 minutes.
Flip, continue for 2 minutes until the second side is golden and firm in the center. Remove from the pan and set aside on a rack so that steam does not soften the crust.
Repeat with the remaining batter, lightly oiling between each pancake.
Plate with the yogurt, nut butter, hemp seeds, berries and, if desired, maple syrup.

title: Chocolate cheesecake with cream cheese, cooked in a pan
intro: Three ingredients, no crust: it all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate when mixing and the gentleness of the heat.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the service

titane: The covered titanium pan works like a closed oven: the heated metal gives the base a crisp color, while the lid traps steam and keeps the center creamy. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat before coating it (thinning the surface with fat to prevent sticking), otherwise the clarified butter will brown before the batter arrives.
steps: Plan ahead: the final setting requires at least 1 hour in the refrigerator after complete cooling.
Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat. Brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter in a thin layer. Remove from heat.
Drain the cottage cheese if needed to remove excess whey.

Chop the chocolate. Melt it in a bain-marie (bowl placed over a pot of simmering water, without contact with the water) or in short bursts in the microwave. Let it cool to room temperature: chocolate that is too hot would coagulate the eggs.
Mix together the cooled chocolate, eggs, cottage cheese and cocoa. Stop as soon as the mixture is perfectly smooth, with no visible curd grains.
Pour into the pan. Cover and let cook for 30 minutes over very low heat. The mixture is ready when the edges pull away on their own and the center still trembles under the cover.
Turn off the heat and let cool completely in the pan, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour. The setting is completed when chilled.
Unmold onto a flat plate, dust with cocoa, slice with a blade rinsed under hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Coconut, blueberry and dark chocolate bites
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the coconut mixture: sticky enough to hold its shape under the pressure of a finger, never soggy.

ing.note: a little more if the blueberries are acidic

titane: The titanium pan acts as a dry double boiler. Its low thermal mass allows it to heat up and cool down quickly: placed over very low heat, it melts chocolate in two or three minutes, without water or a mixing bowl. However, it is unforgiving of carelessness. Stir continuously with a spatula, bringing the chocolate from the edge towards the center, and remove from the heat when a few unmelted pieces remain: the residual heat finishes the job.
steps: Combine the coconut, blueberries, maple syrup and vanilla in the food processor bowl. Pulse until you obtain a smooth, sticky, purple-tinted mass.

Pinch a little of the mixture between two fingers. If it crumbles, add the coconut milk and blend for a few more seconds. Proceed spoonful by spoonful: a mixture that is too wet will not hold together.

Take a heaping tablespoon of the mixture, place it in a silicone mini-muffin mold cavity, press down firmly with your thumb, and smooth the top. Repeat for all twelve cavities. Refrigerate while the chocolate melts.

Place the chopped chocolate in a dry titanium pan over very low heat. Stir continuously with a flexible spatula. As soon as two-thirds has melted, remove from the heat and continue stirring off the flame until you obtain a smooth and glossy mixture.
Coat each bite with a thin layer of chocolate (coating: covering with an even layer, without letting it drip down the sides). Immediately place two fresh blueberries in the center if you have them.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, until the chocolate is matte and firm to the touch. Unmold by pushing from underneath.

title: Coconut-banana rings with dark chocolate
intro: It all depends on the ripeness of the banana: when very ripe, it sweetens and binds the coconut without a gram of flour or egg.

ing.note: up to 130g depending on the size of the banana

titane: The covered pan replaces the oven. Direct contact browns the edges while the steam trapped under the lid cooks the center in ten minutes instead of half an hour. Once the rings are removed from the pan and set aside, the same pan, wiped dry, is used to melt the chocolate over very low heat: no double boiler, no second utensil.
steps: Mash the banana with a fork in a bowl until smooth. Stir in the coconut in three additions. Stop mixing when the mixture holds its shape between your fingers without sticking; it should be thick and homogeneous. Add more coconut, spoonful by spoonful, if it remains moist.
Take a large spoonful of dough, roll it into a ball, and flatten it into a disc 1 cm thick. Pierce the center with your finger to form a ring. Count eight pieces.
Heat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Brush it with a thin layer of coconut oil.

Place the rings loosely in the pan. Cover. Reduce the heat to low-medium and cook for 10 minutes. The edges will brown, the coconut will be fragrant, and the rings will detach from the bottom on their own: that's the signal.
Transfer them to a wire rack and let them cool completely. When warm, they break; when cold, they hold together.

Wipe the pan with paper towels. Remove from the heat while still hot, add the chocolate and coconut oil, and stir until smooth and glossy. Return to very low heat for a few seconds if necessary, but never let it simmer.
Dip the bottom of each ring in the chocolate, place them on baking paper. Coat the tops (cover with an even layer) in thin lines, using a spoon.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes, or freeze for 5 minutes, until the chocolate breaks cleanly when you bite into it.

title: Chocolate fudge, red berries and Greek yogurt
intro: A fudge that holds together by cold and not by sugar: it all comes down to a gentle melting, without ever exceeding the temperature where the chocolate would grain.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the saucepan. Its small volume, less than 250 ml, and the rapid, even heat distribution prevents hot spots: the chocolate melts without sticking or curdling when it comes into contact with the yogurt. Preheat the pan empty for 1 to 2 minutes over low heat; it should be hot to the touch but not smoking.
steps: Plan ahead: the fudge sets in the freezer for two hours, allow for this time before serving.
Line a rectangular dish with baking paper, leaving two edges overhanging so you can unmould more easily later.
Spread the strawberries and blueberries on the bottom of the dish, cut side down on the paper.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 1 to 2 minutes over low heat. It should be warm to the touch, not burning.

Pour the chocolate, peanut butter and Greek yoghurt. Place over low to medium heat and stir continuously with a flexible spatula, scraping the sides (where the mixture heats fastest). Allow 5 minutes: the mixture should become smooth and glossy, with no graininess.
Remove from heat immediately: pour the mixture over the fruit and smooth the surface.
Place in the freezer for 2 hours, until the mixture is firm to the touch. Unmould, remove the paper and cut into eight squares with a blade rinsed in hot water and wiped dry.

title: Mint and barley sugar ice cream
intro: It all depends on the dissolution of the barley sugar in the cold milk: if any grain remains, the ice cream crunches instead of melting.
titane: Gently warm the milk, sugar, and half of the barley sugar in the titanium pan over very low heat, without ever letting it simmer. The base distributes the heat evenly without creating hot spots: the sugar will dissolve in two minutes, and the milk will turn a pale pink. Immediately transfer the mixture from the pan to a cold bowl to stop the heating process.
steps: Plan ahead: the ice cream maker bowl must chill in the freezer for 24 hours, and the ice cream must freeze for another 4 hours after churning; start the day before.
Place the ice cream maker bowl in the freezer for at least 24 hours. It must be completely frozen, with no sloshing when you shake it.
Crush the barley sugar with a rolling pin, wrapped in a kitchen towel. Aim for shards the size of a rice grain, not a powder.
Gently warm the milk, sugar and half of the shards in the pan over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Whisk until completely dissolved and the mixture turns pink.
Pour into a large cold bowl. Add the cream, salt, mint and vanilla. Whisk for 30 seconds, just to blend: the cream should not whip.
Set the mixture aside in the refrigerator for 1 hour. A base at 4°C churns faster and produces finer crystals.
Churn for approximately 25 minutes (mix the preparation while it freezes, in the ice cream maker). Stop at the texture of soft ice cream, which clings to the paddle.
Add the remaining shards in the last two minutes, just long enough for them to distribute without dissolving.
Transfer to a loaf tin. Press plastic wrap or parchment paper directly against the surface, then freeze for 4 hours.
Remove the ice cream 5 minutes before serving, to allow it to soften slightly under the spoon.

title: No-bake speculoos cream tarts
intro: It's all about the temperature: perfectly ripe fresh cheese, very cold cream, speculoos spread barely warmed.

ing.note: taken out of the freezer 30 minutes in advance

titane: A titanium pan replaces a saucepan for warming the spread. Use very low heat, the pan should be barely warm, and keep a spatula moving constantly. Remove from the heat as soon as it begins to simmer: the spread should become runny, not cooked. If it cooks beyond this point, it will thicken as it cools, and the glaze will lose its shine.
steps: Place a mixing bowl and the whisks in the freezer for 10 minutes. Whipped cream in a cold container holds its shape faster and is firmer.
Work the cream cheese alone, with a whisk or mixer, until it is perfectly smooth. No lumps can be salvaged afterwards.
Add the icing sugar, vanilla and 150g of speculoos spread. Mix until you obtain a thick and smooth mixture.
In a chilled bowl, whip the heavy cream (whisk until it holds its shape on the end of the whisk without falling off). Stop as soon as stiff peaks form, otherwise it will curdle.
Incorporate the whipped cream into the speculoos mixture in three stages, using a spatula, lifting the mixture from the bottom up. You are looking for a mousse that retains its volume.
Fill a piping bag fitted with a large star nozzle. Pipe a tall swirl into each tartlet base, starting from the edge towards the center.
Place the titanium pan over very low heat, pour in the remaining 2 tablespoons of batter and stir continuously for a few seconds, until it becomes smooth. Remove from the heat immediately.
Spread the warm pastry over each tartlet, letting it drip down the sides. Sprinkle with crumbled biscuits and place half a biscuit on top.
Refrigerate for 45 minutes, until the cream is firm to the touch. Serve chilled.

title: Dark chocolate cookie dough cups
intro: It all comes down to melting the chocolate: very low heat, constant stirring, and the coating stays shiny instead of grainy.
ing: cup of honey or maple syrup
titane: The titanium pan acts as a double boiler. Its thermal responsiveness allows you to use very low heat and melt chocolate and coconut oil without any hot spots at the bottom. Place the pan on the lowest heat setting, and turn off the heat as soon as two-thirds of the chocolate chips have melted: the residual heat finishes the job. Then pour directly from the pan, without dirtying any other container.
steps: Plan ahead: the cups need 2 hours in the freezer before they are ready.
Line a muffin tin with paper liners (to line: to cover the tin with a protective layer to facilitate removal).

Combine in a bowl the oat flour, almond powder, peanut butter, honey and milk. Work with a spatula until you obtain a homogeneous and flexible dough. If it remains crumbly, add half a teaspoon of milk, no more.
Fold in the chocolate chips by hand, quickly, so they do not melt from the warmth of your fingers.
Distribute the dough in the liners, about two tablespoons per cup. Press down with the back of a spoon to obtain a flat surface: the chocolate will distribute evenly.
Set the tin in the refrigerator while you prepare the topping.

Break the dark chocolate into pieces. Place it with the coconut oil in the titanium pan, over very low heat. Stir constantly. Allow 3 minutes: the mixture should be smooth and glossy, without lumps. Remove from heat as soon as the last bit of solid chocolate disappears.
Coat each cup directly from the pan, in a thin layer. Tilt the tin slightly to spread.
Place in the freezer for a minimum of 2 hours, until the coating breaks cleanly under your fingernail.
Remove the cups and let them come to room temperature for a few minutes before serving. Store them afterwards in the refrigerator.

title: Dried fruit clusters with honey
intro: It all comes down to how you cook the honey: hot enough to coat the surface, but never hot enough to caramelize.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat. Titanium's low thermal mass distributes heat evenly without hot spots: the coconut oil melts without smoking, and the honey remains fluid and clear from the center to the edges. This gives you an even coating rather than brown caramel in patches.
steps: Plan ahead: a resting period of 30 to 40 minutes is needed before turning out the clusters.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat. Hold your hand ten centimetres above the bottom: you should feel a steady heat, with no smoke.
Add the coconut oil. Let it melt and coat the bottom, approximately 30 seconds.
Pour in the dried fruit. Stir for 2 minutes to coat (cover with a regular film of fat). They should become shiny and begin to smell roasted.

Pour the honey in a thin stream. Stir constantly for 2 minutes, still over low heat, until the mixture thickens and coats the dried fruit with a glossy veil. As soon as it slightly sticks to the spatula, remove from heat.
Add the fleur de sel, mix one last time.
Distribute immediately into small moulds, pressing down with a spoon. Let cool at room temperature until completely firm, 30 to 40 minutes. The clusters will release from the mould on their own.

title: Mini donuts made with sliced bread and chocolate
intro: Three ingredients, and everything hinges on two points: the exact amount of milk absorbed by the crumb, and an oil that remains between 170 and 175 °C from the first to the last donut.
titane: Use a short frying technique rather than deep frying: 2.5 cm of oil in a high-sided titanium pan, no more. The metal mass retains heat when you add the donuts, which a small saucepan won't. Flip each donut halfway through cooking, as soon as the submerged side is golden. You'll get the same crust as with deep frying, using four times less oil and with constant visual control.
steps: Remove the crusts from the bread slices and tear the crumb into large pieces in a bowl. Gradually pour in the warm milk, allowing the bread to absorb the milk between each addition. Stop when the bread is evenly soaked, with no puddles at the bottom of the bowl.

Squeeze the dough between your hands to remove excess milk, then knead for 3 to 4 minutes. The dough should become smooth, supple, and no longer stick to your fingers. If it's still sticky, squeeze again: this indicates excess liquid.

Divide into fifteen portions of approximately 30g each. Roll each portion into a ball, flatten it to 1.5cm thick, then pierce the center with your index finger and widen the hole to 2cm. Place the donuts on a floured baking sheet without crowding them.
Heat the oil in the pan to 170°C. Without a thermometer: a piece of dough dropped into the oil should rise in three seconds while clearly bubbling.

Fry four donuts at a time, 1 minute 30 seconds per side. They should be a deep hazelnut color. Remove them from the heat source and place them on a wire rack, never flat on paper towels, otherwise the bottom will become soggy.

Melt the chocolate in a double boiler and let it cool to about 31°C (88°F), until it coats the donut without running. Dip each cooled donut on one side only, squeeze out the excess with a quarter turn of your wrist, and place it back on a wire rack. Let it set for 20 minutes.

title: Dates stuffed with peanut butter, coated in dark chocolate
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: melted gently, it coats in a thin layer and breaks cleanly under the tooth.
titane: The titanium pan heats up slowly and retains heat for a long time. Placed over very low heat, it melts chocolate without a double boiler, and its large surface area then serves as a soaking bath. A single piece of cookware, from start to finish. Turn off the heat as soon as the first pieces have melted: the metal mass finishes the job on its own.
steps: Plan ahead: the dates go into the cold twice, allow 15 minutes then 15 to 30 additional minutes before serving.
Line a baking sheet or large plate with parchment paper. Set it aside flat; it must go into the freezer.
Open each date like a book without separating it into two halves. Fill the inside with a small amount of peanut butter, add a few peanut fragments, close by pressing lightly to seal the edges.
Arrange the dates on the sheet and place in the freezer for 20 minutes. They must be firm to the touch: this prevents them from softening in the chocolate.

Place the pan over very low heat. Pour in the chocolate and oil, stir constantly with a spatula for about 3 minutes. Remove from heat as soon as three-quarters are melted and continue stirring off the heat: the heat retained by the pan completes the melting. The chocolate must be smooth and glossy, without lumps.

Place a cold date in the chocolate, turn it over with a fork to coat it completely, let the excess drip off against the edge of the pan, then place it back on the parchment paper. Continue with one date after another.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel as you go, while the coating is still wet. Once set, the salt no longer adheres.
Return the sheet to the cold until the chocolate is completely set, 15 minutes in the freezer or 30 minutes in the refrigerator.

title: Coffee, chocolate and almond ice cream bars
intro: It's all about the contrast: a pan-toasted crumble that stays crispy in the cold, and a coating thin enough to break cleanly between the teeth.
ing: finely chopped dark or semi-sweet chocolate
titane: The coffee-biscuit crumble is toasted in a pan rather than an oven: you monitor the color and aroma in real time, and stop when the mixture pulls away from the bottom of the pan on its own. The same pan, cleaned and placed back on very low heat, is then used to melt the chocolate with the coconut oil. No double boiler, no stovetop, just one surface for the entire recipe.
steps: Plan ahead: the frozen block takes a full night in the freezer before cutting, start the day before.
Line (cover with baking paper leaving two strips overhanging) a square 20 cm mould. Place it in the freezer.
Blend the biscuits, the 20 g of almonds and the 20 g of coffee beans in a food processor, in pulses, until a coarse texture with visible flakes. Do not go as far as powder.
Pour into a salad bowl, add the malted milk powder, sugar, salt and melted butter. Mix with a fork until the mixture is uniformly moist.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. The heat must be established before first contact.

Spread the mixture in a thin layer in the pan, reduce to medium-low heat and let toast for approximately 8 minutes, stirring regularly with a spatula. The crumble is ready when it smells of roasted hazelnut, has taken on a golden tint and detaches on its own from the bottom.
Transfer (remove from the pan to stop cooking) onto a cold baking sheet. Let cool completely, then break into small clusters.
Remove the ice cream 10 minutes at room temperature, until it becomes spreadable without melting. Spread half into the cold mould, using an offset spatula, in an even layer. Freeze for 1 hour.
Scatter the crumble over the firm ice cream and press lightly with the palm of your hand to anchor it without crushing it. Freeze for 30 minutes.
Spread the remaining ice cream, smooth the surface and freeze overnight. The block must be hard throughout.
Turn the block over onto a cutting board taken from the freezer, remove the paper. Cut 9 squares with a large knife, blade well sharpened, in a single downward motion. Return the bars to the cold.

Clean the pan. Over very low heat, melt the two chocolates with the coconut oil, stirring constantly. Aim for 35 to 40 °C on the thermometer: the mixture should be fluid, never hot to the touch. Off the heat, incorporate the 55 g of crushed almonds.
Dip each frozen bar in the pan, one by one, using two forks to help. Let the excess drain for a few seconds.
Place on a baking sheet lined with baking paper and freeze for 15 minutes to set the coating.

For the finishing touch, melt the 56 g of milk chocolate, pour it into a disposable piping bag, cut a fine tip and drizzle the bars. Sprinkle with almonds and crushed coffee beans. Store in the freezer in an airtight container.

title: Banana and date muffin pancakes
intro: Without a mold, the dough spreads out: what matters here is the golden crust that the pan gives under each pancake, and the patience of not touching it.
ing: one and a half ripe bananas
titane: Pour the batter into the cold pan, then heat it up. Titanium heats up quickly and dries the base before the top melts. Don't move anything while the pancake is still holding its shape: it will detach itself from the bottom once the crust has formed. Any premature attempt to move it will tear the crumb.
steps: Preheat the oven to 170°C.
Cover the dates with boiling water and let them soak for 8 minutes. Drain, then mash them with a fork into a coarse paste.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl until you get a slightly grainy puree.
Add the eggs, milk, melted coconut oil, honey and vanilla. Whisk to combine.
Separately mix the flour, cinnamon, baking powder, and baking soda. Pour this mixture into the wet ingredients and mix just until no dry flour remains.
Incorporate the date paste and nuts with a spatula, lifting the mass without folding it down (a movement that preserves the air in the dough).
Drop mounds of batter, spaced apart, directly into the cold titanium pan, about 2 cm thick. Do not spread them out; the heat will do that.

Cover and cook over low-medium heat for about 20 minutes, without stirring. When the base is golden brown and the pancake releases easily from the pan, flip it over. If the center remains moist, bake the pan uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove (transfer from the pan) to a wire rack and let cool slightly before serving.

title: Pan-fried apple-oat bars
intro: It all comes down to the topping: it must coat the base (hold on the back of a spoon without running) before going under the crumble, otherwise the base absorbs the moisture and never gets crispy.

ing.note: plus a little bit for the pan

titane: One pan, two functions. First, it reduces the apples like a saucepan, then it becomes the baking dish for the oven. The heat penetrates quickly: the crumble base dries and browns from below instead of steaming. Check that the handle is entirely metal before baking.
steps: Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Preheat the oven to 180 °C with convection heat.

Put the apple slices in the hot pan with the honey, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, lemon juice and the tablespoon of water. Let simmer 6 minutes over medium heat, stirring from time to time, until the apples are tender.
Dissolve the cornstarch in the 100 ml of water until you obtain a smooth mixture, without lumps. Pour it onto the apples while stirring immediately.
Continue for 2 to 3 minutes. The filling is ready when it coats the back of a spoon.
Remove from the pan (transfer out of the pan) into a bowl. Wipe the pan with paper towels.
In a mixing bowl, combine the flour, almond powder, oat flakes, baking powder and cinnamon.
Pour in the honey and melted coconut oil. Work with your fingertips until a crumbly texture that compacts when you squeeze it in your hand.
Lightly oil the pan with coconut oil. Press three-quarters of the mixture into it in an even layer, well packed down, bringing it up slightly on the sides.
Spread the apple filling on this base. Sprinkle the remaining crumble over, without pressing, then distribute the pumpkin seeds.
Bake the pan as is for 24 minutes, until the top is golden and crackly.
Let cool completely in the pan before cutting into twelve bars. While warm, they crumble.

title: Date, nut and chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the device: dense enough to hold up when cut, flexible enough not to become compact.
titane: The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, without a double boiler. The even heat distribution prevents burning and sticking. Stir continuously, and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth: the residual heat of the pan finishes the job.
steps: Plan ahead: the chocolate sets in the refrigerator for 2 hours, allow this time before serving.
Line a rectangular dish of approximately 20 × 20 cm with parchment paper, leaving two edges overhanging.

Combine the coconut oil, dates, walnuts, almonds and pumpkin seeds in the food processor bowl. Pulse until you obtain a thick and homogeneous mixture that holds together when pressed between your fingers. The dried fruits should remain slightly crushed.
Pour the mixture into the dish. Press firmly with the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass, until the surface is flat and compact. The more you pack it, the better the bars will hold when cut.

Place the titanium pan over very low heat. Add the chocolate and stir continuously with a spatula, approximately 3 minutes, until it is smooth and shiny. Remove from heat as soon as this stage is reached.
Coat (cover with an even layer) the surface of the mixture with the melted chocolate. Tilt the dish to spread it to the edges.
Refrigerate for 2 hours, until the chocolate is firm to the touch.
Unmold by pulling on the paper. Cut into twelve bars with a fine-bladed knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: No-bake mango-lime cheesecake, unmolded upside down
intro: It all comes down to two temperatures: a perfectly cold mango compote and a barely warm white chocolate, otherwise the mixture liquefies and the center disperses.
ing: The zest of half a lime
titane: Mango compote is cooked in a titanium pan rather than a saucepan. The small volume spreads over a large surface, the water evaporates quickly, and the even heat prevents sticking that can cause the fruit's sugar to caramelize locally. Preheat the empty pan for 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat before adding the fruit: the mango releases its juices immediately instead of slowly settling.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 to 2 minutes over medium heat. Add the diced mango, lime juice, honey, and salt. Cook for about 6 minutes: the mango should soften and release its juices.
Dissolve the cornstarch in cold water, pour into the pan. Continue for 2 minutes over medium heat until the mixture coats the back of a spoon and becomes glossy.
Transfer the mixture (from the cooking container to stop the heat) to the blender bowl. Blend until almost smooth; a few small pieces are fine.
Refrigerate this compote until it is thoroughly cold to the touch, at least 1 hour. This is essential to prevent it from melting the mixture.
Mix the biscuit crumbs, melted coconut oil and salt until you get a wet sand texture.
Line the base of a 20cm springform pan with baking paper. Press the mixture firmly into the pan, using the back of a glass, in an even layer.
Refrigerate the crust while you prepare the filling.
Beat the cream cheese, yogurt, icing sugar, vanilla, lime zest and juice until you obtain a perfectly smooth mass, without lumps.
Pour in the melted white chocolate, lukewarm and not hot, and beat briefly to incorporate it.
Whip the cold cream separately until it forms soft peaks. Gently fold it in (using a spatula, lifting the mixture from the bottom up): the mixture should remain light and airy.
Spread half of the mixture over the crust. Place the cold compote in the center, leaving a 2 cm border. Cover with the remaining mixture and smooth it out.
Refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight. Otherwise, it will tear when unmolded.
Turn the cake upside down onto the serving plate, open the hinge, remove the mold and then the parchment paper. The crust will be on top.
Slice with a blade that has been rinsed under hot water and wiped dry between each slice. Garnish with mango slices and zest.

title: Pan-roasted broccoli cream
intro: It all comes down to the colour of the bouquets: it is this, and not the cream, that gives depth to this lactose-free soup.

ing.note: The top of the stem was cut back to 1 cm to expose the pods.
Soak for 2 hours if your blender is standard

ing: The juice of half a lemon or lime
a small handful of broccoli sprouts
titane: The titanium pan acts as an oven. Preheated empty for 2 to 3 minutes, it sears the vegetables dry before the lid takes over: the trapped steam tenderizes the center while the bottom continues to caramelize. The result is comparable to a 45-minute roast, in half the time, and in a single pan.
steps: Preheat the titanium pan empty over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. The surface must be thoroughly hot before adding any fat.
Pour over the avocado oil. Arrange the broccoli, onion, and potatoes in a single layer, without overlapping. Season with salt and pepper.
Let them cook for 5 minutes without touching them. The vegetables will release on their own when a crust has formed: that's your signal to turn them over.
Slide the garlic bulb, cut side down, between the vegetables in the pan. Reduce the heat to medium and cover.

Continue cooking, covered, for 25 minutes, stirring two or three times. The vegetables should be tender when pierced with a knife and golden brown around the edges. Remove from the heat and let cool for 15 minutes.
Remove the contents from the pan and place them in the blender. Squeeze the bulb to extract the garlic pulp and add it.
Add the dill, drained cashews, nutritional yeast, stock, coconut milk, and lemon juice. Blend to the desired consistency: a slight graininess is preferable to a perfectly smooth soup.
Taste it. Adjust the seasoning with salt and pepper, and add a few drops of lemon if it lacks tension.
Serve with a drizzle of coconut milk, chili flakes, broccoli sprouts and toasted sourdough bread.

title: Chia soup with blueberries and lemon
intro: It all comes down to the ratio of seeds to liquid and a second mixing after resting: this is what prevents lumps and gives a smooth cream rather than a mass of beads.
titane: Toast the pumpkin seeds in the titanium pan over medium heat for two to three minutes. Stir constantly. As soon as a seed pops and a nutty aroma rises, immediately transfer them to a cold plate: the pan retains heat and the seeds will burn.
steps: Plan ahead: the cream must chill for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight; start the day before if possible.
Blend the plant-based milk, yogurt, 140 g of blueberries, maple syrup, vanilla, lemon zest, and salt until you obtain a perfectly smooth mixture with a uniform purple color.
Pour in the chia seeds and stir with a spatula, scraping well the bottom of the container.
Let rest for 5 minutes, while the seeds begin to swell, then stir vigorously to break up any lumps that have formed.
Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 3 hours, preferably overnight. The cream is ready when a spoon stands upright in it for a few seconds.
Toast the pumpkin seeds before using them as garnish.
Divide between two bowls. Top with fresh blueberries, toasted pumpkin seeds, and hemp hearts.

title: Dark chocolate puffed quinoa bites
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the quinoa: if it's not really crispy when you coat it, the bite will be soft.
ing: dark chocolate in pistoles or crushed
titane: One pan is all you need for the entire recipe. The chocolate melts directly on contact with the titanium, over very low heat, without a double boiler or water: the heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots, thus eliminating the risk of graininess. The same pan, dry and piping hot, bursts the raw quinoa in seconds.
steps: Plan ahead: the bites need 30 minutes in the freezer or 1 hour in the refrigerator; allow for this time before unmolding.
Line a mini-muffin tin with paper cases, or take out a silicone mold. Set aside.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes on low heat. The temperature increase must remain gradual.

If you are popping your quinoa: pour the raw quinoa in a single layer into the hot pan, on medium-high heat, and stir continuously for 10 to 15 seconds, until the first grains pop. Transfer out of the pan immediately. If you are using store-bought popped quinoa that is slightly soft, heat it dry in the hot pan for 10 seconds to restore its crispness.
Lower to very low heat. Place the chocolate in the pan and stir with a spatula until it is smooth and completely melted, about 3 minutes. Remove from heat as soon as this point is reached.
Off the heat, fold the almond butter into the chocolate, then the popped quinoa. Mix until each grain is coated.
Divide among the cavities up to the top, press down lightly with the back of a spoon to compact. Sprinkle with a pinch of fleur de sel.
Place for 30 minutes in the freezer, or 1 hour in the refrigerator, until the chocolate is firm.
Unmold. Store in an airtight container: two weeks in the refrigerator, three months in the freezer.

title: Frittata with roasted vegetables, feta and herbs
intro: Everything hinges on the first step: really coloured vegetables in the pan, not just cooked, otherwise the frittata remains flat.
titane: The pan goes directly from stovetop to oven without transferring. Preheat the pan empty (heat it on its own, without oil) for 2 to 3 minutes, sear the raw vegetables for a nice caramelization, then cook the eggs in the same pan. All in one pan, no loss of juices.
steps: Preheat the pan empty over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Preheat the oven to 180 °C.
Rinse the courgette and bell pepper, cut them into regular dice.

Pour the grapeseed oil into the hot pan, add the vegetables, salt lightly and let them sear over high heat for 8 minutes without stirring. They are ready when they come away from the bottom on their own and have browned.
Place the pan in the oven as is, for 15 minutes at 180 °C, until the vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
Meanwhile, chop the spinach and herbs.
Whisk the eggs until you obtain a homogeneous mixture.
Salt and pepper.
Fold in the spinach, herbs and half of the feta. Mix.
Remove the pan from the oven and pour the mixture directly over the roasted vegetables.
Distribute the cherry tomato dice over the surface.
Sprinkle with the remaining feta.
Return to the oven, uncovered, for 25 minutes at 180 °C. The center should be firm and the surface lightly golden.
Let cool slightly in the pan before cutting into portions.

title: No-bake chocolate-hazelnut cheesecake
intro: It's all about the temperatures: a cream that's just simmering, a ganache that's really cold before being whipped, and a long rest that gives a clean slice.
ing: The seeds from half a vanilla pod
titane: Heat the cream for both ganaches directly in the titanium pan rather than in a saucepan. The heat rises quickly and spreads evenly across the entire surface, without any hot spots on the bottom: the chocolate emulsifies (binds into a smooth, glossy mass) without graining. The volumes are small, 100 ml then 150 ml, and the pan handles them without overflowing. Rinse and dry the pan between the two ganaches; it can be used twice.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake rests for at least 6 hours, ideally overnight, start the day before.
Blend the biscuits into fine breadcrumbs. Mix with the melted butter until you obtain a wet sand texture. Press into a 20 to 22 cm springform pan, bottom and sides if you want a border. Refrigerate.

Chop the 100 g of chocolate from the filling and set aside in a bowl. In the titanium pan over medium heat, warm the 100 ml of cream until it simmers: fine bubbles form around the edge, without boiling.
Pour the hot cream over the chocolate. Wait one minute without stirring, then mix from the center outward. Incorporate the 10 g of butter when the ganache is smooth. Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Lightly toast the hazelnuts in the rinsed and dried pan over medium heat until they are fragrant. Remove from heat (transfer to a cold plate) and let cool. Reserve one third for decoration.

Whip the cold ganache: it lightens and takes on a spreadable cream texture. Spread it over the base, scatter two thirds of the hazelnuts over it, pressing them in slightly. Return to the refrigerator.
Whip the cream cheese with the icing sugar and vanilla seeds until it is smooth. Incorporate the sweetened condensed milk.

Separately whip the 200 ml of very cold cream into a mousy texture, smooth, that holds on the whisk without stiffening. Fold it in three times with a spatula, using enveloping motions, to keep the air.
Smooth this mixture over the ganache layer. Refrigerate for 6 hours, ideally overnight.

Prepare the topping ganache using the same method: simmering cream in the titanium pan, poured over the chopped chocolate, rest for one minute, smoothing, then the butter. Let it cool until hand-warm.
Pour it over the very cold cheesecake and tilt the pan to spread it. Refrigerate for 2 to 4 hours until completely set.
Decorate with the reserved hazelnuts, whole or chopped. Slice with a blade dipped in hot water and wiped between each portion.

title: Oatmeal porridge with sautéed apples
intro: It all depends on how the apples hold up: they must brown without releasing water, then the porridge cooks in the same pan and absorbs this sweet base.
titane: The temperature rises quickly and decisively: the apple cubes brown before softening. When they easily detach from the bottom of the pan, they're caramelized. A quick wipe with paper towels, and the pan goes straight onto the porridge, without rinsing or using a second pan.
steps: Peel the apple, then cut it into regular cubes.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. The surface must be evenly hot before the first ingredient.
Pour the apple cubes into the hot pan with the honey, cinnamon, and 2 tablespoons of water. Spread them in a single layer.
Lower to medium-low heat and cook for about 9 minutes, stirring from time to time. The apples are ready when they are tender, lightly caramelized, and come away from the bottom on their own.
Remove the apples (transfer them out of the pan) to a bowl. Quickly wipe the pan with paper towel, without washing it.
Return to medium heat and pour the oats, milk, water, chia seeds, and honey. Stir continuously for about 6 minutes, until creamy and smooth texture that coats the spoon.
Pour the porridge into a bowl and top with the sautéed apples and their syrup.

title: White chocolate and hazelnut ice cream sundaes
intro: An ice cream without an ice cream maker that only works because of the stiffness of the whipped cream: if it is firm before the condensed milk is added, the texture will remain creamy when taken out of the freezer.
ing: wafer bars filled with white chocolate
titane: A titanium pan replaces a double boiler for the two chocolates in the glaze. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat, remove it from the heat, then pour in the chocolate and stir off the flame. The residual heat, evenly distributed across the bottom, is enough to melt it without ever exceeding the recommended temperature. Chocolate heated too strongly will become grainy and lose its shine: remove it from the heat as soon as it starts to melt.
steps: Plan ahead: the ice cream cups spend 5 hours in the freezer in two stages; start the day before or early in the day.

Place the bowl and whisks in the freezer for 10 minutes. Pour the cold cream, add the icing sugar and vanilla, then whip (whisk to incorporate air until the mixture holds) until you obtain firm peaks that do not collapse.

Add the hazelnut spread and sweetened condensed milk. Fold in with a spatula, lifting the mixture from underneath, until you have a smooth and homogeneous mixture. Stop as soon as the streaks of condensed milk disappear: beyond that, the cream collapses.
Divide a first layer of mixture into the ramekins. Sprinkle with chopped wafer biscuits, add a drizzle of hazelnut spread, then cover with a second layer of mixture. Smooth the surface.
Freeze for 2 hours, until the surface is firm enough to support the chocolate without sinking in.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat. Remove it from the heat, pour in the white chocolate and stir until it is fluid. Transfer into a bowl. Wipe the pan, repeat with the milk chocolate.
Coat each cup with a thin layer of white chocolate. Streak immediately with milk chocolate, then place a half wafer biscuit bar in the center before the coating sets.
Return to the freezer for at least 3 hours, until the cups are firm throughout.
Remove them 5 to 10 minutes before serving. The cream softens and regains its texture.

title: Banana, cocoa and walnut cake
intro: Everything depends on the ripeness of the bananas: if they are very spotted, almost black, they provide the sugar and moisture that the wholemeal flour absorbs.
titane: The cake is baked in the oven, in a pan; using a frying pan makes no difference. However, toast the walnuts for five minutes in a dry, very hot titanium pan before chopping them. Stir constantly, and remove them from the pan as soon as they become fragrant. Roasted, they will hold their own against the cocoa instead of being swallowed by it.
steps: Preheat the oven to 175°C. Line a loaf pan (line it with parchment paper, leaving the edges overhanging).
Mash the bananas with a fork in a large mixing bowl. Keep a few chunks; a puree that is too smooth will give you a uniform and flat crumb.
Add the eggs, milk, oil, yogurt and maple syrup. Whisk until you obtain a homogeneous mixture.

Sift the flour, cocoa, cinnamon, baking powder and bicarbonate of soda over the mixture. Mix with a spatula, lifting the batter, until no trace of flour remains. Stop there: wholemeal flour hardens quickly if you overwork it.
Fold in the walnuts and chocolate chips in two or three movements.
Pour into the loaf pan, smooth the surface. Bake for 24 to 28 minutes, until a wooden skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.
Let cool for five minutes, turn out of the pan, then place the cake on a wire rack. Wait for it to cool completely before slicing, otherwise the crumb will crumble.

title: No-bake milk chocolate tart
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the cream: steaming, never boiling, otherwise the ganache will curdle (separate into grains and fat).
titane: The cream heats up in moments in the titanium pan, without sticking or leaving a skin on the bottom. You pour it directly from the pan onto the chocolate, and rinse with clear water.
steps: Plan ahead: the tart needs to chill in the refrigerator for a minimum of 4 hours.
Finely crumble the biscuits. Mix them with the melted butter until the mixture is uniformly sandy and holds together when squeezed.
Press this mixture firmly into an 18 cm tart tin, covering the bottom and sides. Use the back of a spoon to obtain an even thickness. Refrigerate.
Pour the cream into the titanium pan. Heat over medium heat for about 3 minutes, until it smokes and simmers at the edges. It should not boil.
Place the chocolate chips in a heat-resistant bowl. Pour the hot cream over them, covering the chocolate completely. Let rest for 2 minutes without stirring.
Whisk from the centre, enlarging the circles, until you obtain a perfectly smooth ganache.
Add the butter and mix. The ganache should become shiny and silky.
Pour onto the biscuit base and smooth the surface with a spatula. Tap the tin on the work surface to remove air bubbles.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, until the ganache is set and firm to the touch.
Carefully remove from the tin, slice with a blade rinsed in hot water and wiped between each slice. Serve well chilled.

title: Black sesame ice cream
intro: It all comes down to the finesse of the mixture: a sesame paste well emulsified with coconut milk gives a dense and silky ice cream, without any cream.
titane: Before blending, place the dates in a titanium pan with two tablespoons of coconut milk over low heat for two minutes. They will swell and soften. The blender will no longer have to struggle with the fibers, and the ice cream will remain smooth even after freezing.
steps: Loosen the dates using the method described above, then let them cool for a few minutes.
Combine the coconut milk, black sesame paste, dates, vanilla, and salt in the blender. Blend for a full minute, until the mixture is smooth and coats the sides of the blender with a glossy film.
Taste it. If the sesame flavor is too overpowering, add a date and blend again for twenty seconds.
Pour into a shallow container, or into the bowl of a cycle ice cream maker. Smooth the surface, cover, and place in the freezer for at least three hours.

Without an ice cream maker: Remove the container twice during the freezing process, forty-five minutes apart, and stir vigorously with a fork, scraping the sides. This breaks up the ice crystals before they can form a solid block. With an ice cream maker: Run the reduced-fat ice cream cycle on the frozen block.

If the texture is powdery, add a tablespoon of coconut milk and run another short cycle. If the block is too hard, leave it at room temperature for ten to fifteen minutes, break it into pieces, and blend briefly.
Serve immediately, in quenelles, with the coconut flakes.

title: Tropical sorbet in a flash
intro: Everything hinges on the temperature of the fruit: they must come straight from the freezer and go directly into the vat, without the slightest waiting time.
ing: The juice of half a lemon

ing.note: plus one more line in reserve

titane: No pans here, and that's intentional: the recipe is entirely cold. The equivalent technique is mastering the contact. Work quickly, in two or three short pulses, and scrape down the sides between each pass. If the fruit starts to ooze, you're blending for too long: the sorbet will turn into a coulis and freeze solid. A very cold bowl (place it in the freezer for ten minutes beforehand) gives you a head start.
steps: Plan ahead: the sorbet spends 1 hour 30 minutes in the freezer before being served.
Remove the fruit from the freezer and pour it immediately into the food processor or blender bowl. Add the lemon juice and sweetener.
Blend using short pulses, scraping the sides with a spatula, until you obtain a smooth and homogeneous mixture. Allow one to two minutes depending on the power of the appliance.
Taste. If the fruit dominates without balance, add a few drops of lemon; if it tends toward acidity, a little honey.
Transfer into an airtight container, smooth the surface and place in the freezer for 1 hour 30 minutes.
At serving time, let it come to room temperature for 10 minutes at ambient temperature. The spoon should enter without resistance.

title: Moussey avocado and milk cake
intro: A cake without added fat, where avocado replaces butter: it all comes down to the firmness of the egg whites and how to incorporate them.

ing.note: plus a little more if the device is too firm

titane: The folding. Using a flexible spatula, move down to the center of the batter, scrape the bottom, then up the sides, turning the mixture over itself by rotating the bowl a quarter turn. Never use a circular motion: it will expel the air you just incorporated. Add the egg whites three times: the first is folded in quickly to loosen the mixture, the next two are folded in with no more than ten movements.
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C. Line a 15cm round cake tin, base and sides.
Blend the avocado with the milk and vanilla until smooth, uniformly green, and free of fibers. Incorporate the egg yolks one at a time.
Sift the flour, yeast and salt over the mixture. Mix just until no dry flour remains.

Whisk the egg whites with the lemon juice until soft peaks form (the peaks should fall back when you lift the whisk). Gradually add the sugar in three additions, continuing to whisk, until stiff, glossy peaks form.
Loosen the batter with a third of the egg whites, then fold in the rest in two stages. Stop as soon as the color is uniform.
Pour into the mold, tap twice on the work surface to pop any large bubbles. Bake for 38 minutes: a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Allow to cool completely in the mold before unmolding. Slice with a serrated knife, without pressing down.

title: Chocolate and peanut macaroons
intro: It all comes down to temperature: chocolate that melts too quickly becomes grainy and doesn't harden properly.
ing: dark or semi-sweet chocolate in lozenge form
titane: The titanium pan replaces the slow cooker and reduces melting time by three. Its rapid and even heat distribution transforms a very gentle flame into enveloping warmth: simply stir often to obtain a smooth mass, without sticking or overheating.
steps: Line two baking sheets with baking paper. Keep them within easy reach: the mixture sets quickly.
Preheat the empty titanium pan for 1 minute over very low heat, then reduce the heat one notch further. The surface should be lukewarm, never hot to the touch at 10 cm.
Pour the three chocolates and peanut butter into the pan. Do not add the peanuts at this stage.

Melt for 15 minutes over low heat, stirring regularly with a spatula from the edge towards the center. The mixture should become smooth and glossy, without lumps. If you see a dull film forming on the edge, remove the pan from the heat for 30 seconds and continue stirring.
Remove from heat and add the peanuts. Gently stir for 2 minutes, until each piece is coated. Removing the heat helps preserve their crunch.
Using an ice cream scoop, shape even portions onto the trays, spacing them 2 cm apart.
Place the trays in the freezer for 5 minutes, until the rocks set.
Peel them off the paper and arrange them on a tray.

title: Crispy chocolate cookie balls
intro: Cookie bites baked under a lid, then sitting on a layer of set dark chocolate: it's all about the size of the balls, which must remain small so that the crispness penetrates the bite.
titane: The lid transforms the pan into an oven: the heat circulates above the balls, cooking them from the top while the bottom browns. Don't touch anything. The dough will stick until a crust forms; once set, each bite will release easily. The same pan, simply wiped clean, can then be used to melt the chocolate.
steps: Cream the butter and brown sugar together (work them until you reach a smooth, pommade-like texture). Add the egg and vanilla, mix well.
Incorporate the flour all at once. Stop as soon as the dough is smooth and homogeneous.
Add both chocolates in chips, mix briefly to distribute them.
Preheat the oven.
Shape very small regular balls, the size of a hazelnut. Regularity determines the cooking result.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Add the clarified butter, it should simmer without smoking.

Place the balls well spaced apart, in small batches. Cover and cook for 12 minutes over low to medium heat, without moving them. They are ready when they detach on their own and the top takes on a lightly rosy golden color.
Remove from the pan onto a cooling rack and let cool completely.
Wipe the pan. Off the heat or over very low heat, melt the dark chocolate by stirring until you reach a smooth, glossy texture.
Pour the chocolate into small compartments or in disks on a baking sheet. Press a cooled cookie onto each disk.
Place in the freezer for 10 minutes until the chocolate sets completely.

title: Chocolate, raspberry and peanut iced bites
intro: Three layers, no baking required: it all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate and the setting time in the cold.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its heat is evenly distributed, without hot spots, allowing you to melt chocolate and coconut oil directly in it over very low heat without them sticking. The crispies are then added to the same pan, off the heat: a single container from start to finish.
steps: Plan ahead: the bites must spend at least 3 hours in the freezer, organize accordingly.
Line eight muffin tin cavities with paper liners.
Spread the melted peanut butter at the bottom of each liner in an even layer. Reserve in the freezer while you prepare the rest.
Crush the raspberries with a fork in a bowl until you obtain a coarse purée.
Add the honey and chia seeds. Mix, then let rest for 5 minutes: the seeds will swell and bind the purée.
Place a spoonful of raspberries on the peanut butter layer, without reaching the edges.
In the titanium pan, over very low heat, melt the dark chocolate with the coconut oil while stirring constantly, approximately 3 minutes. Stop as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Off the heat, fold in the soy crispies and mix to coat them.
Pour this mixture over the raspberries until the entire surface is covered.
Place in the freezer for at least 3 hours, until the bites are firm in the center.
Remove them a few minutes before serving: the peanut butter layer should become soft again under the bite.
Store the remaining bites in a freezer-safe container.

title: Eggplant gratin with tomato and three cheeses
intro: It all comes down to the eggplant: drained and then seared dry rather than fried, it retains its shape and concentrates its flavor instead of absorbing the oil.
ing: crushed tomatoes grilled over a fire
titane: The titanium pan, preheated empty, withstands the high heat needed to brown the eggplant slices: the flesh sticks, caramelizes, then releases itself. The same pan is used for the sauce, assembly, and oven transfer. A single utensil, no transferring, no wasted juices.
steps: Slice the aubergines into thin lengthwise slices. Spread them on a kitchen towel, salt generously on both sides and let them drain (allow the salt to draw out the vegetable water) for 1 hour 30 minutes. Droplets will form on the surface.
Rinse the slices under cold water to remove the salt. Dry them carefully between two kitchen towels or on paper towels: a damp slice will steam rather than brown.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Preheat the oven to 200 °C.

Brush the slices with avocado oil using a brush. Sear them in small batches, in a single layer, for 15 minutes in total, turning them as soon as the flesh detaches on its own and displays a golden side. Remove them (set aside off the heat) as you go.
Lower to medium heat, wipe the pan if it has stuck too much, then sweat the onion (cook gently without browning) for 5 minutes, until it becomes translucent.
Peel the garlic before crushing it. Add it with the olive oil and a few basil leaves. Stir and let infuse for 2 to 3 minutes, allowing the garlic to release its fragrance without browning.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt and pepper. Let simmer over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, until the sauce coats the spoon.
Set aside two thirds of the sauce. In the pan, layer: aubergines, sauce, mozzarella, basil leaves, parmesan. Repeat until used up and top with provolone.
Put the pan as is into the oven at 200 °C for 20 minutes, until the top is melted and golden. Let rest for 10 minutes before serving: the layers will hold together when cut.

title: Greek yogurt pan cheesecake
intro: Everything depends on the gentleness of the heat: if it's too hot, the egg mixture coagulates and becomes grainy, whereas it should remain silky.
titane: The preheated titanium pan, then covered, acts as an oven: the heat circulates under the lid and envelops the mixture without drying it out, while direct contact with the metal gives the base a golden color. From raw mixture to cooled dessert, no transferring is required.
steps: Plan ahead: refrigeration rest of at least 1 hour 30 minutes after cooking, account for this time in your schedule.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat. Brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter: the surface should shimmer slightly, without smoking.
In a bowl, whisk together the Greek yogurt, eggs, vanilla and honey until you obtain a smooth and silky batter. Work just enough to homogenize, without incorporating air.
Remove the pan from the heat, pour in the preparation, smooth the surface.
Return to very low heat, cover and let cook for 28 minutes. The edges should be set, the center still slightly trembling.
Away from the heat, let cool completely in the pan. Transfer gently to a dish and refrigerate for 1 hour 30 minutes minimum.
Garnish with red berries at the last moment.

title: White chocolate, pistachio and cranberry fudge
intro: It all comes down to the gentleness of the heat: white chocolate turns grainy as soon as it exceeds its working temperature, and a failed fudge is a fudge heated too quickly.
titane: The titanium pan replaces both a saucepan and a double boiler. Its heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots: white chocolate, condensed milk, and butter melt together in minutes, without sticking. Preheat it empty for 1 to 2 minutes over low heat to stabilize the surface before adding anything, then maintain this low heat throughout. Dried fruit can be added directly to the pan, off the heat: no need to dirty any intermediate containers.
steps: Plan ahead: the fudge rests for 3 hours in the refrigerator, start the day before or well in advance.
Line a 20 cm square mold with parchment paper, leaving two strips overhanging on the sides: they will be used to unmold.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, low heat, for 1 to 2 minutes. The heat must be built up before adding the first ingredient.

Add the white chocolate, condensed milk and butter. Stir continuously with a flexible spatula for about 6 minutes. The mixture should become smooth, shiny, and lump-free. If it thickens suddenly or becomes grainy, remove from heat for a few seconds and continue stirring.
Off the heat, add the whole pistachios and cranberries. Mix gently, just enough to distribute them.
Transfer the preparation out of the pan into the mold. Smooth the surface with the spatula, pushing the mixture well into the corners.
Sprinkle with crushed pistachios and press them lightly with the flat of your hand so they adhere.
Refrigerate for 3 hours, or 45 minutes in the freezer, until the fudge is firm to the touch.
Unmold by pulling on the parchment strips. Cut into 16 squares with a sharp knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Flourless chocolate-avocado brownies, cooked in a skillet
intro: Here, avocado replaces butter and flour: everything depends on its ripeness and a short cooking time that leaves the center melting.

ing.note: the flesh should yield under the thumb

titane: The covered pan works like a miniature oven. The bare metal, preheated empty and then greased, transmits direct heat that forms a thin crust on the surface, while the steam trapped under the lid gently cooks the center. For a dough of this size, there's no need to preheat an entire oven.
steps: Heat the skillet empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat. Lightly brush it with clarified butter or grapeseed oil, fats that can withstand heat without browning.
Peel and pit the avocado. Blend its flesh with the eggs, cocoa, honey, vanilla and salt. Continue until you obtain a batter that is perfectly smooth, glossy and creamy, with no green streaks.
Pour the batter into the hot skillet. Smooth the surface with a spatula for even thickness.

Cover and cook for 20 minutes over low heat. The edges should be set and pull away from the sides on their own, the center remaining slightly soft to the touch. Avoid prolonging the cooking time: it is overcooking that dries them out.
Remove from heat and let cool completely in the skillet, about 30 minutes, before cutting. The brownies firm up as they cool.

intro:
# Frontmatter

```yaml
---
title: "Fattoush with Crispy Bread Spirals"
servings: 4
prep_time_min: 20
cook_time_min: 6
theme_candidates:

- Mediterranean

- World Cuisine
needs_review: true
---
```

It's all about contrast: large, cold, chopped vegetables, bread that's still warm and crisp, and an acidic vinaigrette that should only be added at the very last moment.

ing.note: cut in half and then thinly sliced

ing: cup of extra virgin olive oil
titane: The preheated titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat when the bread is added. The spirals brown in a single layer, without oil, and form a dry crust. One rule only: don't touch them. As long as they stick, they're not ready. When they release easily, flip them over.
steps: Cut all the vegetables into pieces of a similar size, large enough to remain crisp under the vinaigrette. Keep chilled.
Finely chop the parsley, mint and green onion.
Combine olive oil, pomegranate molasses, lemon juice, sumac, and salt in a jar. Seal and shake for about ten seconds to emulsify (bind the fat and acid into a homogeneous mixture). Set aside.
Roll the Lebanese bread tightly on itself, then slice the roll into spirals of about 0.5 cm.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, over medium-high heat, for 2 to 3 minutes.

Pour the grapeseed oil into the pan and arrange the spirals in a single layer. Let them brown undisturbed until they release their contents. Turn them over and brown the other side. Cook for a total of 5 minutes. It's best to cook them in two batches rather than overcrowding the pan.
Remove the spirals from the pan to stop the cooking process and place them on a wire rack. They will finish drying as they cool.
Place all the vegetables and herbs in a large salad bowl. Drizzle with vinaigrette.
Mix by hand, thoroughly, to coat without crushing.
Sprinkle with pomegranate seeds, and place the bread spirals on top just before serving. Not before: they soften in two minutes.

title: Cranberry and strawberry trifle
intro: It all comes down to the jelly: a juice heated gently, a perfectly dissolved gelatin, and the layers will hold neatly in the glass.
titane: The juice and honey heat evenly in the titanium pan, over a wide, responsive surface. The heat is distributed without any hot spots, the gelatin dissolves instantly, and nothing sticks to the bottom. No preheating is needed here: we're working with a liquid, not a sear.
steps: Plan ahead: the cranberry jelly sets in the cold for 2 hours 30 minutes, then the assembled trifle rests for a further 30 minutes before serving. Begin this recipe several hours before serving.
Pour 120 ml of cranberry juice into a bowl. Sprinkle the gelatin in a steady stream and whisk immediately to prevent lumps.
Leave to bloom for 7 minutes away from heat. The gelatin should become spongy and opaque.
Pour the remaining juice into the titanium pan, add the honey and place over low heat. Whisk for 8 minutes, until the first sign of simmering, never allowing it to boil.
Remove from heat. Fold in the bloomed gelatin and whisk until completely dissolved: the liquid should become perfectly clear again.
Transfer to a glass container using a flexible spatula, scraping the sides. Refrigerate for 2 hours 30 minutes, until firmly set.

Cut the set jelly into cubes. Assemble the trifle in a large glass or serving glasses with the hulled strawberries cut in half: sponge cake, pastry cream, strawberries, jelly cubes, then whipped cream. Repeat until full and finish with cream.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving, allowing time for the sponge cake to soak up the juices.

title: Golden tofu banh mi
intro: It all comes down to the tofu crust: a very hot pan, a few slices at a time, and no intervention during searing.

ing.note: peeled and cut into julienne strips (thin strips)
peeled and cut into julienne strips

titane: Preheat the pan empty for two to three minutes before adding the oil. Titanium cookware heats up quickly and evenly: the tofu contracts on contact, forms a crust, and releases easily. A slice that resists is not ready. Wait.
steps: Combine the carrot and daikon in a jar. Pour in the vinegar, hot water, honey, and salt. Seal, shake, and let sit for at least 10 minutes. The vegetables should remain crisp.
Mix together the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, garlic, and pepper. Coat the tofu slices with this mixture and let them soak in while you prepare the rest.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Add the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.

Arrange the tofu slices in a single layer, without crowding them. Work in two batches. Let them brown for 4 minutes without touching them, turn them over when the tofu releases easily, then cook for another 4 minutes.
Remove from pan and set aside on a wire rack to keep the crust clean.
Open the buns, spread with Kewpie mayonnaise. Arrange the cucumber, well-drained pickles, tofu, then the coriander and chili. Close and press lightly.

title: Banana Fudge
intro: It all comes down to how long the sugar is cooked: too short, and the fudge stays soft; too long, and it becomes grainy.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the heavy-bottomed saucepan. Its large surface area and conductivity distribute heat evenly without hot spots, preventing the syrup from sticking and crystallizing unevenly. Preheat it for 2 to 3 minutes empty, over medium heat, before adding the liquids.
steps: Line a 23cm square baking tin with baking paper, leaving two strips hanging over the edges. No need for grease, the paper is sufficient.
In a bowl, mix the banana flavoring and gel coloring. Set aside. The gel colors without thinning the mixture.
Preheat the titanium pan empty, 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat.
Pour in the butter, milk, single cream, double cream, and vanilla extract. Stir with a spatula until the butter is completely melted.

Add the sugar all at once. Stir continuously until it just begins to simmer, 6 to 7 minutes, then simmer for another 3 minutes. The mixture should bubble steadily and lightly coat the back of a spoon.
Remove from heat. Add the white chocolate chips, cover, and let stand for 3 to 4 minutes, until melted but not burning. Stir until smooth.
Incorporate the marshmallow cream, then the flavouring-colouring mixture. Work until the colour is uniform, without overmixing.
Spread immediately in the mold with a spatula. Sprinkle with crushed biscuits and cover with aluminum foil.
Let it set for 30 minutes at room temperature, then refrigerate for at least 4 hours. Unmold by pulling on the paper strips and cut into 25 squares.

title: Dark chocolate date squares
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: if it's too hot, it turns white as it solidifies and loses its crunch.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Its heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots: over very low heat, the chocolate melts in two to three minutes, without lumps or sticking to the bottom. You then pour it directly from the pan, without transferring it.
steps: Place the pitted dates in a silicone mold. Crush them with your fingertips, then spread them into an even layer about 5 mm thick. Smooth the edges; this is where the thickness will be.
Mix the chopped dried fruit and seeds in a bowl. Keep within easy reach: the chocolate sets quickly.

Place the chopped chocolate in the cold titanium pan. Set over very low heat and stir continuously with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is smooth and glossy, before the last pieces melt: the residual heat will finish the job.
Pour the chocolate over the dates and spread into a thin, even layer.
Immediately sprinkle with the mixture of dried fruit and seeds. Press lightly with the palm of your hand to make them adhere.
Refrigerate for 45 minutes, until the chocolate is completely set. Unmold and cut into squares with a paring knife that has been dipped in hot water and dried.

title: Chocolate, pistachio and toasted coconut eggs
intro: It all comes down to the roasting of the coconut: it's what gives depth to a filling that would otherwise be too mild.
titane: The titanium pan, thin and responsive, heats up quickly: perfect for dry-roasting coconut. Preheat it for one minute over medium-low heat, without any oil or butter, then add the coconut and stir constantly. Remove from the pan as soon as it turns golden brown; the residual heat will continue to heat the coconut.
steps: Melt the chocolate in a bain-marie, or in the microwave at 30-second intervals, stirring between each. Stop when the mixture is smooth and glossy.
Pour half of the chocolate into a silicone egg-shaped mould. Tilt the mould to coat the bottom and slightly up the sides.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes, until the chocolate is set to the touch.

Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over medium-low heat. Add the coconut and stir regularly for 3 to 5 minutes, until golden and fragrant with a nutty aroma. Transfer immediately to a cold bowl.
Mix the pistachio butter into the coconut while still warm. Stir until you have a homogeneous paste.
Divide the filling among the moulds, smooth the top with the back of a spoon, then cover with the remaining melted chocolate.
Refrigerate for 1 hour. Unmould by gently pushing the silicone up from underneath.
Store the eggs in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 10 days, or in the freezer for up to 3 months.

title: Crispy quinoa, crunchy vegetables and tahini-ginger sauce
intro: It all comes down to the quinoa: it must sizzle in a thin layer and detach itself from the pan, otherwise the salad remains soggy.
titane: The titanium pan heats up in two minutes and transfers heat by direct contact: the quinoa toasts where it touches. Spread it in a thin layer, leave it alone, and wait for it to release on its own. As long as it sticks, it's not ready. This signal replaces the oven and its twenty minutes of preheating.
steps: Mix the cold quinoa with the teriyaki sauce and sesame oil. Work with a fork to separate the grains.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. It is ready when a water droplet dances across it before evaporating.
Pour the grapeseed oil, lower to medium-high heat. Spread the quinoa in a thin layer and leave it untouched for 3 to 4 minutes, until it detaches on its own and shows a golden crust.
Stir, spread again, repeat by sections. Allow 10 to 12 minutes total. The quinoa should crackle like dry seeds in the pan.
Transfer the quinoa to a large bowl and let it cool to room temperature in the air: it continues to dry.

Wipe the pan with paper towel, place it back on medium heat. Toast the cashews dry for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring regularly, until golden in colour and with a hazelnut aroma. Remove them immediately, they burn quickly.

Peel and grate the garlic and ginger. In a small jar, combine tahini, rice vinegar, teriyaki sauce, sesame oil, grated garlic and ginger. Close and shake until you obtain a smooth sauce. If it thickens too much, thin it with a spoonful of cold water.
Thinly slice the red cabbage, cut the bell pepper into strips, grate the carrots into julienne, slice the green onions on the bias and chop the parsley or coriander.

Add the cabbage, bell pepper, carrots, green onions and herbs to the quinoa. Pour the sauce, mix by hand or with two spoons, sprinkle with crushed cashews. Serve right away, while the quinoa is still crispy.

title: Chocolate skillet cake
intro: A muffin batter poured into a hot pan: the bottom takes on a thin caramelized crust while the top keeps the center soft.

ing.note: plus a handle for the surface

ing: A little clarified butter or high smoke point oil for the pan
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat before greasing. Titanium heats up quickly and retains heat: it's this immediate contact with the heat that creates the crust on the cake. Once the batter is poured in, don't touch anything. No spatula, no stirring, the lid does the rest.
steps: Combine flour, cocoa, sugar, yeast and salt in a large bowl. Mix dry to distribute the yeast.
Add the egg, milk, and oil. Whisk until you have a smooth batter, but don't overmix; stop as soon as the flour has disappeared. Gently fold in the chocolate chips with a spatula.
