Preheat the titanium pan empty, over low-medium heat, for 2 to 3 minutes. Lightly brush it with clarified butter (melted butter with the whey removed, which can withstand high temperatures) or oil with a high smoke point.
Pour the batter all at once and spread it into an even layer about 2 cm thick. Sprinkle the remaining chocolate chips on top. Do not stir.
Cover and reduce heat to low. Cook for 18 minutes. The surface should no longer stick to your finger and a knife inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let it cool for 5 minutes in the pan off the heat, then cut into portions directly in the pan.

title: Chocolate banana-coconut cookies
intro: Three ingredients, no flour: it all comes down to the ripeness of the bananas, which provide the sugar and the binding agent.
titane: A preheated, empty pan, then covered, replaces the oven: the bottom caramelizes while the trapped steam cooks the center. Once the cookies are removed, the same pan, wiped dry and still warm, serves as an improvised bain-marie for the chocolate. Zero extra dishes to wash.
steps: Heat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, without any fat.
Mash the bananas with a fork in a mixing bowl until you obtain a purée with no large lumps.
Incorporate the grated coconut and honey or maple syrup if you are using it. Mix until the mixture holds together between your fingers.
Shape about ten small discs by hand, then flatten them slightly. Aim for 1 cm thickness: thicker, and the centre stays moist.

Brush the hot pan with coconut oil. Place the discs without crowding them, cover and cook for 6 minutes over medium-low heat. The cookie is ready to be flipped when the bottom detaches on its own and has turned golden brown.
Flip each cookie with a flick of the wrist, cover again and continue for 6 minutes, until even golden browning on both sides. Work in small batches so the pan does not lose heat.
Transfer the cookies onto a rack and let cool completely.
Wipe the still-warm pan with absorbent paper. Over very low heat, melt the dark chocolate with coconut oil, stirring, for approximately 3 minutes, until it is smooth and shiny.
Drizzle the cooled cookies with melted chocolate, in a stream or with a spoon.
Place in the refrigerator for 10 minutes while the chocolate sets.

title: Brussels sprouts sautéed with parmesan
intro: Everything depends on the cut side: it must touch the hot metal and remain still long enough to caramelize.
titane: The titanium pan heats up quickly and retains its heat even when the cabbage arrives cold. The cut side sticks for a few seconds, then releases itself as soon as the crust has formed: that's the signal. The lid then takes over and steams the center while the Parmesan melts.
steps: Wash the cabbages, remove the stem ends and any damaged leaves. Cut them in half lengthwise.
Bring a saucepan of 400 ml of salted water to a boil. Blanch the cabbage for 5 minutes (a short cooking time in boiling water to soften without browning).
Drain, then dry them thoroughly with a tea towel. Damp cabbage won't crisp up.
Preheat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Then pour in the oil: it should spread evenly and ripple slightly.
Meanwhile, coat the dried cabbage with paprika, salt, pepper and chili flakes in a salad bowl.
Arrange them cut-side down in the pan, without crowding them. Cook in two batches if necessary. Do not touch them for 6 minutes: they will detach on their own once a crust has formed.
Turn them over, and spread the parmesan directly over the cabbage.

Cover, reduce heat to medium-low, and cook for 8 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden brown and a knife inserted into a cabbage roll meets no resistance. Remove from the pan immediately to maintain its crispness.

title: Caramel cheesecake with a chocolate biscuit crust
intro: It's all about slowness: a barely mixed mixture, gentle cooking with steam in the oven, and gradual cooling to prevent cracking.
ing: very cold heavy cream + 30g icing sugar + 1 tsp
Caramel candies coated in milk chocolate
titane: Before pressing the crust, toast the biscuit crumbs in the titanium pan with the butter over medium heat for two minutes, stirring constantly. The butter coats each crumb, and the cocoa releases its bitterness. You'll get a drier crust that cuts more cleanly and won't absorb the filling.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake cools and then stays in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours, ideally overnight; start the day before.

Preheat the oven to 175 °C. Lightly butter the 23 cm springform pan, then line it: parchment paper on the bottom, two large sheets of aluminium folded up and fitted tightly around the outside without tearing. This is your watertight seal.
Reduce the biscuits to fine crumbs. Toast them (coat with fat until damp sand texture) in the titanium pan with the melted butter and salt, 2 minutes over medium heat.
Pour into the pan. Pack firmly on the bottom and 2 cm up the sides, using the back of a glass. Bake for 10 minutes, then lower the oven to 160 °C and leave the crust inside.
Beat the cream cheese alone, 2 minutes, until perfectly smooth and creamy. Add the sugar, beat 1 minute more.
Incorporate the eggs one by one, at low speed, waiting for each to be absorbed. Do not aim to add air: any air incorporated here will make the cake puff up then crack.
Add the vanilla, cream and flour. Mix just until combined, then stop.

Place a dish filled with boiling water on the lower oven rack. Pour the batter onto the still-warm crust, smooth the top, and bake on the middle rack. Allow 60 minutes at 160 °C: the edges are set, the centre still jiggles as one block about 8 cm in diameter.
Turn off the oven, keep the door closed, and leave the cheesecake inside for 30 minutes.
Remove it, let it come back to room temperature on the work surface for 1 hour, then refrigerate for at least 8 hours, ideally overnight.
Just before serving, warm the dulce de leche with the 45 ml of cream, 30 seconds in the microwave, and mix until you get a smooth, glossy sauce. Let come back to room temperature.

Unmould, spread the caramel on top leaving a 1 cm border. Unwrap the caramel sweets. Whip the cold cream with the icing sugar until firm peaks form, pipe rosettes around the edge and top each with a caramel sweet.
Slice with a large knife dipped in hot water and wiped between each serving.

title: Apple-caramel cookies, cooked in a pan
intro: No flour, no oven: the texture comes from cashews and date caramel, and the entire success hinges on a low and constant heat.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty, then reduced to medium-low heat and covered, it cooks the cookies by conduction from below and trapped steam from above: the base browns, the center remains soft. The chocolate then melts in the same pan, over very low heat, without adding any dishes.
steps: Blend the dates, almond butter and water until you obtain a perfectly smooth cream. Remove 60 ml for the batter, reserve the rest.
Peel the apple then cut it into small dice. Roughly chop the cashews.
Whisk the egg in a bowl, incorporate the date caramel, then the chopped cashews, apple dice, coconut and cinnamon. Mix until the batter is homogeneous.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then remove it from the heat while you shape the cookies.
Place portions of batter in the lightly cooled pan, spaced two finger widths apart, and flatten them with a spoon to 1 cm thickness. Work in small batches: this is the condition for even thickness.

Cover and cook over low to medium heat for approximately 14 minutes. The cashews should brown and become fragrant, the bottom should take on color. Turn each cookie only when it detaches on its own from the bottom. Watch carefully: the pan heats up faster than an oven, the cashews burn in just a few seconds.
Off the heat, let the cookies cool in the pan for 5 to 10 minutes, then remove them (transfer them out of the cooking vessel) onto a rack until completely cooled.

Wipe the pan, chop the chocolate and melt it inside over very low heat while stirring constantly, or in a double boiler if you prefer to control the temperature. Coat the cooled cookies, add the rest of the date caramel in a drizzle and fleur de sel. Let set for 20 minutes.

title: Sugar-free white pecan fudge
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the melted chocolate: if it's too hot, it will liquefy the cream cheese and the fudge will never set.
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat before adding the pecans. The titanium surface heats up evenly and toasts the nuts dry, without oil or sticking: the aroma is more pronounced, and the color remains uniform from edge to edge.
steps: Plan ahead: the fudge requires 3 hours 30 minutes in the refrigerator before it can be cut.
Line a square 13 cm mold with parchment paper, leaving the paper well overhanging on two opposite sides: these will serve as handles for unmolding.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat.

Pour the crushed pecans into the hot pan. Toast them dry while stirring constantly, approximately 3 minutes, until the aroma rises. Remove immediately (transfer to a cold bowl to stop cooking) and let cool completely.
Beat the softened cream cheese until it is perfectly smooth, without lumps.
Melt the white chocolate in the microwave in 15 to 20 second intervals, stirring between each. Stop as soon as it is smooth and let it cool for 2 minutes.
Incorporate the cooled chocolate into the cream cheese, in a thin stream, at low speed. Stop as soon as the mixture is homogeneous.
Add the cooled pecans and the salt. Mix with a spatula, using broad strokes, so as not to break the texture.
Pour into the mold, smooth in an even layer. Place whole pecans in a three by three grid, one for each future square.

Refrigerate for 3 hours 30 minutes, until the mixture is firm to the touch. Unmold by pulling on the paper, then cut into 9 thick squares, dipping the knife in hot water and wiping it between each cut.

title: No-bake layered brownie cake
intro: It all comes down to temperature: a brownie that is still warm liquefies the cream and the layers mix instead of overlapping.

ing.note: plus the ingredients listed on the package
in addition to the recipe in the package

titane: The titanium pan is oven-safe: it bakes the brownie base, then becomes the assembly mold. You can layer cream, flan, and whipped cream in the same container, from oven to refrigerator, without ever unmolding or transferring.
steps: Plan ahead: the cake cools for one hour then sets for at least four hours in the refrigerator, ideally overnight, start the day before if possible.
Preheat the oven according to the brownie mix instructions. Prepare the batter following these instructions, then add the extra egg: the crumb will be denser, therefore more stable under the layers.
Pour the batter into the titanium pan and bake for the indicated time. The center should remain slightly soft when tested with a knife blade.
Place the pan on a rack and let cool completely, at least one hour. No layer should be mounted on a warm base.
Meanwhile, beat the fresh cheese with the icing sugar until you obtain a smooth mixture, without graininess.
Fold in half of the whipped topping using a spatula (lifting motion from bottom to top, to keep the air trapped).
Spread this cream over the cold brownie, directly in the pan. Smooth to the edges.
Whip the two custard preparations with the cold milk for exactly 2 minutes. The mixture should coat the whisk without running.
Pour the custard onto the cream layer, using a ladle, placing it rather than pouring it forcefully. Smooth.
Cover with the remaining whipped topping, in an even layer.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, ideally overnight, until the whole is firm to the touch.
Shave the chocolate into shards over the top. Cut the portions in the pan, serve well chilled.

title: Oat, apple and spice bars
intro: It all comes down to the grated apple with its skin: it's what keeps the crumb moist for the next three days.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a square mold and goes directly from the worktop to the oven without transfer. Preheat it empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then remove it from the heat to grease it: the dough starts cooking as soon as it touches the surface, the edges set cleanly and release easily, without parchment paper.
steps: Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Whisk the egg in a large bowl. Add the applesauce, almond butter, maple syrup, milk, grated apple, and vanilla. Whisk until the mixture (the liquid base) is smooth and free of lumps of almond butter.
Add the oats, almond flour, spices, baking soda, nuts, and half the chocolate chips. Mix with a spatula, just until combined.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Remove it from the heat and lightly grease it.
Pour the batter into the hot pan, smooth the surface with a spatula, and sprinkle with the remaining chocolate chips.
Place the pan in the oven as is for 32 minutes at 180°C: the edges should be firm and a knife tip should come out clean in the center.
Let cool completely in the pan placed on a wire rack, then cut 12 squares directly from the pan. Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to one week.

title: Raspberry, cottage cheese and dark chocolate clusters
intro: It all comes down to temperature: a very smooth mixture, really firm clusters, chocolate that's just melted — otherwise the dipping turns into a soggy glaze.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Over very low heat, the heat is evenly distributed without any hot spots: the chocolate melts without sticking or graining on contact with the metal. The thin base also works in the other direction—as soon as you remove it from the heat, the temperature drops quickly and stabilizes, giving you the perfect window for dipping.
steps: Plan ahead: the clusters go in the freezer for one hour before being coated in chocolate.
Blend the cottage cheese with the vanilla and maple syrup, using a blender or immersion blender. Process until perfectly smooth, with no grainy texture. Taste and adjust the sugar as needed.
Add the raspberries. Mix with a spatula using broad strokes to distribute them without crushing them completely — a few rosy streaks are desirable.
Spoon the mixture onto a baking sheet lined with baking paper, in small regular mounds. Space them two centimetres apart.
Place in the freezer for 1 hour, until the clusters are firm to the touch.
Break the chocolate into the titanium pan. Over very low heat, stir continuously until you obtain a smooth, flowing mass.
Remove the pan from the heat. Dip the frozen clusters one by one into the chocolate, let them rest for a few seconds on the paper: the contact with the cold sets the coating almost instantly.
Keep in the freezer for up to three months. Remove them 10 to 15 minutes before serving, or let them thaw in the refrigerator.

title: Gyros with halloumi, spiced honey and tzatziki
intro: Everything hinges on the halloumi crust: one side seared without touching it, honey poured at the end of cooking so that it caramelizes without burning.

ing.note: plus a little something for the finishing touch

titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding any oil. Titanium heats up quickly and retains its temperature when the cold cheese is added: the halloumi develops a clean crust and releases easily, without sticking or residue to scrape off afterwards.
steps: Squeeze the grated cucumber between your hands over the sink to remove excess water. Mix it with the yogurt, dill, mint, garlic, lemon juice and olive oil. Season with salt and reserve in the refrigerator.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat, then pour in the grapeseed oil. It should shimmer slightly, not smoke.
Lay the halloumi slices flat and do not touch them for 2 minutes. As long as the cheese sticks, the crust has not formed: if you force it, it will remain in the pan.
When the slices release themselves, drizzle them with honey, sprinkle with chilli flakes and flip them over. Allow 2 more minutes for the second side to brown and the honey to thicken.
Remove the halloumi from the pan and set it aside on a warm plate.
Lower to very low heat, or turn off the heat. Pass the pitas through the still hot pan, 30 seconds per side, just to soften them.
Spread a spoonful of tzatziki in the bottom of each pita, add the lettuce and diced tomato.
Place the halloumi on top, coat with a second spoonful of tzatziki and finish with a little dill. Serve immediately: the halloumi loses its crispiness as it cools.

title: Fudgy Beetroot Brownies
intro: The beetroot provides the moisture that the flour does not retain: it is what gives this dense and supple center, provided that the cooking is not overdone.
titane: The pan replaces the oven. Preheated empty and then covered, it radiates a gentle, enveloping heat: the top sears thanks to the steam trapped under the lid, while the bottom caramelizes lightly, without sticking. Turn off the heat when the center is still jiggling; the titanium's thermal inertia will finish the job.
steps: Blend the beetroot with the maple syrup, olive oil, eggs and vanilla. Process until you obtain a perfectly smooth puree, with no visible fibers.
Add the cocoa, almond flour, baking soda and salt. Mix until just combined, no more.
Fold in the chocolate chips with a spatula.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 minutes over low-medium heat. Brush the bottom and sides with clarified butter.
Pour the batter into the pan, smooth the surface, and cover. Cook for 24 minutes over low heat. The top should be matte and set, the center still soft to the touch.
Remove from the heat and let cool slightly in the pan. The edges will pull away from the sides on their own: this is the signal to unmold onto a board. Cut into 16 pieces.

title: Strawberry and chocolate ice cream bites
intro: It all comes down to the thinness of the shell: melted chocolate that is too hot thickens as it cools and breaks the bite instead of allowing you to bite into it.
titane: The titanium pan acts as a double boiler. Its heat rises quickly and distributes evenly without hot spots: the chocolate chips melt in three minutes over very low heat, without lumps or burnt bits at the bottom. Stir continuously with a spatula and remove the pan from the heat as soon as two-thirds of the chips have melted—the residual heat finishes the job and prevents the chocolate from becoming dull and thick.
steps: Plan ahead: the bites require two hours in the freezer, so organize accordingly.
Line a muffin tin with paper cases, one per bite. Reserve it in the freezer while preparing the mixture: the chocolate will set faster on a cold surface.
Blend the cottage cheese, strawberries and sweetener until perfectly smooth, with no visible cheese grains. Count on a good minute in the blender, scraping the sides once.

Place the titanium pan on very low heat. Pour in the chocolate chips and stir continuously for approximately 3 minutes, until you have smooth, flowing chocolate. Remove from heat before completely melted and finish off the heat.
Remove the tin. Deposit a teaspoonful of chocolate at the bottom of each case, then tilt them to make the chocolate rise about half a centimeter up the side.
Freeze for 5 minutes, until the base is set and matte.
Distribute the strawberry mixture over the set bases, without exceeding the edges. Smooth with a small spoon.
Coat with the remaining chocolate, covering well right to the edges to seal the filling. If the chocolate has thickened, place the pan back on the heat for 20 seconds, still warm, off the heat.

Freeze for at least 2 hours, until the bites are firm to the touch. Unmold and let rest for 3 minutes at room temperature before serving: the filling regains its melt-in-the-mouth quality, the shell retains its crispness.

title: No-bake chocolate and peanut butter bars
intro: It all depends on the pressure exerted on the base: if not packed tightly, it crumbles when cut.
titane: The titanium pan replaces the double boiler. Placed over very low heat, it heats up quickly and distributes the heat evenly without hot spots: the chocolate melts in three minutes, without needing an extra bowl. Remove it from the heat when a few whole pieces remain; the metal's thermal inertia will finish the job.
steps: Plan ahead: refrigeration lasts at least two hours, plan your schedule accordingly.
Mix the coconut oil, honey, almond powder and cocoa in a bowl. Work with a spatula until you obtain a homogeneous, supple paste that holds together between your fingers.
Line a rectangular mould with baking paper. Pour in the paste and press it firmly, using the back of a spoon or the bottom of a glass, until you have a flat and compact base.
Mix the peanut butter and crushed peanuts.
Spread this layer over the base, smoothing it well to the edges.

Melt the chocolate in the titanium pan over very low heat, stirring constantly. Remove from heat as soon as the first streaks disappear and continue smoothing off the heat: the chocolate must be glossy and fluid, never smoking.
Coat (cover with an even layer) directly from the pan, then tilt the mould to spread.
Refrigerate until the whole thing is firm to the touch, at least two hours.
Unmould by pulling on the paper and cut into bars with a knife dipped in hot water and dried.

title: Mini apple cheesecakes with oat crumble
intro: Three textures in one mold: a compact base, a smooth filling and a dry crumble — it all comes down to the gentle cooking of the center, which must remain just set.
ing: Greek yogurt or soured thick cream
titane: Toast the oat-butter-brown sugar mixture in a titanium pan over medium heat for 4 to 5 minutes before sprinkling it over the cheesecakes. Stir constantly until the flakes turn golden and smell nutty. The crumble goes into the oven already crispy: it won't soften from the filling and will retain its bite after chilling.
steps: Preheat the oven to 165°C. Line 12 muffin tin cavities with paper baking cups.
Mix the biscuit crumbs, melted butter, and spoonful of sugar. Divide the mixture among the baking cups and press down firmly with the bottom of a shot glass. The base should be compact and flat.
Bake for 6 minutes, until the crusts have set. Remove them and let them cool slightly while you prepare the rest.
Cream the cream cheese and sugar together with a mixer at medium speed (cream: work until smooth and homogeneous). Two minutes is enough. Scrape down the sides of the bowl.

Add the vanilla and yogurt, and mix briefly. Finally, incorporate the egg at the lowest speed, just until the yellow streaks disappear. Too much air at this stage will cause the cheesecakes to rise and then crack.
Distribute the mixture over the crusts, filling the baking cups three-quarters full.
Mix the diced apples with the cinnamon and half of the brown sugar.

Rub the oats, cold butter, and remaining brown sugar together with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse breadcrumbs. Toast this mixture in a pan as described above, then transfer it to a cold plate.
Place a spoonful of apples on each cheesecake, then top with crumble.
Bake for 22 to 25 minutes. The centers should be set but still slightly wobbly when touched on the mold.
Allow to cool completely to room temperature, including the mold. Then refrigerate for at least 3 hours, ideally overnight. Serve chilled, either in the mold or unmolded.

title: Pistachio, buckwheat and dark chocolate bites
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the base: blended enough to withstand pressure, coarse enough to retain some texture.

ing.note: plus a handle for the top
only if the pistachios are unsalted

titane: The chocolate melts without a double boiler. Place the titanium pan over very low heat, pour in the chopped chocolate, and stir continuously with a spatula. The metal mass is thin and reacts quickly: as soon as a third of the pieces have melted, remove from the heat and let the residual heat finish the job. You'll get smooth, glossy chocolate, never grainy.
steps: Plan ahead: the bouchées must rest for 30 minutes in the refrigerator before unmoulding.

Combine pistachios, buckwheat, dates, coconut oil and cinnamon in a food processor. Process until you obtain a fine, sticky mixture that holds together when you press it between two fingers. Taste: add a pinch of salt if the pistachios are unsalted.
Line a mini-muffin tin (line the moulds with paper cases) or use a silicone mould. Place one tablespoon of mixture in each mould and press firmly with your thumb or the back of a spoon.

Place the titanium pan over very low heat. Pour the chopped chocolate in and stir constantly with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat as soon as the first pieces melt and continue stirring off the heat until the surface is smooth and glossy.
Distribute the chocolate over each bouchée. Sprinkle with crushed pistachios while the chocolate is still soft.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, until the chocolate is set. Unmould.
Store the bouchées in the refrigerator, or in the freezer for longer storage.

title: Chocolate mounds with rice crackers
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: if it's too hot, it loses its shine and the crackers soften.
ing: neutral oil or melted cocoa butter
titane: The titanium pan acts as a double boiler. Its thick base heats up quickly and maintains a consistent temperature: over low heat, the chocolate melts in three minutes without ever exceeding its maximum temperature. It then serves as a mixing bowl, off the heat. A single utensil is all you need, from the first melted square to the last shaped mound.
steps: Line a tray with baking paper. Set it aside flat, near the fire.
Preheat the pan empty for 1 minute over very low heat, then reduce the flame to the minimum.
Pour the chopped chocolate into the pan. Stir continuously for 3 minutes, until smooth and glossy. Add the oil or cocoa butter if using.
Remove from heat as soon as the texture is smooth. The chocolate will continue to heat on the remaining melted liquid: don't wait.
Add the broken crackers, puffed rice and peanuts to the pan.
Mix with a spatula, lifting from underneath, until each piece is coated. Avoid crushing the crackers.
Drop spoonfuls of the mixture onto the tray and squeeze each mound with the end of the spoon to form compact clumps.
Sprinkle with fleur de sel, then refrigerate for about 40 minutes, until the clumps are firm to the touch.

title: No-bake cheesecake with red berries
intro: It all comes down to temperature: really softened cream cheese, really cold cream, really cooled topping.
titane: Only the compote goes over the heat. Preheat the empty titanium pan for one minute over medium heat before adding the fruit: the heat is distributed evenly across the entire surface, the syrup reduces in a few minutes and doesn't stick. You get a smooth, glossy glaze, without any transfer from the pan.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake requires at least 6 hours of chilling, preferably overnight; start the day before.
Line the bottom of a 23 cm springform pan with parchment paper.
Mix the crumbs, sugar, and melted butter until the mixture is uniformly sandy in texture.
Press firmly into the bottom of the pan using the back of a glass. Refrigerate.
Beat the cream cheese alone until perfectly smooth. If there are any grains at this stage, they will persist throughout.
Add the icing sugar, vanilla, lemon juice, and red fruit purée. Beat until homogeneous.
Whip the very cold cream until stiff peaks form (the cream stands upright on the whisk without collapsing).
Fold the whipped cream into the fruit mixture using a spatula, in three additions, to preserve the volume.
Spread the batter over the cold crust and smooth the surface.
Refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until completely set.
Preheat the titanium pan empty for 1 minute over medium heat. Add the red fruits, sugar, and lemon juice. Stir until the fruits release their juice and begin to simmer.
Dilute the cornstarch in cold water, pour into the pan, and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the syrup coats the back of a spoon.
Transfer to a cold container and allow to cool completely. Warm glaze would melt the filling.
Spread the topping over the cheesecake, then refrigerate for 1 hour before slicing.

title: Cinnamon churros
intro: Everything hinges on the panade (cooked dough made from water, butter and flour): dry enough to hold the flute, flexible enough to come out of the piping bag without forcing.
titane: No need for a deep fryer: pour 2 cm of oil into the titanium pan and fry briefly. Heat to 180°C (350°F), check with a drop of batter which should rise to the surface in three seconds, and turn the churros halfway through cooking with tongs. The thick base retains heat when you add a new batch, which prevents the churros from becoming greasy.
steps: Combine the water, butter, sugar and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil over medium heat, the butter must be completely melted before the first bubbles appear.

Lower the heat. Pour the flour in all at once and mix vigorously with a spatula. The dough will gather into a ball and pull away from the sides of the pan in about one minute. Remove from heat at this precise moment, beyond that it will dry out.
Transfer to another bowl and let cool for five minutes. Dough that is too hot will cook the egg.
Add the egg then the vanilla. Work until you have a smooth, glossy dough that falls slowly from the spatula.
Fill a pastry bag fitted with a star piping tip. Heat the oil in the pan to 180 °C.
Pipe 12 cm sticks directly above the oil, cut with scissors. Four or five per batch, no more. Allow 2 minutes per side, until a deep golden colour.
Drain on paper towels for 30 seconds, no longer.
Mix the sugar and cinnamon in a shallow dish. Roll the warm churros in it: the sugar only adheres to a warm surface.
Serve immediately, with the chocolate sauce on the side.

title: Chocolate cheesecake on a flourless brownie base
intro: It all comes down to gently cooking the appliance: the edges set, the center still mobile, then a night in the cold which finishes the job for you.
titane: The cake is transferred from the pan to the oven, and the technique shifts: it involves stopping the cooking process too soon. Gently shake the mold about a centimeter. If the center ripples like a cooled custard, it's ready. The residual heat trapped in the mold will finish setting as it cools. Waiting until it's visibly firm will result in a slightly grainy texture when sliced.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake cools and then refrigerates overnight; start the day before.
Heat the oven to 170 °C. Line the bottom of a 20 cm springform pan with baking paper.
Melt the dark chocolate with the butter in a double boiler, or in a saucepan over very low heat. Remove as soon as the mixture is smooth.
Incorporate the sugar and cocoa, then the egg. Mix until the batter becomes glossy.
Add the almond flour and salt. Work just enough for the dough to be homogeneous.
Spread the dough in the pan in an even layer. Bake for 5 minutes: the base should simply firm up on the surface. Remove and set aside. Lower the oven to 160 °C.
Whisk the cream cheese with the sugar until the grains disappear. Add the eggs one by one, mixing at low speed to avoid incorporating air.
Bring the 120 g of cream to a simmer. Pour it in three batches over the chocolate and cocoa, emulsifying in the center (stirring in small tight circles to bind fat and liquid). Let cool slightly.
Combine the chocolate mixture and the cream cheese batter. Mix with a spatula to a smooth texture, without bubbles.
Pour over the pre-baked brownie base. Tap the pan on the work surface to expel air.
Bake for 40 minutes at 160 °C. The edges should be set, the center still trembling over a diameter of five centimeters.
Let cool to room temperature, then refrigerate overnight, without covering for the first hour.
The next day, chop the dark chocolate. Heat the 80 g of cream, pour it over, wait one minute without stirring, then mix from the center outward to a smooth ganache.
Top the cold cheesecake. Slice with a blade dipped in hot water and wiped between each cut.

title: Roasted tomato and red pepper soup
intro: It all comes down to roasting: brightly colored vegetables before the oven give a dark and concentrated soup, whereas simple oven cooking only produces a mild puree.

ing.note: The top was sliced off to expose the pods.

titane: Preheat the empty skillet for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat before placing the vegetables cut-side down. This creates a Maillard reaction (browning of sugars and proteins due to dry heat) that a baking sheet alone never produces. The skillet then goes directly into the oven: no transferring required, all the juices remain in the same container and end up in the blender.
steps: Preheat the oven to 200°C. Place the empty pan over medium-high heat and let it heat up for 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour the avocado oil. Place the tomatoes, peppers and onion cut-side down on the pan bottom. Season with salt and pepper.
Slip the garlic bulb between the vegetables, cut-side up, and cover it with a small ramekin turned upside down: the trapped steam will confit it instead of burning it.
Sear for 3 to 4 minutes without stirring. The cut faces will release from the pan on their own when they are set.
Put the pan in the oven and roast for 40 minutes, until the skins blister and the tip of a knife slides through the peppers with no resistance. Remove and let cool for 15 minutes.
Transfer the vegetables and all the cooking juices to the blender. Squeeze the garlic bulb to release the garlic pulp. Add the dried basil and the broth.
Blend until perfectly smooth. Taste and adjust the seasoning, thin with a little more broth if the soup seems too thick.
Serve with a drizzle of olive oil, a few drops of coconut milk, a splash of balsamic reduction and fresh basil.

title: Crispy rolled wafers
intro: It all comes down to thickness: the thinner the layer of dough, the faster the wafer dries and breaks cleanly under the tooth.
titane: Preheat the pan empty over low heat, then wipe it with a thin film of oil. On this dry, hot surface, the batter won't stick: the waffle will release on its own once golden brown. This spontaneous release allows you to roll it without tearing. Never force it with a spatula before this signal.
steps: Whisk the egg whites with the icing sugar, vanilla sugar and salt until soft peaks form. There's no need to beat stiff: the goal is simply to dissolve the sugar.
Sift the flour and cornstarch over the mixture. Mix until you have a perfectly smooth batter.
Pour in the vegetable oil and mix briefly, just until it disappears into the dough.
Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over low heat. Wipe with a paper towel soaked in grapeseed oil: the surface should remain dry to the touch, without any puddles.
Pour half a tablespoon of dough and immediately spread it into a very thin disc with the back of the spoon.
Let it cook without touching it. When the bottom is golden and the wafer releases itself from the base, immediately roll it around the handle of a wooden spoon while it is still flexible.
Remove the rolls from the pan and set them aside on a wire rack. They will harden in 5 minutes.
Wipe the pan, lightly oil it again, and repeat. Adjust the cooking time of the first waffle as a guide for the following ones: titanium heats up quickly and retains its heat.

title: Speculoos and mascarpone icebox cake
intro: It all comes down to two things: a very brief soaking of the biscuits and a fairly long resting period so that they become soft without falling apart.
titane: Melt the speculoos spread in a titanium pan over low heat. The heat rises quickly and spreads evenly without any hot spots: the spread becomes smooth and spreadable in seconds, without ever becoming grainy or separating. Remove from the heat as soon as it flows into a ribbon.
steps: Combine the liquid cream, mascarpone, icing sugar, vanilla, cinnamon and 70g of speculoos paste in a cold bowl.
Whisk or beat the mixture until stiff peaks form. Refrigerate.

Melt the remaining speculoos spread in a titanium pan over low heat, stirring constantly. Stop as soon as it is fluid and spreadable: if it gets too hot, it will become runny and seep through the layers.
Pour the cooled coffee into a shallow dish. Dip the biscuits one by one, for just a second on each side. They should remain firm to the touch.
Arrange them side by side in a 20cm square dish, in a tight and even layer. Break some of them to fill the edges.
Spread about 90g of melted paste over the base, then spread half of the whipped cream evenly with a spatula.
Start again: soaked biscuits, melted dough, leftover cream.
Finish with a drizzle of speculoos spread, biscuit crumbs and grated chocolate.

Cover with plastic wrap, pressing it directly onto the surface of the dish, and refrigerate for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight. The biscuits should have a cake-like texture. Slice with a knife that has been dipped in hot water and wiped dry between each slice.

title: Pistachio, date and dark chocolate bars
intro: It all comes down to the texture of the base: blended enough to hold its shape when cut, coarse enough so that you can still feel the pistachio under your teeth.
ing: A few crushed pistachios for finishing
titane: The titanium pan acts as a double boiler. Placed over very low heat, it distributes heat evenly and melts the chocolate without a saucepan or simmering water. Two conditions: stir continuously with a spatula, and remove from the heat as soon as the mixture is fluid. The temperature rises quickly; a few seconds too long is all it takes to burn the chocolate.
steps: Plan ahead: the base should be frozen for 1 hour before assembly.

Process the pistachios, cashews, dates, coconut and cardamom in a food processor. Add the water and continue until you obtain a fine paste that clumps when pressed between your fingers without crumbling.
Line a rectangular 23 × 13 cm mold with parchment paper, leaving the edges to overhang. Press the paste onto the bottom, compact it with the back of a spoon until the surface is perfectly level.
Spread the pistachio butter over the entire base in an even layer. Scatter crushed pistachios over it and press lightly to help them adhere.
Place in the freezer for 1 hour, until everything is firm when pressed with your finger.

Place the titanium pan over very low heat, pour the chopped chocolate into it. Stir continuously for 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from heat as soon as the chocolate is smooth and flowing; it will finish melting off the heat.
Unmold by pulling on the paper, cut into 14 bars with a heated knife blade. Coat each bar with chocolate (pour a thin, even layer that covers the surface), scatter pistachios over it.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes, until the chocolate sets. Store in the refrigerator for about ten days, or in the freezer for up to three months.

title: Mango-coconut ice pops with a chocolate coating
intro: It all comes down to the mango/coconut milk ratio: enough fruit for density, enough fat to keep the ice cream soft to the bite.

ing.note: depending on the acidity of the fruit

ing: dark chocolate with no added sugar
titane: The titanium pan placed over a pan of simmering water replaces the double boiler and dipping bowl. It heats the chocolate without creating a hot spot, and its wide surface accommodates the stick flat: a single pass is enough to coat it.
steps: Plan ahead: the sticks will set in the freezer for 2 hours 30 minutes, organize accordingly.
Blend the frozen mango with the coconut milk until you obtain a perfectly smooth texture without graininess. Taste. Add the honey only if the fruit is too acidic.
Distribute the mixture into eight silicone molds. Tap the molds on the work surface to remove air bubbles, then insert the sticks.
Place the molds flat in the freezer. Allow 2 hours 30 minutes for complete setting.

Combine the chocolate and coconut oil in the titanium pan. Place it over a saucepan of gently simmering water on low heat, and stir with a spatula until the mixture is smooth and glossy. Remove from the water bath at this point.
Pour the melted chocolate into a tall, narrow container to facilitate dipping the sticks.
Unmold one stick at a time and dip it into the chocolate remaining in the pan, turning it with a smooth motion. The coating sets in seconds upon contact with the cold.
Serve immediately, or return to the freezer for up to three months. In this case, remove the sticks 15 minutes before eating.

title: Mini speculoos cheesecakes
intro: It all comes down to the contrast between a well-packed, almost compact base, and a whipped cream that remains airy until serving.
titane: Before binding them with butter, toast the biscuit crumbs for 2 to 3 minutes in a dry titanium pan over medium heat, stirring constantly. The dry, even heat awakens the spices and evaporates any moisture: the base holds its shape better when cut and retains its crispness after two hours of chilling. Remove from heat (transfer immediately to a cold container) as soon as the aroma develops, otherwise the sugar from the biscuits will burn.
steps: Plan ahead: the cheesecake must refrigerate for at least 2 hours before being unmoulded and served.
Mix the 200 g of crumbs with the melted butter until you reach the texture of damp sand: the mixture should press together between your fingers without crumbling.
Divide into six glasses or into a muffin tin lined with cases. Pack down firmly with the back of a spoon or a small glass with a flat bottom.
Whip the cold heavy cream with a whisk until it is firm and the whisk leaves trails in it. Stop there: beyond this point, it will grain.
In another bowl, work the cream cheese with the icing sugar and vanilla until the mixture is perfectly smooth. Cream cheese that is still too cold would create lumps that are impossible to correct.
Fold in the whipped cream in three additions, using a spatula (blend by lifting the mixture from the centre outwards to preserve the air).
Pipe or spoon the mixture onto the bases and smooth the surface.
Coat each cheesecake with a thin layer of speculoos spread that is just warm and fluid enough to spread on its own.
Refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours. The surface should be firm to the touch.
Sprinkle with the reserved crumbs at the last moment and serve well chilled.

title: Lemon Whipped Cottage Cheese
intro: It all depends on the mixing time: below two minutes, the cottage cheese remains grainy, above that it becomes a smooth cream that holds its shape on a spoon.
titane: The finishing seeds and nuts are tossed dry in the titanium pan over medium heat for two to three minutes, stirring constantly. No oil is needed: the coating is sufficient, and the dry heat awakens the oils without burning them. Remove from the pan as soon as the aroma develops, otherwise the residual heat will finish the job for you.
steps: Zest the lemon over the food processor bowl, then squeeze it. Set aside half of the juice: you will adjust the amount at the end.
Add the cottage cheese, grated garlic, salt and pepper. Blend for two full minutes, scraping down the sides once halfway through.
Check the texture: the cream should be smooth, without any perceptible grain under the tongue. If it remains grainy, continue for thirty seconds.
Taste it. Adjust with the remaining lemon juice, salt, and pepper. The acidity should be clearly noticeable; it carries the rest of the flavors.
Spread in a shallow dish, make a furrow with the back of a spoon, pour in the olive oil. Sprinkle with herbs and toasted seeds.

title: Instant orange, carrot and ginger ice cream
intro: It all comes down to temperature: the fruit must come out of the freezer completely frozen, otherwise you will get a lukewarm puree instead of ice cream.
titane: Toast the pecans (dry-roast them without oil or fat to develop their flavor) in a very hot titanium pan, without any oil. Shake the pan every twenty seconds. As soon as the nutty aroma rises, remove them from the pan (transfer them immediately to a cold plate): the residual heat from the metal will continue to cook the pecans and they will turn bitter.
steps: Take out the titanium pan without any oil, and heat it over medium heat. Add the chopped pecans and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly browned. Transfer to a cold plate and set aside.
Place the orange, carrot, banana and ginger in the blender bowl. Pour in only half of the almond milk.
Pulse the mixture, scraping down the sides of the bowl between each pulse. Add the remaining almond milk one spoonful at a time, only when the blade is running dry.
Continue mixing until you obtain a smooth, satiny mass that holds its shape on the spoon. Stop there: beyond this point, the mixture will heat up and lose its consistency.
Divide between two chilled bowls, sprinkle with toasted pecans and serve immediately.

title: Roasted beetroot, cashew and harissa dip
intro: It's all about the texture: cashews soaked enough and a long enough mixing time so that the dip becomes silky, never grainy.

ing.note: soaked for 15 minutes in boiling water, then drained

ing: small handful of fresh mint leaves
titane: Roast the diced beets directly in a dry, covered pan over medium-low heat. The titanium cookware heats up quickly and retains heat: the exposed surfaces caramelize while the steam trapped under the lid cooks the center. Seven to eight minutes before the end, remove the lid to allow the moisture to evaporate and the sugars to concentrate. In the same pan, while it's still warm, toast (dry-heat to release the aromas) the cumin for thirty seconds.
steps: Preheat the oven for roasting the beet.
Cover the cashews with boiling water and let soak for 15 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water.

Heat the pan over medium-low heat. Add the diced beet, cover and let cook for 15 minutes, stirring twice. Uncover, continue for 8 minutes: the edges should brown and the flesh should yield to the tip of a knife. Transfer from the pan and let cool slightly.
In the still-warm pan, off the heat, stir the cumin for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Combine in the blender bowl the beet, cashews, silken tofu, lemon juice, tahini, olive oil, garlic, zest, harissa, toasted cumin and salt.
Blend at full speed for 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down the sides. Stop when the mixture is smooth and glossy, with no grains under the tongue.
Add the water one spoonful at a time, blender running, until desired consistency: the dip should fall slowly from the spoon. Adjust with lemon and salt.
Transfer to a bowl, make a groove with the back of a spoon, drizzle with olive oil. Sprinkle with mint and crumbled goat cheese.

title: Shredded tofu wrap with spices, pan-fried
intro: It all comes down to two things: really pressed tofu, and a thin enough layer in the pan so that it browns instead of cooking in its own steam.
titane: Preheat the titanium pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat before adding any oil. Then pour in the grapeseed oil, wait until it just begins to simmer, spread the tofu out, and leave it undisturbed. It will stick at first, then release on its own once a crust has formed: that's your cue, not the clock. The same pan will then be used to make the sauce and glaze the tofu (coating it with a reduced sauce until it's glossy and glossy), without transferring anything.
steps: Drain the tofu, wrap it in absorbent paper and press it under a weight for 10 to 15 minutes. The water that is removed now will not soften the crust later.
Grate the tofu, or slice it into thin strips with a vegetable peeler. You're looking for irregular strands, not cubes.
In a bowl, mix the tofu with the paprika, cumin, garlic and onion powders, pepper, chili powder, and cornstarch. Mix with your fingertips so that each strand is coated.
Heat the empty titanium pan for 2 to 3 minutes over high heat. Add the grapeseed oil and wait until it simmers slightly.

Spread the tofu in a thin layer over the entire surface. Let it sear without stirring. When the strands pull away from the bottom on their own and sound crispy when lifted with a spatula, flip it in large batches and repeat. Cook for 12 to 15 minutes in total, reducing the heat to medium-high if the spices are browning too quickly.

Push the tofu to one side of the pan and reduce the heat to medium. In the remaining space, stir in the gochujang, soy sauce, minced garlic, juice of half a lemon, honey, and water. Cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the sauce is smooth and hot.
Bring everything together and stir for 1 minute over low heat: the tofu should be coated and shiny, the sauce should no longer run to the bottom.
While the food is searing, cut the lettuce and cucumber, and remove the pickled turnips.
Warm the buns, spread the yogurt and garlic sauce, top with tofu and then vegetables. Roll up tightly.

title: Watermelon, red berry and lime salad
intro: It all depends on the temperature of the fruit and the timing of when you add the dressing: too soon, the watermelon releases its water and the salad becomes watery.
titane: No cooking involved here; the pan stays in the cupboard. The key is the salt. A pinch in the vinaigrette, not on the fruit: it distributes evenly and brings out the watermelon's sweetness instead of masking it. The same principle applies as adjusting the seasoning of a sauce off the heat.
steps: Combine the watermelon, blueberries, strawberries, and cherries in a large bowl. Work with the very cold fruit, taken out of the refrigerator at the last minute.
In a small bowl, whisk together the honey, lime juice, zest, and salt until well blended (the honey should be completely dissolved in the juice, with no stringy bits at the bottom of the bowl).
Pour the vinaigrette over the fruit just before sitting down to eat.
Mix with a spoon, lifting the fruit from underneath rather than stirring, so as not to crush the strawberries.
Roughly chop the mint by hand and sprinkle it over the surface.
Serve immediately in bowls that have been chilled in the refrigerator for 10 minutes. Alternatively, let the salad rest in the refrigerator for 20 minutes before dressing.

title: No-bake chocolate cookie cake
intro: Everything hinges on the chocolate sauce: it must remain smooth and glossy to coat each piece of biscuit without making them soggy.
ing: The zest of half an orange
titane: The titanium pan serves as a saucepan for both heating stages. Its rapid heat distribution eliminates hot spots that would cause the chocolate to seize (separating the cocoa butter from the mass, resulting in a sandy texture). Between the base and the ganache, a rinse with hot water and a wipe with a cloth are all that's needed: the cocoa residue won't transfer to the second preparation.
steps: Line a 20cm springform pan with baking paper, base and sides.
In a titanium pan over medium heat, combine the milk, cream, butter, and sugar. Heat, stirring, until the sugar and butter are completely dissolved.
Reduce the heat to low. Sift the cocoa directly into the pan and whisk until the mixture is perfectly smooth, with no lumps at the bottom.
Remove from heat. Add the chopped dark chocolate, orange zest, coffee, and salt. Whisk for about 5 minutes: the sauce should become glossy and coat the back of a spoon.
Pour the sauce over the crushed biscuits and cocoa nibs in a bowl. Mix with a spatula, lifting and folding, until each piece is coated.
Transfer to the mold. Press down in an even layer with the back of a spoon, packing the edges down well.
Cover with film and refrigerate for a minimum of 8 hours, preferably overnight.

Rinse and dry the pan. Heat the cream in it over medium heat until it just begins to simmer, but do not boil. Pour it over the dark chocolate, milk chocolate, butter, and salt, which have been combined in a bowl.
Let it rest for 2 minutes without touching it, then gently mix in the center, in a spiral, until you obtain a smooth and shiny ganache.
Let it cool to room temperature, then pour it over the completely cooled cake. Smooth with a spatula.
Refrigerate for 1 hour, until the ganache is firm to the touch.
Remove from the mold and slice with a knife that has been rinsed under hot water and wiped dry between each slice.

title: Pan-fried spicy beef turnovers
intro: It all comes down to the crust of the beef: if the meat sits untouched, it browns instead of boiling, and the garnish retains that seared taste right under the cheese.
titane: One pan for two cooking methods. Sear the beef over high heat, wipe the pan clean, arrange the turnovers in a rosette pattern, and bake. The handle is oven-safe, so no need for a baking dish, no transferring, and no second washing up. Wiping the pan is essential: any juices left in the bottom would burn during the seventeen minutes in the oven.
steps: Heat the empty titanium pan over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in the grapeseed oil: it should ripple without smoking.
Discard the onion and garlic. Sweat them (cook gently without browning) for 2 minutes, until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the ground beef in a single layer. Do not stir. Let it stick and then detach from the bottom on its own, about 4 minutes, before crumbling it with a spatula.
Season generously: garlic and onion powder, smoked paprika, cumin, chili, pepper, salt. Mix, then add the two peppers.
Stir in the tomato paste. Cook for 3 minutes over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until the tomato loses its acidity.
Add the spinach and a splash of water. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered for 6 minutes, until all the liquid has evaporated. Transfer the filling to a serving dish and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Wipe the pan with paper towels. Cut each tortilla in half. Place a little mozzarella in the center of each half-circle, then 1 to 2 tablespoons of filling, and fold into a triangle.
Mix the olive oil, parsley and salt in a small bowl.
Lightly oil the pan. Arrange the triangles in a rosette pattern, overlapping them slightly. Brush with parsley oil and distribute the remaining mozzarella.
Bake the pan as is for 17 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the cheese is melted. Let it rest for 3 minutes before serving: the filling will hold its shape better.

title: Homemade waffle cones
intro: A very thin dough, cooked piping hot and rolled within three seconds: everything depends on the speed of shaping.
titane: The batter hardens as it cools. Place your shaping cone (wooden or metal) next to the waffle iron before even pouring the first ladleful. Peel off the still-soft disc, tightly wrap it around the cone starting from the tip, hold for five seconds, then let it air cool on a wire rack. If you don't have a waffle iron with molds, a hot titanium pan will give the same result in a smoother version: spread two spoonfuls of batter into a thin disc, cook for one minute per side, and roll while still hot.
steps: Whisk the eggs and sugar until the mixture is smooth and slightly pale.
Pour in the warm melted butter, milk, and vanilla. Mix without incorporating air.
Add the flour and salt all at once. Whisk until you obtain a fluid batter, without lumps, that coats the spoon in a thin layer.
Let rest for 5 minutes, while heating the cone waffle iron (or the titanium pan over medium heat).
Place a small ladle of batter in the center, close and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until a dark blonde color and a caramel smell.
Release the disc with a spatula, roll it immediately around the cone mold, pointed end well sealed. Hold the pointed end closed for a few seconds while it sets.
Let cool upright in a glass or on a rack. The cone becomes crisp in a minute. Repeat with the remaining batter.

title: Crispy quinoa, raspberry and cocoa butter
intro: It all comes down to the quinoa: puffed dry in a hot pan, it retains a crispy sound that neither fat nor cold can soften.
titane: A single pan for both heating stages. Heated empty, it heats up quickly and distributes heat evenly: the quinoa grains burst cleanly in seconds, without any added fat. Wiped dry and then returned to very low heat, the same pan replaces the double boiler to melt the cocoa butter without ever overheating it.
steps: Plan ahead: the croustillants need one hour in the refrigerator before they set firm.
Heat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-high heat. It must be thoroughly hot before the first grain.
Pour the raw quinoa all at once, without any fat, and stir constantly. The grains pop and turn golden in 10 to 15 seconds, just like popcorn.
Transfer immediately to a cold bowl. The aroma should be toasted, never burnt.
Wipe the pan, return it to very low heat and melt the cacao butter while stirring, about 3 minutes, until you obtain a smooth liquid.
Meanwhile, grind the freeze-dried raspberries into a fine powder using a small mixer or spice grinder. Reserve one spoonful for finishing.
Off the heat, stir into the cacao butter the cashew butter, maple syrup, vanilla and raspberry powder. Mix until you have a homogeneous and glossy mass.
Add the puffed quinoa and mix with a spatula, without crushing the grains.
Drop spoonfuls onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, spread them into regular discs. Sprinkle with reserved raspberry powder and pistachios.
Refrigerate for 1 hour. The croustillants are ready when they are firm to the touch and come away cleanly from the paper.
Keep the croustillants in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to two weeks, or in the freezer for up to six months.

title: Soft cookies with chickpeas and dark chocolate
intro: Without an oven and without butter, everything depends on the thickness of the discs and the gentleness of the fire: too thick, the center remains raw; too hot, the edges burn before the dough sets.
titane: The covered pan acts as an oven. The lid reflects heat back onto the tops of the cookies while the titanium surface bakes the bases. Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over low-medium heat, lightly oil it, then leave it alone: the dough will stick at first, then release on its own once the crust has formed. That's your cue to flip, not the clock.
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas before blending: the smooth texture depends on it.

Blend the chickpeas with the peanut butter, honey and vanilla until you obtain a perfectly smooth paste. Scrape down the sides of the bowl once or twice: any remaining chickpea pieces would be visible when tasting.
Transfer the mixture to a mixing bowl. Add the almond flour and baking powder, mix until homogeneous.
Fold in the chocolate with a spatula, without overworking the dough.
Form ten balls, then flatten them into regular patties 1 cm thick. Regularity matters more than roundness.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium-low heat. Hold your hand ten centimetres above: the heat should rise noticeably, without smoke. Brush with a thin layer of oil.
Place the patties with space between them, cover and reduce to low heat. Cook for 10 minutes without moving them. They will release on their own when the base is set.
Gently flip with a thin spatula, cover and continue for 5 minutes: the edges should be lightly golden and the centre firm to the touch. If browning happens too quickly, lower the heat further.
Let cool slightly on a rack before serving. The cookies will finish setting as they cool.

title: Date, pistachio and dark chocolate ice cream bar
intro: It all comes down to the regularity of the layers: tightly packed dates, pistachio butter spread to the edges, melted chocolate barely warm.
titane: A titanium pan replaces a double boiler. Place it over very low heat, without preheating, and pour in the chopped chocolate. The mass of the metal distributes the heat evenly: no hot spots, no cracking. Stir continuously and remove from the heat as soon as the last pieces melt; the residual heat finishes the job.
steps: Plan ahead: the bar freezes in the freezer for one hour, allow for this time before serving.
Line a loaf pan with parchment paper. Split the dates lengthwise, remove the pits and arrange them flat, sticky side up.
Press them with your fingertips until you obtain a full and even layer, without holes. This is what will hold everything together.
Spread the pistachio butter and spread it with a spatula over the entire surface, right to the corners of the pan.
Coarsely chop the pistachios. Distribute half of them over the pistachio butter.
Break the chocolate into pieces in the titanium pan, over very low heat. Stir continuously with a spatula for 2 to 3 minutes, until smooth and glossy. Remove from heat as soon as fully melted.
Pour the chocolate over the pistachio layer, spread evenly and sprinkle with the remaining chopped pistachios. Press lightly to make them adhere.
Place in the freezer for a minimum of 1 hour, until completely set. Unmould, then cut with a knife or break into irregular shards.

title: Dark chocolate seed crackers
intro: It all comes down to thickness: a dough spread too generously will give a soft biscuit in the center, never that crispy texture that stands up to chocolate.
titane: Toast (dry-roast to enhance the flavors) the pumpkin, sunflower, and sesame seeds in a dry titanium pan over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring constantly. As soon as the sesame seeds turn golden and the seeds start to pop, transfer them to a cold bowl: the heat from the titanium pan would continue to cook them and cause bitterness.
steps: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F), fan-assisted. Line a baking tray with baking paper.
Combine all the seeds and salt in a large bowl. Pour in the water, mix, then let it sit for 10 minutes: the flax and chia release their mucilage and the mass becomes sticky, almost gel-like.
Place 8cm pastry rings on the baking sheet. Fill each with a spoonful of dough and spread evenly with a spatula to a thickness of 2-3mm. Remove the rings.
Bake for 20 minutes, until the edges are golden brown and the center no longer yields to the touch. Let cool on the baking sheet, without touching: the crispness will develop as it cools.
Melt the chocolate in a double boiler at a maximum temperature of 45°C, then let it cool to 31°C while stirring. Dip each cracker halfway or completely, and drain against the side of the bowl.
Place on baking paper and freeze for 10 minutes. The chocolate will set cleanly and break easily. Break in half when ready to serve.

title: Chocolate Easter Egg Crisps
intro: It all comes down to the temperature of the chocolate: melted gently, it coats each bubble of rice with a thin, shiny layer, without ever graining.
titane: No double boiler, no microwave. The chocolate melts directly in the titanium pan over very low heat, the spatula working around the edge rather than in the center where the heat is concentrated. The same pan then becomes the mixing bowl: the rice bubbles are coated in it without transferring. A single container, from start to finish.
steps: Plan ahead: refrigeration for at least 1 hour before serving.
Line a muffin tin with nine paper cases. Keep it within reach: the mixture sets quickly.
Place the chopped chocolate and coconut oil in the cold titanium pan. Set it over very low heat.
Stir continuously with a spatula, pushing the chocolate from the edges toward the center. Allow 3 minutes. The chocolate must be smooth and glossy, never smoking.
Remove the pan from the heat as soon as the chocolate is completely melted. The metal remains hot and completes the process on its own.
Pour the rice bubbles into the pan and mix gently, lifting the mass rather than crushing it. Each bubble must be coated.
Divide the mixture among the cases with a spoon, without pressing down.
Make a small nest in the center of each mound with the back of the spoon.
Place three or four mini eggs in each hollow, pressing very lightly.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour. The cracklies must be firm and come away cleanly from the case.

title: Pumpkin and black bean fritters with lemon tahini sauce
intro: It all comes down to how well the dough holds its shape and patience in the pan: a doughnut that is turned over too soon will tear.
ing: Greek yogurt or plain plant-based yogurt
titane: Preheat the empty pan for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat before adding any oil or butter. The heat rises quickly and remains even across the entire surface: the crust forms within the first few seconds of contact. After that, don't touch it. The doughnut will release itself when the top is set—this is the only reliable sign to flip it.
steps: Coarsely mash the black beans in a bowl, leaving a few whole pieces for texture. Add the eggs, pumpkin puree, oat flour, onion, herbs, garlic powder, smoked paprika, cumin, salt and pepper. Mix until you have a homogeneous, bound batter.
Let rest for 5 minutes: the oat flour absorbs moisture and the batter firms up.
Preheat the pan empty for 2 to 3 minutes over medium heat. Pour in the grapeseed oil or clarified butter, tilting the pan to coat the bottom. It should shimmer slightly, never smoke.

Shape patties about 4 cm in diameter and about 1 cm thick, and place them in the pan leaving space between them. Cook in two batches rather than one: an overcrowded pan loses heat and the patties steam rather than fry.

Let them set for 4 to 5 minutes without touching. When the patty releases easily under the spatula, flip it and brown the second side for 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer to a cooling rack rather than paper towels, to keep the crust crispy.

While cooking, whisk together the tahini, yogurt and lemon juice. The mixture will initially seize up: this is normal. Add the water in two stages, whisking, until you have a smooth, coating sauce. Season with salt, add garlic powder if desired.
Coat the still-warm patties with sauce and serve immediately.

title: Marbled chocolate bark with Halloween candies
intro: Everything hinges on the temperature: chocolate made too quickly will grain, and no amount of decoration will make up for a dull paste.
ing: baking paper cut to the diameter of the pan
titane: The titanium pan replaces the oven here. Its responsiveness allows you to melt the chocolate over very low heat, without any heating steps: you place it on the stovetop, remove it, and place it back on. The base continues to radiate heat even after being removed from the heat, which is enough to finish melting. Do not preheat the pan empty, unlike when cooking with salt—the chocolate would be damaged upon contact.
steps: Plan ahead: the bark takes one hour in the refrigerator, account for this time before serving.
Line the bottom of the cold pan with parchment paper, laying it flat. Place on very low heat.
Spread the milk chocolate in an even layer. Let it warm through without touching it for one minute.
Add the white chocolate in islands over the surface. It melts faster: it enters the scene later.

Guide the melting with intervals, approximately six minutes: thirty seconds on the heat, thirty seconds off the heat, gently smoothing with a spatula. The chocolate must stay glossy and fluid, never smoking.

Off the heat, marble it (blend the two chocolates on the surface without homogenizing) with the tip of a wooden skewer, using slow, crossing movements. Stop as soon as the pattern pleases you: overworked, it turns to uniform beige.
Immediately sprinkle over the mini chocolates, the sprinkles, the pumpkins and the ghosts. Press lightly to anchor them in the still-soft mass.
Slide the entire pan into the refrigerator, or slide the parchment paper onto a cold baking sheet. Allow one hour until completely set.
Peel off the paper and break the slab by hand into irregular pieces. The break must be clean and crisp.
